column2: review
Had a blast riding the moto bikes around the island, bring all your documentation, drivers license etc.

Best nature, fresh air and photographic views. Easy to go there, and local travel expenses are so low (if you use public transportation  like bus and ship). You should rent a bike and explore freely the whole island.

We had a fine time on Udo Island, where we rented one of the funny little electric cars and were able to see most of the island. It's better to arrive earlier in the day then we did, so you can spend time enjoying that Charming Island. Another highlight was feeding the seagulls with chips you can buy for $2 on the ferry.
It has good scenery on the water there is a bus tour that took you all around the island and they have crystal clear beaches.

What a fun little island! Exploring the island on a motorized bike/trike was an awesome experience. To rent the trikes an international class A drivers license is needed (US Military living in Korea can use your ID card and Korean drivers license). No license is needed for the motorized 2-wheeled bikes. This is the easiest way to travel the island making frequent stops to see the scenery or stop at one of the many cafes or restaurants. We saw tour busses, and a few regular cars, but seems like the majority of visitors chose the motorized trike to see the island. The ferry from Seongsan Port on Jeju to  Cheonjin Port on Udo runs every 30 minutes and the ride was about 15 minutes. There was an air-conditioned room on the upper deck but it was floor seating only. It is possible to see the whole island in a few hours.

Udo, which means cow island because of its shape, has been a popular island trip from the island of Jeju.  Taking about three to four hour to circle on an electric bike, it s a great day trip (there are plenty of lodgings for those who want to stay longer).  With only a handful of full size cars on its road, it s a fantastic place to ride a bike around.  Also, for a small island, the amount of dining and cafe options are impressive. Just going around to sample some cafes and restaurants can easily fill up a full day on Udo.  As the island is famous for peanuts, there are lots of peanut flavored products available ranging from ice cream to makgeolli (Korean traditional wine).
lot of things to do in the island!  No matter you want to eat the Hallasan Fried Rice with a complimentary funny cooking show or walk around and enjoy the scenery

We took a taxi from our hotel in Jeju City, which took about an hour, to the Ferry Terminal. It was pretty easy to buy the ticket. Once we got to the island, it wasn't really clear what to do, so we followed everyone to a small building that was selling bus tour tickets. We didn't get the bus we wanted, though they both seem to just drive around the island and you can hop on and off. We found out later that we could have rented a little tricycle moped. We enjoyed ourselves. Worth the trip.

we went here early morning but already have a lot of visitor. The ferry very convenient, when you in ferry terminal, remember need to fill up a form (like immigration) total 2 sheets and need to keep it because need to check when you return. around 20 mins will be arrive. Udo is very big and beautiful Island, have a lot of local culture and you can spend at least half day to visit. Trips: Although have a lot of restaurants but the price have a little bit higher.

The island is beautiful, yet very cold especially in winter time. We aimed for halla rice and peanut ice cream. Just the shop near the port has peanut ice cream (not just putting nuts on that!). We used the sightseeing bus and by foot to travel around the island.

If you are travelling with small kids, i suggest to drive a car into the island. (They allow car to enter the island if having kids below 6 years old), really regret that we park our car at the multi storey parking, with all the high hope to rent a electric scooter (the one with 3 wheels)The electric scooter is strictly for 2 person only (they dont allow 2 adult + 1 baby too)Only those with Class A international license allow to rent the electric scooter (i am a Class B international license holder (allowed to drive car only)If you plan to travel the island by bus, it will waste lots of time on queueing and waiting for the bus. The bus driver will not explain any tourist spot in english, so you will have a hard time to decide which is the good spot to get down from the bus.Overall the island has nothing special with we are not allow to ride the electric scooter and generally the island is too crowded with tourist.
we rent the bicycle for island sightseeing.It was fun, relax and enjoy. The food was delicious, peanut ice cream was good.

But too overcrowded by visitors even at September! :)Possible to rent bicycle or scooter (electric or usual) or quadro-unit and make your trip around the island (but you need actual international driver license with correct category!).It's big enough for walkers.Very small and narrow road all around island - be very, very, very careful as main part of drivers are young people with very little experience of driving and winds in their heads (sorry, but true!) :)
Beautiful coastal scenery and  transportation is very accommodating and flexible. Various stop worth staying for pictures taking.

A very pretty island which u must go.We rented the motor biking which do not request you to have a driving licence.You can have close connection with the natural environment and the whole experience is amazing. Peanut ice cream is also another must try item there

Udo Island is one of the most beautiful places on earth. The island is surrounded by charming beaches and coastline. Just felt that a day trip here is not enough. Be sure to try its delicious peanut ice cream, peanut smoothie and peanut pizza! You can also rent a tuk tuk like tricycle around the island. A must visit indeed! :)

So we saw great reviews and some great pictures online. Thought this was a must see place. To be fair, the island has some real potential to be fantastic, however it was a hot August day, it was getting very crowded.Highlights:- some really nice sights to take in and you can tour the whole island in about 4hrs (including stops along the way)- one let we went for a walk and ran into some people camping. Very pleasant and offered us coffee. We hadn t encountered too many people willing to go out of their way, so was a nice touch. - took a high speed boat ride around the cliff that looks like the cow laying down (hence the name cow island). That was great and worth the 30k KRW for two adults.Low points:- way too much garbage around. Just about every beautiful sight is ruined by plastic bottles and litter. - a lot of areas were closed like it was low season (or maybe we were just early in the day)- lots people standing around endlessly. Got a little frustrating at times. Advice if you do go:- we took the bus. It was good, but we were on a bus schedule. If I did it again, I would have rented a small electric vehicle (which needs an international driving license to rent). Not sure if the cost, but they looked fun and you control your own timeline then.
In short, you will be walking/driving with chaotic buses, motor cycles, bicycles, walkers & rental cars in single lane. Terrible visit.

We took the ferry at around 9:30am. 15 min rides and we are there. Since we did not have our international driving license, we can only rent the electric tandem bicycle which was great for the kids.Cycling around the island is around 12km. Just go with the flow and stop at leisure for peanut ice cream.Must stop plave for lunch is ha ha Ho Ho Cafe famed for the burger. The best burger we ever had.We ended our bicycle trip at around 2pm and managed to catch the 2:30pm ferry back.
you can travel around udo for juz 1 day enjoy the scenery travel juz with bus . but ferry ticket at jetty for tourist u need passport when you buy the ticket.

It's a beautiful island just 15mins ferry ride away from Jeju Island. Rented cars are not allowed to travel over so we parked our car at the terminal port in Seongsan. Upon arrival at the port in Udo, you will see a few shops just right infront of the port start promoting their offering on bike rentals. Standard rental is 2hrs (KRW 10,000 per pax) for a standard bicycle. So great to tour around and have the best seafood pot ever along the coastal. Peanut ice-cream is a must have, it is so good! We did not manage to visit any of the recommended sightseeing places due to short of time but we had a great time cycling around taking pictures, along with the beautiful weather. Definitely will return again.
This is a beautiful island with beautiful beaches and scenaries. You can take the ferries and on the island you can hire a bike or take the round the island hop on bus.

It took about 10 minutes to travel on a ferry to visit Udo (thanks to G map)!I decided to walked around the coastline after lunch on arrival.An interesting island with some public arts and you wouldn t stop taking photos!It worth spending some time walking around! (A number of transportation options are available, such as bike, e-bike and bus)!

Udo island is a nice place to visit enroute to Seongsan llchulbong. The ferry ride took 30 mins to this scenic island made of volcanic rock. On the island there are abundance of seaside food eateries and cafe. Rent a motorized double-seated scooter to travel round the island.
This nature island was very nice & the Day trip here was very good option, Biking around was memorable. It's a bit to book ferry round trip & need to check carefully if you don't want to miss it!

Easily accessible via 15min ferry from Jeju Seongsanpo harbour, Udo is ideal for a short day trip or sorta those places in Korean dramas whereby couples miss the last ferry and have to wing it for the night). Anyways we made sure to check the ferry schedule. We had 2 hours and decided to walk instead of renting motorised vehicles (didn't have IDL), bicycles (too hot) or tourist hop-on-hop-off bus (too rushed). Other than tourists nearly running down pedestrians and into other vehicles, it's a nice place to explore & hike for nature lovers. Ferry return is a little pricey at –8500 but should be ok if staying over. We tried the peanut icecream but didn't think it was that great. Basically vanilla soft serve with sprinkled peanuts. Perhaps the wrong shop.

Come in the morning to avoid large crowds. The island is so peaceful - different from the Jeju mainland. A return ticket costs 8500W. You can see a lot of pension homes here. I rented a regular bike (10000W) and cycled around the island. The path was relatively easy with only very minimal inclination. It took me about 4-5 hours to cover the whole island, together with stops for photographs and visit to the lighthouse. I did not stop for any food though. By the time I left, which was about 2 pm, a large number of people started arriving. Also, parking at the Seongsanhang Port was 8000W, but I got a 50% discount (not so sure why).

Nice little island to spend the day. If your a foreigner bring your passport with you to buy your ferry ticket.on the island itself you can walk around but by far the most popular way is to rent a bike. Pedal or electric powered that can seat 2 people.You will need a drivers license for the electric one though. Cute little beaches around and you can stop off and try some of the peanut ice cream which Udo is famous for. Also you can hike up to Udo lighthouse and get a good view from the top and see most of the island. A good way to spend a day

In my opinion the best way to go around the island is a bicycle. About 16km. Took us 4h to make it, with stop in every single possible place, including a lunch brake, rest on a beach, etc. Most interesting for us were diving women, we had a chance to see at work in few places. Probably the island is crowded in a season. In May we had good time and enjoy the trip very much.

I recommend riding the bicycle if the weather permits to enjoy the island fully! It took me about  about 3-4 hours (with picture stops) to complete the whole island and it was a very enjoyable and easy ride.
Nice Place to visit for a quick favor of what Jeju is like. However, the place is too commercialized and is expensive. Bus do not go to very single tourist location and you need to walk a fair bit.
It s a small island but very popular! Very easy to get on the bus to go around the island! Very windy there! Recommend black beach and Cow s head peak!
We brought our hire car on the ferry over and stayed for about 3 hours. There is some nice scenery however it wasn't enough to justify staying for an entire day.

The day were there, there was a big festival going on and all forms of vehicle rentals were not allowed.  So it gave us time to walk and browse around the ferry terminal area.  Many delightful cafes.  Will go back to do the nature trails around the island.

We drove to Udo Island by taking the ferry from Seongsanpo Port.  We had to pay ferry charges for the car and the number of persons going to the island. We spent about  6 to 7 hours on the island. While we drove around the island, my daughter & friend rented each a bike when we reached Udo.  Scenery and the beaches in Udo Island are not as nice as in Jeju itself.  The fun parts were riding the e-scooter or bike around the small island, stopping by for the famous peanut ice cream and hiking the udobong peak.

Strolling numbers of beaches in Udo or climb the peak of Udobong. Simply taste the peanut ice cream and hallabong ice cream from the various stall along the coastal lines. The local turban shell is a must try in Udo. Getting around is easy either by shuttle bus, ATV, bike ride or just a pair of feet is all you need.
Spent 6 hr on the island with a car.Lots of things to see and do. Tasty fresh seafood everywhere.Easy drive on car ferry to island.

It is a must visit place if you are nature lovers. The beaches are so scenic. You could try many fresh seafood dishes. Eat at the icecream stalls overlooking the fields. Canola flowers are everywhere here in April
The island offer  you very scenic view. The Bus ride was fun, the driver is indeed funny. You have to try the famous peanut ice cream. We visit few cafes which is very instagramable.

All the reviews I read of Udo made it sound so beautiful and quaint but I found in reality it was actually rather anti-climactic. The sights don t begin to compare to those on Jeju and while the island is quaint I didn t find it endearing enough to justify the trip over. The peanut ice cream is worth trying though!

Nice getaway island. We drove to the passenger terminal, park our car and take the ferry. The ferry ride there was fantastic. We fed the seagulls flying around the boat. it was a spectacular view!To travel within the island, take a bus or pay for a bike..it is a covered bike really cute. Or you can ride a bicycle.We took the bus, need to pay 6k won. There is a ticket office for shuttle bus. Buses numbered k1,k2,k3,rtc..there were 4 stops.the first stop has many actuvities, cafes, restaurants.You can spend an hour or more here. Second stop is lighthouse so we stop too.   The 3rd and 4th stops are the beaches. We did  not get off the  bus  l

If you have the opportunity to visit Jeju, please go to Udo Island.Even it is tiny little Island it has quite many things to explore.I learn to ride a horse, try the gu jeng ki (a green shel seafood) and met the hanyeo. The cliff view there also magnificent. I love the peanut dumplings.

From the Jejusi bus terminal we took bus 201 to Udo. It took about 1 1/2 hours. Definitely download the app Naver to navigate your way around the island, as Google Maps does not have any results for public transportation. We spent 4 hours on the island. Ferry ride from the port is only about 15 minutes each way. Buying a ticket can be a little chaotic as there are no signs in English but we just held up 2 fingers for two passengers and were given 2 round-trip tickets. Upon arrival in Udo expect to be bombarded with shop owners yelling at you to rent bicycles, ebikes, motorcycles, or 3-wheeled cars (for 2 people). 2 people renting 2 ebikes for 4 hours cost us 40,000 won. Need int l drivers license for the latter 2. I definitely recommend the ebike over the bicycle unless you really want to get strenuous exercise. Lots of hills and 11.4 km of trail to follow. Lots of little mini-towns where you can buy food, have coffee or peanut ice cream (recommend). Tons of photo opps so take your time. We finished in 3 hours, 40 mins (and my hubby wanted to stop A. LOT. Last ferry back to Jeju is at at 5 pm this time of year. Plan accordingly.

Very nice place for a day trip. Rented a quad bike for half a day at 30000 Won. Beautiful scenery and enjoyed the slow pace at the islands. Tasted their seafood ramyeon in one of the local restaurant. Would recommend to try if you happened to pass by.

After visiting the Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, we proceeded to head to the ferry terminal for Udo Island. We were surprised we couldn t get a cab during winter. Hence, we ended up walking to the ferry terminal instead.Note you need to show your passport and fill up a boarding form in order to take the ferry, at 30 mins interval. We took the 1400hr ferry. A 2-way ferry ticket costs 8,500 won. Upon arriving the island, one has the option of renting an electric scooter, manual bicycle or take the bus. For us, we took the round island bus. Bus fare is 5,00 won, which you can hop in and out at any attraction stops.  We headed to Udo-bond Peak stop and hiked up. Unfortunately, it was drizzling the whole day. We spent about an hour before returning to the ferry terminal.I suggest you allocate an entire day for Udo island. If the weather is fine, it is worthwhile to stop by all the attractions, enjoy the beach and food there.

Nice day trip to this island off an island. Nice food choices all round and you can take the hop on hop off bus if you aren t able to rent the electric vehicles or bicyclesThe island is not too big but there are lots of things to occupy you for a day. Beaches, food, trails, speedboats, horse riding, atvs  etc
We crossed this area on our walk through the Olle trail. Very scenic place for a walk and enjoy the afternoon.

I think the best way to enjoy the island is to rent the electric bike. We moved at our own pace and did many photo stops. There are many nice corners and colourful restaurants for photo taking. Great place!

Must visit place if u come to Jeju Island. I rent a bicycle, cycling & round the island. It will takes around 2-3 hours. It will getting easier to stop everywhere and snap the picture. I visited Udo Island end of March and it full with the Canola Flowers!!! Don't forget to try the nut ice cream too. There have a lots of stall and restaurant selling it!!

Had a great day out on Udo Island We got the bus from Jeju City bus terminal . It s about 1hr 20 mins on the bus but the journey is really scenic so we quite enjoyed it. The ferry was really easy and quick Once we got onto the island we hired electric bikes to get around . These were great . We had 3 hours on the island to cycle around and have lunch - we should ve hit there earlier in the day as would ve had more time to explore, but overall, a great day out

Here really is a nice and beautiful place. Rent a bicycle to walk around the island during autumn is soooo good. Worth to visit it. I ate a sashimi bibimbap there, is fresh and yummy. 3 hours is not enough seriously, if you wanna go through the whole island, unless you ride your bicycle without stop, haha.

A beautiful tiny island that is definitely worth a visit!Prepare a full day there. And get your International driving license ready to rent the mini scooters there which is a totally different experience!We ditch our rented car and never regretted. But do note that each scooter can probably take up to 2adults and a toddler max if u have kids. Bicycles are an alternative too.Start your morning early as it s probably some drive to the port.
Most of the top hill is closed off due to rain and slippery incline so we were only able to visit the lower parts. Should try the peanut ice cream!

Had a half day to roam around this small island and i had an amazing time. There's a bus the goes around all tourist site so better to go there early in the morning to visit all. Catch a ferry from the harbour and believe me that this is good to find peace of mind and goal setting.

we tried to take bus and ferry ourselves to visit Udo. The weather on that day was very good, there were a lot of geographical scenes in Udo, beaches were beautiful, besides taking bus for seeing the whole island, take a walk along the seaside was also very good.  eating seafood in a famous restaurant, also tried the famous peanut ice cream of this island.

This island is 15min away from seongsan ferry terminal. You just have to fill in the passenger particular and show yourpassport. The island is full of atv for rent, do look out for the bus as the road are quite tight.  I shipped my car over at the price of 21000wonDo try their seafood ramen and peanut ice cream!

From our recent experience and what our driver/guide told us:(1) rental cars: totally not allowed in busy summer. We visited in October so his car was allowed to take us onto the island, and still it was very crowded with the scooters and the bus, after a two day closure due to the wind(2) bring your passports (or other ID): although we had a rental car and were not going to rent any scooter, we were still asked for the passports before we boarded the ferry(3) when you plan your itinerary, if Udo is a must for your trip, be ready to make flexible rearrangements due to weather. We had to change our hiking in Hallashan due to a two day closure of the ferry service because of the wind. Check your weather forecasts as you get close to your Udo visit. If you plan to stay there overnight, also ask for cancellation or delay policy.(4) snacks not to be missed: peanut ice cream and peanut rice wine (although I should say it's a snack!) peanuts are local on Udo Island(5) reserve a whole day or most of the day if you want to fully enjoy Udo.  Even we had a car, we found it quite rush with some time wasted on the traffic (and it was only October, not the busy summer!)(6) romantic?? The reviews below were quite right about the beep,beep, beep.......of the scooters and the bus so I guess if you really want a Romantic Udo, it's better to stay overnight and after all the day visitors are gone, I think you should be able to enjoy a serene starry sky (but we didn't stay I could only imagine....)Enjoy Udo!

We thoroughly enjoyed our day on Udo. We hired manual bikes and stopped at the little beached and cafes along the way. It was cold and really windy so I think it was quite quiet in terms of people compared to a normal day which is why I think we enjoyed it so much. The bigger beaches (especially the black sand beach at the end) are a terrible example of sympathetic tourism and are blights against the beautiful natural landscape. Blaring music, ugly buildings and structures detract from the stunning island itself. We chose to eat at a cute little cafe which had character and that was away from the others.

I am a huge fan of Udo.  I have been numerous times and I never get tired of exploring a new road or a new cafe.At times it is soooo overrun by tourists that it can be a little overwhelming, but if you are smart and plan your trip during quiet times of the year, it is really rewarding.  The roads are quieter, the stores less busy.  There are numerous ways you can tour the island:I usually take my car.  I have heard that NO rental cars are allowed on Udo anymore.  so be aware of that.But once off the ferry there are so many scooter and electric bike shops* around.  *Foriegners be aware that you do need a license to rent these!ProTip:  I absolutely recommend you get off the beaten path and go explore the inner part of the island. So many cute cafes and splendid views!

Udo is like a big kids playground. You rent an electric scooter and scoot around this fun little island. We looped it in about an hour and a half, stopping for iced cream. The rental was 3 hours and so we explored the middle of the island off the beaten path. You cant really get lost and apple maps or navient works great (so does cell phone data). Some expert tips:Get the  Harley Davidson  2 man bike.Its rain covered, and you wont get too hot like the enclosed units. Adjust the seat forward (lever under your leg) to free up some space behind your seat for your bagOnce you get your scooter, scoot scoot! Everyone follows the same clockwise loop around the island. Open that throttle and pass those dottling tourists. Udo Awaits!Use your horn, and folks let you pass. Beep Beep!Skip the first two big pulloffs where everyone stops. Its way too crowded and you may have to pay to park! Watch for the big bus! It runs opposite motorcycle traffic and takes up most of the narrow roadway. So dont drive in the middle of the motorway. The bus driver is very safe and watches for confused motorcyclists. It was very safe.Otherwise, beep beep, scoot scoot, and enjoy the Electric Scooterland of Udo!
The view on Udo myeon is excellent where can take a look of half of the island. But you better rent a car and drive there.

Four of us rented an electric bicycle once arrived the island. It was a great way to tour UDO. The scenery was lovely and wished we could use our international driver license to rent the motor cycle bikes. The ferry ride across from the main island to UDO was pleasant. We only spent about 3 hours and do wish we have more time. We took lots of photos and surely we will come back next year when we return to South Korea.

Use the city bus to the port, took me around 1h30mins from Jeju City. Bought the return ticket at kw8500/person. Rent a scooter near the port for kw25,000/2 hours. Beautiful ride with ocean scenery, due to time constraints, didn't manage to hike to light house. 2 hours is just nice to see udo with lunch and stop along the attractions. After udo can trek to sunrise peak and catch the women diver performance at 3pm. Just follow the olleh trail and you will be find.

A workout by renting bikes at port to ride around the whole island.  You get to see very different types of sand and beaches, you ll better realize why they call it mini-jeju island.  The island s famous peanuts have thin skin and not bitter as your typical peanut skins.  If you have elderly with you, there are golf carts for rent too!

For most people, this place is kind of hard to reach because the public transportation in Jeju is not really comfortable. But if you rent a car, you really need to visit this place.You need to take ferry from the east part of Jeju Island. Inside of the island, you can borrow a bicycle to travel around the Udo Island. Don't miss the authentic ice cream of this island (see the pictures).
I love the weather there. it is so fresh with cool breeze and fantastic landscape. it is such a great place for taking photo or filming.
Have your passport  and money for the Udo Ship ticket and you will take your glorious  time  on the Beach, in the cafes, just walking or riding around

The most common way to get to Udo is by ferry. Just a reminder to bring your passport to get the ferry tickets. You may take your car on the ferry but I think it is unnecessary. There are a lot of tourists heading to Udo every day, you can rent a small car, electronic bikes or just bikes to get around the island. Our family went around, took some photos, ate peanut ice cream and ate more peanut ice cream. You can take really nice photos here but to be honest there is not really too much to do.

Korea can feel very touristy and materialistic. Udo is the antidote to this. A beautiful, small island... with stone fences and perfectly kept fields of rye. Cute cafes and stone beaches. You can walk all over or cycle or drive your own rickshaw. Picturesque and less changed by tourism. I wished I had spend 2-3 days here instead of Jeju.

Basicallu it's a small island, so we can walk / rent bicycle - motorcycle - small car / hop on bus to get around. Almost no activities. Just stop by here n there to take picture, buy ice cream, dine, etc. If you just want to relax and embrace the beautiful nature around, this is a good place. Our family rent bicycle 10.000 won per bicycle. It took us 4 hours to go around the island slowly.

We had high expectations of Udo, having read many great reviews. It turned out to be very touristy - lots of commercial establishments and activities (e.g. hipster cafes, rental bikes, women divers, boat/submarine rides). We enjoyed the quieter parts of Udo (e.g. Udobong Peak trail), away from the crowds. Please note that drivers of the mini-buses spoke only Korean which posed some challenge in communication. The traffic can also be quite chaotic at certain parts, with the mini-buses having to navigate through the many cyclists/bikers and tourists on the roads.

I had high hopes for this spot, but it is hard to recommend it.  What was once a pretty island is now circled by identical seafood restaurants, cafes, burger joints and other tourist shops.   Biking a loop around the island is nice enough, but the road is jammed with little electric "rickshaw" things and noisy scooters.  Honestly, this place would be a perfect case study of bad development for a tourism management class.

Been here with guided by local tour. Take ferry service about 15 minutes reach Udo. You may choose option for shuttle bus services getting around island. But local bus driver only can speak Korean during introduction of each drop point. Bike available for rent as another option to around this island.
a smmall island about 3.5 km off jeju. same as jeju, it's also a volcano lava island. can take hop-on-hop-off bus to go round the island with very reasonable price

We spent a nice & easy day on the island.  The island is small enough to complete within a day and yet big enough for you to do/see.  The ferry ride to the island was a short and easy one.  We didn't drive there which was good since we already pre-planned to ride around the island.  There were many rental shops to choose from.  There were many different types of vehicle you could choose from, e.g. manual bike, ebike, mini-car (not sure what you call them), etc. Do note that some will require international license.  We opted for the ebike which was in good use for the uphills. The route around the island was scenic and very instagrammable.  Many caf챕s to choose from. It is a good place to roam in your own pace and taking your own time to absorb the pretty views.Definitely a place worth going.
My friend told me to make sure I visit Udo island before leaving. We truly enjoyed the ferry ride and riding around the island on a bus.

Visited 4 times during my one year assignment in Jeju. Udo Island is very beautiful and peaceful. Rent a bike to tour around the island will definitely bring you fresh air and excitement. Stopped by at any cafe to try their peanut ice cream from udo! Really nice! I give average for their hallasan fried rice, it s good to try but the taste is just normal. Udo has a very nice beaches around and good for photo:) recommend to go when you visit jeju.
What a beauty! Cant stop taking pictures while doing Olle trail. Took about 6hrs. Please do not forget the sunblock if you come in the summer. Locals are friendly.

We visited Udo with my brother as part of our trip on Jeju. It is easily accessible via ferry (don't forget to bring your passport to buy a ticket!). We did the recommended tour (4h, with lunch time) and it was beautiful: campaign, port, cliffs, lighthouse... We definitely recommend it. We rate it 4 stars and not 5 because of the garbages on the island, it wastes the beautiful landscapes!

We caught the 7:30 am ferry from Seongshan Port to Udo.  The ferry left a bit early so we actually arrived at the island by 7:35.  The ferry ride should be about 15 minutes.  Cost was 17,000 kwr for 2 adults for round-trip tickets.  We struggled with whether we should have brought our car on board and immediately regretted not doing so once we landed.  Seems it is off season so not busy at all.  The first place we stopped at was the mango shop, where they also have a shop In the back for vehicle rentals.  Stopped there and tried to rent a mini-car/scooter but the staff said no rentals today because of the festival (seems it is the seashell festival).  Anyway, with no other option, we just took the hop-on and hop-off bus (5000 krw per person).  It s about 21,000 krw round trip for a small car.  First stop was the lighthouse, got there at 7:45 and went back down to catch the next bus at 8:30.  The next stop after was the black sand beach.  Then to the other lighthouse on the northern tip of the island.  We concluded our trip at the stop after that which is the other ferry port.  We caught the 10 am ferry.  We skipped the white sand beach which is probably the most popular site as a lot of Korean dramas were shot there.  Some tips:- bring your car if you have one so you can visit the island on your own schedule - try the peanut ice cream at Jimmy s Natural Ice Cream- most of the food places may be closed on a Sunday
Highly recommend when you plan a visit to Jeju. Udo is simply beautiful. Deep blue ocean, clean and clear sea with canola blooming in spring, there s nothing more you could ask for

Udo is a beautiful place that we have no regret to visit and spent 3 hours to round the island with rental electric car for KRW35000. Most shop offer KRW20000 for 2 hours and we find it will be a rush that you can t really enjoy the scenic view of the island. Returned ferry ticket cost KRW8500/person. Rental car is currently not allowed to enter the island as a one year control started Aug 2017 so we parked it at covered parking near the port before we depart to Udo.
i am lucky to visit udo on a sunny day. we are amazed by the unbeatable view and superb environment. spent a relaxing day in udo.if you go to jeju, you MUST go to udo!

We finally able to go Udo after few days of gloomy weather. Today just perfect as the sun is finally out. Do get into hop on/off bus with 5000won per person and you can get into the whole attraction places with some driver speak good english

The most memorable thing was rather on the ferry to Udo Island.The seagulls were hovering over those who had Calbee prawn crackers ready to feed them. They followed the ferry from Jeju all the way to Udo. That was a sight!Udo generally has good scenic views and interesting coral beach with clear blue waters.

We came here to the Seongsanhang Port Passenger Ferry Terminal to take the ferry to Udo island but the ticket counter was closed on 1st March 2018 which was a Thursday at 12pm , went and asked another ticket booth counter nearby and the lady told me in mandarin language that it's close due to bad weather as it was a windy day .
The landscape is a volcano, and the scene is very gorgeous, especially while the sunset or sunrise. The breeze from the sea makes you feel so good.

In short, a MUST GO when in Jeju-do. The beautiful breathtaking view of the ocean and on good days, clear view of Halasan mountain from the beach. We were there on 2nd Feb, and if it was not because of the freezing cold weather i would have jumped in the sea myself! Reaching U-do by ferry (15mins ride) and there are cute scooters for rent. We went with a travel agent, hence, we toured by bus. We went to two main places, one with a speedboat ride circling the island they claimed to look like a cow laying down and another by the beach of U-do. The water is of emerald in colour and dark blue  here is a picture for reference.

If you are looking for a remote island off the coast of Jeju then this might not be for you. However, if you are after an island that is a short ferry ride away and has many activities to offer then this is it! Udo is beautiful, and attracts many tourists especially in the summer time. You can rent a bicycle for the day at about 10,000-12,000W, or rent an electronic bike/scooter thing (with an international drivers license). Caves, mountains, as well as many beaches to explore. Stay the weekend on Udo or ride the ferry back to Seongsan, you'll have a great time :).

We didn't spent much time here as we are rushing. Overall is a nice place to visit. You can rent a bike or motor cars to go around the island or take the bus tour. At first we planned to drive car inside the island. However, due to many vehicles in the island and to avoid traffic jam, they have set the rules that only local island cars can drive into Udo island. I forgot the timeline but it took around one year period. For those who plan to drive car enter the island you may need to further check on it. When purchased the ferry ticket, you are required to fill in the two forms. Please bring along your passport as well. The counter personnel not many can speak English where we feel a bit challenge. Overall, is a nice place to visit. And if possible do spare around one day to enjoy the environment here.
Great place ever! Blue sky, white clouds, sand beach and mountain! You should go there to feel yourself!
Great island with awesome view and beaches. I like this island most in South Korea. I wanna go back again.
Our family day trip to Udo Island was a fun-filled day. We rented bikes and motor cars to get around the Island. It was a great day!

I went there in Nov. This is a small island but need to rent a mini car/motorcycle/cycle for travelling around the whole island.  We chose to take the tour minibus with total of 8 stops in different part of the Udo.  THe ticket can be bought near the pier. There are some beaches which all looks gorgerous! However its autumn time which we cant swim there.

I enjoyed the scenic beaches with aquamarine waters.. u can rent a escooter or take the shuttle bus (loop) to explore the island..there are many interesting cafes on the island..the specialty shld be their peanut ice cream..

We went to the island based on the reviews we read.Overall we were disappointed with the island,, it looks very nice but unfortunately the entire beach area around the island is strewn with garbage, and is very apparent against the black rocks. We hired bicycles and cycled around the island and could not find a spot not spoilt by the garbage sight.Also remember to bring your id along as is needed when you purchase your ferry ticket to the island.
It's very relaxing and convenient to take the shuttle bus to see various areas of the island. Tourists could hop on and hop off at each stops. Alternatively, there are bicycles available for renting.

We spent a day on Udo island and enjoyed the bicycle ride along the coastal road here. However, because we were based in Seogwipo city, the journey to the ferry itself was 1.5 hour per way - so I would suggest you visit Udo if you are based in Jeju city or somewhere around this port. Or else, you may not seize the best out of the trip.There were not many food options near the ferry port on Udo island, so you can have lunch on Jejudo first, or head to some gathering places near the White Sand beach or the Cliff area where there would be much more eateries.Pricing for bikes here was quite standard so you may not have to bargain - but make sure you pick ones that work :) Check their brakes and bells as you will need them for sure.

worth the trip there. if you are pressed for time, rent one of the electric operated tricycle and make a tour round the island in 3 hours. if you have more time you will be able to enjoy the sceneries and more tourist attraction sites better

This place is very good. If you leave to this place then have to prepare ride licence.because if you rent to scooter then you can travel comfortably. This place have beach. very good view of beach.And if you come here then you should eat  Jjajangnodle. this food is very very  delicious.

This is very beautiful place, I am very highly recommend the tourist to visit there. because it is the good experienced. Here is the island out of the city, more relax, comfortable and have more nice peoples in here.

It was a really wonderful experience to cycle around the island, although a little tiring. You can rent a motorcycle or trike as well. It is really busy and sometimes a little crowded on the roads. There are many restaurants and a few beaches. Excellent food to be had

Actually I really want to visit this place after watching korean tv show : 2 days 1 night because I see canola flowers field that really beautiful. Actually it s quite hard to communication here as a foreigner because not many people can speak english. But they are so kind and helpful even though we need some effort if want to say something by using some gestures. You must try peanut ice cream and Hallabong fresh Juice (tangerine) that really sweet and delicious! You also can find peanut soju here if you want to try.You can also buy a round trip ticket bus there to see this island around or rent a electric car for 2 people.

We reached the ferry terminal at 11am and waited for a short while for the ferry. The ferry depart quite frequently so there is no worry for that. As mentioned by other people, you will need to bring your passport to purchase a ticket. If you intend to rent a motorised vehicle in Udo, you will need to bring along your international driving permit. We rented a covered motorised scooter for 3h at KRW40,000. The scooter has doors and can seat 2 people. It took us less than 2.5h to cover the whole island, we even took 45min lunch break in between. The entire island is around 17km, so if you intend to make stopovers for photo taking, renting for 2h will be good enough. Just follow the coastline and you won't get lost. I highly recommend travellers to opt for the motorised scooter for a relaxing trip around Udo island. It will take you just half day. There are not many cars on the road but there are many scooters and bicycles which share the same path. There are many tourists and they might not observe the driving rules very well, so do be careful when driving on the roads. However, if you intend to see some of the other sights on Udo, they are not accessible for these transportation as you will need to take a separate ferry to go there. There seems to be many people taking the shuttle bus in Udo, so I don't really recommend people to do so if you have an international driving permit.

Before you want to take a ferry to Udo island, please take note that you need to bring along your passport to purchase a ticket. You will be given 2 tickets, 1 for departure & 1 for arrival (you have to keep this and pass to the boatman at Udo when you want to return to main island). A tip is to get the korean map together with your language s map because they have more details of the island as compared to other languages. The ferry comes every 15 minutes so you do not have to worry if you miss it. Inside the ferry, there are flooring with thermal and you have to take your shoes off before stepping into the resting platforms. Otherwise, you may choose to stand outside those rooms and there are some outdoor seats at the top of the ferry. Please also take note that there are 2 ports at Udo, so your ferry might stop at either one.Once you reach the island, you will be greeted by tons of shop assistants trying to get you to rent bikes to you. You will need an international driver license to be able to drive any motorise vehicles. Upon confirmation which is the vehicle you want, you have to leave your passport with the register counter. They will provide you with a map to go around the island. We were informed that the whole cycling trip takes an hour. However, here comes the challenging part. There were no proper division of the road for those driving trucks, buses, cars, motorcycles & bicycles. You can be riding your bicycle and have a full speed bus chasing behind you and pressing the horn at you. Cars and trucks from the opposite direction also travel at fast speed towards you, which we had to stop many times to give way to these fast moving vehicles. After getting to the first beach, which was really beautiful, the rest of the trip towards the next beach was tough as there were many upward slopes and split roads which have no proper signages to tell you which way to go. We had to go in to random houses and ask in broken korean for which way to go. However, when we reach the lighthouse area, we managed to locate Jimmy s icecream shop as suggested by our Jeju driver. I tried the mandarin orange ice cream while my friend tried the apple mango ice cream. Everything tasted natural and yummy so I would recommend it to tourist who visit the place. However, from the road before this ice cream place onwards to the last 5 mins of the ride, it was all upwards riding.We took almost 3 hours to finish cycling around the whole island (We have done quite a few rides in Singapore so I don t think we were slow in cycling around the island). So for those who have no license or feel that you re not up to 2-3 hours of cycling, I would advise you to take the tour bus to get from places to places on the island.

i'm really disappointed with all the bloggers i watched on youtube that spoke about going to udo. this is why. where they all mentioned and spoke about if you need to hire bikes or an electronic scooter you will need to bring a passport (which you must do if you want to do the island in relaxing fashion) none of them mentioned that you need a passport to get to the island. so my partner and i turned up with 1 passport as he would be driving over there not me. but when buying the ticket st the ferry terminal, they demanded passports and got in a huff when we explained we only had 1. so be aware. once there it's a fun day out. you don't need to know much. you get there and you get off the ferry you hire transport. we went for the electronic bikes and they were perfect. make sure you take sun screen for your face

This is a perfect one-day trip from Jeju, I can imagine it gets packed in season, but on this midweek October day we were pretty much the only people on the Olle trail around the island. It's mostly really easy to follow, with a mixture of red and blue ribbons tied to trees and fences, plus distinctive arrows at junctions. The trail is about 11.5km but we also climbed to the highest point and took a detour to another beach, dawdled, stopped for photos and snacks and still got round in less than 5 hours. Just time for a peanut ice-cream and a snooze on the beach before taking the ferry back. A really relaxing, varied day, like a step back in time to a simpler way of life. Highly recommended/

You should go there. Lovely view. Great for riding a bike around the island. It takes only 1-2h only but the view is so stunning. You should not eat at restaurants at the dock. There is a lot of places to eat along the way. Food is a bit more expensive but acceptable.

The highlight of my trip to Jeju was visiting Udo, which is small enough to be traversed by bike in a matter of hours. My girlfriend and I were glad to chose the pedal-bikes over the motorbikes and car tours because, with all the different little coffee shops and sites to explore, you'll want to take your time. While you may not find much in the way of "impressive historical sites" compared to other places in Korea or the rest of Asia, this is a beautiful place if you're just looking to relax, meandering the coast with friends or a loved one, and enjoying some local treats. It's also very scenic, so super easy to capture scenic photos. The people were also super-friendly in helping you get around, even despite the language barrier. I'd love to return again.
Brilliant place to visit stunning views from the top. Quite a treck to the top up lots of steps but well worth it.

This Hallasan Fried Rice is a must have, must Go, must try, if you are in Udo Island. It is available at the 'Pungwon' restaurant. It is about 20mins walking from the harbour. If you are driving, key in the Tel no. 7841894 in your GPS device.First you will have to order either Black pork or cuttlefish according to your preference. There is a minimum number of portions to order based on the number of pax. There were 4 of us and we order 2 Pork and 1 Cuttlefish. We will begin by BBQ the meat. Until we are about halfway through, you can order the rice from the staff. The staff will put aside some meat and start by cooking the rice. The whole idea of Hallasan Fried Rice is that the staff will tell you the story about Mount Hallasan and the islands nearby; all these while making the rice into the shape of a mountain. He will then pour in the egg mixture and meat and cheese... and after numerous of flipping the rice, it's done. Fret not if you don't understand Korean, they have Chinese staff who can do the story telling in Mandarin. The process of hearing about the story is very interesting coupled with the visual of the staff cooking the rice. Not to mention, it tastes damn good too!

Very cute little island, great for 1 day trip.  It's too big to do it by walking, but you can rent scooter (only with international driving license), bicycle or to take hop in hop out bus. There are 2 kinds of busses: one that makes only 4 stops (3000 KRW) and another that goes all around the island (5000 KRW). I think the one that makes only 4stops is good enough, as the rest you can do by walking. We took the hop in hop off bus for 5000 KRW, but we used it only 3 times, the rest we walked around. Enjoy your time there!

This island took us almost 2.5 hrs to reach. We used public transport from our hotel to reach the intercity bus terminal and changed busses to the harbor. The bus ride took almost 1.5hrs but was very scenic. At the harbor, we filled out the boarding form and stood in queue for the ferry ticket. The ferry ride was 20min to the island and the ride was interesting with the sea gulls catching food thrown by other passengers. On reaching the Island, we took the hop on hop off bus .... red and got off on the 1st stop - for the light house. There we took the motor boat ride around the cliff edge. The guide was speaking in Korean so we couldn't understand much but enjoyed the view. We have a nice lunch of buttered spicy shrimps there and peanut ice cream. Then took the bus to stop 2 where we walked around the rocks and the smaller light house.  We saw both the white and red sand beaches. All in all a good day spend.
Remember to try their peanut ice cream (Udo peanut). With beautiful beaches, scenic peaks, and flowery fields,Udo Islandis perfect for a laid back. You may take bus to place if interest in Udo.

I can imagin Udo is a quiet and beautiful island to stroll or bike sometime, but the day we visited was full of people.  We arrived there already at noon and rented electric bicycles to start rounding the small island.  The road was full of small vehicles and bikes moving or stopping by the road, I did not feel I was in the nature but a hustle corner.  There were quite some restaurants and cafes along the route, the one we went was full of people, price of food/drink is in high end.  It took us 3-4 hours to round the island due to time for camera and lunch.  Back to the electrical bike, which could power to assist you, but battery did not last long, it usually fails in the last up slope (the last check point with a cave and cliff) - and it is tough for rider to move uphill without gear.  So I suggest you rent a normal bike, it is cheaper, more reliable, and rider can wear hat but not the heavy helmet.  I will say if you want to visit Udo, visit in low season, not summer, which is really crowded and extremely hot - no tree, no shelter along the road.

Udo a.k.a cow island is a nice little Island in Jeju. We took a local public bus to the pier and took a short ferry ride to the island. This island island is shaped like a cow, hence its name. It was very popular among tourist and you should schedule a day trip here. The ferry ride was breezy and enjoyable. On reaching Udo island, we were greeted by the statue of a cow. You can walk (I don't recommend it as the island is quite big), rent a bicycle or take the hop-on-hop off bus for KRW 5,000.  We took the bus and visited the various tourist attractions. Along the way, we stopped and visited the lighthouse park among other places. Before reaching back to the harbour to board the return ferry, they collected back your tickets. That means you can only board the bus for one round trip on the island. Udo island is a nice place to visit in spite of the many tourists here.  Wear good walking/hiking shoes, have plenty of drinking water and wear a hat and sunscreen for protection against the sun as there is very little shade.  Be prepared for lots of walking and climbing to the lighthouse.

I went to Udo with the ferry, the queues were super long to buy the tickets but it was quite fast. The island was very crowded. I got a normal bike for 10000 won. Go to the shop on your far right. the shop straight ahead when you inboard the ferry is super crowded with Korean tourists who look for a 3 wheel scooter. These scooters are everywhere. You need to be super careful as no-one really knows how to drive them. The island is super popular among locals. Thousands of scooters and selfie-hungry teenagers looking for the best pose next to the lighthouses. Moreover prices are high and the island is full of plastic rubbish (bottles, cups, bags). I would only recommend to go during low season. But most probably the rubbish will still be there as some piles looked already quite old. The peanut ice cream is nice but not worth the money.

We spent a day there and we thought it was a nice little town with some beautiful natural sites like the falls but it's awful that people litter all over the place. We had the peanut ice cream which is was delicious. The island bus tour was easy and cheap and one of the drivers spoke perfect English.

What a quirky little place to visit! Just wish I had got my international drivers license before we left Australia though because then I would have been able to drive one of the fun little 3-wheel vehicles to get around the island. A short ferry trip from Jeju Island and then a bus trip around showed us the sights. A must-do is to get off the bus at the first stop and explore the 2 caves down on the beach - stunning and quite a spiritual experience. Absolutely loved our visit to this little island!

udo was one of beautiful & must visit place in jeju. we spent 1day for it for visit such  pretty landscape. we took shuttle bus for tour around the island. diff view & diff landscape. i love light house hill & whale cave. better reserve enough time for visit & enjoy the scenery

Really beautiful little island off another beautiful island.Great for a an afternoon or day visit and easy to travel. We went by ferry and got ourselves a scooter to travel around the island as we were short on time. Was really fun to use the scooter, probably the highlight of the island.But made us see the place quickly and so many places to eat! The people were really nice too and would visit again.

This small island is good for half or full day depends on what you going to do. The island provide with free shuttle bus but not sure it is summer period. Got two routes east and west. Check with driver before get into the bus. Light house stop and black sand see is a must.

It is a very pleasant place to visit in jeju. Passports are needed to buy ship tickets. A 15 mins ride to udo certainly worths. The scenery are breathtaking and the whole atmosphere of the place is comfortable and relaxing. A good place for temporary escape from the busy city life!

Visit to Udo has to be the best bet on my trip to Jeju! It was not on my itinerary until I reached Jeju - initially put off by a journey over because I don't drive and I was afraid I will lose my way, miss ferries etc. Glad I went Udo!It wasn't difficult to reach the port to catch my ferry as I got guidance from the staff where I was staying (December Hotel Jeju). I took bus and watched the scenery along the way till I reached the terminal stop. Bought my ferry tickets and was quickly onboard (there seems to be more ferries than I thought and read). Watched others feed the seagulls food on the ferry ride and in a short while, I arrived at the island! There were many options on how you want to travel around the island and so I took the most rustic and simple way --- bicycle! It was not difficult and I got to choose a cute pink bicycle as my companion for the day. I took the clockwise path and followed the many other visitors on the road.Udo brought me many surprises - many people but not rowdy, beautiful beautiful waters and beaches (see my photos), cool yet warm, quiet along some paths but not totally deserted. I liked the fact there are many photo stops, and the food I tried there were delicious! I love the Hallasan Fried Rice at the shop I chanced upon randomly - stopped cos I felt hungry. And it was one of the greatest food deal I had!I would choose to come here, earlier, again next time. There were some other areas I didn't manage to explore as I wanted to catch the ferry back. I could have also spend some time chilling at the cafe for a snack or drink. I find this the best way to enjoy Udo, away from all the hype of Jeju itself. Love it.
Udo island is located near Seongsan port. Half day will be enough to visit this island. I tried the peanut ice cream from U-do Prince, taste good.

Udo or  Cow Island  lies off the UNESCO World Heritage island of Jeju and is so named because its profile resembles a sleeping or resting ox. The fun begins with a 15 minute ferry ride from Seongsan Harbour, costing –5,500 return trip. As the boat glides over the choppy waters, you can watch on deck the antics of Korean school students on excursion feeding the seagulls in mid-flight, with lots of shrieks and screams. Upon arrival at Cheonjin Port, shuttle buses will be waiting to take you around the island for a round (hop-on hop-off) trip ticket which you pay after the first stop. It s a pity we could not understand the Korean commentary provided by the bus driver, as he had his captive audience in stitches along the journey. We enjoyed the rustic scenes of thatched farm houses and fields, surrounded by the azure blue seas. We made stops at Geommeolle Beach (black sands and cliff backdrop) and Seobin Baeksa Beach (white grains of rhodolith). The half day excursion to Udo was a joyful and unruffled experience!

Udo- we went early, were there before 9am. Spent roughly 3 hours on the key spots.1. Ferry to Udo- Our jumbo taxi driver drove us over. Needed to fill out all personal details plus showing our passports when purchasing tickets. Return trip for 5 of us plus driver plus jumbo taxi return was KRW70,000. No queues, not crowded. We went there on 2 Jun 2017 Friday. Just a 15-min ride, need to leave the car diring the trip. Have a good view of Sunrise Peak from the ferry.2. Peak- For a good view of Jeju and Udo, walk up to the peak. Be alert that the track along the coastline uphill is not an easy one for people who don't exercise a lot.  Useful to have hiking stick with you for this short track.3. Geommeollae Beach- Absolutely gorgeous scenery.  A must go place. That's where the famous peanut icecream shops are. There are two.  We tried one and it tasted well.4. Beaches- We went to two. Unforgettable colour and tranquility.  Must go as well.

The island is beautiful but difficult to get around with out renting a motorbike. However, motorbike only fits two people and you need an international driver's permit. The wind was too strong to walk around or bike in. There were a total of 3 of us that went and it would have been worth it to drive the car over from Jeju island because it cost the same as a tourist bus for all three of us.Other than figuring out transportation, it's a beautiful island to chill at and enjoy nature.

It is a short ferry ride from Jeju and an island worth visiting. It is a very small island so even just a few hours in Udo is enough to see all of its beauty. We rented a motorbike to get around the island. Make sure to remember to bring your camera~

Among all the interesting place in Jeju island, i personally love Udo the most. The sky really blue, sea really blue, sand really white, stone really unique, food taste nice...you have it all. I rent a car for the trip in Jeju, therefore i bring the car to Udo by ferry. There were three of us in the car, i feel it worth the ferry ticket. As in Udo, most of the "mini car" or special bike we saw are mostly two person, so unless you rent two, you cant fit in 3 persons. So if you are driving, you have more than 2, bring your car with you. Parking is very easy to find. But please go to the port earlier as buying ticket and finding entrance to board the ferry can be very confusing..so you will need more time.

It takes almost one and a half hour to arrive the Island from Jeju-si. But the view was stunning on the Island. There is a shuttle bus service which has 4 stops across the Island and 5000 won for each passager to have an unlimited ride. There is a famous icecream store at the first stop which sell peanut icecream which is very delicious. The beach at the third stop is so stunning with a beautiful ocean. However, the restaurant on the island are quite expensive, so better prepare your own food if you have a tight budget.

So according to our tour guide since we've spent few days at Jeju Island, Udo Island which is to the east of Jeju with a short ferry ride is not to be missed.So we went, and he was right.Beautiful day, sunny blue sky, clouds, nice breeze, beaches, scenic sights everywhere.  We even hiked up to the lighthouse.Came back down and tried the "famous" Udo Island ice cream.  Meh, not a big deal in my book, though it quenched the thirst a little.

Spent half day on Udo Island walking around different spot by tourist bus! The bus tour is highly recommended to visitors without driving liscence since you can get on any bus of the same company with the ticket. Each stop has its uniqueness but still highly recommend the first stop! Simply stopby and enjoy Jimmy's Icecream along the seaside... guarentee this to be the most memorable part of the trip! The beach is also highly recommended since you feel like visiting Maldive with the clear water and blue sky. Try to arrive the ferry terminal to avoid overcrowding!

Lovely island with walking trail along the island.  Having to take bus from Jeju city for about 45 minutes and then ferry ride to the island.  It was of about an hour from the city at least.  A lot to see in the island and the flowers are lovely.  You could choose to take bicycle or motor bikes or driving around.

I read reviews/blogs about what & where and the most economical way to explore east of Jeju in a day. One of the blogs I read mentioned about Udo on her trip (you may look for theLostWanderer's blog-Jeju in 3 days for more detailed trip in Jeju). I just love this islet. I rented a manual bicycle to get around for KW 5000 for 2hrs, yet you can rent at KW 10000 for 3hrs to the entire day. Well for my time is constrain, & travelling on a budget & also wanted to keep myself fit as a preparation for Mt Hallasan hike, gladly I did. Other than bicycle, you can rent an e-bike, ATV, and a scooter. The tranquility & scenery that the place could offer is magnificent. Shouldn't let this islet slip from your list once in Jeju.I took bus #701 after I visited Manjanggul Cave & Gimnyeong maze park (same bus stop where I alighted for the cave) & alight at Seongsan Habour. At the port, I paid KW 5500 (to & fro) for I'm going back the same day to the main Island of Jeju.

We were lucky: at the moment of our visit there was this Seashell Festival: a lot of seafood and music close to the ferry terminal. It takes only 15m to get there by boat and to walk up the hill is +/- 40min walk. you got a wonderful view over both sides of the island. There's even a little outdoor museum about lighthouses :-). Besides this festival, I think it's worth a visit and you can do a tour around Udo (or U-do) on a bike: rental service is at 50meters of the ferry terminal.

I was quite disapoonted when we visited the island. It's pretty and the beaches are nice. But if you've been around Jeju island for some time, there's not much here that you can't find in the main island. You can skip this if you need to cut your itinerary.

We took their local tour bus to go around, where it will go around the island for sightseeing. The first stop was near the udobong peak and great view of the sea. We had lunch and ice cream there (niceeeeee). We have spent too much time here and we decided to go back after 2-3 hours, and technically you will have to board the same number of bus to go back to the port. We met a kind bus driver that took us directly to the port.

We caught the ferry over to the island (remember your passport or other form of photo ID) and hired a two person battery operated bike which was great fun.   Hired for 2 hours which was ok but if you want to spend longer at each stop then I would recommend at least 3 hours.   We went all around the island.  We stopped the longest at a small village where you can go down some steps to the beach and go and investigate a large cave.   There was an outdoor cafe on the beach serving fish -  very busy.  Can't remember the name of the village but it was towards the end of our circuit.  Definately a good weather day activity.

You definitely need more than 5-6hrs to explore this beautiful island. Last ferry which leaves back from Udo is 6pm so kindly plan your day accordingly. We were there only for 2 hrs so took a bicycle to explore this little paradise.  Views and trails on this island are amazing with a lot of food options available. My recommendation is to rent the little car to drive around if you are short on time and its easier to go up the slopes in the car . The ferry ride is also not very expensive up and down from Udo.

It is difficult to take the local bus to go to the Ferry station so we took a taxi from our hotel near the city centre. The ferry ride is short but the sea air is refreshing and it is kind of fun seeing excited kids feeding the seagulls. The scenery is beautiful on the island but the hop on and hop off bus service is pretty rough.I think they are overbooked and big groups also have special buses nobody else are allowed on. End up waiting a lot to get to the next site. Annoying..!

the best thing to do in jeju, it wasnt that attractive for me while i search udo online, my friend made me go with her, when i got there, im so glad i did it, it was so laid back, so nice, the circle island bike was awesome, the sunset, nice people. we enjoyed it a lot and forgot the boat time. we were late for the boat back to jeju, so we have to paid for personal boat, was way so expensive.

I specifically spend half a day here during my trip at Jeju and has no regret. We rented a electric scooter with KRW30k for 2 hrs, do note that you need International Driving License to rent it. We had burger at HahaHoho cafe and the Pork burger is delicious. The landscape and view is so pretty. The road is narrow so I don't recommend you to drive rented car there. Udo island trip is definitely one of the highlight of our trip to Jeju!

We were fortunate to catch a not-as-crowded ferry at around 2plus and stayed till 530pm and got back around 6pm. Ferry ride takes around 15mins but get up early and start walking towards the exit if u don't want to be Squashed w the main crowd! Upon arrival on the island, we decided to take the bus tour (costs 5000KRW/pax) which stops at 2 locations- the lighthouse peak as well as the beach.I must say Udo is very very windy so make sure u gear up and tie your hair if necessary!Hiking up to the lighthouse took us around 15mins up(lots of stairs, but after that it's v scenic). We had a good view of the whole island, despite being drizzly throughout the day. Dennis Cafe is really nice, cozy and affordable peanut ice cream as compared to the crowded 'Running man' ice cream shop which wasn't actually good. If I could go back, I would definitely bring my international driving license and rent an E bike!
Leave in the early morning from Jeju and spend the whole day on Udo, you will not regret, it extremely enjoyable.

Udo was beautiful but our Korean two (2) hour tour wasn't sufficient. Apparently taxi's are hard to come by on this SMALL island. We would have liked to eaten elsewhere besides the port but our Volcano Rice & Pork resto was equally fun & good, near the bus drop off & Keith Harding mural. Hard to miss... enjoy

It is a definite must-see on Jeju Island. Although there is not much else to do beside sightseeing. That said the bridge excels at what it offers, which is the breathtaking scenery and beauty. Thumbs up from Vietnam !!!

Travelled by ferry from Seongsan habour (price 5500W two way). Upon reaching the island turn right to the carpark to purchase bus tickets (price 5000W). Bought the red tickets (you can only board the red buses with the red tickets and blue bus for the blue tickets). The bus is a hop on hop off bus (can only go forward not backward); you'll have to hold on to your ticket to board the bus for the next stop. Buses come every 20-30 mins. First stop was udobong peak - we had peanut ice cream (must try!!! Albeit a little sweet. Udo is known for the peanuts). The climb up is a little slippery so I won't recommend it on a rainy day. Requires some fitness to make it to the top but it is not too difficult. Otherwise a very relaxing climb that my family and I enjoyed very much! Stopped also at the Beacon mound (second stop on red bus) which was a nice selfie spot and then headed to the beaches before catching the ferry back to the mainland (last ferry back to jeju 5.30pm). The island is quite touristy though; expect things to be a bit more expensive.

We took the ferry to Udo island, the ferry trip was fun with many seagulls flying around us. We booked 5 electric bicycles for 2 hours (need to bargain with the price). Electric bicycle no need international driving license. Think 2 hours is very rush as we don't have enough time to slowly explore the beautiful island. Halfway we go lost and need to rush back to return the bicycles to avoid the penalty. Need to exercise caution while cycling as the roads are shared with cars, buses, other mobile vehicles. No separate road for bicycles. It's a nice island to explore
You absolutely have to visit the island. The beaches was so blue and clean. The wind is good. Too bad we didn't stay over and enjoy the beach more

If your time in Jeju is limited, skip all those man made museums and put visiting Udo island as one of your priorities. If you have an international driving license, highly recommend to rent a scooter to tour the island, and don't forget to try the Hallasan Fried Rice.

Accessible by ferry. Udo is a tiny island so you wont get lost while wandering around this island. Filled with canola fields during spring, fresh breeze, peaceful atmosphere, sights of female divers, it is perfect for a daytrip. However if you plan to drive, just be extra careful as the roads are narrow.

It's a tiny island which will only take about 1 and a half hour to explore around with an auto-bike (renting required) or spend about 2-3 hours cycling around the island. This place is surrounded with mountains, sea, greens, flowers and lovely people. Lots of tiny restaurants and decent cafes can be found in the island. Would recommend everyone to try their peanut/hallabong ice-cream! It's something very different and worth to try.
Came here on two different trips, both memorable. Ate the black beans noodles, the ice cream and tried the local seafood.

this is a very good island in jeju, just about 10min from the pier to there and meanwhile you can see many seagulls follow the boat, just for asking the snack in your hand~the island is a good place for a walk, or you can rent a bike, motorbike or electric car(these 2 types needa an international car license) just nearby the pier.and please remember to bring your passport to there cos you needa show your passport when you buy the boat ticket.

U-do is more of a small village, the citizens are so down to earth and friendly! Lots of fresh seafood be sure to try them out! Hop on a tour bus, driver will intro the island to you!Great for family vacations or exploring the island with friends and taking lots of amazing photos

If you are driving, I recommend you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak first at around 7am to catch the sunrise at around 8:00am something.For me it's better seeing the Seongsan Ilchulbong in a far away place rather than hiking it for 30mins. So before reaching the gps route you would notice a lot of cars parked at the road side. Stop for a while and from there you would see a crowd of people waiting for the sunrise at the seashore and infront is the mountain touching the sun.If you like, you can still proceed with the peak 1km away from the stopover and hike a bit at the stairs to see the peak.After that a few kms away is the Seongsan Port going to Udo Island.Gps to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak 710-7923Gps to Seongsan Port 7825671Upon reaching Udo island in a 15min ferry ride for 5500won, you can either walk, cycle or rent a scooter. You need an international drivers license to rent a scooter for 25000won for 2 hours, which i think is really short. Circling the whole island with a bit of stop over would already take you 2 hours. Not much to see in the island, a bit of flowery patches, mermaid statues and lighthouse and that's it.
You can access it by ferry. Rent a scooter at the Island. With little kids I would recommend to take the car with on the ferry. Nice sights and views!

The moment I set my eyes on this island, I knew I was in heaven. The water looked extraordinary blue and the view was nothing short of a perfect dreamy scenery. We took a day trip on the ferry from jeju. On the island, we took the hop on hop off bus. Take any bus, doesn't really matter.. They will then tell you which color buses u can hop onto at the next destination along with a list of places they will stop at. I think it costs around 2200 won. The island was crowded specially with all the bikes but still it is not to be missed. The first stop was the udo peak. A hike of around 30 mins to a lighthouse from where you can see the entire islans. The view of the sunrise peak on jeju all along the hike was incredible! Then the bus took us to 2 beaches..one was a black sand beach which had a little cave but tides were high that day. We missed the 2nd beach and went to the last one with white sand. This beach was quite close to the port and we walked to the port from here along the coast. It was a beautiful walk and less crowded.There are lot of shops and cafes in front of the last beach.

If you plan to go to Udo, spend at least a day here. Enjoy every part of Udo : Udo Olle Trail, Udo lighthouse, Beach. Trying the popular Halasan Fried Rice and peanut ice cream, so yummy. Really enjoy my time in Udo, fresh air, clear blue water, white sand, warm local people, beautiful scenery. This is what I picture Jeju in my mind. Everything in Udo are beautiful for me. I will regret if I didn't come here, this is my favourite part in Jeju.

Udo island offers push bike and motorised bike hire for a small fee at both of the docking locations. You can also drive your car onto the ferry and just drive. I used the push bike so I could enjoy the feel of the coast roads without rushing past but you'll still see everything (without the muscle pain) with the other options. There are several little eatery places scattered along the road that offer very fresh and yummy food. I spent about 3-4 hours riding around the coastal road stopping for freshly squeezed juice, lunch, the local peanut ice cream and peanut rice wine. If your looking for adventure this isn't for you but if a quiet relaxing back to nature is what your looking for be sure to stop by.

Great day out doors. Many options of travel within the island (drive from mainland, rent bicycles, various motorized vehicles) making it really easy.Roads are narrow so personally would avoid driving. Further the ferries can only hold that many cars which means expect long wait times during peak periods.Many nice small eateries for coffee or ice cream along the way. Beaches are really pretty too and water clear though I didn't see anyone swimming in dec (winter).Only thing that I didn't quite like was the rentals were pricey at 70000 won for 3 hrs (two motorized bicycles and one two seater). And that was after some bargaining . The guy mentioned that it takes 45 min to go around the island without stops

Udo Island is what I imagined Jeju to be..beautiful coast line beside grassy fields. A relaxing day trip soaking up the amazing scenery. Well worth the (little) effort if you are in the area, and consider a day trip if you aren't!The port is about a 15 minute walk from Sunrise Peak. You buy ferry tickets in a white dome building; start by going to one of the desks with pens and boarding cards. Fill out 2 boarding slips EXACTLY the same (one collected on your trip to Udo and the other collected on your way back). For example, we were a party of two, and on BOTH slips we wrote BOTH our names and details. When you have completed the slips, go to one of the ticket windows and present the slips with your PASSPORT (for international travellers), and if like me, you don't know any Korean at all, just smile and say "Udo". The lady will ask you if you are returning the same day and issue you return tickets costing 5500 won each. She will also tell you the last ferry time coming back from the island, in our case (November) it was 5pm.Off we went! The ride is about 15 minutes and you get lovely views of Sunrise Peak on the way. When we disembarked, we were immediately greeted (sold to) by various venders renting out pedal bikes or motorised vehicles. We chose the "old fashioned" bikes and had a wonderful time. It costs 10000 each bike, for the whole day. We took 2-3 hours biking around the coast (map provided) taking breaks to admire the scenery and have lunch. If you didn't make any breaks, our vendor thought it would take 1-1.5 hours around. My partner and I are healthy late-20-somethings that don't bike often, but we felt the trip was pretty easy and relaxing as its mostly flat. There are not many cars either, and other motorised rental vehicles zipping by, are small scooters/2-3 seaters, so biking around feels very safe. There are numerous eateries and toilet facilities all around the island. We stumbled upon a cart selling home made pies (Bulgogi, Spicy Chicken, Red Bean and Apple) and they were delicious! I wish I knew the name of it, but if you happen to see it and feel like pies..these are yum!Fit in a trip to Udo if you can..Its a beautiful place to spend some time..

Udo is a small island just off Jeju island and is a 15min ferry ride. Once you are there you can hike, hire a bike or get on a round island hop-on hop-off bus which are quite frequent.The island is a lava plateu but some beaches have golden sand or white coral sand.The island is lush and green and is apparently very fertile.As it is touristy, prices can be high but it is definitely worth a visit if it is a good day.Give yourself plenty of time.
