Wonderful places with amazing scenery. We joined the round island shuttle trip for just 2000 won and you can go around the islands. If you are lucky enough, you can get English speaking bus driver to explain more details on Udo Island. Wonderful!!

A wonderful way to enjoy beautiful Udo is actually by walking the Olle Trail 1-1. There's a total of 26 trails totaling 425kms round Jeju. Website jejuolle.org. Distance is 11.2km which covers the major places on the island. Trail starts & finishes at Cheonjin-hang(port) where you arrive by ferry from Seongsan Harbour. Its a relatively easy & flat trail taking 3-4hrs. Only slight challenge is Udo Peak. There is a century old lighthouse at the peak with a Lighthouse Park with miniature lighthouses in Korea & around the world as you make you descent. Need to watch out for scooters & buses while walking.
I rented a motobike and rode all around the island in 2 hours. This Island is a gem. Don't miss it. The ferry price was very cheap and you can have good korean foods on the Island.

My friend and I loved this place. We drove in to Udo, boarding the ferry in our car (quite an experience in itself!), and only had 4 hours to explore. Jump shots at the various beaches, hiking up to the tallest part of Udo, trying Hallasan fried rice at the Pungwon restaurant, and having peanut and tangerine ice-cream at Jimmy's ice-cream were all memorable experiences. Driving around, and many a times through one-way lanes between low stone-walls that Udo is known for, was exciting as well. Udo is a must-go!

Upon my arrival on the island, I bumped into Taiwanese travelers who recommended the Hallasan fried rice. The restaurant is within 15-20 walking distance to the port (where you got off the ferry).The fried rice was covered with vegetables and squid. The owner would go to each table to pour egg yolk and cheese and make the dish look like a volcano. While frying the rice, the owner would tell stories of the Jeju island and Udo island in fluent English. The fried rice then was turned into a heart shape. My family and I videotaped the process and had fun. Oh, the friend rice did taste yummy!

Try to give yourself a little extra time to buy tickets as they day we travelled it was packed with tourists.The short ferry trip was wonderful, and offered great views of Udo as we approached. On reaching the island the first thing we observed were the amount of rental companies offering bikes, electric 2/3 seater buggies, scooters and tandem. In fact anything you can think of to explore the island. Ido is famous for peanuts and you will find many of these on sale in the quaint little cafes and shops dotted around main road. If you get the chance you should try the local " Udo peanut Makgeolli" The island is truly beautiful and if you do decide to join the hoards on electric vehicles shop around a bit as there are lots of rental companies eager to offer their wares. It is also important to ensure that you have an "international drivers licence",, as they appear to have tightened up since a number of accidents lately and wouldn't accept our UK credentials.All in all great trip with lots of ferries running bak and forward throughout the day.

The ferry to Udo island is fairly close to the Seongsan Ilchulbong peak, close to a 15 mins walk. The ferry ride is 15 mins only, and you get to see some amazing views all through. In the island, there are many beautiful beaches and cafes. We rented bikes (do remember to ask them for a map if you do!), and rode all around the island. A complete round on the ocean road took like 3+ hours, but was loads of fun. Cos we could stop by at beaches to relax, or cafes for a quick bite or drink. We took lots of incredible pictures. A perfect day spent in gorgeous weather!

Udo is a very windy and beautiful island. The views from udo peak is breathtaking. There is a round trip udo tour bus for 5000won per pax which shuttle you to 5 attraction stops of the island. First stop is to the black sand beach where you can see the black sand beach and a cave (during low tide). If you want to go to the udo peak, you will need to walk a distance, climb up a hill to reach the udo peak. My first trip to udo was with my Jeju taxi guide and he drove us to udo and brought us up. My second time here was kinda cocked up because the udo tour bus driver only conveys in korean and our taxi guide this time did not accompany us to udo. Hence we did not made it to the peak. Nonetheless, we explored other stops (beaches and beaches). The sea and beaches are very beautiful. Udo is famous for their peanut and orange ice creams which I felt is a waste of money. Per cup of ice cream topped with some peanut or orange juice cost 5000won. Mcd ice cream taste nicer and bigger quantity. Oh yes, if you are willing to spend more you can rent bicycle and cycle around the island. And if you have international driving licence you can rent motorized vehicle to travel around. The roads are small and there's many tour buses shuttling people hence certain areas are abit congested.

I would die to visit Udo again, it's a tiny island and can be covered in one day with a scooter which can be rented once you're off the ferry but I'd love to stay a few day next time so I can really enjoy the island.  Everything here is like straight out of a book, the beaches, the hiking trails, the lighthouses, the food, OMG the food.  Anyone visiting this island, I recommend starting early morning and renting a bicycle, a scooter if you're good with directions or pay for a bus ticket that with have drop off locations as well as pick up so you can explore at leisure and when you're ready to go to your next location, just stop by one of their pick up locations and you're ready to go.
Udo is a must visit place in Jeju island! go there as early as you can, so that you can spend a day trip there! Half day trip not enough time to look around.

This was the last stop on our vacation. Unfortunately it was also the only grey/cloudy/cold day. The island was still a must see for us. The ferry ticketing area can be very confusing, so be prepared if you don't know any Korean. We figured it out after about 5 minutes of standing around, staring in confusion. Once we reached the island, we rented an electric car (from Gulliver's Travels) with side-by-side seating for 占35,000 for 2.5 hours and cruised around the island following the path. The beaches were incredible. White sand, crystal clear water at the shore, turning into turquoise water a little farther out. Even with the grey sky, it still looked amazing. We didn't climb out to the lighthouse (if you climb to the top of Hallasan on your visit, you'll understand why. Ow.) but we got some great photos of it. Peanut ice cream is way overrated in my opinion, but it was still a must since we were on Udo! My husband got the hallabong ice cream. We liked that one more, but the stuff they put on it tastes like mashed up hallabong peel, so it was bitter and we just scraped it off. There is a restaurant that serves (I forget the name, I am guessing) Hallasan fried rice. They make it look like a volcano! We really wanted to go, but needed to catch the ferry back. Overall, if it had been warmer and the we could actually see the sun, it would have been much more enjoyable. We talk about going back and spending a night on the island so we have the time to walk around it, instead of having to drive/rent a bike.

For us it was a bit of a disappointment that we would need international driver's licence to rent 50-125cc scooter/motorbikes/small car like vehicles on the island. So it is a good thing that they have the electronic scooters, which don't require the licence. They are way cooler to cruise around the island with.It was a clear sunny day, and we spent 2 hours driving around the island, stopping every now and then to enjoy the scenery. There are a few places to visit on the tour so no need to rush around the place. Be sure to make it to the last boat back to the mainland in time (for us it was 5:30pm, but people kept coming there late so it left just before 6pm). From the boat we were able to enjoy the setting sun, which was a great finish for the trip. The boat ride there and back was reasonably priced, and the scooters we got were 25,000KRW for 2 hours. We went there a bit late so the only minus was that the place available for us was with no insurance for the scooters. Still, if you visit Jeju and have extra time on the east side of the island, be sure to visit udo!
Very beautiful island and worth a full day to walk around. Nice ice cream but food there quite expensive.
This is a great place for a day trip, especially if you rent a bike and ride it around the island. There is also some good food throughout. Take a day and head out there.

This tiny, delightful island feels miles away from anything familiar and mundane.  I highly recommend renting an electric scooter (for about 25 bucks for 2 hours) and driving around the entire island.  Driving around the island only takes about an hour, but give yourself extra time to stop for photo ops.  The place is dreamy and laid back - you can even spot the famous haenyeo (women divers) at work, and see their "dressing stations."  There is no "one particular amazing" thing to see on Udo, but rather it's about the whole experience of exploring this off-beat place and losing track of time.

We visited Udo in our recent visit to jeju island. We couldn't see the whole island due to rainy weather. One thing the visitor should be careful about the renting of battery bike or other types of two wheelers. The store owner will ask U something unethical rate for rent and the behaviour of them are really very very bad. They behave with us very rudely.

It takes 15 min to get to Udo by ferry from Jeju, which schedule every 60 min.When you reach the island you have many shops that will offer you to rent small electric vehicles for 2 hours, it will be enough for browsing around all the beautiful circle road of the island. if you're planning to have lunch or some other activity, take 3 hours. 2 hours cost around 20,000 KRW for an electric scooter (1 person).Important Tip: 1. Take detailed pictures of the rental as they will sometimes try to blame you on some scratches they found when you return.2. Can't be miss is the "Rise Mango" 100% that sell all over the Island.

Udo is an amazing place We took our car in the ferry ... Costs only 22000 KRW for return trip plus 6000 KRW for each person. We stopped at so many places and took pictures every where. You could also rent a scooter or electric car, but it you have a car, I would recommend taking your own car esp if you are a group unless you like to enjoy on bike. But be ready to face high wind.Though people recommend a few hours only, this place is worth full day spend.

It was our 2nd time visit Udo,absolutely loved it.Few tips for anyone who plan to visit Jeju:* Bring your ID with you! We went to Udo in July and we were asked to present ID at ticket office, Seongsanri Port. Saw lots tourists queuing at ticket office and pretty much everyone was holding passport!! We didn't have passport with us, but luck enough I had my driving licence in my purse. My boyfriend didn't have any ID with him, and we bought 2 ferry tickets with showing 1 ID only.  * it's an absolutely beautiful place. Tried peanut ice cream which was very refreshing. * scooter or bike? My opinion is get bike!! It costs 10000 won to get 1 bike and you can ride as long as you want, no time limit what so ever, it costs 25000 won to get a scooter, and you need to be back within 2 hours. It was kinda electric bike, so presuming the power only lasts 2 hours. If you plan spend move than 4 hours on this lovely island, bike is the option, not hard to ride around and you can stop at any cafe for a ice cream or drink and chill out at the beach for 1 hour. That's what we did :) rather than just sitting on the scooter and kept checking time consistently to make sure to get back  within 2 hours.
Much to see, places to stop and "smell the roses." Traffic a bit chaotic but go slow and expect everyone else to disregard the rules of the road AS WE KNOW THEM :) Be flexible and open-minded :)

A beautiful island and it was nice to travel around in an ATV along the coastline although 2.5 hours wasn't quite enough after taking a break at a cafe. It might be a good idea to stay overnight at Udo too.

We arrived at 3:30 on Udo, and rented 2 electric scooters from a stand close to the dock. It was a bummer that i couldn't rent a real scooter (you need to bring your int. license btw). It was a lot slower, so it gave us more time to have a more relaxing ride. We visited 2 beaches, and both of them were very clear and very clean (Beware of silver fish though깎). Also, you wouldn't want to miss haha hoo because my friend told me they're incredibly popular. We got some peanut ice cream, and some tea with honey and the special jeju fruit that i can't name (which was absolutely incredible!!!) since everything else was sold out. I would have loved to spend more time there because we only got 3 hours on Udo. In all, it was an amazing and memorable experience.

Rented a scooter for 4 hours and went around the entire island. Renting is easy- just go to one of the places right next to the ferry docks. You have to go to the cliffs and the black sand beach below them. Cross the beach to the rocks where they have the boat then go inside the cave. Walk all the way to the left and go out the small opening- this place have practically no other tourists. Then if it's low tide- climb to the right to the small opening into another cave but this is a lot cooler!
Beautiful. just amazing island. I could not make up my mind to return back from this place. Took a shuttle bus which take you around the island.

Udo is a beautiful island but I would recommend a day trip as Jeju island has a lot more to offer. My friends and I climbed Seongsan Ilchulbong in the morning and then hopped on a boat to Udo, the port is very close and boats go regularly. If you have a car I would recommend leaving it behind as the queue for cars was extremely long. Once we got there we boarded one of the shuttle buses, while they're restricted in where they go it only costs 1,000 won for a single trip, versus renting an electric car that cost about 40,000 but only last 2 hours. The beach we went was not nice, the water was dirty and full of rubbish but the locals didn't seem to mind.Overall it's a nice island but the beaches on Jeju are a lot nicer and cleaner, a day trip is all I would recommend.

This island is only about 10 mins away by ferry from Jeju Island. The environment is very clean and very beautiful. You can either take your own car or hire a scooter to go around the island. It only takes less than 2hrs to complete a full circle. I seriously recommend you to spend a least a day or two.
We rented a scooter and drove around the island for two hours (including lunch). We had fun and enjoyed every minute, but I wasn't overwhelmed by the scenery to be honest.

A really cool place to hang out for half day. Take a return ferry from Port.  If staying near beach in jeju then walk to sanho beach. Stay for few hours and then come back to ferry point. Now take a bike or electric car... for merely 40000 krw. But it's only for 3 hours max (after bargain). But need an international I'd.  I visited with my wife n 3 year son. Took electric car. Stopped at breathtaking  points where bus does not take you. So driving in own vehicle a must for best time.

We decided to go to Audi because of the 3 different beaches the were there (and for Haha Hoho Burgers). Getting there was more difficult than expected. We had a rental car which was nice to be able to retreat back to air conditioning. But the line for the ferry was so long that it took about 2 hours to get on the ferry. Once on the island our first stop was for lunch at Haha Hoho. We were lucky in that they didn't sell out of burgers by the time we got there at 1:50. Buy by the time our burgers were ready 2:40 they were sold out and not taking any more orders. So get there early for lunch. The drive around the island was nice  and picturesque. The first beach we stopped at was a disappointment. The water was green with algae and smelled. There was also quite a bit of trash. With the number of people there I would expect more maintenance. We stayed only briefly hoping for better beaches down the road. The next stop was a black sand beach nestled in a cool looking cove. But again there was trash everywhere. We didn't stay long. The first two beaches were a "bust."  The third was the "coral beach." It was clean but the water still green with algae and seaweed. The beach was rough under our feet but the kids had fun. It was pretty crowded and the water became deep quickly so not much space to play for new swimmers. The views from the island were great, especially at sunset. Overall we were underwhelmed and felt we probably should have stayed on Jeju and just visited the northern beaches.

Due to lack of time, I decided to take a blue/ yellow tour bus (5000KRW for 4 destinations). For those, I prefer the 2nd one which I can enjoy peanut ice cream.The weather was so much hot, which made me tired quite fast.If you wanna rent scooters or cars, international driving licenses are required.Peanut ice cream was not that delicious, but you know, what they sell is creativity, not ice cream.

An absolutely beautiful island that will take you at least half to a full day to properly explore. Rent a bike or a moped and go around the island, stopping for maybe a burger and the location's signature peanut ice cream. With idyllic beaches and spectacular views it is an unforgettable must-visit destination during Jeju.

The best way to do U-Do Island is by car or scooter.  Rent a car prior to boarding the ferry and take it across OR walk on to the ferry and rent a scooter on the island.  Fantastic sights and places to eat.

Small island - the main road that goes around the island is around 13,8 km. A good way to explore is to rent a vehicle - electric scooter, electric motor cycle, electric bike, or bike - and go as you like. But all the electric is required international driving license.

Loved this island off Jeju Island!  If you're staying in the Jungmun area, this requires about an hour taxi or car ride to the port where you catch a ferry (15 minute ride) the island. Best to buy a return ticket at the ticket office (the taxi driver helped us to do this, lucky for us as you need to show your ID or passport to buy tickets!).  The sun came out for us and the island was in all its glory - blue skies and blue sea - absolutely worth the trip.  Can easily spend half to one day here. Not sure how it works with the bus options though if you hire a cabin to stay along the bus route.When you arrive at U-Do, there are various bicycles/cars that you can hire (if you bring your driving licence), however, you can easily buy a hop on hop off bus ticket.  The bus driver talks for some of the way during the bus tour but if you don't understand what's going on, it's just as easy to enjoy the view from the window.  Nature is all around.Apart from the surrounding sea and boats, you can see horses and women divers (next to their orange buoys) in the sea.   We also enjoyed a black pork burger, mandarin juice at our first stop and also a peanut ice-cream from Jimmy's.This visit was another one of the many highlights to our trip and I would love to come again!  Pre-teen kids also enjoyed the beautiful breathtaking scenery.

Udo was formed by an volcanic eruption in the 12th century. We took the ferry boat then signed up for a on/off bus tour and it was worthwhile. The bus stopped at 6 different locations to include three beaches (black sand, gold sand and white sand), near the large volcanic mountain that is the hump that makes up Udo (you can walk up  to the top but given the limited visibility, we  didn't), the Udo Museum (free if you are taking the on/off bus), and Biyang-dong (a small island off of Udo). Because of the weather we did not swim at the beaches but the other attractions were worthwhile, especially Biyang-dong. We were told that because of the rain there weren't the crowds that you normally have on Udo. There are plenty of good restaurants as well. If the weather had permitted, we would have rented bicycles and  ridden around the island (apx 14 KM). I would plan for just over a half day.Costs: Ferry apx 10,000 won per person round tripBus tour: apx 6,000 won per per person (one complete circuit)

We hired bicycles at a shop adjacent the pier and cycled around the whole island. Along country roods, there were many scenic spots, mostly adjacent to the sea,  where we could take pictures. Besides, there were many cafes and kiosks where we could dine and rest.  Cycling around the island in a relaxing pace took about 3 to 4 hours. It was a very good experience.

A cheap half-day activity. Udo Island was the perfect little get-away. We took a nice little ferry ride over to the island and rented peddle bikes to ride around. (You must have an international driver's license, however they took just our American driver's license.. depends on who you talk to) Took us about 3 hours to loop the whole thing (with stopping for icecream, a snack, a drink, etc) Beautiful views around very corner. Make sure to stop and get a burger at HAHA HOHO (located on the left around the bend from ferry drop off) it was definitely an Udo highlight as well as their local icecream. Pack some snacks and have a picnic, great spots to stop and enjoy! Friendly NOTE: Bring sunscreen! The sun is brutal!
Stunning view, especially the beaches. I've chosen to walk around Udo to enjoy every inch of this nice little island. Took me about 5.5 hours (with photo taking) to walk around the island by foot.
Ferry ticket only 5500 won. Book a bus tour only 5000 won... remember take the red and white bus.. other color bus need more time wait for bus... very beautiful at the udo head hills

We went to Udo island on 27th May 2016. Weather was pretty good and sunny. Udo island is a full one day trip. We took a taxi from our hotel in jeju city to intercity bus terminal. Booked our tickets to Seongsan ferry terminal bus#710. It runs on an interval of 20 minutes. We took our bus at 9.40am. It took us approximately 1hr 30min to reach the terminal. From there, we booked our return tickets for the ferry which takes you to Udo island. Return ticket is valid for the entire day and no specific return time is mentioned on it. So you can spend the day in Udo and take any ferry from Udo back to the terminal. To book ferry tickets first you will need to fill some form lying there on the tables. Then show the filled form at the ticket counter and they will give you the ticket. Ferry runs every 30 mins from the terminal. And it takes 15 mins to reach Udo by ferry. Upon arrival to Udo island, you need to walk for 2 minutes and you will see various vendors for renting bike and bicycles. For renting a bike, you need to have driving license and for foreigners international driving license. We didn't have it, so we booked a hop on hop off tour bus. There were two vendors for the bus tour - red buses and blue buses. Red bus tour vendor offered 5 destinations and blue one offered 4 both at the cost of 5,500KRW per person. We booked the red one as we wanted to cover 5 destinations. Also, red buses were available in abundance and blue buses seemed to be pretty less. Once you book the bus ticket, you need to keep the ticket safely with you for the entire trip as whenever you'll board the bus you need to show it to the driver. So DO NOT lose the ticket. Hop on the bus for your first attraction and on the way you will get to see beautiful Udo island with small and tiny roads and farming everywhere. For going to the next attraction, you can hop on any of the bus as the bus service is really good and arrives every 20 minutes at the attraction point. We loved all the attractions except for the museum which I guess was our 4th attraction on the list. You may also skip any of the attractions by not getting off the bus. We also tried peanut ice cream there which was really good and refreshing. Also, you can take a speed boat ride on one of the attractions. In our list, it was the first attraction point to the beach. They charge 10,000KRW for speed boat per person and take you to eight scenic views. We also located so many dophins in the sea which was so exciting. After all the attractions are covered, bus will drop you back to the ferry terminal and while boarding the bus driver will finally collect your ticket.All in all, a memorable and a pleasant trip for us. Just avoid going there on a rainy day. Good luck!!! :)
Udo, literally " Cow Island" in Chinese, has this name because it looks like a cow lying down. The whole of Udo is a lava plateau.

We rented bikes, very old bikes... and toured the island.  It is easy to do so and there is lots to see.  We arrived at 11am and saw the Udo women divers out collecting seaweed and shellfish.  By afternoon they had seaweed drying all over the island.  There were lots of picnic spots, coffe shops, and other forms of getting around.  This is a great day trip from Jeju or you can stay on island.Not alot of English spoken but did run into a couple of people in coffee shops that spoke English.  We didn't mind.  All signage is in English so it is still easy to get around.

Though Udo is a small island, no matter you are renting bicycle/moto or even treking, its easy to get lost especially those tourists with limited Korean. So, just share my experience, make sure where you are onboard the island. There are 2 ports, please check the leaflet the ticket office pass to you. It helps to fix all troubles or uncertain durinf Udo trip.GPS is not quite user friendly there. When you clear the starting point, basically you can follow the simple map. Pls remind that you can use return ticket depart from either ports. Don't be panic. Check the leaflet again, don't throw it away! Enjoy, really a nice place and recommend to stay 1 night in the island too!

Loved my visit here. It is one of the most relaxing islands that I've visited. Food's great and driving around the island is a pleasant experience. They have nice cafes and sceneries along the coastal road. getting around is easy with a car.

Such a beautiful small island. You can reach Udo island by ferry then there are buses available in the island to move you around. Try their peanut and orange ice cream. Personally, I like thier peanut ice cream very much. Highly recommended.
came here through booking a tour with driver Mr Ann. highly recommend him and this place. This place is highly scenic and great if you do not have time to complete long trails in mount hallasan.

Unfortunately, it rains during the day of our visit. Nevertheless, we have a great time exploring the island by udo tour bus. Have a very tasty creamy seafood pasta and peanut ice cream by udo Prince. Will visit again and explore by cycling or motor buggy.

Welcome to the Beautiful UDO, thats the word that will welcome all guest who will travel to this small island. I rent a bike for 10,000 Korean Won  (3 Hours) and I only used it for an Hour lol. There's a lot of thing to do andnsee in Udo and dont miss it. Ill be back soon.

Someone told me Udo is beautiful, so it's in my wish list when I visit Jejudo. I went there on Saturday (7.5.2016). At the harbour, there are many different type of transportation vehicles for rent to travel Udo, so, basically the narrow road at Udo is full of vehicles, no matter is two wheel, three wheel or four wheel. I did the Olle trail 1.1, travel on foot, it was frustrated and irritating when need to walk together with so many types of vehicles, noisy and crowded. But, luckily the trail does divert some part of the trekking route which is away from the vehicle road, hiking up to the light house hill and also farm house and farming area.

We got there around 4:30pm in the afternoon (last ferry boat leaves the Udo island at 5:50pm, unless you are staying overnight) so we didn't have too much time to explore, however, the electric car ride was fun (two seater $15/hr) to cruise around the island, must check out the Light house and Park. The best time to go there is in April/May when all the flowers and trees are in full bloom.

To go there: take bus #710 bound for Sheongsan Ferry Terminal. You have to tell the driver where you're going before boarding the bus. Buy a ferry ticket from the ticket counter (5,500– - round trip).We were there on 2nd May ~11am, the weather was windy but there was sunlight. We bought tickets for hop in and out bus from the ferry terminal. It will take you to 4 different attractions on the island, we only managed to enjoy the first 2 because it started raining (good thing we don't have an international licence, because u can rent a motorbike there too), and it was already windy, so the cold was too much for us. But I would recommend this place. Come once you're here, come at least once. I love the view. Too bad it was raining so we have to keep our trip short.

Udo is gorgeous and so relaxing. You can just rent a bike, they also have electric bikes and they are so easy and comfortable to ride. And on your own pace, go around the whole island in 2 to 3 hours, taking pictures, stopping by to enjoy beautoful scenary. I loved spending half a day, where you can enjoy natural beauty and simple life without big buildings, traffic or noise. Just a short ferry ride from the port in east jeju.

We were lucky with the weather to visit the place, and it is important because during the rain it might not be so attractive.The nature is very beautiful, you will take good pictures for sure.We took a small electric car (for 2 people), but it was comparatively expensive for only 2,5 hours. It is possible to go around the island during that time but only without staying at all tourist points. Moreover, you cannot really enjoy the trip because of being in hurry.All Korean suggested to try peanut and mandarin ice-cream, that we did. Again the price was high, and mandarin one was so sweet that make us to put it in trash right away.People in the island are friendly, and even offer to pick us up to some places by car and shown the shortest way.Taking a boat to see caves was the best experience during the whole travel. For only 10 000 won you will have a lot of fun as the boat goes so fast, and definetly amazing view on the island.

Breathtaking views, beautiful weather, awesome photo-ops, cool ferry ride! Make sure to take the bus tour($5pp). I found it was more convenient to hop on and off as you please instead of riding a bike or scooter, and you just use your tickets to hop on another bus. They don't speak English, so go with a friend if you can. Out taxi driver was nice enough to help us get our ferry tickets and suggested we take the bus tour.

Do not plan your visit to the island if the weather is rainy. You will need your passport or driving license if you want to rent a bicycle, bike or any other vehicle. It will take you 3-4 hours to go around and see the island.
You have to go. It takes 15 min to go udo from seongsanpo by ferry. Beautiful sea beautiful vilage. You can see Emerald sea.

Visited here as part of my tour package. There is a ferry that can transport cars and people to the island. Upon reaching the island, we took a bus tour n brings us to a few locations. The most memorable one will be the hike up to the lighthouse. Tiring but fun and you can see the great ocean around. Took slightly more than a half day of tour in this island and it's fun :)

Udo is a beautiful island by itself but due to the time constrain we had, we didn't had time to digest the beaches and scenic views. We had always wanted to rent an ATV there and even applied for international driving license as advised by many reviewers, however, we were greatly disappointed as the rental places only rent ATV to holders of Korean driving license. IDL are not accepted so don't waste money to apply for one. We rented electric bike in the end but had a dispute with the rental store nearest to the udo habour. One of our electric bike tyre went burst as the tyres were already old and the store owner wanted us to pay. We had an disagreement as the tyres when rented to us were already worn out. I must attribute to miscommunication as the people at udo are not conversant in English nor mandarin. We beared half the cost only after calling udo police to mediate the situation. But not much help from the police who told us to "go home". Quite a memorable experience for us though.

We went to udo island in ferry with our car inside the ferry. That was a good experience. Island is nice, but the attractions are not so breathtaking as explained. Can visit once. Beach was good. And the electric small 2-seater rental car was nice.
We rode a road bike and it was so exciting! I will not forget the memories of Udo with my friends. It was so beautiful (the beaches), and I loved the friends there!

nice view everywhere. took the ferry and saw people feeding the birds. took the bus tour but seems more fun taking the ATV which many young people are taking. we took the speed boat at udo peak area and was quite fun & exciting. can spend at least half a day in udo.

spent a long day in Udo - so idyllic and relaxing.  There are endless seaside beaches, cliffs, cafes, ...  Just drive your own car there (via car ferry - costed us 32k Won) for a small car and 2 pax, or rent one of the bikes, motor tricycles (very cute), and just drive and stop anywhere (almost) you like and take photos, drink coffee, or just doing nothing and daydreaming. Excellent scenery, food- freshest seafood, burgers, ..... How nice to spend a day.

We drove our car over to Udo Island via a ferry. It was a great experience. A tip for drivers to head for the parking at the jetty as you have to fill in a form with your particulars (car number, drivers details) to purchase a ticket at the tour office. It only takes 15 mins to cross the island and thereafter we drove around. There are no maps so we went one round. It was very crowded being a Saturday so try to go on weekdays. There are a lot of interesting cafes, 4 beautiful beaches, lighthouses, lots of lovely spots for sightseeing and great photos opp. You can also take a speedboat at the black beach or visit the caves. We took the seafood pot with instant noodles for lunch in a local small restaurant. The last ferry was at 6.00pm but maybe earlier on weekdays. Overall, it was a very interesting day trip and we enjoyed ourselves.

Udo is a small island to the east of Jeju Island - about 1 hour bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal to Cheng Shan Port and take another 15 mins on a ferry to Udo.  Udo offers a beachside road around the island.  If you have an international driving license, you can rent a small electri car to drive around the island, if not, you can still rent a eletri bicycle or use local bus.  There are many restaurant and cafes along the beachside road.  Sometime you can see a small white sand beach between those dark volcano rocks.

Transportation to the island: rent a car to drive there, or get 4 people to share a cab (costs around 50,000 won from jeju city). There's also the bus option but I wouldn't recommend as its not the easiest to navigate around the ferry pier. Then take the ferry which leaves every one hour, costs around 5500 won. The ferry is a short ride, only ten mins away! Transportation within the island: the shuttle bus costs only 5000 won, pretty convenient, and it'll take you to the main 4 spots. There's also option of ATV and car rental, which id recommend ATV since its mostly single-lane roads on the island. Food: everyone wanna try the peanut flavored ice cream but I found it's extremely mediocre. It's not 'peanut flavored' but just normal ice cream with peanut powder sprinkled. Save your stomach for the seafood pot! Although not the cheapest I've had, but still pretty worth a try! Get the option with octopus cook on the table if you can stomach the scene (I know lots of my friends can't). A lot of light walking you can do around the island, the weather was still quite cold so we couldn't get into the water. I love that you can go hill climbing at one spot and the dip your toes into the (chilly) ocean the next.
Taking the shuttle bus around the island was convenient and easy. Visting the island on a nice sunny day is a must!

We rented an ATV at the ferry drop off, (an international driving permit is necessary), the clockwise drive around the coast was easy and dotted with many eateries and cafes. Stopped at mulko's house for some excellent seafood lunch, then picked up peanut ice cream near the bottom of the udobong trail. There's peanut rice wine and peanut bread available as well. Took 11am ferry over and 2pm ferry back. Highly recommended
Wonderful place to visit when in Jeju island. That said, you must be ready to do lots of walking and climbing. Make sure you got the right attire.
The Udo island is one must visit place in Jeju trip, you can easy to explore the whole island by using bus purchase one ticket or rent a motorbike.

From Jeju City Local Bus Terminal, take bus #701, stop at Seongsan Port. It takes 90mins, 3300won.Fill up the boarding form for the ferry, before you proceed to buy the ferry ticket at the counter. Round trip charges 5500won, which takes 10mins per trip. Expect a lot of visitors during weekends or public holidays.At Udo, there are shops offer rental of bicycles, ATV, automatic scooter, etc. which can accommodate every one either youths, elders or children.You could enjoy cycling around the island the best during a windy chilling day.When I think of Udo, I will remember the kindness of restaurant owner of щ 대Ъ珥. When I was eating, I accidentally hit my dental braces with the spoon, and I was rubbing to ensure it was alright. The ajumma approached me and asked me what happened, I showed her my braces, and she was quick-witted to get scissor to cut banchan into smaller pieces, while cutting, she repeatedly saying "ottoke ottoke".. I was really grateful to her, and I enjoyed the lunch well.

We drove our rented car onto the ferry which took us to Udo in 15 minutes. If the weather hadnt been so cold, we would have tried the fun looking electric scooters. We stumbled into a seafood restaurant to the left of the ferry terminal and enjoyed a sumptuous seafood kimchi hotpot. Ordering was not a problem as the service staff spoke mandarin. The place was an obvious favourite with locals. We spent 4 hours exploring various sites and even got lost. A friendly local policeman kindly pointed us the right way. We stopped by quaint coffeeshops and hugged their cute puppies. We were reluctant to leave this idyllic tiny island.

We started with a speedboat tour around the island. This was so much fun, because it's in an inflatable boat, and it goes super fast! My husband is Korean and told me to hold on with both hands. I am a Floridian so I thought I have done this before, but no! Hold on with both hands! The water are very rough there. You got to see the dragon head rock formation, the elephant rock formation, and the moon cave. He stops briefly to let you take pictures but I suggest a water proof camera with a strap so it does fly away or get wet.Then we went to look at all the restaurants. We took a bus to the middle of the island so we could hike to the light house. The hike was awesome the lighthouse was eh, okay. But the sights along the way we're really cool. The nature, and the ocean below was beautiful

Udo, is a small island located on the east side of Jeju Island. You can get there by taking a boat (around 20min) on the east side of Jeju. you can also bring your vehicle onto the boat and bring it to Udo.The island is quite big that you cannot walk around the island by feet. If you are not bringing your own vehicle, you can rent a ride near to the harbor BUT you need to have a driver's license. So prepare an international driver's license maybe (I am not sure if they accept international license though:( )There is also a bus that goes around the island and once you buy a ticket near the harbor, you can get off from the bus and get back into any bus without any extra charge.The sight around the island is beautiful. You can stop your vehicle at any time and enjoy and take photos.

I came to Udo on my 4th day in Jeju and it was the spotlight of my trip. I love the island itself and everything about it. You can rent a bicycle or a motorbike to go around the island. I didnt bring my licence so you didnt let me rent the motorbike even I told them that I am Vietnamese, I really can drive ( in Korean ) =)) It was a funny conversation, but I end up with riding the bicycle for 4 hours .. quite tired but amazing place and worth to visit.I went to Korea alone, and my days in Jeju was quite boring but Udo made my trip more memorable ^^

So happy we took the time to make the climb.  It's a lot of stairs to the top, so I would suggest you take along some water, and possibly some snacks, so you can take a rest part way up.There is one way up, and another down, which keeps things moving quickly.
Great to hang out with a scooter. Many scenic views and nice small restaurants and artist. It is really young place that I didn't expect at the beginning.

This place is great, fresh seafood sold at the coast, seeing the sea ladies in action (we were lucky and saw her catching an octopus with a fork like stick) and beautiful scenery of the coast, sea and land. It's a short boat ride over from the main island, then one could choose to take their bus at a fee, which will stop by 4 or 5 stops near the beach, cliff, etc  then bring u back to the starting point. Alternatively, you could rent a motorbike or four wheel drive. For the latter, one needs an international driving licence. One thing that's everywhere is their peanut ice cream, basically soft serve with peanut powder. Also, there's grilled cuttlefish everywhere.

If you are traveling alone, not planning to ride a bicycle or rent a car on the island, you can buy a local tour bus ticket. The price varies as they are several bus company. The local tour bus stops at several highlights of the island. The bus driver will introduce and talk about the island (in Korean). The scenery is excellent, a must-visit-place in Jeju. You need to spare at least 4 hours for U-do Island.

Take a ferry from Seongsan, jump on a bicycle for the day and peddle round stopping at all the attractions. It's only 1.5hrs to cycle at a slow pace round the entire island so easily done via a day trip from Seongsan or even Jeju City if you got up early. We stayed on the island itself but truth be told there's not much added value, just do a great fun day trip / cycle - and we are very much NOT cyclists by the way!

Udo island is a small island at east of Jeju Island. It is named after cow because of its cow alike shape. Once you reached the island, you are able to find few bike rental shop. You can rent a electrical scooter with roof or normal scooter to tour around the island. Bare in mind the speed limit is 30 km/h. Most of the rental shop offer two hours rental only. Generally, it should be sufficient if you don't linger at each place too long. Do try the peanut ice-cream as the island is famous for peanut plantation. Get your camera ready as there are many beautiful scenaries to take photos.

We went there by car that we brought from jeju. It's really beautiful nevertheless. 1 day is enough to tour all of it. If you want to try horseriding, there's some that offer price 5000 won per ride, while others 10k won. There's many place that offer horseriding, so if you want to save your budget without sacrifing the experience, walk some more to find cheaper ones.Try the Hallasan fried rice! It's really worth it!

We decided to take the ferry to Udo at the last minute. We could have taken the rented car but decided not to. That was a right decision in my view. We took the hop on hop off bus and visited most of the tourist attraction. Be mindful of the bus schedule. Most people don't understand or speak English so one has to be patient. The scenery was lovely and the island unadulterated. I recommend to spend half a day here - just relax. The island is well known for peanuts which I find quite expensive. We had seafood ramen and abalone porridge. Yummy!

for one day trip, from the city, it's easy to take a bus to the pier, you can ask your hotel or guest house about timetables for buses.Get there early and when you arrive you will find a lot of people renting bikes and motorcycle and tuk-tuk and ATV. However, they ask for international licenses but you can show them any licenses some of them will accept, try with more than one store.for the motorcycle was 25,000 KRW for 3 hours.

Circumnavigated this little island on a bike in an afternoon, and it was a lovely excursion. The older culture is still somewhat alive (weeding through the tourist stops), but even the bitsy coffee shops are endearing. Bicycle is the way to see this place, for sure!

Take a boat is convenient from Jeju to Udo (we were driving , the boat is able to carry the car) only 30 minutes boat, then arrive at Udo. We drive along the coste road, stopped by the hill, it is a 30 mins climbing, once reach the top you can have a overview of this Island  We literally turned around the island by car. Tried sea food abalone and some shellfish. It was very good experience. We star at 11.30am boat to Udo and finished at 4pm to take boat back to Jeju main land. It can be a 3-4 hours visit.

You can imagine: blue sky, strong wind and black shore.  Lots of shops and restaurants around the small island.  Locals can hire a small motorcar but for foreigners without local driving licence, bicycles seem to be the only choice.  It takes about 3 hours to finish the round-island cycling with adequate sightseeing.

We took a cab from Ramada Plaza for 30,000 wan. It took about half an hour. The bus home 710 was great and took an hour. 3000 wan. The island was good fun. We cycled the island stopping along the way to see things. The elder diving women were really cool. Sad to see the garbage around from the sea :( Udo is in such a highly populated area of the world garbage is a big problem. It makes me want to really try to become green at home in Canada.

You can easily spend a half or full day sightseeing around the island. They have tour buses which will take you around to the major sights but I'd recommend renting a bike. There are heaps of places to rent bikes from after you get off the ferry. You'll need an international license to rent a scooter or ATV. But there are no serious hills in the island so (if you're there in fall/spring with fair weather) I'd really recommend a bicycle. It was so lovely cycling around the island and easily jumping on and off my bike to snap pictures.The bike rental was 4 hours for 10,000 won. They shop will give you a map of the island with tours and sightseeing locations on it. Although you don't really need it as you basically just cycle the seaside road. Don't forget your camera or to eat the famous peanut ice cream!

Loved it. Great cycling route. 16km can be done in less than an hour. But take a break to enjoy a coffee or some delicious food and just enjoy the food. If you want to test out future tourism, take one of the available electronic scooters.
Loved the ferry ride to the island, it was about 30 mins if not less. You can take the bus tour of the island, but the driver (also the tour guide) speaks Korean only. ^^

I went to Udo with a group of friends. It was really nice, we went around the island with rented bicycles (10.000 KRW for the afternoon). We swam in an incredibly clear water.I recommend going to Sunrise peak afterwards, walking along the coast gets you there in 15 min and seeing the sunset was an amazing experience.

Seriously, just go UDO island to experience a different feel as the island is quite small. I managed to complete a circle with my rental vehicle within 1-2 hours. There's quite a lot of spots that you can get down and walk. (fuel will drain quite a lot as there's quite a number of up-slope)

My first time to Korea focusing on Jeju and Seoul. Generally I would think the overall experience to South Korea is kind of over rated. I expected more based on the comments from friends, reviews by travellers and most importantly seeing it in Korean Dramas.Udo island is an exception, it gave me the best experience in the entire 8-day trip, except the weather wasn't too good on my day trip to Udo. Rented a bike to travel almost the entire island which i think is the best mode to explore remote areas without using too much energy.  Hopping up and down to take photos by the beach, colorful cafes, yellow canola fields, uphill and downhill.Unforgettable squid volcano rice was one of its kind and one of the most satisfactory meal in the entire trip.

I have spend a week on Jeju Island in September, and of my Highlights was Udo. I had time only for a day trip, and if I ever make it back to Jeju, my priority will be to spend at least one night there. Its such a lovely, small and relaxed place. From Seongsan its only 15 minutes to Udo by Ferry. There, you can take the local bus that runs along the island, you can rent small tuk-tuks / quad bikes / scooters or bicycles, you can join a tour (I think only in Korean) or you can walk (like I did, but then of course you dont get to cover the whole island).
We took a car passenger ferry to to Udo island from Jeju. This a small but beautiful island. We drove around the island and try some fresh seafood.

To get to this island, one has to fill in a form and pay for the fees. All is convenient and easy peasy. Then, the ferry ride is quick. We opted for a bus tour. The tour was in Korean and we couldn't understand a thing but considering it is one of the easiest method to get around the island,we just go along with it. We would like to ride one of those adorable scooters but we don't own an international license. Overall a good experience.

yes, it is beautiful! you can either cycling, riding ATV or follow a bus tour to go around Udo. I paid 5000won for the bus tour which started from the jetty. Many tour buses going around the 4 main attractions, you can simply hop on hop off the tour bus. The first stop which brought us to a hill had a magnificient view from the peak. Don't give up hiking up to the peak! The beaches in Udo are amazingly beautiful, different tone of blue and green sea water, white sandy beach and fresh seaweed grown on the rocks. Love U-do for being so nature and awesome!

I visited here with my family, so we drived our rental car. But if you don't have an international license, then rent a bike or motorcycle.You can rent it in a reasonable price.There are 5 bus stations here and those are nice sights.There is a beach in two sights and one of them is a popular site for jet boat.And the other one is popular for water leports.And whole Island is a heaven for riders.If you love mountian bike or road bike, then take your bike to this island.This is a perfect place for cycling.And there are many nice restaurant and dessert cafe, so enjoy yourself here.
Loved this island, I recommend exploring it by foot.  We interviews the monk the temple for our film "Jeju: A Bicycle Adventure" and he was super kind and served us coffee and drink.

After parking the rental car at Seongsan Harbor, we hopped on the ferry (KRW 1,500) to cross over to Udo. Upon alighting from the ferry at Cheonjinhang Harbor on Udo, we headed to the Udo Tour Bus counter and got ourselves a ticket each (KRW 5,000). The whole tour is conducted in Korean. Not a single hint of English but it was enjoyable. The bus driver was also the tour guide, telling us about the significance of each stop. He'd stop for 20 minutes at each place of interest and if you do not hop back on, fret not, you may hop on the other tour buses. Keep your ticket stub.The whole tour took about 2 hours. The village roads were really interesting. If I visit Jeju again, I would want to stay overnight at Udo. The atmosphere is good, the air is fresh, people are nice.

It is a small island. we took the boat from Jeju. In a lobby full of Korean people, speak no English or Chinese. It was a bit challenge for me. ;) helpful enough, when I tried to talk to the ticket officer, she spoke a little Chinese. The boat took around 15 min. it is a pretty simple boat, with both people, and cars. with 30 min. time interval.Landing on Udo, we chose the red bus tour. 4 stops. the first stop is the best place I should say. Brilliant view! sea with sea wind. And there are some bars and restraunts where you could take a seat and rest.The rest of the 2-3 stops, are normal. On the bus, the driver were saying in Korean languange, which we do not understand at all. But we heard laugh from time to time, which we believe everyone else enjoyed the drivers speech.It is a good short stay. sun shine is strong, get prepare with some protections.

Udo is a mini-Jeju, with traditional elements such as stone walls, farms, female divers and ocean cliffs all compressed into a much more manageable area. I rented a bicycle with a basket from an old ahjussi for 4000krw (3 hours). His stall, or rather tent, was located just at the ferry terminal. There are shops across the street that rent out bicycles, scooters and motorcycles.Cycling around Udo was a breeze. It was mainly flat terrain with some gentle slopes here and there. You will ride past white sandy beaches, rocky pools, farms, stone walls, female divers, cute puppies and cafes. Remember to grab some peanut ice cream, the island s specialty.For more information and pictures on Udo, visit my travel blog https://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/

Udo isn't for everyone and I actually wish that a lot fewer people would visit because the island can get crowded with tourists in cars or on ATVs and scooters. I have lived in Korea 2.5 years and travelled extensively during my time here. I will be going back for my 4th visit next week, each visit for no less than 2 nights. The snorkelling is great especially in places that most Koreans deem "too dangerous" simply because the water is deep. There is one of the best raw fish restaurants in Korea on this little island. The sea surrounds you and the sights are lovely in every direction. There really isn't a lot to do on the island which is exactly why I love it. Sea. Seafood. Sights. It is all amazing.

Very peaceful place that must be visited when you are in Jeju.  When you arrive in Udo, you can join the mini bus tour after getting off the ferry.  Of course, you can also rent the motorbike and drive around.  Be aware of the ferry time going back to the City.  It was definitely a highlight of my Jeju trip. xx

Udo is an island very close from Jeju-do. It's next to Seongsan-ilchul-bong, which is also famous. It takes about 15 minutes by boat from Seongsan port. You pay for entrance to the island with the boat fare. The usual course seems to be walking up the hill in Udo, Gummerlae, and checking out the lighthouse surrounded by lots of stones stacked on top of each other for wishes to come true. The weather was perfect when we went, very sunny :)

We went around the island via a three- wheel vehicle we rented for two hours.  It was definitely a nice view going around, a lot of attractions to see, white beach with very deep blue water, lighthouse, mountains, cliff, and the island was almost in a very vibrant color of yellow due to the rapeseed flowers blooming that spring time. We also chanced upon old women divers, which were popular in the island. We had lunch and tried one of specialty in the restaurant which was sea urchin seaweed soup! It has a very nice flavor and very filling.  We also ate peanut ice cream!

I heard about Udo Island from a few of the other ladies I was traveling with. They had seen pictures and couldn't wait to visit. I tagged a long for some good fashion outdoor fun. We rented bikes for the afternoon and took a ride around the island. The weather was perfect and we were able to see some great scenery. We visited a couple of the beach places and were able to take incredible pictures. We took a ferry ride over and it was amazing. Getting tickets and filling out paper work to take the ferry was incredibly easy and everyone was very helpful on the island. We were able to eat some great seafood and awesome ice-cream. Great spot to visit!

Taking a quick ferry ride will bring you to a breathtaking place called Udo Island. Rocky coasts, beautiful beaches, and crystal clear waters are what you will find on this little farming and fishing island. I decided to rent a bike on my trip and wander around the coastline. In my opinion, it was the best way to see the island. Amazing photo opportunities and tons of places to get some fresh seafood along the way. The clear and shallow water is great for children to play in. Tons of little tidal pools as well. Biking allowed you to be outside and experience the people and the culture of the island. It is probably not a place for people that do not enjoy the outdoors or those that are afraid of a little bit of exercise!

Udo Island, a small volcanic island 10 minutes by ferry from Jeju Island. A day out on this island can be a bore to those who have no affinity to the outdoors, particularly that of the sea.But if you love the care-free life of roaming from one sandy beach to another rocky one. In between with lots of coastal features to be awed by, then this is the little paradise on earth.Udo is an island which allows you to go the entire distance around the coastal roads, in under 4 hours, including stops for pictures, strolls, ice-cream, desserts and of course a whole host of meals.  There are rugged, rocky coastlines and little stretches of sandy beaches with emerald waters.Getting from point to point on the island is very easy, either on bicycles, rental motorbikes and scooters. Mainlainders can ferry in their car for their own pleasure. We rented a motor-scooter for 25, 000 Won for just over 4 hours. The rental is for 2 hours (Won 25000)

I have just come back from Udo and i am happy i decided to go there.originaly it was  not in my plan. Based in Jeju-si I took bus710 (3300짜) to Seogsan port,1h20min drive. Then ferry (return ticket 5500짜) 20min. I rent bicycle (8000짜/3hours) and start Udo tour around the cost. It is 18km around island so if you are in hurry it is possible to make it much faster 1.5h enough. I also made a couple of detours inside island to see how people live. Everything is small and cute there:roads,houses,fields,fences made of stones.I recommend to climb Udo hill -nice view from there and climb is easy. It was sunny day and i get sunburned so please do not forget sunblock cream. It is windy island and one doesn't  feel is being sunburned.

We love this place!!! It is so so so so so so so beautiful! Travelled with my hubby and 2 kids and took the earliest ferry to Udo. The ferry we took is those that doesnt come with seats and we have to sit on the floor like the Koreans do. Rented 2 scooters and rode the around the entire island for 2 hours with our kids sitting behind us. It is really safe to ride but you need to make sure you have your international driver license with you before you can rent a scooter. My hubby doesnt know how to ride a scooter, but no worries, simple instructions and quick lessons were given and within 10 mins we were off to our adventure. Though it was winter when we visited, the wind did not stop us from visiting every checkpoint to take photo and of coz, eating the famous peanut icecream. I really felt like I had jumped into a K-drama, especially when I have my Oppa with me, haahaa! It was quite cold so we din manage to get into the water. But already we had spent like 4 hours just wondering around the island. The fun part was to get lost into some residents farms and got directed to get onto the right path. The sceneries are breathtaking! I cant describe better. Really beautiful. Definitely highly recommended, even for people with young kids!

This island is like a mini-Jejudo. You can see entire Seongsan Ilchubon from this island. This place is more relaxing and peaceful than Jeju-do, a bit off-touritst path compared to other places. I like the view at Udobong at its atmosphere. Which I had more time, so I can bike around the island.

I stayed at Ojo Haenyo Guesthouse area, hopped on a taxi to get to the port to Udo. The port is actually very near but I chose not to walk there. Paid less than KRW4000 for the taxi, cheap indeed.Bought a return ticket at less than KRW6000, ran towards the ferry that was about to leave for Udo, and in less than 30 minutes, we reached beautiful Udo. In case you're wondering, the ferry ride is too short to get motion-sickness :pIt rained during my short trip to this island so I didn't rent a bicycle. Instead, I got on the hop-on hop-off bus, the ticket was about KRW5000 or so. Super cheap. But the driver/tourist guide spoke only in Korean. But no worries, I did enjoy the tour.I managed to walk up to the lighthouse, had the famous peanut ice-cream overlooking a gorgeous view of the beach and a cliff, I also went to one of the beaches there. Udo is as gorgeous as Jeju. There are nice cafes with free wifis. Street food, local food, souvenirs; Udo is small but it has everything for visitors. Do wear good walking shoes, bring a ponco with you, and get on the last ferry if you can as this island is beautiful!!

we've been Udo island on the day 2 at Jeju Island after hiking to Sunrise Peak Seongsan Illchulbong. we going to the port by walking about 15 minutes from Illchulbong, and takes ferry only for 11.000W returns. the ferry takes 15 minutes to island and schedule every 10 minutes. We have only for 3 hours at the island before going back, so we chose to hiking Udo peak. takes 40 minutes - 1 hours to reach the peak, just follow the path. really recommend to going Udo island, very beautiful scenery of Seongsan Illchulbong and the cave.You also can rent a bike for around the island or motorbike if you have international license. Or shuttle bus.

Udo was a really fun trip! We rent a bicycle and went around the beautiful island. You able to see beautiful scenary and how local people living their lives (houses and farming) . Restaurant is everywhere and easy to get food. Thought it would be super expensive since its in an island..but its not. Ferry was pretty easy and fast (10-15mins) too. You can easily soend 2-3 hours here. Highly recommended !
Ride a scooter around this island. You will not regret it! Also have a burger at the place in the northern part of the village, it's pretty good for asian standards.
It is better to travel the island by bike.The seafood there was good and cheap but the beach was not very suitable for swimming.

When you come to Jeju, you have to go to the lovely island of Udo. It is very touristy, but it still has much to offer and so many lovely views. The Udo icecream experience from the bluffs to the kind people, interesting black sand beaches, breath taking views, suje burger (in ho ho ho restaurant, even the ferry ride is an experience... grab some beers and enjoy the ride. We ferried over our rental (–26,000) for two pax to a grand total of –37,000; it's –5,500 a piece for a single passenger on the ferry roundtrip. They have little buggies for rent there as well, they are the real danger for anyone driving on Udo. But its an overall lovely little place and be prepared to go full selfie mode there because every view is amazimg.

This is a great little island for relaxing! Be sure to rent a bicycle in order to explore everything, as walking would take most of the day. There are a few nice cafes and restaurants along the coast, but mostly, I recommend buying yourself a can of Cass beer and sitting near the sea to enjoy the views.
Perfect place for renting a bike and it takes about 1.5 to 2 hours to paddle around the island. Coffee shops and attranctions along the way.

Drove to Udo island on a self-drive trip and took ferry from Seongsan pier in the morning. It was easy driving in Udo island - it was a tiny island and there weren't many tourists around. While strolling up Udo-bong, saw a group of physically challenged students brought to Udo-bong by their teachers. A very heart warming sight. There isn't anything much to do yet if you are interested in exploring the nature (like I do), it is a good place to spend a morning just feeling the nature.

drove there via ferry car ferrying services. Was a little confused on where to purchase the tickets but just follow the crowd. Paid about 30000 won for car and 2 paxs to get across the island. When I arrived at the island, it was very windy and it really felt cold! However, I enjoyed the fresh air and flower fields there!

I went when the canola flowers (rape flowers) were blooming. It was overcast and cold but dispite that the 4 of us had a great day. I love the peanut jam and bought some to take home. The ice cream was ok but I think I would have liked it more if the weather was sunny and hot. We hired scooters to get around and I would recommend others to do the same.

The island is windy. Quite convenient to go around as there's shuttle bus with blue and red route that bring you around the island. The bus driver will narrate in Korean to explain the places, although we don't understand but is a fun trip to go along with mostly korean. The field grows full of canola flowers (yellow), very beautiful. Also, with nice cliff with plunging waves, good place to take pictures. The water is clear blue at the beach. Unfortunately, we only planned for half day trip so we can only complete the blue route. So, best to plan for a day as it probably takes you full day to admire the scenery.
In good weather you can spend the whole day there. Beautiful island with nice views. You can rent a bike and cycle around the island .

Windy Island15 minute taking ship from Sungsan dock to Woo-do, it s really convenience to visit there.The road were well maintained and there were variety of vehicles could I used.Before I got there, I heard that the peanut jam is famous and ice-cream made by peanut is good. Some people also strongly said to me  you should have Spicy seafood noodle soup(Jjamppong) . Well, I actually tasted it..so..so..nothing special.Many people recommend me to visit the island woodo, there are not a special place at all.You can take almost everything in Jeju what Woodo can do..
If you have come all the way to Jeju Island it seems quite silly to go the Udo. There really is nothing spectacular about it. Jeju Island has enough to occupy a visitor.
I took a bus tour on Udo. The beaches on Udo are light blue in colour - really amazed me! Would definitely like to go again in summer!
I like the beautiful beach and lighthouse. Peanut icecream is my favourite. we can see the traditional diving woman swimming to catch sea urchins.

Very lovely island. But travelling is an issue if you do not have international license to rent the atv. The roads were pretty narrow hence, a little scary to ride bicycle around. Hence the best would be by feeder bus.The seafood noodle, peanut makgeolli and peanut yogurt were fantastic and must try!

My partner & I chose park our car at seongsan harbour so we could take the ATV. To our dismay, their ATV can only carry 1 driver. Therefore we rented the sheltered scooter that can sit 2. The rental of that scooter is charged at an exorbitant 15,000krw/hr. We exceed the return time by a mere 20 minutes and had to top up 10,000krw T.T Advise to all: Just drive up your car to the ferry. It's much cheaper than spending so much on a cramp scooter, especially during winter.Aside from the transport misfortune, our day afternoon in udo was well spent, but could be better. We took the 12 noon ferry and reached udo at 12:30pm. Last ferry back to seongsan was 4:30pm. We did not have time to hike up, nor enter the cave. Spent too much time cam whoring to take in every bend of the scenery. The Seobin-baeksa beach is beautiful, surrounded by crystal clear waters.Advise to all: Go in earlier, so cater time for hiking, cam whoring, and chilling by the beach. Must have lunch too, the seafood noodles has the freshest abalone and soup ever.

Island best explored by driving, ATV or bike rental. Ferry across from mainland Jeju also carries vehicles. Road kinda narrow so one need to be careful, I blew a tyre when my right wheel rammed into a rock or kerb :-(  Lots of climbing if you really wanna explore in-depth. Many small eateries on the island. Very scenic island with lots of photo opportunity. Be wary of last ferry back or you would be stuck there overnight

We went to Udo during the winter season. We decided to take the bus to tour the island. The bus was supposed to stop at 4 points. When we got off at the second stop, we couldn't find the same bus when it was time to head to the next stop so we just took other buses. Transportation aside, Baeksa beach is worth a visit, and peanut ice cream is a must try.

This was really a nice long walk. Will advise to wear good walking shoe. The route was easy to walk just that when the wind come you can feel the wind blowing at you. You have to walk all the way up and you will be able to see the nice surrounding. It was really nice and we really enjoyed it.

We rented bycicles and ride around (It was about $15 for 2 bycicles) The stones on the beaches were special. We tried the dish of raw fish and noodles in the restaurant where my friend said to have appeared a movie/show. It's near the beach. The fish was fresh but we dont like the taste much. It's a really naturally beautiful place comparing to others in Jeju. You would want to spend half-day there to fully go around the island.

It's my favourite place in Jeju! It's not just an island as we thought it would be! Rmb to bring along your international license if you are planning to ride any motorised vehicles. We biked around the island which in my opinion allows you to see more attractions. Do time checks regularly as the ferry leaves at around 5pm, note that the timings given on the booklet is not accurate. Had the best Jakk Pong (seafood noodles) on this island near the cave! (just follow the smell) try the peanut ice cream! its better than the hallabong one.

Had a lovely half-day here. The island is small, but has beautiful beaches, and a tall hill. We rented a scooter and had a slow day driving around, seeing the sights and having our snacks.I'd say it's a fairly good place to take it easy and go at your own place to be close to nature, but not so close that a cafe by the sea isn't too far away.Visited in early November.

My sister and I went to Udo on a ferry ride after spending a couple of hours at Seongsan Ilchulbong. Because we did not want to go back at dawn, we limited our time to be on the island for about 2-3 hours.It is actually best recommended to spend half a day touring the island either on bus or motorbike. Since we did not have much time, we only walked to the nearby beach which was pretty deserted and that was the best part. Most of the tourist places in Jeju was crowded, but not Udo at the time we were there. The beach was beautiful with small stones and black rocks layering the sand. It was beautiful.There were plenty of cafes within walking distance but we chosed a bench facing the sea in front of a GS25 mart.I love the serenity the island offered. I just wish we had more time to go around the island.

Spent the sun rose moment at Seongsang Ilchulbong, which was a wonderful sight it self. After,  we say in the cafe waiting for the ferry stated to operate. Walk from Seongsan to the Udo ferry terminal for about 20 to 30 mins.Fillup a form with names and contact number, purchased round ticket (do not loose it) and get board, straight forward. Ferry travel the channel for only 15 mins.On Udo island terminal, immediately you find a shop for transport rental: bike,  motor bike, trike, ATV and others.We choose hop on hop off bus. Any bus will drop you to four different spot ONCE,  in the island which was near to an attraction. If you decided to skip the spot you'll still need to wait for the next bus which is another 30 mins. At the last spot you need to showed the bus driver your ferry ticket also.

getting to the jetty might be an issue unless you take a cab. I walk from the sunrise peak and it took me awhile to reach the jetty..if you plan to go a complete circle around island is better you rent a bike or car (you will require to have international license). taking a bicycle is hard.. I rented a bicycle and manage to visit the east side only.. in 3 hours...

When you visit JEJU island, UDO is a must-visit spot, especially in summer.UDO is a small island next to Jeju island.You can go to UDO by taking a ferry.It takes about 20 minutes and you can load your rent car on a ferry as well.A ferry back and forth between jeju and UDO frequently.The best thing in UDO is to enjoy the swimming in the shell beach.Instead of sand, the beach in UDO has  small stone and shell. Due to the small, round stone and small shell particles, the color of the sea is wonderful.Also you can rent a bike or small 4-wheel motorcycle and enjoy the scene around the island.I visited UDO twice and it was always above my expectation.

Rent bikes and escape the tour groups, and you can stop where you like. We found Udo was quieter than the rest of Jeju Island. There are plenty of coffee shops, small eateries and ice cream places. Things to see include lighthouses and beaches - but there is a huge amount of litter around the rocks and headlands.  Peanuts are grown on the island and there was a peanut festival at the ferry terminal when we visited.

It is probably a bad idea to go round island with the 5000 KRW tour bus - all the 4 stopovers were swarmed with tourists, but with just 2-3 hours to spare, we did not have much choice. First stop was at Udo-bong leading towards the Udo Lighthouse. Next was the Geommeolle Beach with black sand and rocks. The other two were beaches. At the last stop it was a little confusing as to which tour bus to board (to end the tour) as there were apparently 2 ferry terminals, and each terminal would sell tour bus with different docket colours.If we were to come again, we might do the 1.1 Olle Trail, perhaps by bicycle. At some parts of the island it was really picturesque coastline and we saw the haenyeo divers.Sans the big turnout of tourists, Udo will get a better rating definitely.
We road around on our bikes on this cute little island. Wish we had more time. Also wish that they clean up the island a bit. It was a shame that the tourists left so much trash behind.
I nice out of the way place. Has some nice quiet beaches. Easy bike, ATV, and scooter rentals. Great peanut ice cream. Little farms everywhere. Short ferry ride.

We really enjoyed Udo. It's a small little island located about 30 minutes(ferry ride) off of Jeju. We got to the island with only about three hours before the last ferry was going to leave, so we wanted to pack in all that we could. First, we got some peanut ice cream. Then, we rented bicycles and tooled around the island's coast. It was beautiful and several times as I took in the sights, I kept thinking, "How cool is this? How many people I know will ever get to have this experience?" It was a neat feeling to be exploring a quaint and little-known spot in the world. We found a little beach and cooled off before heading back to the ferry.

Udo island in jeju is a must see attraction. From jeju have to take ferry to get there, you can take your car or you can go there and take either ATV or Motorbike to tour the island. We had took our rented car since we had bags and baby stuffs. There are many photo spots, beaches , light house etc., across the circumference of the island. A must go place if visited jeju.

Rent a bike (costs about 10,000 KRW / 10 USD for 3 hours) to go around the island. It took me only 2.5 hours to go around with quick rest at one of the coffee shops (about 20 minutes). Take your time and enjoy your ride on Udo!

I simply love this place! It's so peaceful and so beautiful. When you arrive the island, u are spoilt for choices in getting around the island. U can travel via car, atv, bike, bicycle or tour buses. I will suggest bicycle. It is really very threaupitic to cycle the whole island which is about 16km. You definitely need more than 4 hours so go as early as you can. The beaches are so beautiful. Water is crystal clear. There arent much shower areas near the beach tho so do think twice if u wana swim at the the beach. Do check out the lighthouse at the top of the mountain too. Udo is famous for their peanut icecream. If you are a fan of peanuts, do go try it.

Taking ferry to the island with a car is a little bit pricy, so it's better to get and ATV and go around the island. One hour or two chill hours are enough to go around the whole island.Hey!If you are searching for something cheap but decent, then I would recommend hostel called Galaxy in Seogwipo. I was planning to stay there for one night, as I thought it's yet just another cheap hostel, but ended up staying there for 2 nights. There are some beautiful beaches and food places, so you might want to take it easy..If you want some more information on what you can find on the island, you can check out this video: http://youtu.be/X2RwSnOMgYk?list=UUYEqXBrHobdnJF591_o-vcg

We visited here in the fall during the annual Peanut Festival...yes, peanuts are grown on this island off the east coast of Jeju Island.  Autumn was a good time to visit there because it was cooler and not so crowded.  Our pension owner, Mr. Lee, picked us up at the ferry and drove us to our accommodation, right across the coast road from the famous white coral beach, the only one of its kind in Korea.  The coral beach was beautiful but much smaller than I'd expected and impossible to walk on without closed shoes.  The pension, called The Log House, is not only close to the beach, it is close to a cluster of restaurants and coffeeshops.  It is possible to do a lot of hiking and go up to the lighthouse for a 360 view and to catch the first glimpse of sunrise...which can be spectacular.  Because it was during the Peanut Festival, we could sample peanut wine and other local products, including several types of peanut icecream. We had a great room at the pension, on the corner with great views of the fishing boats and the famous Sunrise Peak crater across the channel.  The pension owner, Mr. Lee, spoke enough English to take care of all our needs.  At other pensions, little to no English is spoken by the staff/owners.  The owner also drove us to the ferry the next day.  Although bikes and ATVs are available for rent, the roads are a bit curvy and narrow for my comfort level.  If you like adventure, go for it!  Be sure to bring your international drivers license.  Enjoy!

We took the ferry from jeju to udo as it was a must see... we went there off season, it might be the reason why we were not impressed by anything on the island, and disappointed for the beaches. must be tried during the tourism season otherwise you will face many closed activities

If you are ever in Jeju-do, you have to make a day trip to Udo...
