Udo means "Cow Island" - so named because the shape of the island looks like a cow lying down... but try as I might, the island on a map doesn't look like a cow to me, but I guess the ancients who named it looked at things differently from me...  :PYou can drive your Jeju rental car onto the Udo ferry for a fuss free 15min journey over to this lovely island. Once there, you can tour the island by car! There are many beaches you can choose to hangout at, my favourite is Hagosudong beach for it's crystal clear waters and fine white sand. however Koreans aren't really into bikini culture, the Korean women go to the beach in long sleeved t-shirts, hats and umbrellas... So if you wanna sunbathe, you have all that white sand to choose your fav. spot! there are many cafes on Udo for you to grab a burger or sandwich for lunch if you are into western fare and also many restaurants that serve seafood Korean style. The seafood comes from the "Hae-nyo" sea-women who dives around Udo to haul in fresh Abalone, sea-urchin, octopus and the like for our enjoyment. As you tour around the island, you will be able to see these sea-women in action in various parts of the sea. My family and I love the relaxed vibe of this little island. In Udo, you can also take a speedboat tour of the natural caverns dotting the cliffs and coasts. the speedboat drives all the way into these caverns for you to observe up close the cave formations. This is my second visit to Udo and I recommend it to any nature loving, beach going traveller.... :)

Our kids (7&10) enjoyed the rock climbing, surf and sand...not to mention the modestly price ferry ride.  We attempted to rent a motorized vehicle but there were no rentals for four people...maximum people limit per vehicle was two and one of us did not have a driver's license...so we took the modestly priced bus trip.  Note that a home-country drivers license will not work.  once we figured out the system (no English speakers found on the island of Jeju.), it worked to see most of the island.  The peanut ice cream was all variations of soft-serve...low quality ice cream.  There were enough snack shops for coffee or short orders.  Okay for a day trip.
very nice island. one can spent 2-3 days while roaming around the island. a very beautiful place with lot of good natural views of mountains.
Actually this cozy small island is what jeju island is about. Most of jeju island is increasingly urbanized but udo maintains its small town fishing charm.  Best place to eat seafood.

You won't wanna miss the awesome peanut ice cream.  The beaches was clean and beautiful.Too bad we have to leave with ferry by 12noon, otherwise I believe I can enjoyed more.However, I was lucky to have at least 2hours tour in Udo Island.  Because I was told by the tour guide, last week she lead a tour to Udo Island within 45mins due to bad weather they have to hurry and leave on time, otherwise you have to overnight over the island.

We didn't get to spend as much time on Udo as we would have liked. I would have liked to so the Olle Trail but there wasn't enough time.  We had walked up a steep hill thinking we could get to the lighthouse but you go at it from the other side.  If you don't want to walk rent a motorcycle.  Don't forget your driver's license.  I hear the lighthouse is wonderful and we will go back.  Lots of cute little places to eat or have coffee and there's a nice beach. There's not really a fee to get on the island but you have to take a ferry and there's a fee for that.

Udo island is perfect for short day trip where you can enjoy the peaceful ambiance of the ocean while aboard a ferry.It may seem so plain and simple but for me it is perfect for a qucik romantic get away with a breeze of fresh air..It feels like the ocean is all yours...

Small island off the Jeju coast makes for a nice day trip/excursion from the main Jeju island. We enjoyed the climb up the one and only peak for excellent views, as well as some stunning coastal caves and cliffs, lighthouse, crashing surf, and volcanic rock. At first blush it may not seem too nice but Udo kind of grows on you. I'd recommend renting a moped or bicycle and bopping around the backroads; that would be the best way to see and enjoy Udo.

We took the ferry to Udo Island. We went as walk ons with our tour guide. The ferry ride was short and easy. We were happy we had our guide with us because the weather was not very good that day and they were closing down the ferry service due to rough seas. We were glad she could translate this information for us.  We went over for a short visit and took the last ferry back to Jeju which was around noon. Because of the ferry schedule we did not have much time on Udo. We did go to 2 lookout spots. They were very pretty but the weather interfered. It would be a nice place on a sunny day, but there doesn't seem to be much to do on the island so plan on relaxing.

A great place to enjoy beautiful scenery, fresh air, the sun and the beaches. The island tour bus service is very convenient (only need to pay once) and runs on round trips whole day long, bringing you to 4 different scenic spots if you do not want to rent the bicycles, ATV or scooters. There is also a nice restaurant named Rodem Garden which offers spicy squids on hot plate and can add on with hallabong fried rice after you almost finish the squids.

It's a small island on the east of Jeju. It can be reached by taking ~10mins ferry from pier near Seongsan Ilchubong. The coastal landscape of the island is wonderful. It's definite worth a half day tour there. The most important thing is that you can see Seongsan Ilchubong from the outside as you take the ferry.

It was nice to visit Udo in the spring time. The rape flower fields were out of my imagination, and there was also a nice view on the Udo peak, where you can clearly see the Seongsan Sunrise peak on the other side of the sea.

Took a 15min ferry to Udo and a tour bus that you could get on and off from at the sights, visited the Udo Peak, The black sand beach where we ate fresh abalone and the pristine coral sand beach...extremely clear water and so beautiful!!

Getting the short ferry over to Udo is a treat and when you arrive on this small island you are made very welcome. Plenty eating places and nice walks around the island. A bus can take you around or there are bikes etc to hire.

Do it with your partner, not with your mates, not with your friends and not with a group. This is a tiny island and the ideal thing to do is to rent a bicycle and just glide around the island for a few hours. It is mostly just farms and a couple nice views, but it does make you feel like that scene in wedding crashers if you do it right. Half day is all you need, the ferries are fairly punctual but check to make sure as you would not want to get stranded. Not the number 2 thing to do in Jeju by any means, but it is pleasant.

i have visited the Seongsan in Udo. I think Seongsan is a must go place because it has average difficultiy to climb up (108m). It's named as one of the new 7 wonder natural places. reasonable entrance fee applied.

This was a nice little excursion from the main island. Gotta take a ferry which means you need to head over to Udo early and be prepared to come back in the early evening as the ferry schedule will dictate your movement. There used to be a nice coffee shop halfway up at the base of the stairs to the lighthouse exhibits (October 2013). They had the cutest dog too but they were closed when we went back in December 2013. We took our car on the ferry. But you can also walk onto the ferry and then rent mopeds or four wheelers once you get to Udo so you can get around. I was thankful for the GPS in the car though because the roads are very winding, narrow, confusing, and I don't think are marked with names.

Friends, my husband and I rented ATV's, Scooters and a Golf Cart to check out this island. It was so much fun touring around and stopping at the beaches and different view points. We even saw the diving ladies who dive by only holding their breath! This wasn't the most spectacular views of Jeju we saw but the adventure was a lot of fun!

Udo feels like more of an island than Jeju itself, because it is much smaller and rural. You can hire a car, golf buggy, cycle or simply walk around this scenic little island. Very short and cheap ferry ride from Seongsan, so add this into your trip to Sunrise Peak.
Not much to do, but if you rent a vehicle, its certainly worth a couple of hours to see what it has to offer. Even if just to see how the locals live.

Parked our car at Seongsan Ferry Terminal and the ticket booth for Udo is in the building on the left. We rented ATVs from the shop just in front of the terminal. Though it was pricier as compared to what other reviewers had paid for, it was very convenient for us to return vehicles just before we board the ferryThe island is beautiful :) contrary to what some reviewers believe,  there is a path up to the lighthouse. It is by the side of a road near the area with many food storesTwo hours is enough to explore the whole island, but I would highly recommend 3 - 4 hours to leisurely and fully enjoy what the island has to offer

There isn't much on this island, and with a scooter, you can travel round the island on a leisurely pace in 2 hours. If you are there to relax and enjoy the beaches, then you would love it. But going there in autumn when it is cold, there isn't very much but just to bike around, get something to eat, and take some pictures.

We visited udo island around August right after we visited the sonsang ilchulbong peak. Ferry cost around 4K per person, and 25K if you bring car. So far, we found one beach in Udo that we consider as  the best place to swim because of the wave is quite big.. compared to the one in main island.We failed to reach the lighthouse because the GPS can't properly shown the location.When swimming, they provide quite clean-public shower facilities, but prepare your own toiletries .

Nothing much really. The walk up the lighthouse was nice in terms of view but disappointing as you can't reach the lighthouse as shown in the brochure. You can find equally nice beaches in Jeju-do, so don't waste time and money to go Udo.

Udo was easy to get to and a great place to camp with full amenities. There are 2 main beaches; one on the West side and one on the North East side. Both are beautiful but the one that has sand made of seashells (West Side) is a little hard on your bare feet  and it was much busier there. The other has soft fine sand that makes for a great camping spot. There are no taxis on the island. In hindsight, we would have taken the other ferry to the port that was a bit closer to Hagosudong Beach (the NE side), but there is this drop on and off Bus Tour System that costs 5000won/person. You can get on from the ferry, drop off and set up your camp at the beach, then hop back on. It runs frequently but only stops at 4 main sightseeing spots (beach 1, beach 2, caves and ___ ) . We were able to use the bus for the two days we were there for on the same fare, but there are times/stops that are crazy busy. We watched at least 6 packed buses go by before we decided to stay the night. Honorable food mention: Pirate Caf챕. Really interesting place and staff. Great BiBamBap and you get to sign a plaque and hang it from their wall when you re done eating.Friendly people, campfire and camping friendly, personal beer cooler (at the convenience stores directly behind the beach), and lots of cats.

2 things you must take with you for visiting Udo island - swimming suit and international driving licence. In case you want to rent ATV or scooter you should have international driving license, otherwise you will have to enjoy beauty of the island riding  bicycle. There are 2 sandy beaches available. Ferry can bring your car straight to the island.

This was our second trip to Udo.   We were riding around Jeju Island by bicycle so decided to explore the island on foot.   The weather was very hot and exposed (Summer), so you really need a big hat.    The island is quite unique, we walked up through the middle of the island and enjoyed the barren landscape.   We came across a Buddhist temple and met the lone monk there who chatted and gave us cups of coffee and tea.  He also introduced us to his friends - a haenyeo and visiting Butoh dancer who we interviewed for our website.   We briefly visited the beaches which were nice but crowded.  The unique landscape and interesting people was the best thing about Udo.

Udo was the best place in my jeju visit. although the weather was very hot, but its windy too. My hat even blow off by the wind. The sea and sand were just too beautiful. its really a relaxing place when seeing the green grasses dancing all over in front of you. Besides, the zha jiang mian was really tasted good. it costed 8000won. the peanut icecream was famous too, 3000won. We sent a whole morning there. In the island, we can take bus, rent bicycle or scooter.

Udo was the best part of my Jeju visit. My sister and I rented scooters for two hours to get around the island, stopping wherever we wanted to take pictures or rehydrate (it was blazingly hot). We stopped at one of the beaches for a couple of hours, but it was just too hot to sit still on the sand. Rented scooters for the rest of the day and just zoomed around the island. True, there isn't too much to do on the island besides going to the beach or riding around the island. And the scooters/ATVs available for rent are a bit expensive (15,000won for 2 hours). But if you're looking for a relaxing day with beautiful sights, I highly recommend a visit.

The coral sand beach was really nice! Not much to see or do beyond that, and another two beaches - one very crowded white sand beach, and another black sand beach that nobody seemed to care about other than for a walk. The reviews make it seem like it's some kind of paradise, we just found it crowded, full of concrete and terrain that is parted for construction, not much vegetation. There are a few lighthouses and it looks like people could venture out on the rocks by the beach if they felt like it. What saved our trip was a little place called Chocolate Castle by the Sea, a burger restaurant that had amazing burgers and a great homey feel inside. We biked the whole island in 3 hours, with stops.

Likes: some great views, fresh sea food (abalone, snails etc)Dislikes: scorchingly hot and humid in summer, lots and lots of visitors, commentaries on the bus are all in Korean so you need to figure out on your own what the driver says or just follow the crowd.

We rented a 125cc scooter for 2 at the Udo ferry terminal for KRW 25,000 that got us to cover the entire island within 2 hours. Having the scooter allowed us to take in the sights and attractions with ease as the shuttle bus was packed with more people waiting at every bus stop we had passed by.

Black rock, golden sand, turquoise waters, green fields. Such a colourful island, easy to cycle around. The contrast of the simple life of haenyo and farmers with those vacationing was also felt strongly.

the way to this island is like my favorite of all the places in jeju... we took a 10 mints ferry from jeju city and the water was so beautiful and amazing... the ferry ride was also awesome. it was my first time on a ferry. we didnt stay on the island much but we rented a boat and saw around.. it was cool. we had a cool boat driver too.. we didnt have enough cash so he let us do it with half price. people in korea are too nice sometimes. if u have a licency you shld do ATV's too
It was a good place to bring the girlfriend and rent a scooter for a 2 hour, romantic, oceanside drive.

Took a bus from Jeju bus terminal (1.5hrs) and arrived at the port. Ferry to Udo island is just 15 mins away. Arrived at Udo, we join the hop on & off bus that takes us to 4 destinations. Bus interval is every 30 mins. It is a beautiful island not to be misssed out. Spent at least half a day or more at the island.

If you love the sea, sand, mountain and great scenery, you will need to make a day trip to Udo!  You can take a ferry to Udo from Seongsan Harbour.  I highly recommend that you rent a car in Jeju and drive that over to Udo as there are so much to see and do in a single day.  You can drive your car up onto the ferry to Udo.

Udo island is indeed beautiful. It is definitely worth it to visit this island.My friends and i were pressed for time, so we decided to board the udo island tour bus (–5000). If you have time to spare, you might want to hike around the olle trail. It takes about 10-15 minutes to reach Udo Island from Seongsan port. A return ticket will cost you –3500.

Even in March, Udo is beautiful--and in March, there are few visitors. When we were there, haenyo were out at low tide collecting seafood among the lava rocks, banging the rocks to bring them out. We stayed at a traditional hotel (thin mattresses on heated floor) near the lighthouse on the main road. Eat al fresco at the nearby restaurant across from the healing-stone throne is and check out their fresh "ginseng of the sea" (slices of a raw sea-cucumber-like animal). On the mainland, be sure to check out tiny Gangjeong Village, on the southern coast just west of Seogwipo, where villagers and Jeju priests are braving police, the navy, Hyundai, and Samsung 24/7 as they protest a huge naval base being foisted upon them. The mayor was jailed a few days ago for chaining himself around the neck to a rafter, when police rampaged and tore down protesters' headquarters, replacing it with boulders to prevent reconstruction. The protesters are very friendly, by the way. It's on the Ollie hiking trail, where it crosses over the Gangjeong River and passes the gates of the "destruction" site. A beautiful waterfall meets the sea and can be viewed by taking a path on either side of the bridge. Poonglim Resort is nearby, with full spa and small steam bath facilities.

Rent a bicycle or ATV to enjoy the scenery here. In spring rape flowers are all over the island. The cliff by the sea are amazingly nice. Good place to go with your love ones if two of you want a short getaway by yourselves.

Very nice island. You take a ferry from Jeju Island to Udo in 5-10 minutes you get there. I rented a quadricycle and it was fun to discover the island by this transportation mode. The ocean is clean and warm; pretty nice to bathe!The shops however don't speak English normally. If in Jeju, I totally recommend Udo as a spot to visit.

Rented the ATV for 3hrs40m for 45, 000won and that was the most fun we had on our trip so far. The island is small so we ventured the coastline stopping to see the beautiful clear waters,  rode on horses and took photos by a quaint lttle lighthouse. The peanut ice cream was a little disappointing as it was more icey and the paeanut taste was barely there. The people in Udo are really warm and helpful.

This was recommended by a friend and it ended up being the highlight of our trip in Jeju! We rented an ATV and just drove around the island taking in the sights. Udo Island is also where the famous women divers go to catch abalone, octopi and other seafood and it was cool just to watch them work. The shore caves were definitely a must-see for us and they did not disappoint. I would definitely go back to Udo if I'm ever in Jeju again.

We rent a bicycle and just cycling along the sea coast. It's very windy and we even spotted the hanyeo picking up the seaweed! If you visit the island at the right timing. U can see lots of canola flower! We saw partial here and there still very pretty. If you are being lazy, you can just rent the ATV bike (which most of the people do so). If you plan to have lunch there. Give yourself 4-5 hours to explore this island (take photo, had an ice cream etc etc). Note: we didn't walk all the way up to light house as it is already mid noon and we can see something similar @ seopjikoji so we let go this one :)

Udo Island is a small island located in the east side of Jeju. We visited there due the great reviews given below in TripAdvisor. It cost about 5,500 won for the ferry ride to and fro. My friend and I wanted to ride the ATV while we were there however the rental shops were strict on the rental without international driving license so in the end we took a tour bus that stops at 4 different locations and cost 5,000won per person. The bus comes at an interval of 30 minutes so once you get down in one location, you can stay at the location for 30 minutes before moving on to another place. As we went there in Spring, the canola flowers are blooming beautifully. We also went to the Black Sand Beach and also the Hyopje Beach. Quite a good worth of money if you are looking at short tours around the island.

Beautiful small island - green hills, lava rocks and small beaches. It's about one hour and a half by bus from Jeju-city to Seongsan ferry terminal (final stop) and 10 minutes by ferry.  We rented ATV to get around the island. The weather changed quickly and suddenly we found ourselves in the middle of the storm. We had a lot of fun riding ATVs through the heavy rain and felt like we are true rangers.  It was too cold to go swimming and by such a weather we couldn't explore the shore caves. So we skip it for the next time.

Do not go to Jeju without checking out Udo. A beautiful island off the coast, you can walk the Olle trail here, or rent bikes to cover more miles! Beautiful in spring or fall. Definitely check it out!

There are several beautiful beaches on Udo, but we preferred the"popcorn"beach above the others. Cristal clear water and white popcorn like beach sand. you can rent snorkel gear from the cafes near the beach. We went there after watching the sunrise from sunrise peak. Ferry was W35000 for a return including our car. Do take your own snacks and drinks.

Udo is just picture perfect. We spent a few hours driving around this beautiful small island in early October. It only takes a few minutes on the ferry to go to Udo. You can hire scooters on the island but we actually brought over the scooters that we had hired in Jeju. It was approx 8000 (i think) to bring the scooter over and back. It was extremely busy when I was there but I did travel during Chuseok so I am not sure how busy it would be outside of holidays.I would definitely recommend a trip here as there are some fantastic and beautiful views. Just hire a scooter and drive around. As i mentioned earlier, if you are planning to hire a scooter on Jeju itself then do so and bring it over and it will be cheaper than renting one in Udo.

This island is not in your usual tourist-package because you really need 1 day to cover the whole quaint island. But it is worth it. The whole place had lots of walls made up of volcanic rocks, making it look almost Irish. And the scenery around the island is just quite breath-taking. We drove and put the car in the ferry as well. Only complaint is that instructions were all in Korean at the ticket office, so hard to figure out what to do. Also, what would happen if one misses the last ferry back to the main island???

Udo is simply beautiful. You should rent either a bike or a moped once you arrive. You can easily circle the whole island with stops in a couple hours. The enclosed beaches, volcanic rocks, crystal clear water, and very green landscape is exquisite.The road is not really crowded even during the busy summer months. I really enjoyed Udo Island, but then again what major natural location in Jeju-do disappoints? Whether you visit the lava tube caves, craters, dramatic coastline, waterfalls, nearby islands, beaches, mountains, and forests, Jeju-do is a natural paradise.

This review was told to me by my awesome afternoon English class student.  I love Korea; especially because I have great students."It is very beautiful island. Next time I will go to U-do Island with Diisha.You should visit the ocean.  There are many nice beaches.  I didn't like the lighthouse because it was scary.  I liked the lunch. The noodles were delicious/very good. The smell was good. You can see everything in one day.  I was there for four hours.  (Monica/Sing hae).

The first impression and experience was good. After a while, everything else looked the same. The same sea, mountains and stones, albeit in a different formation. There are beach bikes for rent, which I think will be fun but we didn't enjoy that because we had hired a taxi for the Jeju trip.

This could be an amazing place to visit provided you have good weather and great friends. Scootering around the tiny island can be fun if you stop off at the beaches, swim along the way and explore the caves and tunnels by the black sand beach. Definitely keep an eye out for the giant burger restaurant and the peanut Makgeolli stand (留嫄몃━, it's alcoholic rice wine!), both are delicious! Don't over-hype it or expect too much, just go to have fun and you'll be happy you went.

We got an ATV (40000KRW for 2 hours) and rode around the island. It was really fun and you get to explore the whole island. There are small little cafes where you can just park your ATV and pop in for a coffee and a cake. The water is amazingly clear and blue.

The best way to experience nature and the beauty of Udo Island is not necessarily by being seperated by metal and a loud motor, but it sure is fun!  One of our best days while on vacation was riding the ferry to Udo and renting ATV's to tour around the island.
beautiful place, wish i could spend more time there, great memories

Most people visit Jeju-do for the scenery, but I feel that the best scenery was not their waterfalls, but Udo itself. This island is stunningly beautiful, and when the weather is sunny, you can fully enjoy what it has to offer. The island isn't too big, and can be explored fully and quickly via scooter or ATV. I rented the ATV for 2 hours for 25000 won, and it's totally worth it. A driving license is required for some stores, but if you don't have one, you can find other stores that may be more lax with the regulations... I do not recommend it personally for safety reasons, but if you really did so (just like me), ride within your own abilities and comfort level and do not speed! Most of the driving is done on tarmac, so it is relatively safe. Along the way you can always park your ATV and stop and take some photos! I would recommend spending some time at the beach, the water is really clear and the sands are clean! There is also this coast where crashing waves will hit and splash all over you if you get close enough, quite an interesting experience too. Over there you can also enjoy some of the local seafood caught freshly. There is also horse-riding available , which can be found somewhere off the Udo port.If possible, spend at least half a day there! The Seongsan ferry terminal is about a 20 minute walk from the famous Seongsan Ilchubong, so it's recommended to go Udo after you scaled the peak in the morning and have some time to spare in the afternoon.

There is a bus from Jeju bus terminal that takes 1hours and a half min and you have to take a Ferry that costs 5,500won.If you dont know how to plan one day travel I would like to recommend you to go Udo and  Seongsan Ilchulbong that is closer to each other If you start your day early you will probably have more time thoughTo see all island it takes 3~4hours by bus that there is Tour bus which costs 5,000wonHowever i would like to recommend you to ride a bike for some partIt is beautiful to ride around the sea and you can feel relaxed.There is 3 beaches that you can visit and those are all different atmosphereespecially there is Coral beach that are exists only 3palce on the world Please go towards the end where people are not crowdedYou will see more pretty coralUdo is famouse for peanut that if you like plz try only small amount since it is a bit expensiveI am not sure if there is famouse food for foreginer but street food is okay As my memory Udo is one of the best part in Jeju island I will recommend for my friends

This small island with a unique history and is classified as a national recreation area.  It  is accessbile by a low cost ferry from  Seongsan which includes the entrance fee to the area.  Bus tours and ATV rentals are available.  The island has many small farms and peanuts are a major crop.

You need to take a ferry from the terminal near the sunrise peak and I had to queue for nearly 15 minutes to get the ferry tickets. Follow the direction sign to board the ferry. We waited at the wrong place but were fortunate to have a korean informed of the correct location. The ferry took 20 minutes to reach the islet.The islet was small but not small enough to travel on foot. There are several transport options to see go round the islet - shuttle bus, ATV, motorbikes or bicycles. We chose the shuttle bus. There are several locations which it brought us to. The driver would explain more about the attractions but in korean language. At each location, visitors can alight the bus and visit the attractions. Once you are done, you have to find the bus boarding point (strangely at some distance from the alighting point). The bus you board would be different from the one you alighted from.It was really crowded on Udo Islet. The attractions are just some natural geological formation, similar those on the Jeju island. They were scenic but got a little boring after some time.

Most of Udo island except the attractions are rural farms. We went to Udo island with a few local Koreans from jeju island. We took a 15mins ferry. I was surprised that there are no seats on the ferry, people sit on the floor instead, korean style. Interesting experience. As I went with locals, I thought they would know the way. No! They didn't and we walked 1h around the island before reaching the peak. It was beautiful. The grass was green n the sea view was nice. Though it was really windy. And thus very cold even though it was summer. Be sure to wear enough clothes.

Went there twice. Once on a rainy day and on a sunny day. Do not go on rainy days! We went on the bus tour which told us that English tour will be provided but the guide spoke korean throughout instead. Bus tour took us to a few attractions which were pretty scenic and impressive. However, the wind was too strong and it was freaking cold. Always have a poncho/raincoat prepared in case of rain! Went on a sunny day the next day and rented the ATV for 15,000 won for an hour. Managed to explore and rode the ATV round half of the island. Fantastic experience, would definitely recommend it and do it again! Also, try the peanut ice cream!

A quick 20 min ferry ride from Jeju.  We went there on a rainy day, however so did not get the whole experience of Udo.  It looked to be a beautiful and very serene island.  Seafood is good here.  Homemade peanut ice cream was also very good here.A great option for a day trip.

Ferry ride from seongsan port was 11,000 W for 2 people and only took about 15 minutes.  There's a really good review by katja below, so I won't go in depth.  If you don't have a lot of time, take a scooter or ATV.  We had a lot of fun cruising around this island on ATV!!   As soon as you get off the ferry there are two places to rent from - ATV was 20,000 W for 2 hours; Scooter was 10,000 W for 2 hours.  If you stop several places you'll be pushing 2 hours but can definitely get it done.  Can be a little difficult navigating if you cannot speak or read Korean.
Great beach, with nice views of Sunrise Point.  Bit of a jaunt to get out there on the ferry, and cold during the winter, but worth it.

Udo is a really small island, you can go around by bicycle in several hours. Udo is a volcanic island, so it has several nice beaches with white and black sand, impressing lava rock formations, caves etc. We went there several times, every time for 2-3 days, and every time it was just wonderful. You should go and spend a few days there if you want to relax in a quite and peaceful atmosphere with no nightlife, co crowds, no big attractions but with beautiful nature. Still, if you want to get in touch with the rest of the world - no problem here, our Korean mobiles were working fine, Internet was available right in the "arrival hall" of the port and in many "minbaks" (small Korean-style hotels).You can get there easily from Seongsan port  (＿깆–고) of Jeju island by ferry in just 10-15 minutes. Ferries depart every hour from 08.00 till 17.30 or 18.00 depending on season. Most accommodations are found on on the White Coral Beach (Seo-bin-baek-sa, ＿鍮諛깆– or  Sanhosa, –고몄– ), 10 minutes walk from the port. They are all small 1-2 floor buildings located directly on the beach with seaview (Pensions, Minbaks). We never booked anything in advance, but found a room on site, but we went in May and October - not highest season. The rooms were always nice and big, also with kitchen and all the necessary kitchenware. Also there are small shops with snacks and some Korean restaurants.So, what to do in there?- swim in the pure emerald water of White coral beach, see the special kind of sand, it really feels like you are in tropics ^^- rent a bike and go around the islandThe road goes nicely along the shore, there were almost no cars except on the busier Jeju-facing side, and we enjoyed the scenery very much!  - Geommeolle Beach (寃 硫 )This is a black sand beach with very beautiful and unusual rock formations and caves, and we spent a very good time there. You can go in caves and see small rocks piled up on each other. And once a year they have a symphony concert in the caves!!Also, if you are a diver with a certificate, there is a diver center there. We tried to do it, but we did not have a PADI certificate so they refused, they do not do fun dives.And  we took a motor boat (10 000W/person) to see farther caves with a spectacular view of Udo cliffs (Hu-hae-seok-byeok, ＿댁＿踰). If you are lucky, you can also see a peculiar site called Ju-gan-myeong-weol - sun reflecting at the ceiling of a cave giving a "moon shape". We also went up the hill, nice view of both Udo and Jeju!!What problems you can encounter in Udo?- languageLocal people are friendly and try to help, but they do not understand English!!So if you do not speak Korean, print out Korean names of what you want to visit and some basic Korean phrases (preferably in Korean, not transcriptions, because pronunciation may be tricky). BUT! the owner of the LOG-house speaks English very good!- foodThere is no Western restaurants on the island, only Korean!! The shops on the beach only sell snacks like Ramen, but there is a bigger mart inland called Hana-ro Mart with fruits, vegetables, milk, etc. (–濡 留, try to ask locals for directions and go there by bike, you will find it, there is no place to get lost ^^). And it could be a good idea to bring some food with you from Jeju, especially if you want something like cheese, wine etc.

It was very nice taking a walk along the beach of Udo, the sea is clean but unable to swim because of sharp rocks. We are happy that they keep this place just the same as it is, not making it into a tourism spot. And once again,  most of them cannot speak English, we couldn t say any word to the locals and the tour guide was helpful all the way through.
Udo is small and very beautiful island. You can take the ferry from Seongsan for around 15mins. There are many buses on the island to take you for sightseeing.

Breathtaking!  Seongsan Ilchulbong is one of Jeju's Crown & Jewel destinations.  This beautiful natural wonder provides awesome 360 degrees views, fresh air and an escape for all the current issues impacting the World.  The hike up there is a lil' bit strenuous, but the result waiting for us at the top is pretty rewarding. If you visit Jeju this trip is a most...enjoy!

We went there directly from the airport via bus (because it was too early for us to check in at our booked hotel).  At the place, the lockers were not available, unfortunately, and we cannot leave our bags somewhere. So we had to carry our things up to see the Seongsan Ilchulbong. We did not attempt to climb up to the peak due to our heavy bags. Instead, we opted to see the observatory at the side of the mountain (it was free... the side going to the peak has an entrance fee) and has a nice view of the sea and the mountain. Can even go down to the sea shore if you like (we didn't). The view from the observatory was breathtaking vast ocean, blue sky and cool green mountain. Will definitely go back someday to see the peak! Also, we tried the Hallabong softcone (ice cream) just near the entrance road to the place, and it was so delicious!!

This place is just a little hike for most. It does have about 300 steps up, but they are set up for a nice pace. Great views up and down, but not much to the crater itself. During morning this place can be very crowded. Visiting later in the day allows you to experience everything more quickly with less crowds. Lots of places to eat in the nearby area. Recommend you dedicate 40-60min for your visit.
If you are a nature lover, you should definitely go to this place. Scenic beauty and fresh air can get. Amazing and incredible place. Worth it to visit.
An absolute must while in Jeju. The walk up is stimulating rather than stressful and the morning views are wonderful. 5,000 won well spent.
The view from the top where well worth climbing to the top but it is a lot of steps up and down and they are step.

Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak is the most eastern part of Jeju Island and has the same terrain as Punchball. When you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, you can see the beautiful sea and clear sky endlessly, and when you stand at Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with a cool breeze, you feel good. Also, there are many tourist attractions nearby, so it is convenient to move around. In addition, there are many restaurants that cook braised kingtail fish and roast caught in Jeju, and there are many unique and delicious restaurants around. I recommend that you visit Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak with your family at least once.
The great place to hangout..i like the view.. have many shop,cafe to chill outAnd if you lucky you can see the women looking for a seafood , also can enjoy the fresh seafood

It was early afternoon & very sunny, & super hot during our visit. Coupled with the long walk & return climb up from the bottom, it was terrible in the heat.Perhaps if we had come in early morning or in spring climate, would probably have enjoyed it better.The Jeju Women Divers Performance was a disappointment. With due respect to this fantastic women, the show was too commercialised.Have read much about these tenacious women & was looking forward to something better than this.However, our guide arranged for us earlier to meet up with these women not far away in another area.Most are in their 70s & had been doing this job almost their whole lives. They are so fit even at this age.Certainly respect them.There are paid boat rides as well round the area & horse riding too.

Best for sunrise. There are well-built boardwalks up to the peak of the extinct volcano. Overran by nature but the shape of the crater is still visible. The view of Jeju from the peak of the mountain is amazing, never fails to disappoint.

I visited Seongsan Illchulbong at 7:30. It was sunrise time and it was my first time to see sun rising from such a height. The effect of sun rays on the ocean made everything so beautiful. I can guarantee one thing that it is much beautiful if you see in person than seeing in pictures.

It is most satisfactory to complete our climb to the top to experience the cold air, sea breeze and overlooking at the mountains and sea below you.  The feeling is so good and the view is just simply awesome!  It's a great place not to be missed!

The queue was long starting from midnight. The tag was given starting 2:30am. The limit was for 1300 first come first served. The waiting was in 2 celcius temperature. The trek up started at 5:30am in an orderly manner in a hushed procession like atmosphere. At the top of the plateau there were decks facing the direction of the sunrise. All was ready for the first sunrise of 2020. Unfortunately it did not happen. The clouds was too thick and we headed back an hour after the sunrise time. Was I disappointed? Not really. The whole experience was exhilarating, the wait, the trek, the anticipation of the sunrise. It was a memorable experience which I hope to repeat one day.
Worth the climb up to the top with awesome views and unexpected greenery environment on the former volcano.

It was a cold, sunny, windy day, visiting this mountain. Make sure you wear enough layers!  Admission was 2,000won if you wanted to go all the way up to the crater, or free for just the lower level.  Be prepared to climb many steps to get to the top, and see crater.  On average, take 30-40 mins return to do this.  Otherwise, the view is nice from all levels...definitely worth checking!

I had no idea that there were going to be stiff hills/stairs to go top of the place. I was expecting kinda easy, but it was bit harder than I expected. Going to the top was a little tiring, but the view you get to see is magnificent. Make sure to have a bottle of water on the way! About 20-25 min of walking, and less than 20 to go back down. Would go again!

This place has a magnificient view of sunset and it is definitely an instaworthy place for those who love nature. We took our time to climb uphill, stopping at various points to snap photos. Although we didnt go up to the peak, the view where we were was astounding. I will go here again if I ever go to Jeju. Lovely!

We need to rent a car (邕竊to get there. The driver said walking up there requiring 30 min, yet is quite easy to arrive the top. After reaching the top, you could enjoy the sunset of the seongsan city which is worth it !
Great New Year's Eve. There was a huge crowd of families there, entertainment, bonfire and a fantastic firework display. Very well organised  loved every minute.

We went there because closest hotel, we driving to there and saw that is not to much visitor maybe was late evening, we try to going up, however in the middle of the path have 1 counter ask us to buy a ticket, we only want to walk around so we haven't paid and plan to leave, but we saw some of people can go up on the other way, actually is the same road but one for entrance and one for exit, you can go inside in the exit way but only have limited area you can visit. if you want to go up, you must need to paid

It is a truly magnificent sight to see this natural phenomenon of this Unesco Heritage Site. It's a short climb up with well maintained steps and the view from the peak is superb. We didn't make it for the sunrise as we stayed in Jeju City which is 1.5 hours away by local bus. However, the sunset is stunning. I went in December so the wind can be very chilly in the evening. Definitely worth the climb!

Went during the winter season (end Dec), the cold isn't unbearable but the wind is! The climb may not be the easiest but it's doable. Plus you see many tourists and elderlies climbing it together with you, so it isn't that bad of a hike up. When you're up, the view is to shout for. Awesome view!

A popular tourist stop on Jeju Island. A lot of uphill walking is required and would be a problem for elderly folks or those with bad knees. However this is a really lovely location for scenic photos. The old ladies who dive for octupus and shellfish is a must visit as well though be aware of the very steep stairs up and downwards.

Breathtaking view of Jeju at the Peak of Seongsang iichulbong. Is cooling while walking up the Peak during winter. But no regret and is worth to go up the Peak and see the huge crater. Is not difficult to walk up, there is properly staircase and path. Young children and elderly also can walk up. There are CCTV at some of the pitstop.
Seongsan ilchulbong is a place must visit when travel to jeju. The scenery is superb and can enjoy the women diver show as well.
Truly Amazing view of the sunset. The climb up is not for the unfit but once up there I betcha your first word will be WOW.
Simply amazing. From the moment you start the climb up till you reach the submit the views wqs just out of this world. Once on top it is just wow all the way. A must do.

We went on the first Monday of the month, and the mountaineering trail was closed, so do take note when planning. However, the first portion of the trail was still available for free, which was still amazing and less of an exercise. The view from all spots were breathtaking, making this spot a must-see when you re in Jeju.Do catch the woman s diver show at 1.30pm and 3pm, located down the trail. It was an interesting experience to see the elderly women dive down to retrieve the seafood in the ocean, and you can buy and eat some of their fresh catches at the shop nearby.Highly recommend for a magnificent sightseeing experience in Jeju!
To hike up about 300m altitude in 20 mins with 2 kids who are faster than you, it's an achievement. the view of beautiful!

Certainly a must-visit destination in Jeju! Soak yourself in the impressive view of this UNESCO heritage site. We came on the first Monday of the month, and unfortunately the paid trail to the peak is closed. Blessing in disguise is that portion of the trail is open free to the public though it only brings us to mid-way - perfect for those who find it too challenging to climb to the top. Don t miss the women divers show which is on the left trail, at the foot of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Showtimes are 1.30 and 3pm. It s complimentary. And you can choose to buy and eat fresh abalone at the little restaurant. Overall a truly relaxing and uplifting experience!

Arrived at the Seongsan llchubong at about 615am, an hour before sunrise at 715am. The ticket counters were not opened (opens at 730am) but the trails were available. We hiked up the 1.5km or so trail up and it took us about 30mins with a couple of rest stops. Most of the trail were stairs, only the initial path was rocky. It s rewarding and got to see the beautiful sunrise and Seongsan town/ port in the background.

We went to Seongsan IIchubong after our lunch.  We bought our admission ticket –5,000 per person.  When we enter the park, we saw that the climb can be quite steep and decided to take the left trail which has very nice scenery of the cliff and sea.  If you do not intend to climb up the Peak, just take the left trail which has gentle slopes and its free admission.  You can also watch the Haonyeo performances around 3 pm from the left trail.

The short hike is easy with stairs. I went up for sun rise and sunset. The view is magnificent. There are convenience stores CU and GS25 nearby, but GS25 is further. The CU is not opened so early for sunrise hike and its staff is rather unfriendly though. Overall, I would hike again Seongsan ilchulbong if I visit Jeju again.
This place is very popular in Jeju for climbing mountain and see natural beauty from the top. Highly recommended.

My wife and I visited Ilchulbong at 5 pm, and unfortunately, couldn't catch the women divers in action. We made it to the top and it was quite a steep climb. We were completely winded by the time we reached the peak which has a beautiful viewing deck. The moon was up on one side while the sun was setting on the other side. It was our last day in Jeju and Korea and the beautiful sunset against the skyline of Jeju was the perfect ending we could have  asked for.
Beautiful sloppy landscape by seashore, wonderful crispy fresh air, women divers hub, worth to visit!
Going out is fun, coming down is easy. My 5 yrs old enjoy so much. The view is impressive but the parking is limited

We reached Seongsan around 5am, few peoples has started climbing. Trail quite dark all the way up. City view in the dawn during climbing is pretty. Reached to the top and sun has started to rise. Good facilities provided for the guest to view the sunrise.

We went at 10am and there was a huge crowd, all trying to climb up .  Took about 40 minutes climbing up, making many stops in between to enjoy the view below.   It was  too crowded at the top and there isnt really much to see, except for the view of course.   Most people climb up, take a quick photograph and quickly climb down.

It took us 30 mins to climb up. Was very windy at the start but the heat from the climb took over. Lol. Managed to catch the sunrise. Everyone cheered when the sun peeked out. Bring some breakfast and hot drinks in a flask to enjoy. Yes there were PRCs talking very loudly disrupting the peace. I tot they banned PRCs to Jeju? Oh wells.Climbing down was a chilly experience but u get a really nice view of jeju going down. Lots of photo ops.

Our hotel in old sity side. But from there use local bus( from bus terminal) W3000 one way,when we back was W1600..So cheep.Anyway,this place was 1hour round trip. quite steps has but some of them points has so nice views!!! 1 thing , this place is very windy spot.. When you go must check your clothing and hat or cap...

Go early to enjoy the sunrise! But pls take note of the closing day because there were many tourists in the same boat as us who went on the first Mon of the month. Only a portion of the trail was open and couldnt hike to the top (free entry though). Still,nice views.
Very beautiful view from the top of the hill surrounding area is good for hiking a walking World heritage place can be crowded in high saison

I might not have came at the right time to enjoy the view which was why I might not have enjoyed it that much? I arrived about 1 and the sun was so hot. Paid 5000 for entry ticket and climb to the TOP. The view was good but I felt not worth the sweat and effort haha. But upon making the way down, it is a must to go see the female divers who dive without any equipment to catch seafood like octopus. Their show time is at 3pm. Make sure to watch it.

The best time to go is early in the morning, to see the sun rise. I had gone a little after the sunrise and many people were already on their way down. The views are spectacular and the way up is very safe, and good for all ages. This was probably the most memorable part of Jeju Island.
Went as part of a day tour with Yeha Tours. This was part of their East tour. Sooo worth all the steps! About 12-20 minutes to top. I slept so well that night.

If you want to see sunrise, please go to Seongsan Ilchulbong: It's very beautiful place. You should wake up in the early morning. It'll take 20 mins to climb in the peak. And you can experience excellent atmosphere there. You can take lots of picture because of its beauty. Good luck to you, hope you can see sunrise in the Seongsan Ilchubong

This spot is one of the UNESCO Heritage places, however to enjoy its beauty you d need to visit it on a sunny day. Unlikely, it was raining heavily and was foggy when I was there. Despite that, I enjoyed the trip and the place itself, besides it was fo free if you walk around. (you d only pay for the entrance if you want to go up to the extinct volcano crater). Landscape was amazing and loked kind of alien. Eventually, I found this spot beautiful in any weather conditions.

I initially wanted to climb this peak to watch the sunrise but due to the unpredictable weather on Jeju Island whilst we were there, we decided to visit when we thought the weather would be dry at least.As it is when we reached the peak it was a bit blustery and on our descent it began to rain heavily.But this place is totally worth making the effort to climb the steps to the peak. At various points when climbing up you are greeted with really cool views. Definitely worth a visit.
Itis well worth the hike up to see the view of the coastline and Udo Island. Close to the ferry to Udo.
best view to see sunrise but so crowed. if you want to take some photo without many pp around, you should come early then start to climb on. many nice small food talls and restaurant near by.
Climb less than 30 minutes you can reach the top. Lots of stops to rest on the way up to the peak. Stop and enjoy the view on the way up.
Amazing beach the mount and amazing women diver.Good fresh air and many kind of traditional street food

Gorgeous view of the ocean and surrounds, but extremely crowded in summer. You should be moderately fit to make it up the steep stairway here. Tip: walk on along the main coastal road to the east of to get an alternative view of this World Heritage site.

We visited on a sunny day, a nice change from the rain from the day before.At the entrance, you have the choice to walk around the short & free pathway by the sea or you could pay an entrance fee to hike up to the top of Seongsan for a birds eye view. We opted for the hike up.I wasn't very fit so it took me a couple of stops before I got up eventually..but the view was worth it. If you go earlier, you could catch the performance by the Haenyeo down by the shore at the bottom of Seongsan. Sadly, we did not manage to catch the performance.

When we arrived, we were welcomed by beautiful views of the meadows and fences. The view from the top is also very nice.Not recommended for parents and young children, because the trip to the peak is around 20-30 minutes depending on each person's stamina.Overall the view of the is very beautiful.There was also a female diver show catching fish without modern equipment around 11 or 12 o'clock (forget the exact time), mostly of the female divers are aged. The catch is sold quite expensive.
Nice View and good for health,Guys try going this place and you will feel the Fresh of Air at top of mountain.

To make it to the summit of Seongsan, you will need to endure the flight of steep steps uphill. Good thing is that there is quite a number of rest benches for travellers who gets tired of climbing plus a drink stall mid-mountain that sells expensive isotonic drinks! Once you are at the summit, you will be rewarded with breathtaking views of the green crater. Worth the steep climb so don't give up! Another tip is that you have to plan your climb time well. Set aside 2 hours in the mountain and be sure to come back to watch the Haenyeo grannies preformance at the foot of the mountain. The performance times are 130pm and 3pm only.

Probably even better at sunrise, but we have been there about 11AM.Great view from the top. Center of the voulcano is nothig special at the time.Take a hat or umbrella and other protection from sun, even at not too sunny day.* Operating Hours:April-October 07:00-20:00November-March 07:30-19:00* Fees for foreigners: Adults 5,000 won / Teenagers & Children 2,500 won

Amazing views all the way up and at the top. If visiting in summer - better to visit in evening or early morning.  We climbed up twice - once at 5pm and then at 5.30 the next morning.  Both were excellent - with different sun position giving different light and shadows.  Both worth it.  Fee is 5000 won per person ( half price if child or youth under 24).  If you go before 7 in the morning - there is no charge.  When you come down make sure that you take the path around to the right - good views down to the small beach and also on the main peak

visited by family with 3 teenagers in a hot August day. It was really hot, humid day, and we climbed Seonsan Ilculdong around 3 o'clock. It is said that it took about 25 mins' walk to the top, but it was very hard to climb because of heat during hot August day. It is nice picture taking place.Do not bring little kids. It is not for the young children. I saw many children who just wear sandals climbed the all steps to the top, and they cried and were angry because of the heat and hard work. Actually, Seongsan Ilchulbong is nice picture taking place from far, but there is nothing spectacular on the top. It is better to climb Seoungsan Ilculbong in the spring or fall, not in the summer. Otherwise, it is good enough to look at it from the parking lot and take a walk around shore areas.
The hike takes about 25-30 min, but it can get quite intensive especially if you are planning to do it in the heat of summer. The view however is really spectacular. Would highly recommend it.
Best place to sightseeing and the view is amazing.You will regret if coming to Jeju but not visit Seongsan Ilchubong

We stayed at Clouds Pool and Spa Hotel which is 1km away so we could reach there at 5am to do the climb. It is fairly an easy climb aided by a lot of stairs. We had breakfast at Paris Baguette which is opposite the mountain. They open at 5am. We had peaceful breakfast as we were the only couple there. The top of the peak offers beautiful panorama view of the green grass crater, sea view skyline and the other side is the Jeju city bird s eye view.  Air is fresh and very windy on the peak (I thought I could fly away). There were only 3 persons on the peak when we arrived. We could stay there for about half an hour to enjoy the scenery and the peace. The female divers abalone catching activities happen at 1.30pm or 3.30pm below the mountain. It s another steep way down from carpark infront of Seongsan Mountain. From my hotel room, I could see people walking up to the mountains all day and evening. It s definitely a must visit when you come to Jeju!

The hike took about 30 minutes or so. Those with mobility issue may have trouble going up. However, there is another free trail that is accessible and easy for those who can't climb up.The ticket for the hike is KRW5k each.When we reached there, the weather was misty, hence we did not see get to see the famed "Green Tea Lava Cake". In fact, we didn't get to see anything other than we have hiked up.

This is perfect for solo and family travelers that are vacationing in Jeju. Adult admission is 5,000 KW and is well worth it. The hike takes about 30 minutes to an hour and can be  fairly steep in some areas. There are many shops, cafes, and restaurants around the area once you are done with the hike to the top. If you time it right, you will be able to see the famous Women Divers of JeJu who perform at 1:30 PM. The heritage behind it is very unique since it has been carried one for generations.

It absolutely great experience! The view is absolutely beautiful from the top. You have to experience it yourself. Keep your stamina full charge because you have hike to the top. The ticket is 2,000 won.

Admission fee for adult is 2000won. You will be able to enjoy walking up to the peak and see the entire sea/ Mountain View. It will be good to wear covered shoes or sport shoes so it s easier to go up the steps. Not only that, there s a 대  performance available but I missed the timing. But the 대  will be at their store selling fresh seafood. It s a good place for solo travellers :)After exploring ilchulbong, head over to ㅼ“대 吏 for some abalone porridge :D

Must visit this place if you are in Jeju.  This is the place where you can also watch women divers performance and taking the horse ride too. If you want to catch the Sunrise at the peak, start to climb at least 30 mins before the sunrise. Please check the weather first. If you are not that fit, start to climb 1 hour before the sunrise. Take note: Stairs all the way from the bottom to the top. A lot of resting area along the way.  Alternatively, from the entrance, walk towards the ocean on the left.  You can catch the sunrise from there too if you are too lazy to climb.  The view around the mountain is fantastic.  Many eateries, shops nearby.  It will be very crowded from 9am onwards with many tour buses.  Many parking lots nearby if you are unable to get any parking at the mountain carpark.
A must-see but be prepared for a tough climb to the top. View is fantastic! Go early if you are driving to get a parking lot (free). Beautiful flowers.
It Looks very high but it s not as bad as it looks.  The path is excellent and has mostly stairs. And the view is really worth it
It was a great walk with well-managed path/trail/stairs!View along the was up and down was also great!You ll not be alone as many people keep you company.I enjoyed stretching my legs in this visit!
A great scenic trekking suitable for most. Best to view for sunrise and sunset. The trail takes 45mins for a slow leisure climb to the peak.

We hiked up to the peak for Sunrise with our boys age 6&8. We started at the bottom around 4.45am. There were many people along the trail and everyone walk in the dark. Surprisingly, torchlight or headlamps are not required. With some rest on the benches along the way, we reached at 515am. The sun started to rise around 5.30am. It was truly beautifully.

The hike up the hill was made easy with steps. But it can be tiring for elderly people. Nevertheless, one would need to take it slow and easy, don t rush to get up there. Once you hit the peak, you will enjoy the scenic view of the crater. The cool breeze at the peak makes it even more worthy.

Best to arrive early to avoid the hordes of tourists. Wear comfy shoes because it is asteep climb up steps. Don t bring your strollers. May not be a place to bring the older folk who might have trouble walking.

Climbed it on a windy afternoon. Will take you around 20-30mins if you are reasonably fit. Spectacular views all around even before you reach the peak. Very worth the exercise. Its a 200m climb and steep at some sections. Wear comfortable shoes and clothing. Will recommend climbing early to catch the sunrise at the summit.

I thought we were the minority few that would brace the darkness and hike up. Boy, I was wrong. When we reached the Sunrise Platform, some 100-200 people were there with us.And when the golden egg yolk broke the horizon, there was a chorus of 'ooooooh' as people gasped in awesome wonder. It only took 2 minutes or so for the sun to fully risen from the horizon.If the ticket counter is not open for sunrise hikers, please do not wait. Get in and begin the hike. Bring a flask of hot coffee and enjoy. Sorry, no food allowed in the park.
This is a fantastic place to see the awesome landscape of jeju. There is quite a bit of walking so wear comfortable shoes. It will also be rather hot in the summer as well.

Came early at 5.15 am. Reached the peak at about 5.35 am but there was no sunrise. Maybe because it was a bit cloudy due to the rain? The view however was still spectacular. I am a solo traveller and was worried about being the only person there early in the morning but nope, a lot of people including locals were there. The path was not too dark and it was a fair hike up. A few areas to stop by if you ever needed some rest. If you come in the morning for the hike, you do not have to pay any entrance fees which is actually necessary during the day (2000W).Oh the woman divers show. It was really a  show  and then, they were off to the sea. I didn t wait until they were back though. You need to pay the general entrance fee to Seongsan Ilchulbong of 2000W to gain access to the area of the woman diver.So basically I came here twice - once for the morning hike and the other one for the woman s diver show.

Sunrise peak in English, this volcanic cone is 182 metres high. That works out to about 25 stories which is roughly how high you have to climb to get there.And to get there early enough to get a good position, you need to get up pretty early. We woke at 4am for a 4.30 start (this after a 60km bike ride the day before and another 60 to come on the day. We went up rather more briskly than we had planned (exuberance?) and were one of the first to arrive.First, let me acknowledge the impressive steps, in stone and wood, that have been built to help people get to the top (and the separate staircase that leads you down). Kudos to the engineers and builders. They even thought of rest stops which also work well as photo opportunity spots.The amphitheater-style seats at the top are well-thought out too and provide a good view.Sunrise was scheduled for about 5.30 and a fair crowd had gathered by then.Unfortunately, the sky was overcast and we could only glimpse the sun as it occasionally peeped through the clouds. But it was spectacular nonetheless.There was no admission charge as we were up and down before the ticket booth opened at 7am.It is still worthwhile visiting even if you don't want to watch the sunrise.

Superb scenery especially on the way up the peak.Great place to take photos of the island.The climb up is no kidding for older people as steps are very narrow and steep. Luckily there are places for you to rest along the way up.

A nice little hike up to the top. Not very long, Maybe 20 minutes but ALOT of stairs. Your legs will be feeling it. Good View at the top and its nice to see all the people taking 1 million selfies of themselves while at the top.

The first 3 days were full of heavy rain and drizzles. Went here on the 3rd day, it took us more than an hour on the bus to get there. And it still rained. The hill is gorgeous but all I can say is try to pick a day without rain because it was quite slippery (figures since we wore flip flops to avoid our sneakers from getting wet). From here we went to Pyoseon Folk Village which took another hour. So from Seongsan Ilchulbong we took bus no. 295 to Pyoseon Community Centre then changed to bus no. 212 to Pyoseon Folk Village.

We drove from seogwipo which took around 1H drive from 4am because the sunrise at 5.40am. It took us roughly 20-30mins uphill trail to reach the peak (sunrise view point). Worth spending a morning for this beautiful sunrise view.

Seongsan Ilchulbong is a tuff cone that has been formed from not so old (5000 years old) volcanic eruptions. It is 180-meter-high and one can walk to the top. Note that it has been well accommodated: there are stairs starting from the bottom to the top so that the walk is fairly easy. It takes about an hour for going to the top and come back, depending of course on how long one stays up-hill to enjoy the view. The view is the main thing here. It is just amazingly beautiful!First of all, one should pay attention to the different rock formations, some of them, featuring interesting shapes (see one of the two pictures I shared). Second, it is really great to stop all along the way up to enjoy the view from Jeju (see the second of the pictures I shared). On the top, one gets an amazing view on the other side (i.e. the sea). I was there in the middle of the day (there was no other way out in my case), but I can fairly well imagine the extra in being there at sunrise or sunset.Finally, note that there is an entrance fee, but it is very reasonable (about 2 USD).Overall, I strongly recommend this place and the walk. One moreover should definitely try to be there at sunrise/sunset. Please make sure to have enough water (it was really hot on the day I walked there) and be prepared: it could be crowded. The place is quite popular. There is a good reason for Seongsan Ilchulbong to be one of the top attractions of Jeju Island.

Great hike up the peak, totally worth it on a clear day. Views around very beautiful. The women diver show visible from the top when you come down. Takes about an hour to go up and back down . The view especially on the other side is the surprise when you get to the top. Even the udo island is visible from a distance . Make the effort and be rewarded.

It's a lot of stairs and little walking to get to the top, but it's worth it with great views and a wonderful sea breeze. On one side you have views of the crater, on the other of Jeju island. There are lots of other tourists (mostly local) going up and down so be prepared for some level of crowds. There was abundant parking when we visited. There are also plenty of food stalls at the bottom along with bathrooms. On the way up, there are lots of benches, rest areas, and viewing platforms. We saw people of all ages - really old to really young doing the climb. If you're in town and you have a couple hours to spare, we'd recommend it!

Interesting background as to how the peak was formed. The hike to the top gives a gorgeous view of Jeju Island, and if lucky the peak of Hallasan. Lots of visitors but the place is quite big enough not to make it crowded.

Made it a point to see the performance by the elderly female divers but was a little disappointed. Worth a watch if you can make it. One motto that we came up with was, "If you can climb Hallasan, you can do anything."Surely enough, climbing llchulbong wasn't too difficult maybe 20-30 minutes climb?
I could just sit here for a couple of hours enjoying the scenery and it's beauty. It was windy in October but very calming and relaxing. A good place to "re-charge" and be away from the city life.
Not for people that do not exercise.We went there is rain and fog, cannot see most of the features but it is another kind of experience.  Some strange rock formations.

The hike was an easy one with stairs. Less than one hour slow pace hiking up. My brother brought his baby as well in baby carrier. There are a lot of souvenir shops nearby. In my experience, the souvenir sold there is much cheaper than the one in Jeju City.
Beautiful but packed with tourists. Lots of walking but definitely worth it. Probably the most crowded place in Jeju but you won t feel claustrophobic here.

From Seogwipo , we took bus 201 and it dropped us off at the entrance. The mountain is just so beautiful to look at. It s a very easy hike, just 25 minutes to the peak. Bring some water . Drones are not allowed.

To see the sunrise, one has to wake up early and hike along the stairs and some stone steps and must remember to bring along a torchlight or use our smartphone's torchlight as it can be still very dark during the hike. I really loved this place. The view before climbing and the view from up is just great!If you want to go for a short hike this is the place for you! The walk up is about 15 -30 minutes, if I remember well. But it is worth the walk up!
Really worth it. Only one way up and one way down, no u-turn. It's pretty steep Nd take energy to climb. Amazing view.
We went near to sunset and all photos taken were nice with soft orangy hue on our face. :) It was easy climb steps to the peak and the scenery is beautiful!
The steps are challenging but safe. The wind, though, quite strong and full speed, but the view from the top was amazing, we stayed and watched sunset.

This was one of my favorite parts of Jeju. We went during the sunrise which reading everywhere said was most ideal, and it was gorgeous. It s a lot of steps to get to the top. I would suggest bringing a bottle of water.

As I can clearly assure that you wont be regret if you visit this place. This is my second visit to Seongsan Ilchulbong. We went there to catch a majestic sunset. Am a nature buff and this one is just Loveㅿ A good few minutes hike and a foxy view atop awaits you.One must not miss this when in Jeju.

The taxi driver was really kind to walk with us, but he didn't "warn" us of the difficulty level and duration of the climb! :) We had lots of beautiful photos taken, in between the rest stops, and finally reached the peak with real sense of accomplishment!

Also known as Sunrise Peak, this crater formation can be ascended and descended in about 50 minutes total. Path is uneven and includes lots of stairs, some steep. It s a must hiking course in Jeju. You ll be leading to the top by hundreds of well made stairs. All can be seen on the top. The place is very windy but it ll dry your sweat and the great top view will make you take lots of pictures. Enjoy the view!

One of the most visited Tourist attraction in Jeju, the Seongsan IIchulbong peak or the Sun rise peak was formed due to Volcanic eruption thousands of years ago. Went there a few days after Xmas and the weather was cold and hence made the climb easier. If we had came during summer I would never have wanted to make the climb. As it is with the cold weather and strong winds we made the climb with 2 or 3 stops in between to catch breath and take photos of the magnificent views. If you have kids or old folks to take care I wouldn't recommend the climb.

Although this mountain is nice from afar, I will still recommend to take the ~ 30-40 mins hike up. It s a bit tiring but they have many rest stops if needed. Fantastic views from the top to make the trekking worthwhile.

The hike up takes about 30 mins depending on your fitness level and speed. It is pretty easy climb up the steps and boardwalk. It was drizzling when we were there. Nevertheless, the surrounding view on top was nice. At eye level, the crater wasn't obvious as it looked more like a downhill slope. It would be great if a an observation tower is built to have an aerial view of the crater.Entrance ticket 2000 won. Suggest you relief yourself just before the entrance as there isn't any toilet facilities at the peak.

For those who are not really into long hikes and yet still want a good panaromic view of Jeju s surroundings, this is the place. There are also live performances apparently involving the female divers but we missed the timing.

I think that it's not as grand, but the stairs are well kept and in good shape. There's a lot of people and a lot of food too. Parking wasn't an issue for us.I've been twice, and maybe it wasn't anything special to me as I didn't get to go in the morning to watch the sunrise. But be prepared to walk up with a lot of people

There were many scenic views at this attraction. I enjoyed both the ascent and descent. Even with the chilly breeze, one is sure to perspire upon arrival at the peak. The view into the crater at the peak was another awesome feast for the eyes. The sea as the backdrop served as a picturesque addition to the already scenic composition. These minimalist free divers were equipped with their orange flotation devices, masks and dry suits, sustained their tradition daily in the frigid waters to harvest seafood from the shallow depths. Why pass on this opportunity?
A great place to visit for fantastic coastal views of Jeju. The boardwalk was well constructed and easy for most people to walk. The women divers  shows are scheduled at 1.30 and 3 pm.

We did the sunrise peak climb as part of our tour of Jeju with Yeha bus tours - it wasnt at sunrise, but it was pretty pleasant nevertheless.We started off by watching the women divers at the bottom of the cliff. The walk up the stairs is hard on knees but not specially challenging and can be done in 15-20mins. We arrived just prior to sunset and it was very beautiful to watch the sun go down on the opposite end of the island, would definitely recommend it. The hill itself is really pretty and a great place to get some photos.

A great place to start off is the Women Divers exhibition center to see the old photos and explanation from the staff on the history of Women Divers. Than a slow walk up the peak for a great view ....  the wind was hallowing when we climb up and the local told us its a normal day ...   plenty of great eateries just a short walk from the entrance after the climb . A MUST visit .

20min climb up to peak, short time but take some energy to climb up, come down is easy. So get ready to take off your jacket even is cold day. But worthy, nice view. And can see haenyeo performance as well, but must check the time. One day 2 slot, afternoon is 3pm.
Be prepared to climb flights of stairs to get to the top to enjoy the great view. Good pair of shoes would be helpful.
Great place! A must visit if you re in Jeju. Do give it a climb if you have the endurance. Awesome view and lots of picturesque scenery. If you are in luck, may even catch the sea ladies diving.
Always a joyful climb up the steps to the top and capture a view of the ocean. Awesome view, great exercise! Must do in Jeju

This sight is at the extreme south east of Jeju. There are many great views and cafes within this area. This is a short hike up a beautiful hill and after the hike there is a haenyo performance where old ladies dive without oxygen tanks to collect abalones. I regretted not spending a full day in this area to chill.
The hike up will take around 20-30 mins depending on your speed. It's pretty steep stairs going up but you can take your own sweet time to enjoy the breathtaking view while hiking.

Imposing scenery! So many photo opportunities on this beautiful landscapeWent back twice cos I didn't realise the hanyeo diver women show is there..was searching around somewhere else.  Time your visit to see these amazing old ladies diving at 3pm.
One for the books.The climb is worthit though we weren't able to watch the sunrise due to the gloomy weather. The view is relaxing - makes you think of living on this laid back place in Jeju..

went there after breakfast and was a good time to start if you didn't care too much of sunrise view. Even though it was windy and chilly, got up to the top sweaty and hot. you see see pretty ckear view from the top; Udo island, the wind turbines in the east, Seopjikoji in the south.

Well worth the hike even on a cloudy day. If you go to see the sunrise like we did and it's dark don't forget to read the signs! We totally missed the sign that said no eating at the top...Oops! Plenty of parking and bathrooms at the bottom.

Walk to the top is quite easy with good views.Don't miss the signpost to the women divers near the bottom on the way down.  They do a few shows a day and you don't have to pay extra to see it.Lot's of parking and eateries in the area

Knowns also as Sunrise Peak. We went there on afternoon as we did not know this place  can see beautiful sunrise. Must visit place when you in Jeju Island. Worthwhile hiking by stairs about 45 minutes. This wonderful craters formed from volcanic eruption l00,000 years ago. Entrance Ticket KRW2000. Twice a day can see women divers go to the sea and singing before catch their seafood such as abalone, sea urchin, etc. Overthere you can ride pony horses
It was tiring but the view was worth it! Please bring a bottle of water on your way up. Take photos of the sceneries  going up and down,they were beautiful!

Unfortunately there was so much wind and rain during our stay on Jeju Island, based in Seogwipo. That day, we braved the elements and took the bus to visit the beautiful site of the volcano Seongsan-ri.The visit was worth the climb.

Came at autumn,  the weather was 18degrees but once you start climbing,  be ready to take off your jacket. A total of 50min hike with magnificent view is totally worth it. Love the crater and all round view at the peak.

Once my family landed at the airport, we rented a car and drove! This was a great option to Hallasan for family members that could not hike the summit as the trails are very nice, and the views are achieved after only a moderate walk and stair climb.

I didn't know I was looking at this famous peak when we approached in a taxi (looking for a lunch spot that our kids would approve of). I was saying "Wow, look at that" as we drove towards it. Reminder: do check this place out , esp during sunning days. Very stunning !
