The TV screen will flash seongsan-ri entrance and you can press the bell to alight (photo attached). Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. I have car sickness but it was still bearable for me. We alighted and headed to the black beach along Seongsan. It was called the black beach as the sand was black. Not sure why we need not need to pay for the entrance fee to Seongsan that day (25th April) but we were happy as the temperature was about 17 degree Celsius. We wore T-shirt with a windbreaker only as the sun kept us warm. A windbreaker will be good as it can be quite windy especially if you walk along the beach. There were 2 track at Seongsan. One track led to the peak of Seongsan which consist about 10 flights of stairs (Pretty doable even with poor fitness   just take as many rest breaks as needed). At the peak, you will be able to have a panoramic view of the city and the surrounding water bodies. The other track is along the coast area with pretty wild purple (I think is Lunaria annua)  and yellow canola wild flower and volcanic stacked rocks.After Seongsan, you can continue to the Jeju Olle Route 1 to Al Oreum along the ocean area. The Jeju Olle Route 1 will pass by canola flower patches for photo taking, a nice ocean view with beaches for scenic viewing, a new hotel named as The Cloud, the ferry terminal, along many beautiful seashore. We stopped at one of the seashore where we witness locals harvesting gastropod, sword razor clams and cockles using simple equipment. We were friendly and allowed us to take photo of how they harvest sword razor clams. If you are interesting in harvesting, remember to bring a good jacket as the wind was strong in April. Putting on waterproof boots will be good too. We continued to walk along the coast where cuttlefish were being dried along the coast. There were many restaurants along the way too. As we continued the walk, we noted that there was no bus stop along the walk after the fish port/market (there was a Ojo Haenyeo House bus stop). The next bus stop was at Jongdal Elementary school which was quite a distance away.After walking through the coastal area, you will walk through a village for a short period before reaching the expressway. The walk towards Al Oreum required you to cross an expressway and the route up the Al Oreum seemed alittle deserted with trees but there was still a road up. You will contine to see the orange/blue ribbons that were well spaced. However, we started the walk at 1pm and took too many stops for picture taking. Therefore, we were unable to finish the walk to Al Oreum.We decided to back track  and took bus 701 from the Jongdal Elementary school stop at about 5.30 pm back to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal (we take on the side nearer to the expressway, not the opposite). Therefore, make sure you start the Olle route earlier if you want to reach the top of Al Oreum where you will have a bird-eye view of the paddy field and coastal area. The bus journey took about 2 hours to reach Seogwipo-si.Jeju Olle Route 6 & 7 We did not do the entire 6 & 7 trail but we visited Chilshimni Poetry Park, Hwangwooji coast, Oedolgae observatory and Oedolgae. This was a scenic trail and I highly recommend. We stayed at a hotel along Jungang-ro road, that was near the Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. From our hotel, it was a 10 minutes walk to Geolmae Eco Park. The park led us along Seohong-ro road to Taepyeong-to road (where we passed by Hotel Yeon) where we were able to see the Saeyeong Bridge. After the bridge was in sight, we followed our instinct to the Bridge. There was an ice-cream stall that serve grape soft-serve that was delicious. We made our way onto the bridge to view the pristine bluish-green coastline and headed to Saeseom Island. Saeseom Island was a short 20 to 30 minutes trail that brought us to a rocky coastline where you can view two lighthouses (red and white). You could walk to the white lighthouse on the rocks but at your own risk. There were many locals fishing along the rocky areas too. In short, the trail along the Saeyeongyo Bridge was fairly easy yet scenic enough. We were there on the 22nd of April and the weather was about 15 degree Celsius in the day. A light jacket with windbreak will be sufficient. Afterwhich we headed to Chilshimni Poetry Park (which you can view Cheonjiyeon Falls for free) as there was a stairway along the left side of main exit road (where all the tour buses parked, pedestrian walkway path with brown wood). The stairway seemed to indicate going up a temple. However, we landed in Chilshimni Poetry Park. We took pictures of the waterfall and left Chilshimni Poetry Park to follow the orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon to Hwangwooji coast and Oedolgae. The orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon were along the park main road (Namseongjung-ro road where Park Sunshine hotel was). Then, You need to turn in to Namseong-ro road and you will see a brick wall painted dark blue with pinnochio seated on a bench (photo attached) you will passed by a  hip 몃媛– Hostel (the hostel name is in Korean as I cannot find the English name online - photo attached). u will then past by Poong Gyung Hotel in Jeju (not the one u can find online - photo attached) before arriving at Hwangwooji coast. I love Hwangwooji coast bcos it was like a private pool. There were only a few Korean that day, playing, swimming and hunting of sea creatures in the private pool. It also has a good view of the Saeyeongyo Bridge from a far.  After-which we head to Oedolgae and walked till Dombenang-gil Road. We decided to head back as I needed the toilet. At the entrance to Oedolgae, there was a public toilet acorss the road. The toilet were will keep with toilet paper provided. You can watch the sunset if you have time. However, we decided to walk back to our hotel as we were tire. Jeju Olle Route 14   1If you love beaches, this is a must walk route (at least it was really breathe-taking for me). We stayed at Seowipo, we took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. You can press the bell to alight. For my other bus trip, the stops were announced correctly and was reliable). We actually stopped that Jungmun Tourist Complex to go the the Teddy bear museum and Cheonjeyeon Falls before proceeding to the beach. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. We needed to change bus 702 (opposite the tourist infrmation counter) to Hyeojae beach. It cost 3300 won. The journey on the bus we great as you will pass by paddy field, wind mills and wild flower fields (photo attached). You will see a beautiful beach 1st (Geumneung Beach) but don t get down, get down at Hyeopjae beach as the view is nicer (about 2 stops away). You can walk down to Geumneung Beach later as it was part of olle route 14-1 (There is a public toilet down the stretch if you need). The weather then (April 26) was 12 to 17 degree Celcius and remember to buy a jacket and windbreaker as it was very windy when we were there. We so blessed that the sky cleared up to reveal one of the most beautiful turquoise beaches I have been. The beach was wide and the colours of the water clear and blue. There are many caf챕 where you can buy a hot drink from. Noted that the caf챕 only allow you to use the toilet if you buy a drink (the receipt will print the password to get into the toilet). You can always use the public toilet. We decide to walk along the orange and blue ribbon trail (Jeju Olle Route 14) and it was one of the best trail for me. We complete only part of the the trail where we walk through the villages to the fishing port. The route will bring you to a serene path with light house and the wind mills. The the path became rocky nearing the windmills, and we decided to walk out through the rocky back alley of a shellfish place (away from the orange/blue ribbon) and landed at a bus stop. We took bus 702 back to seogwipo. It was a must go beach but only on a clear blue day where the magnificent of the beach will show up. In Summary, I always thought that you would need to rent a car around jeju. However, during my 4 days trip (even Hallasan was done using public transport   can look at my post at tripadvisor), all our travelling was done throuh public transport. We were able to view those usual scenic places that ple usually go too! The good thing about walking was that we could stop at anytime we want to take picture or do something we did not plan for (Eg: watch how the local harvest shellfish). However, we were the kind that love to walk and could spend 7 hours walking. Therefore, we could travel in jeju with a budget using their public transport.

I completed every single course over a period of a year so the following comments are just my opinions. If you are staying for a short period of time in Jeju courses 6 and 7 are the most popular and will probably get the most from. Both are very scenic and you will get to see some of the major sights. If you start at one of the information sites, you can pick up a Jeju Olle guide which has maps and information of the trails, guides for the Buses, to get to and from the starting points. Also I'd recommend downloading Kakao Maps app on your phone and you can zoom in and see the actual trail that you are following when you are on it. It comes in handy especially for me when I made a wrong turn on my trips. If your doing the entire course I'd recommend buying a jeju Olle Passport. Carry it with you and get it stamped at the starting points and halfway way points of the trails. I was living near jeju city and caught most of Buses from the Jeju inter city bus centre. The 101/201 express buses will take you to/ or near a lot of the starting points but I'd recommend picking up the Olle Guide first and the info in that is invaluable.Most of the Starting points are close to the roads unless you are going to one of the 3 islands. I used booking.com most of the time to book places to stay overnight as I don't speak Korean. Jeju has a lot of places to stay and there would be abundant places to stay except for maybe a couple of the more remote locations on the trail. There are offical Olle trail Hostels throughout the trails to which are very nice. If planning for no Korean speakers just check before hand that you are not traveling on a Jeju holiday as a lot of paces close down and might be harder to find a place to stay. Of course take plenty of water and there's usually 7/11 of CV's around the place where you can get snacks to eat.The trails themselves are very beautiful , Different scenes ranging from Black volcanic rock on the coastlines, Forest trails, Beautiful beaches, Hill sides, a lot of Oreums (Jeju extinct volcanoes) small towns with a chance to see wildlife and a lot of friendly people. For myself my favourite trails were routes 11, 18-1 Chuja-Do island), 1-1 (Udo island), 7. For me the stronger trails were on the southern eastern point of the island starting from route 6 through to 15.Getting to the supporting islands it you might take note you will need your Passport to catch the ferry to Udo. You must show it when buying a ticket. There are a lot of ferries going most of the day to Udo. They have a very nice Peanut ice cream there. The smaller island Gapado at the time I went there were only 2 ferries in the day and its not the most reliable service and the ferries can be cancelled due to bad weather can be cancelled due to bad weather so check beforehand if you can. Chuja-Do island was one of my favourites. When I done it they had 2 ferries a day and you can not do the whole trail in time to catch the next ferry back so be prepared to stay over night. I have heard of instances when the weather turned bad and people had to stay a couple of nights on the island because the ferries were cancelled so just plan for that just in case. it is a beautiful Island though and one of my favourites.I would also recommend going and joining the Olle Walkers Facebook group. They take guided walks along certain courses and have great information about weather and so forth. all you need to do is contribute to the group from time to time.

A way to escape from daily hectic life. You can walk at your own pace and choose the route and scenery you like (coastal road, hiking). I completed Route 1, 1-1, 20, part of route 6 & 7. Just choose the route and follow the olle sign, relax and enjoy the view Olle wanna show you. Is quite safe, I am a girl and I walked alone.

We went there by taxi. Only did part of it for about 2.5 hours. Beautiful though it was sleeting and very windy. Enjoyed taking pictures. Would like to come back and spend the whole day. It must very pretty in Autumn.

If you enjoy nature, hiking one of the olle trails is a must-do while you're in jeju. It will not be an easy hike and not all parts of the trail are scenic but there are sufficient sights to blow you away and be left in awe of nature. This is also the best way to experience jeju's natural beauty (after all this is what its most famous for and not for teddy bears). It is also arguably the least touristy thing to do during your trip here. You can do as long or as short of the trails as you like; there are trails passing through hot tourist destinations where you'll see many tourist buses, local villages, rice fields, even resorts. You'll walk on sand, on rocks by the ocean, and if you time it correctly you'll be able to catch a gorgeous sunset along jeju's coastline. Be sure not to get stuck in a remote area after sunset as it can be difficult to get out. If you're doing a multi-day hike, there are many pensions located along the olle routes and you can just pop in for a night.Suggest to go with at least one other person in case you get lost (there are some places where the markings are not so visible/well maintained). If you rented a car, dont drive. Wear comfortable shoes and bring lots of water and snacks!

First obtain the Olle walking trails book from tourist information counter near the central bus station. From there you can ask for recommendations. I chose the scenic routes and it required walking up slopes which allowed paranomic view of scenery and also along the coastal area which was slippery due to rain. Some routes bring you directly to the beach whereby you can enjoy Jeju famous mandarin oranges and buy souvenirs such as their honeyed tea and famous chocolates! Do ask for discount like for all tourist attractions and at times the lady boss will throw in more pieces of the chocolate.You can also take partial route but check for the correct bus and you need to check which stop to alight. Unfortunately despite being a popular tourism attraction bus drivers can't communicate in English. Good luck if you encounter locals who can speak English.
Its hard to finish the entire trail, but its a must-do! You can discover so many things by walking on this trail. It cuts through many important attractions... Just follow the yellow ribbon

We did Olle 8, 9, and 10 trails, they are free of charge. These trails are truly amazing, within easy reach by public bus. They are very well maintained, yet in a natural setting. The trail design is incredibly diverse, taking you through towns, homes, single track, beaches, forests, mountains, farms, and historical sites. There are enough toilet facilities and convenience stores along the way  for convenience. We barely saw other people on the trails, although we were there during midweek. The walking is easy to moderate, and the route is well marked. The scenery is breath-taking!!!

I walked Routes 6 and 7 on 23rd-24th Oct 2017. The distance was 15km and 18km respectively.The weather was perfect - sunshine and cool breezes. These 2 routes are reputed to be the more beautiful ones. There are a couple of picture-perfect waterfalls and breath-taking shorelines along the way. 2,000Won per entry is charged for the waterfall. Along the way are small fishing ports where one can get to taste local seafood. There are small cafe along the way too, where one can sit, relax and taking in the beautiful scenery. Coffee is +/-4,000won. As I was staying at the starting point, from the finishing point I took taxi back It costs about 8kWon. Oh yes, there are clean restrooms every 5km or so. Just a little minus point, the blue & red ribbon is not easy to be found in urban area. So try looking for the blue line on the tar road.

I saw one picture in instagram and decided to go Jeju olle train route 8. Actually, Route 8 is restricted, but you will see everyone just walk into. It is called 'Gaetkkak Columnar Jointing (媛二쇱©₩由щ )' It is better to wear comfortable shoes since you have to walk on rocks, but you better dress nice if you want to have a good picture. I saw many girls dressed up and walked on the rocks which looked extremely tiring but worth it. You might need to line up to take a photo, and I also waited to take a photo at specific spot. Now I have really cool pictures ;)

Very scenic throughout the trail with different surroundings - you would trek pass fruit farms, river streams, stone trails and lush trees (watch out for the spider webs!)We started at the finishing point of trail no. 7 and made our way back towards the starting point so that we would end up at the rock pools at Oedolgae for a dip. The markings were easy to follow (some had descriptions) and there were many resting pit stops along the way - toilets, pavilions, convenience stores etc. One of the pit stops we made was at Mango Holic - fresh cold mango desserts to cool us down on a hot day!Would recommend to wear sneakers and sun screen and allow 4-6 hours to trek comfortably and enjoy the whole trail.

We attempted to run the trail 6 and 7 on a windy morning and although it wasn t ideal for running, we loved it. The scenery was breathtaking, the views along the coast were almost too much to take in at once at times. The only problems were crowds at times along the route, but even that wasn t such an issue, since they were all quite friendly and easygoing, allowing us enough room to pass (usually). Also there are loads of stairs which also doesn t make it ideal for running but we enjoyed the added challenge. Overall very highly recommended.

Highly recommend everyone to do at least one of the Jeju Olle trail routes. We chose route 6 as it s being classified as the easiest route. The route is filled with beautiful sceneries. Some part of the route takes you onto the roads, into the bush, along the coastal and up some hilly roads. We meet a lot of locals along all way and they are helpful & friendly. Lot of cafes for one to take a rest too.

Joined the 2016 Walking Festival to walk the olle trails & it was a fantastic experience. Yes it rained (which was unusual in October but with global warming!) & was initially disappointing as the scheduled performances were cancelled. Nonetheless it was amazing to see so many people walking together. After the Walking Festival which covered trail 1 & 2 I did trail 1-1, 5,6, 8 & 10. Each of the trails were different and beautiful. I was fortunate to get the assistance of Jim Saunders who gave me information on line & Ms Han at the Tourist Information Centre located next to Seogwipo Bus Terminal & e Mart who spoke good English.Ms Han helped me by writing in korean the bus stops & landmarks for the different trails so that I could show the bus drivers my destination  when I boarded using the T-money transport card. She even took the trouble to show me the different landmarks using satellite pictures on her computer in locating the Starting Point of each trail. The Olle Guide Book in English (which I obtained at the Olle Trail counter at the airport)was also very useful & well written.I enjoyed every trail & got to see Jeju on foot. It was also fun meeting locals walking the trails. I plan to return to walk the other olle trails.

Attended the 1st day of the 2014 Jeju Olle Walking Festival, infectious mood with music and performances at various parts of the scenic seaside trek during the full day walk. We climbed up the Dodu-bong, a short hill with a panaromic view of the route, planes taking off from the airport runway and the sea. While it was quite sunny, late afternoon the sea breezes can get quite chilly. However at the end of the trek there were performances and hot local food, so overall it was a satisfying Day 1 of the trek.

We did Olle Trail 1 (15kms) starting in Siheung and finishing in Gwanchiji Beach. Trail started next to Siheung elementary school and it was very well signposted all the way. The information center 1km up the road has no info in English and the gentleman didn't speak It either, although it's not really needed to follow the trail.The first 5-6kms are beautiful as you go up a hill, from where you can see the coast (including Seongsan Ilchulbong) on one side and the plains and Hallasan on the other, and you're surrounded by forest.Once down the hill, trail gets very boring for 8-9kms as it's on paved trails next to main roads. Final part from Seongsan to Gwanchiji is nice again as you walk next to the beach/sea.

i went to Jeju Olle Trail number 7. it was really awesome. i was travel alone and this place really good for refreshing your mind, relaxing, just enjoy the sound of the wave and the wind. trekking without feeling exhausted. and this place are one of shooting location for Jewel On the Palace :)!!!! must visited

We rode most of the Olleh trail routes by bike and it was awesome.  We made a film about it (titled Jeju: A Bicycle Adventure) and met heaps of interesting people to interview.   I'd definitely recommend it as a not-to-miss part of visiting Jeju Island!   I'd like to walk some of the Olleh Trail routes next time to experience it differently and more slowly.

The Jeju Olle Trail is an island-wide wooden path that takes you to the hills, rivers, beaches, and into the woods of Jeju. This is the perfect break from the busy urban jungle or if you want a break from the treadmill. Once on top of a hill, you will be offered a great view of the island.I took route 8 and connected to another route. I jogged some parts of the path and walked some (as some parts of the path are composed of stairs). It may be safer to walk since some parts of the path have no railing.Bonuses:There are huts and platforms that serve as resting areas. I encountered a local doing yoga in one of the huts.The river-side path has toilets and emergency rescue equipment ( life buoy, life vest, rope). Tips: Bring a camera, some sights are worth capturing; wear running shoes; and bring a phone, your GPS can be helpful in estimating your location.The path goes through or into private properties so be mindful not to trespass.

Jeju Island features a trail system that circumnavigates the island allowing the most highly motivated to hike the island, on foot.  If you want to see some great coast line and get the most out of a modest walk, look for trail #7.  It takes you along some great coastline with fantastic views of the cliffs, rocks and water.  In several areas, there are steps that take you from up high down to the surf.  If you stick to the trail, the elevation changes are modest and should be doable for anyone of moderate fitness.
Great hiking trails.   We did #7 along the coast by Oedolgae rock.    Check to see which particular route best fits your needs.

The marker for Routes 13, 14 and 14-1 are located in one spot. We got confused at first that we ended up completing abour 2-3km of Trail 14 until we got to another marker that we realized we were following the wrong path. We went back to the spot and started looking for the 14-1 trail. We spent the first half of the day doing Trail 14.When we headed to Trail 14-1 which was the intial plan, it was past noon already so the sun was up and it was hot (we did the trail on a summer day). It was a cool experience because the trail will bring you to the peak where you get a great 360 degree view of Jeju! It will take you inside a forest. You might even meet some horses along the way. By the time you'll get to the midpoint, which is the Osulloc Museum, you will realize how much you miss civilization and strangers. The trail will connect you to nature. You'll even find yourself in a dense forest! There are a lot of blue/orange ribbons so you won't be lost. This trail taught me to simply trust and find the blue/orange ribbons and enjoy/embrace nature wherever the trail (or life in general) may take you. Haha. This is definitely off the beaten path but it makes your Jeju tour even more special and truly your own. I would want to do more of the Olleh Trails in the future :)

We took Olle Trail number 1, and there were nothing much to see along the route, except for the hills that we climbed at the first one third of the trail. After we reached ground level, the trail took us to smaller villages which just looked like average cottages.
We hiked trail n.8 and it was just so beautiful! The scenery is incredible and the trail was very well labeled so you can follow it easily.

If doing Hallasan is not in your plans, then go take some nice walks on Jeju's Olle Trail Routes. They are shorter mostly and they appear all over the place in Jeju. Sometimes just 20 minutes walks and some much longer. We were impressed with the conservancy of nature and the trails on Jeju.

It was very meaningful to spend 3 days to join the Jeju Olle walking festival in November, 2018. One route per day not only an physical exercise and challenge to myself but also a good opportunity to meet friends or make new friends there. No one push you to walk faster but we could take pictures, enjoyed nice views and landscapes on each route. Local food for lunchs were delicious. What a beautiful island, good for gathering and good for vacation. I love Jeju. It was my third time participating Jeju Olle Festival. Different experience every time.

The trail system in Jeju is quite extensive and well mapped out. Our hotel was right on Olle 7 so one day we went tracking. What started on a normal surface road became a rough surface hiking trail through bushes, up and down a rocky coastline. The trail is indicated by ribbons, from what I understand different colors for different olles. when in Jeju hiking should definitely be on the to do list.

This excellent beach has a lil' bit of everything.  Located not far away from Jeju City/Airport, Hamdeok provides great atmosphere filled with Restaurants, Coffee Shops, waterfronts and one of the most beautiful sunsets in Korea! We sat down in the beachfront walk, cracked open a couple of beers and enjoy the evening breeze.  It was so cool watching people prepping their dinner and drinkin' some Soju while the sound of the waves and live music was heard across the darkness of the night.  We follow the music and found this young talented musician playing guitar and singing on front of a young crowd.  That was the Cherry on top of the Cake!  Stroll & Enjoy!

Because Jeju is a volcanic island, it doesn t have too many beaches relative to its 300 km of coastline.  Hamdeok Beach is one of the closest beaches to Jeju City.  It s also one of the most picturesque in Jeju making it quite crowded when it s warm enough to go into the water.  Unfortunately when we went there were a lot of seaweed washed up on the sand.  Despite the crowd, the parking lot was quite large and there is a good selection of cafes and restaurants nearby making it a decent visit even if you don t go into the water.

The beach has beautiful, clear  waters, and really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries and tea.We went there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. There are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice near the beach . Easy to get a taxi there too. Parking lots are available too.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.
Although the weather wasn t hot to swim yet, we have enjoyed the beach and it s surrounding. Beautiful place for pictures, stroll around the area and food. Kids had fun playing in the sand.

Last summer, our school went to Hamdeok Beach as a field trip. The place was conserved very neat and clean. All of my friends were excited to play around. The beach was enormous and the water was green and blue, looking amazing. However, the weather made us suffer very much. The temperature on that day went up to 29 degree, and all of us were almost burned. I highly recommend that you guys go to Hamdeok Beach when the weather gets cooler.

The beach has beautiful, clear emerald waters (the pictures doesn t do the place justice as its much better experienced in person), and a really nice cafe by the sea with good pastries. We got there by Bus 101 from CJU airport followed by a short walk. Near the beach there are tons of places to eat, such that you will be spoilt for choice. Easy to hail a taxi there too for those who wants to travel to their next location  by cab. Parking lots available too for those who are driving.Highly recommend this place for beach and sea lovers and those who enjoy coffee by the sea.
Beautiful beach in jeju, street parking available and is free. nice scenery and good for kids. toilets available to washing off the sands after playing at the beach.

Its winter now so there is no crowd at all except for the occassional photo maniacs. Beach and the clear blue water was out of this world but rubbish can be seen everywhere. My daughter went around picking up the rubbish cos it really did not do justice to the beauty.
Lovely lovely place with lots and lots of food options. Download naver and check them out. Google doesn't work very well in south Korea.

I stayed 4 night in Hamdeok Beach. If you are visiting Jeju for the very first time, you might want to move around because Jeju is quite big. Hamdeok is a great location to start your trip. It takes 20 mins by car, 30~40 mins by bus from Jeju International airport. It has many bus lines which offers you easy access to Airprot, Mountain Halla, Jeju city centre and even Seogwipo. I love the beach itself, but also there are lots of place to eat and chill. If you like to camp, there is a camping & caravan park at the end of beach. I loved it !!

Visited at mid-day in August.  It was very hot but beautiful.  had a picnic near the carpark and took a stroll along the trail on the east end of the beach. There is a small freshwater spring on the beach at the start of the trail
Even on a cloudy rainy day it is still beautiful.  The waters were clean. There are restaurants and cafes lining the beach.  Free fountain to clean feet.

This beach was absolutely breathtaking! The sparkling fine sand, emerald clear water, and green hills all around made for a perfect beach day! Unlike what was stated in previous reviews from July 2019, we never had any problems with being able to swim freely and as far out as desired. There was also no line set out not to cross. This is the first beach I've been to with provided shading tents and umbrellas, but it was definitely nice for when we wanted a short break from the sun! We also never had to pay to use these, so I'm not sure if that is something only done during the busy season. The beach was not over crowded, especially at low tide, and it was easy to find little secluded areas if you wanted to be away from the majority of people. Locals were walking and swimming around to clean up trash, so it was honestly one of the cleanest beaches I have been to! Plenty of yummy restaurants to eat at, as well as bars for those wanting to stay out late and still have a view of the water. Be warned, there are no stores close by that sell towels, sunglasses, or other beach essentials, so make sure you are fully prepared! Definite "must see" while in JeJu!

It s a very busy beach but it has lots of lifeguards which is always a good thing to know. The only reason why I am rating this beach a 4 is because there s a lot of trash which is very sad. Other than that it is fun to play at(they also rent out tubes).

Hamdeok is perhaps the most popular beach in Jeju but this was the first time I visited the island on summer during peak season. The beach is packed with families who took advantage of the low tide during the day (about ~30cm of water in a 50m stretch, at least on two weeks while was there) and let the kids in the water for a very enjoyable and risk-free time at the ocean.However I was surprised by the amount of "lifeguards" there. They will drag a security rope marking a no-swin zone after it starts getting "deep" (just after the water reaches your chest) which ok its a security measure specially with so many kids, but for adults who want to take a dip is horrible. They will start blowing their whistle and order you to go back even though half my body was above water.But the worst part is that they -- the lifeguards -- place beach umbrellas all across the beach and charge you –20000 (~20USD) to open and use them! It's already very weird that the lifeguards are also operating a rental service at the beach, but thing is they will NOT allow you to sit anywhere near them without paying (even not using the damn umbrellas) unless you look foreigner (white) so they don't loose face. I don't so I got reprimended like if was a Korean and they wouldn't leave my side until I moved.Isn't the beach a public space? This didn't happen just once but every day during my time there, overall an awful experience due to these threatening and autoritharian lifeguards.

Nice looking beach and lovely water, but don t recommend if you want to swim. Lifeguards are over authoritarian and you re only allowed in a 10x10 square with many other people (who have inflatables)! We had a pretty bad experience here where the lifeguards seemed to be picking on us for no reason. Also not allowed to sit/walk on certain parts of the beach. Overall poor experience only saved but spotted an octopus!

Cute little beach. Hamdeoks a nice area to chill out with a lot of cafes by the beach and you can eat with a view of the ocean. Koreans are not very big on swimming but you can jump in and go for a quick dip yourself. Only down side is sometimes there can be a bit of rubbish around. But recommended for a day trip

The beautif beach is lined with numerous hotels and restaurants. There are also activities like kayaking available. Do go there early at least before 10am to avoid the crowd.Easily accessible by public bus, it stops right in front of the beach entrance.

Ample parking space is what stood out when we parked our vehicle. Lots of restaurants across the road from beach. Family friendly. Good place to swim or just relax on the beach. Observed one strange thing that the sand on major part of the beach was covered with mesh. We were told it was to prevent it from flying off due to strong winds
Very beautiful beach for a short visit. Spend some time at the cafe , drink coffee and have some amazing bread

The beach was very beautiful. It has clear blue water and there were several restaurants and cafe where you can sit and enjoy the view. It was too windy when we visited though and the sand was everywhere. Spring may not be the best time to visit.
Amazing blue waters.  Be sure to Go to the delmoondo cafe there. Saw families catching small crabs there too.
Around 6.30 am there is no traffic and the road along the coast is nice for a morning run. Lots of volcanic stones.

Our first place of visit on Jeju Island. Took a 40min cab ride from Jeju. Later learnt about how Jeju intercity bus worked and took the bus after. Taxi ride was reasonable about US$10, getting a cab was a little tricky. Took a short walk up the hill overlooking the bay. And enjoyed a nice pastry breakfast at the cafe and bakery.
Stayed at Hotel at hamdeok beach, and i definitely didnt regret it though it is little far. But, the beach view is definitely worth it.

Well, it is a beach. With bus 101 roughly 15 minutes away from Jeju city.As far as I remember the beach feature something like a free gym and a few toilets.I did not see much of changing facilities, showers or lockers near the beach.In my view Hamdeok Beach is less good than the beaches in Busan.During my time in Hamdeok Beach I saw three surfers who practiced their skill.

First stop for sight seeing in jeju and found the beach was crowded, specially family with children. Went straight to Delmondo cafe to have a better view and it was also pretty crowded at the deck with chairs facing the beach. Looked for facility to change and for shower as the water was tempting clear and the weather hot. Sadly, only found changing room but no shower facility.
Lovely bay with 3 beaches. Cafes and bars back the beaches. Sands are white and seas lovely turquoise and blue. Very accessible.

We got so much help from the people to get here on the first day in Jeju. The view was really great and we felt released to enjoy the wind when walking through the trail. The horses and goats look so cozy around the trail.

We didn't plan to visit this beach. We had reserved a photoshoot at one location, and the photographer brought us here. We were amazed at the scenic view of the beach and spent almost half of our day. There are restroom and shower room near to the beach. Unfortunately, the shower room was locked.

That was the first place we visited after arriving at Jeju. Really enjoyed the chill atmosphere. In September, the weather was windy and a bit cool but still loved it. We also stopped by at Delmoondo cafe.
Beautiful beach where you can just relax and enjoy the scenery. Good for families but could get crowded.
Water was crystal clear - not too cold. Many great restaurants nearby. Floats available for rent. It was a little busy, but not too crazy.

This beach is a good one.  The sand is soft and powdery and the clear water very gradually gets deep which allows us to comfortably walk unusually far into the ocean.  The other special characteristic is that there is a big change from low tide to high tide.  The high tide, which occurred around 10 pm when we were there, completely covers up a pretty large beach area.  It's pretty fascinating.  The food and drink shops near the beach were a bit of a letdown for us because they were overpriced.

Spent the day here after going to to the Tuff Cone. I like how they have a lot of business by the beach and how the main beach is enclosed like a cove.  You have either the option to pay to sit under an umbrella, I believe it was 20,000 KRW for all day or you can just go find a shaded area to sit by the rocks.  We chose to latter as you wouldn t be in the sun and didn t have to spend the 20,000 KRW.  The water is beautiful and clear, there are plenty of lifeguards at the beach, and it s a family oriented beach.

Because of the location in the north part of the island, Hamdeok beach is the calmest beach ever that you can find. It is good for you to earn how to swim because it does not so much wave. Best time to visit: Fall (summer is too hot in Korea)

Come with my little girl, stayed at the hotel besides the beach.It is very hot in jeju in july, 35 degree in the afternoon.  We went to the beach at noon, water is clear and cool and the sand is smooth.Rental of umbrella and shelter at 25000w and 100000w respectively.  It is recommended to bring your own shelter.

It is a beautiful beach. Very crowded but still has space for moving around. Don't worry about jam-packed squeeze, no, it's not. But might be hard to get a umbrella table to occupy if you're going for a dip. A stroll is strongly recommended even if you don't swim.
It is an average beach, nothing special. The water wasn t warm.  There is a lot of sand, not just rocks as in some areas of Jeju.

I am in love with Hamdeok.  I have been so for over 6 years now.  The water is often sparkling blue and green.  The sand is soft.  The sunsets there are fantastic.  Plenty of activities to do/food to eat/drinks to drink.Pro Tip:  Head up to the oreum on the right of the beach for a fantastic view!

This is a beautiful white sand beach. Although there were many local tourist, no one was swimming so I was not sure what was happening. The beachfront is lined with restaurants and hotels. Even the night scene was beautiful with the lighted building. I would recommend visiting this place when you are in Jeju

I live quite close to this beach and really love it. On days ending on 1 and 6, there is a traditional market which is nice. Many restaurants to choose from, as well as an Olive Young, Spanish restaurant, Starbucks, etc however I prefer buying CU drinks and sitting in the sand. Sunset is AMAZING here.
this beach is very shallow up to 1 km from the shore with white sand. basically quite safe even for those who are not good smimmers and kids

This is so amazing beach to walking around and relax even 11 pm we still walk and feel so peaceful and good food and good clean bar I always stay here when ever come to jeju and you can take the bus anywhere you want to go around jeju it s beautiful island and I am from Hawaii tham you know what I mean alright
A fun beach, with lots of shallows for swimming and playing in the water.  The park is well kept, there are great coffee shops and restaurants. A very nice sandy beach which is hard to find in Jeju.
this is the nice beach evervi seen, all water us so clean.beside have lots of resturant , hotel.. mini shop

We went to visit many beaches during this trip. This is the only one we visited twice and would love to come again in the future to stay around this area! Nice cafe by the beach, nice trial you can climb up and many great photo spots! Don t miss this spot when you visit Jeju!

It s an easy drive from Jeju City. There s a nice park and some restaurants and stores. I was there in February and it was cold, windy, and even snowing, but the beach was still beautiful with the black cliffs and the white sand. I m sure it d be perfect in warmer weather!
Lovely beach for an evening visit. Clean, picturesque view with nice cafes around . Would recommend a visit

This was rated as one of the top 3 to visit in Jeju so we actually stayed at the nearby Airstay Hamdeok Hotel.  It  was very nice.  The beach is clean and had pristine waters and black rocks.  The sand was fine and felt good to walk on with your bare feet.  There were some really nice picturesque views so we took a ton of photos. There was a connected path to a hill and it allowed for some decent small hikes.  We went in March so the flowers on the hill were blooming with yellow and purple colors.  There were also some white flower blossoms coming out from the trees. With the ocean or the city views in the background from the hill, it allowed for some very unique photos for your memories.  After the little hike, we played around in the water on the beach and it was nice because it was low tide and you could hang out in one of the exposed sand bars. It was very pretty and relaxing. Definitely a must see if you're in Jeju!
You could enjoy your holiday in jeju island.specially hamduck beach is the best.Come and see it and relax at Jeju island !!!
beautiful beach, clear waters witha great view. a cafe is nearby where you can sit by the beachside and enjoy a hot cup of coffee with some nice pastries

This place is accessible (1.5 hours away from Jeju Bus Terminal/Airport by bus 101.  It was too cold to swim in october (and I didn't bring my trunks) but I hope to swim here another time!  Cafe Delmoondo is just next to the beach - I went there cos I needed to use the toilet (and bought an ice-cream just to be a customer), but food was so good there I ended up having lunch!  This is a nice place to hang out if you are staying in N Jeju because it was not too crowded (at least not in october), and because the view was really nice (the sea was emerald green, as the blogs say, and quite breathtaking)

I would rate this the best swimming and relaxing beach on Jeju. It is really beautiful with 3 different beaches to enjoy. As there are 3 it is generally not as crowded as other beaches. There is also a hill to climb and many food and drink options. A Really wonderful place
We stumble upon this beach enroute to the caves. We didnt regret it a bit. The view is stunning and one of the most beautiful beach we have ever seen.
Not a lot to see at this time. Probably a lot more activity during the summer season. Nice sandy beach.

We spent a very nice day at the beach. Nice white sand, warm water. There is a place to rent lifejackets and floating articles. Not too much people in september.A lot of pkaces to eat/have a drink nearby.
Beautiful beach and surroundings!Very clean and vivid colours You can also try some water sports here, but seems like you had to stay around the renting area
Its a nice beach, a bit small, lots of kids but nice. When we went the waves weren't very large, so didn't bother going in the water. But we walked around and there's a nice park nearby.
Nothing really interesting, just a small sandy beach with lots of koreans taking a swimm and playing....
Spent several afternoons here. When you have nice sunny weather for the day the beach is a good place for young kids - the water is calm and clear. Highly recommended.

No shower only feet wash. Only white people into the sea. I think there is no bikini sold in Jehu. If you want to meet bikini girl, go Taiwan. Only white people wear a bikini here. Even kids not. There is water activities center with cannon, crab boat, surfing boat. But no business today.
Great beach for walking, swimming and relaxing. Volleyball tournament there once a year :) Many great places to eat and stay in the area.

The best we have seen in Jeju.Though the water was a bit too cold for us to swim, it's great for wading during low tide.You can even rent clear bottom kayak to paddle around.There are lots of convenient stores, burger and coffee places and other local eateries around there.Definitely worth a visit.
Not easy to find a nice beach on Jeju, but this one is one of not many. Really beautiful, wasn't crowded while we were there, many restaurants nearby.
There are 3 beaches here , also a hiking trail where u can see horses on the cliffs. just the perfect family spot.

The main part of this beach is full of kids and you will need to pay to sit on the beach...(there are table services). Also, the area is restricted. You can only go to a certain area. Instead, if you go to another part, which is 10mins by walk, you can enjoy more and free to sit... This beach does not have many waves.
The depth of water is shallow after u swim. towards ocean for 100 meter u can still stand on the sand
small & clean water but sand just so so. since cloudy so that the color not too significant but still well enough. one of jeju beach but i don't see quite much special on it.
Very small beach. Lots of families attending the beach as well. Pretty easy to get to by bus. Worth seeing.
A super crowded place. I do not recommend it unless you like crowded beaches to show off or meet :)The infrastructure are fine (drinks, food, etc)
A nice beach with white & fine sand. We were having our relaxing tea time at Cafe Delmoondo,  admiring the scenic view of the beach.

The beach is next to the main hotel area and suitable for swimming. It has soft white sand, mixed with some lava stones (where small crabs hide). At my visit it was almost empty even though the water was warm and very clear.
This really is a great beach, one of the best on the island, a fantastic place to camp or hire one of the caravans there.
A nice day out in the beach. Lots of people playing beach volleyball. One can spend an afternoon enjoying coffee and the ocean

It's a very long beach with very gentle slope; you can walk pretty far towards the sea. The water is clear and has very beautiful blue color. The nearby hill offers a (short) trail and a fantastic view, both towards the sea and Mt. Halla.
Nice small beach. Clear water. We had sunny day so the beach and water together  was very beautiful. Have a walk there it improves your day.

we stayed at Black sands area and walked by Oll trail 18-19 to this beach. beach looks nice although water is cold and of course could not enjoy it fully. lots of restaurants around obviously overpriced for coming tourists.

Small area with lovely white sands - not good for swimming on a windy day, but the views are great and there were no crowds. Some small food shops close by and you are close to walking trails and terrific rock scapes by the water. Loads of plastic rubbish and litter take away much of the beauty of the place, but it is still very worth a visit.

We visited on a particularly windy day which made it unfit for swimming. However, the landscape itself was great to look at, especially the black volcanic rock contrasting with the white sand and turquoise waters. I'm sure this beach would be stunning in better weather.

I loved Hamdeok Beach. We live in China and visited during Golden Week, assuming the rest of China would follow us to Jeju (as is typical during ANY holiday traveling in China) and we were pleasantly surprised to find that there were little to no Chinese tourists, or really any tourists in the neighborhood. It was quiet, clean and so peaceful! I would return again in a heartbeat.

Not that big, but a nice place to stay on a sunny day. In april it was not that crowded. You got a beautiful view on the Ocean, the green hill you can climb (part of the Ole Trail - a lot of handy paths) and the vulcano rocks where a lot of married couples are getting their pictures. Also a plus: the Caf챕 Belmoondo (not a typo) with rather high priced but delicious drinks & food and a beautiful terrace. Funny fact: there are a lot of wide plastic rags on the sand: easy to walk and sit, but a rather strange view.

I go here every day to walk up the steep hill to the right of the beach for exercise.  It's the start of the No. 19 Olle Trail.  I usually always see bride and grooms having their photos taken on the beach and in the fields of rapeseed.  Views from the top of the hill are amazing.  Sometimes if there are horses around I'll pick grass and feed them in exchange for a little pat and nuzzle from them.  If you look carefully there are quite a few different flowers around.  If you pick a green rapeseed that hasn't yet flowered and peel the stalk you can eat the stalk.  It tastes like sweet brocalli.  The cherry blossoms are lovely there too if you happen to be there in early April.  The water is clear.  I like to feed and water some of the stray dogs.  It kills me that I can't give them a home.  They appreciate a bit of a cuddle too but you can see their priority is getting food.  There are some very good restaurants in Hamdeok as well.  Ive put a pic of one of the ones on the main street of Hamdeok. .its a local one that serves a set menu at lunch time and its very good.  The sunsets are spectacular.

Very pretty beach on a sunny day. The colour of the water is so beautiful. Nicely prep walkway all along the whole beach area. Lots of places for coffee and a quick lunch. We had dinner at a local eatery, the owner was nice and friendly.  He helped BBQ our black skin pork belly for us. So yummy with water Kimchi and beer.

It's not hot or cold and the water is warm. It's gorgeous, you can really go far in the water and it's not deep and you can see all the way to the bottom. I'm coming back tomorrow for another swim. Worth the visit!

We were here in October, so we weren't swimming. We drove by here one day to check it out, a day or two after a typhoon hit, and the beach was trashed a bit (just from trees and debris and stuff), but people were cleaning it up and there were still lots of people enjoying the beach. It looks like a nice place to spend a day, and there seemed to be a bunch of restaurants and cafes dotting the beach as well. We stopped at one of the cafes for a coffee and to enjoy the view of the water for a bit.
Great beach Great viewsAnd amazing picture spotsI recommend having a coffee at a cafe dolmondo ..  there which is right over the beach Beautiful scenery
Thought I was in the Carribean. The beach is segmented into small sections but beautiful nonetheless.

Visited Hamdeok Beach (⑤댁) with my boyfriend. We took a walk around the beach. It was really windy and cold. The wind was strong. The beach is very clean and beautiful. The waters are clear. We took some pictures there and we happened to see couple having wedding photoshoot (with the beautiful scenery).Many people from various age groups visited this beach. It is a nice place to take a walk and chill out. There are hotels, shops, convenience stores, cafes and restaurants nearby the beach. There is also public toilet nearby the beach (near the carpark). We drove there. It is very convenient and we can get some snacks while chilling out there.

Even though it was rainy weather during the days spent in Jeju, hamdeok beach compensated for the bad weather with with pretty coastline, wide range of eateries, cafes and also an olle-gil trail to explore the area. Drive along the coastline for a scenic view too. We stayed in co'op City hotel for a night, comfortable hotel where offers guest free beer in the evening. Beach area is less than 30mins drive to Jeju airport.

Went in the morning. The view is breathtaking. Must visit. Korean artists love this place for a good reason. Featured in some korean shows as well. It's very pretty. Packed some sandwiches, lay a mat, have a breakfast and feel the breeze.

The beach area as well as the water are looking clean. The sand is white. We did not go in since it was late October. The view is nice and the neighbourhood has shops and restaurants available. There is a coffee shop directly at the beach where you can rest if you find a place to rest. Usually the shop is quite crowded. At night time some fireworks ongoing. We had the Golden Tulip hotel and we were enjoying the view to the beach every morning.

We went to three or four different beaches on the island and this one hands down is the best. We didn't swim as it was in September already but spent a couple of hours strolling on the boardwalk. There are plenty of eateries across the street from the beach and some were on the beach side as well. The view was fantastic and definitely worth a visit. Also, parking was quite easy as well. We stopped for coffee (of course) and sweets at the nice coffee shop right on the beach before leaving and sitting there drinking coffee and watching sunset was a real treat.

We went there after a typhoon so beach was a little mixed up. It was a bit too windy for comfortable swimming, but all in all the cafes around the place and the atmosphere on the beach were good. And it was easy to get there from jeju city with buses. We visited in the beginning of October and it was still warm enough for just relaxing on the beach.

First thing we've noticed is how civilized this beach is - loads of restaurants, shops , cafes nearby. We were lucky enough to visit it in September, when holiday season is over for majority of Korean guys - so, it was not that crowded. Water was very clean and the only downside, that it was already a little bit cold. If you walk few hundred meters in a right hand direction from the main beach (towards the hill), you would see a camping ground with even smaller strip of sand - and we were absolutely alone there.
Really nice beach with a lot of restaurants near by.The water was really clear and the beach was clean so good for snorkeling and swimming.

Had a long bikecycle trip from Jeju-do city to which I ended at this beach.It's like a small bay with white sand beach. was pretty crowded although it wasn't the season. water sport wasn't operational

This place is truly breathtaking, it was easy to get here by taxi or bus from the main terminal. Once you arrive you'll be mesmerized by the beauty of this beach. It's also a good option for a rainy day as there are lots of cafes nearby to shelter you from the weather but still be able to enjoy the view.

After the unpleasant beach at Udo, arriving at Hamdeok beach was a delight. With just a short trip from Jeju city this little beach village is amazing. With many restaurants and cafes along the water, one could spend a nice long day here. The water is nice and clean with showers and changing rooms available nearby.

Lovely place (June). Water was warm and beautiful. Walk a little bit and you will find more places and not so crowded. There aren't many restaurants for foreigners. I recommend to try the burgers at the red container (can't remember the name). If you don't enjoy fireworks, better don't do after 7pm. There are better things to see and do in Jeju but some people don't understand that!!!

Peaceful and clean.  The water was refreshing.  The sand was fine.  The sun was shining and it just doesn't get much better than playing on this beach!  Perfect tide pools for small children to play in.  Snorkeling for the grown ups.  Plenty of places to eat and drink nearby.  Just lovely!
Very very nice beach! It is a must!!! We loved it and also my kids. If I could I'll spend more visits to this place. My kids didn't want to leave!

Beautiful beach, many people during summer but still acceptable. Very good for children because the water is very shallow. The only thing i didn't like ia that i couldn't even cool down in the water because it was so hot, like in a bath tub.There is no sunlounger, so if you want to tan, you need a mat.

The area of the beach is nice but the sandy part and the open water space is soooo small... You cannot even go for a swim here. The water was dirty and full of water plants. I honestly thinking every beach in Europe is way more attractive than this. Italy, Greece, Croatia....Have they actually seen clear azure waters?! If this is jejus prettiest beach then im really sorry for koreans

I guess we are spoilt in Australia, was taken here whilst on a business trip to Jej-do island by Koreans , though it was nothing special unfortunately. But as I said we are spoilt for beaches in Aust.

The beach is beautiful on a sunny day - calm, clean, safe and relaxing. Suitable for couples or family with seniors/kids. We got there by bus no. 10 from the city. Very convenient with good facilities. You pay a small fee to shower otherwise the usual toilets are available if you just want to have a change of clothes. If it rains there are plenty of cafes to take shelter at.We spent a few hours at the beach in the afternoon and had a seafood banquet for dinner at one of the many restaurants close by during sunset.

The beach was fine and no rocks, but a lot of seaweed. The water was clear and very shallow, so it's good for kids, but I was a bit bored since I like to play in the waves.I think they should clean the beach more often since I found too much trash around
Nice beach not far away from the airport. Too overcrowded during the swimming season in Korea, you can find stores and places to eat around the beach.

The beach is nice, clean and not too crowded but a bit small. Many hotels and villas are located along this beach. Therefore, if you want to be stick on it, just take one hotel here, normally just 5 minutes walking. A good place to relax and have romantic time.

This beach is a great place for tourists! Upon arriving there are lots of vendors with delicious food and things you might need for the beach (towels, hats, beach mats, swim suits, booze, etc). The main beach is usually very crowded (understandably). I like to go to the beach to the right, it's just a 5 minute walk on the sidewalk, clearly visible with a clear understanding it's leading to another beach. This part of the beach seems to be less crowded with all of the same benefits! Great place to relax, enjoy the sun, and swim in the water!
What a place! Blue ocean with white sand. Breathtaking view. It's really a great place for couple. Should use taxi for going there for shorten time.

C1 ( 2016.07.12 ) This beach was smaller than I think, but there had good view and fresh air. Many people enjoyed sea bathing, and well managed, I think. The view with beach and cliff was beautiful, and many famous restaurant and cafe was operating. Good beach in Jeju area.

This beach is just right in front of my hotel (Golden Tulip) and this is a very calm and relaxing beach to walk around.There were not many people and I went there during the late afternoon so the weather is not too hot and it was very very nice.
Pretty beach and calm water. It's nice to sit and chill by Cafe Delmoondo.  We spent hours here.  You can just sit or walk on a trail or the street with restaurants.
The beach is superb front of my hotel. Just walking 5 minutes.. a lot of restaurant here. The water is so cool and an amazing view. Not so crowded.

Came here to checkout the views and totally loved it. A nice small town to chill at with lots of parking if you're driving. Many restaurants, cafes and food trucks along the beach. Beautiful white sand and blue waters. Not crowded. Definitely coming back here! Didn't get enough of it.

We only spent 4 nights in Jeju and happened to pass by this place on our way to the city center. We decided to spend half a day soaking up the sun. These 5 hours were a highlight! The town was pretty quiet and the beach wasn't too crowded. Beautiful views! There was a nice restaurant on the water to get snacks. Water was refreshing! Note: I noticed a camp ground on the far right side of the beach. Cool idea for the future. BE AWARE there are very large spiders over near that boardwalk. Yikes!

Hamdeok can be reached from airport by bus or taxi in 30 minutes. There are many hotels, convenient stores and restaurants in that area so We can get accommodation easily.We were staying at Ramada Hamdeok, about 1 km walking distance from the beach. Strolling at sunset time was very enjoyable. Nice weather, nice view, not too crowded. Just fine.We were hanging out until dinner time, took barbecued seafoods at outdoor table by the beach. To order the food and communicate need extra effort because we can only speak english, but the Resto staff can speak mandarin well. The food was good, drinking some soju and babunja make us warm...
Hamduk Beach is very wide in Jeju-do.This beach's color blue and clean.I swam and swam and swam.There are many pub and food-court.

There are no words to describe the beauty of this beach. OMG a little piece of heaven. The water, the sand, the view was soooo beautiful and peaceful. Loved it!!!!I'm a girl who grow up  on a beautiful Mediterranean island and Hamdeok beach made me feel like home!!! Please take me back there!!!

It was pretty cold even in May at the beach due to the strong winds. No one was there to swim but still it's a beautiful place to snap pictures and nice cafes surrounding the beach to simply chill and relaxI do not if I was there too early b4 the cleaners or .. Anyway the beach line was littered with trash and full of seaweeds making the walk on the shoreline kinda displeasing.
Had a few hours before catching flight, chose this beach because of location, but turns out it was a good choice. the rocks, and clear water was something you do not see in the US

We come from a country surrounded by beaches but this one for us - topped it all. Its so calming with its cliffs overlooking the ocean. One can go up the mountain trail or can just sit along the benches near the cliff. The beach has white sand and during low tide one can walk far . For us, this beach is worth revisiting.

I was underwhelmed by this place (and the island in general) but then I live in Thailand and am used to great beaches. There is nothing special here, I certainly saw no "white sand" and "turquoise water." Just a very average beach and an overpowering smell of the seaweed they harvest here. I would skip this - and Jeju altogether frankly.

This beach, East of Jeju city, on the North coast, is a real gem. Our favourite part is the smaller bay to the East of the main beach. You can rent a static caravan right on the beach there, with an unbeatable, uninterrupted view of the sea. Great snorkelling around the rocks to the right and you can walk up the small oreum further to the right. The main beach has a good eatery that sells Western food and Stella Artois!

I hadn't heard all that much about this beach and I was really pleasantly surprised, in a big way. The beach itself is fairly wide, and the sand is great. Moreover, the water is crystal clear, and the water is warm, so if you actually want to go swimming, it's a great spot (unfortunately I didn't have enough time). But this place is more than just a beach. Right behind the beach is a nice little town so it is lively and you have shops and dining options there. On the beach you have a nice fancy  coffeeshop that is perfectly located, directly overlooking the sea. Add to that the rocks on each side of the beaches, as well as the small mountain to the East, so this place is not only perfect for relaxing, but also for taking pictures.
A small beach. Crystal clear water. The wind was very strong when we visited that area. As it was winter, nobody was in the water.

This place was AWESOME!!! Do yourself a favor though -- stay at the resort that is immediately there. We didn't and regretted it for 4 straight days ... This beach is really good and we spent 6-8 hours there a day!

This place was gorgeous! It is a Korean beach so it is crowded please keep that in mind. I am a Floridian and we have some of the best and most peaceful beaches on earth. But this, even for me, was truly an experience. One the amount of people was impressive but less crowded than Busan beach. Try to get here early and pay the money for the umbrella spot. They all cost the same, but you wanna be in the first row so you can see the water.The water is truly beautiful. The color is very different than floridan green blue waters. The ocean here is the deepest darkest blue I've ever seen, and the part that meets the beach is a light bright crystal blue. There are many families and watching the kids is really cute. We spent a lot of time floating around. Next time I would bring a float so we could inner tube around like the locals did.You can order food and the vendors or restaurants will bring them to your umbrella.Fried chicken is a must for Koreans on the beach. We actually were super hungry before going (next time we will do it differently) so we went to Korean food chain Mom's Touch that serves amazing crispy fried chicken in bbq glaze with pickled radishes. So on the beach we got ice cream and fresh fruits.Warning for travelers: more of a cultural heads up. There are showers- like beaches in America have...you do have to pay to use them, but there are no private changing rooms or showers it's all a show for anyone to see. Now it is gender separated, but don't be shocked to find you'll have to strip down in front of strangers. My husband is Korean and didn't warn me, but it was too late once I walked in, plus he already paid for my shower and I really needed a shower. But here's the thing you'll notice that no one cares about you, and no one looks at anyone. Just shower off, do your thing and you'll be outta there in no time. If this is too much for you to handle...then skip the shower and head back to your place to shower in your comfort level.

I came in October so i cannot swim here but seeing only the beach has satisfied me. It is a nice beach with white sand, water is very clean and clear. It would be nice if i can come back here in summer.

Hamdeok Beach is really splendid! Clear aquamarine water, super fine sand, mountain in the  background.... the view is to die for! You will find beautiful volcanic rocks all around the area. Your experience at Hamdeok (⑤) will vary wildly. It's a beach where things happen. Even swimming. Pros: Hamdeok is surrounded by some fairly muscular resort action for a beach of this size, and it gets more than its fair share of activities. Volleyball tournaments, beach parties, and above all the music festivals. If you happen to be around for the Stepping Stone Festival in July, go. The best concerts I have seen in Korea have been at Hamdeok. The audiences are happy, diverse, family friendly, and enthusiastic, and for the most part enjoy very moderate amounts of both testosterone and alcohol poisoning - emphasis on "for the most part". Hamdeok is fairly central. It's close to Jeju City and many of the activities and sites that make Jeju a growing tourist destination, but far enough away from the airport that you are not always drowning in swarms of airplanes and their contents. You can find a variety of decent places to eat in the vicinity. The sand and surf is a very pleasant combination of white, blue and green. If you've been to Australia or Hawaii, you probably won't be impressed. However, for Korea it's superb, and for Jeju it's a solid place to go if you want to do some casual swimming. But take note: this is not where you go for snorkeling or quiet sunbathing. Hamdeok does boast some strong outdoor lighting for evening swims, which is nice, as well as some convenient and beautiful coastal walks/hikes, often punctuated with spectacular sunsets. Cons: This is a small beach which can very easily become overcrowded, or even insanely overcrowded. It can also be noisy enough during the weekend to drive away even the most dedicated of extroverts. The first time I went to Hamdeok I became convinced that the loud speakers - all blaring entirely different music and/or announcements at the same time - were actually designed to create overlapping kill zones. There are tables with umbrellas for rent on the beach, as well as stands with various floating devices, but they are all of average quality at best, and I found the entire set up disruptive of the beach experience. The swimming is fair, but don't expect to do much more than just swimming. I've seen waves at Hamdeok, but not often, and certainly not much in the way of water sports like surfing. And keep in mind that Korean lifeguards are assiduous in their monitoring of swimmers - i.e. you won't be able to go out too far before the whistles blow. The bathroom facilities are weak, with austere changing areas, and ice cold showers that you have to pay for. Bring your own shampoo, etc. Hamdeok is also growing in popularity, so the current balance of tourists-to-beach may soon tip into an unacceptable range. There are already times when driving along the beachfront road becomes an exercise in patience and defensive driving, often due to gallivanting hordes of people under the influence of tourism, which is far worse than alcohol when it comes to lowering inhibitions and promoting idiocy. There has also been a troubling increase in the kind of businesses that want to capitalize on the "tourist beach experience", selling tawdry souvenirs, poorly handled food, and watered down drinks made with the worst commercially available ingredients they can find. You will know them by their flashing lights and loud, thumpingly generic club music being boom-boxed into your face. However, considered these places a "pro" if you enjoy the spring break mentality and mild diarrhea. Lastly, the weather of Jeju is capricious, so just accept the fact that it will probably rain at least once as you storm the beach. But that's just Jeju.

Having never seen a lava tube cave before, we were very keen to go here. We live on Jeju Island so it wasn't a terribly long trek to get there. Not exactly on the beaten path, but not too far off either. Once you arrive, there's a small information center that explains the history, science, and mythology surrounding the cave. There's also a restaurant on site, which we didn't use, and then there's the short walk to the cave entrance. Here's the only reason I didn't give this a rating of 5. I have some minor mobility issues stemming from multiple knee surgeries and the entrance to the cave is a fairly lengthy and sometimes steep set of stairs that can be wet and slippery. Once you're in the cave, however, it's not too bad to traverse unless you have much more significant mobility issues. There are a few places where you have to go up ramps or small sets of stairs, all of which are industrially produced. The cave itself is quite dark and damp, and I'd recommend long sleeves if you're prone to feeling cold. Definitely wear good walking/hiking shoes as the cave does not have a full walkway installed. You're walking over ground that is solidified lava. It's about a 1km walk to the end of tourist access where there is an impressive lava column, which they claim is the largest in the world. There's an observation deck approaching it, but you cannot go past and actually touch the column. Along the way, there are decent informational placards in multiple languages, including English. The explanations are reasonable for most people, including children, to understand. Our kids, ages 7 and 5, enjoyed the experience, particularly because you could get right up beside the cave walls and touch them, along with other artifacts inside the cave. For anyone interested in geology or volcanos, it's a great experience. Price is reasonable too. We paid 12,000 won, which is currently a little over $10 US, for four people. Supposedly children under 7 are free with ID, but we didn't ask about that for our younger one.

There is good lighting and regular interpretive signs.  Wear good footwear as it it wet underfoot even on hot and dry days.  It is also nice a cool on a summer day.

It is beautiful,  seeing nature transformed.  Wear comfortable shoes with traction,  closed toes. It can be slippery and the rocks can be slick. Bring a light jacket bc it is cool down there.
