All that allows you just to take in the majesty of the space and lava formations in the hushed atmosphere, reminiscent of a great cathedral. 1km from start to finish then 1km back.

I had been to better more fun and interesting cave. There was no proper pathway and not many lights along the road and thus might be slippery to walk in the uneven rocks in the darkness in most parts of the cave. Due to the absence of lights and also the uneven road (rocks in their natural state) we didn't get rinser much except for some specially stationed rocks. The cave was very very long but only 1km open to tourists and though it's 1km one way and you have to walk another 1km back. Do wear proper shoes and bring along a torch.

This was part of a day tour. After climbing a mountain and being someone who doesn't exercise, this place was too much for me. Like mentioned in other reviews, this place is dark, the path is naturally uneven with puddles of water from rain and natural water. I came out earlier to enjoy some hot ramen at the convenience stall and didn't regret it.

We took the public bus here. It took about an hour from Jeju Bus Terminal. We got off at the stop called "Manjanggul Cave Entrance". However, it's another 2.5km walk to the cave. There's a very infrequent bus that goes all the way there but you're either going to have to walk (hard in the heat), grab a taxi (regularly around, and I think 3000 krw) or hitchhike! We chose to take a chance and see if someone would stop and give us a lift ( which they did).It's 2000krw entrance fee which is very good value. You get to walk 1 km into the lava tube. It's a bit slippery and wet so wear shoes with a decent grip. The cave is lit enough to see without needing to bring your own torch. There's also information boards throughout the cave.It's lovely and cool in the cave which is an added bonus as it was quite hot outside. I highly recommend a visit to these caves.

Really great to see and well maintained. Wonderful visit. Went on a rainy day and it was still a pleasant experience. The bus to the cave is very slow and infrequent so you either have to walk or take an expensive taxi which is inconvenient, but otherwise very good

I'm from Hawaii, but this cave was very impressive, not to mention a welcome reprieve from the heat and humidity!Walking on wet lava rock is not for the faint-of-heart, so wear a good pair of tennis shoes that can provide some traction, because it is slippery!

I really enjoyed my visit here. I've never visit a volcanic cave before but its an very cool place (literally!). The temperature in the cave is much cooler than outside, although be careful, because they keep it quite dark so it can be difficult to walk on without good shoes.

This was an amazing experience. The walk through the lava caves is a very enlightening experience and we had a very good time. Slightly difficult terrain to walk on but nothing too dangerous. On the whole would definitely recommend this attraction when at Jeju.

This incredible cave flew with lava before. It is typical Jeju world heritage and must visit. The lava flew through all the tunnels and forms interesting geographic features. And another lava melted the roof of the channel and runs down to the first layer of lava. As usual, 2000 for an adult ticket.

I find walking in this lava cave is interesting as it is so cool inside and surprisingly there is no bad smell as it is rather wet. The cave produces it's on air conditioning as the temperature inside is around 15-17 Celsius. Some areas are well lighted and some are not, proper walking shoes are needed as there are many uneven areas along the path provided. Good experience for the ones who loves outdoor!
We visited as part of a conference group. It was amazing seeing the size and beauty of the place. It was wet and cold so definitely good shoes and jacket. Well worth a visit.
The place is nice and well maintained, it was a bit cold down there so i would suggest a light sweater and comfy shoes as the floor was uneven with lava stone and made it hard to walk

This lava tube is huge.  The part open to the public is a bit over half a mile in although the entire system is much larger.  The natural formations are fascinating and beautiful in their own way.  The place is "other worldly" and so different from life on the surface. Be aware that there are many steps (some steep) down and up.

The lava tube is different from other lime stone or erupted caves I seen before, this one is very big and the its formation and feature is fantastic.  Try to avoid the high crowd and prepare jacket, poncho and hiking shoes.  We took good camera and tripok to take picture.

My family visited Manjanggul Cave in late July 2017. It was sizzling, humid day, and Majanggul was the best solution for my tired family. It was cool and refreshing inside. It was quite big and long to explore. we had great fun. One of complaint was that it was quite crowded, but no wonder that everyone wanted to be inside the cave during the hot summer days.

My husband, 17 month old son, and I visited the caves and had a nice time. It was different from caves I'd seen before because of the lava that formed this one. The walk is 1 km of uneven pathways in dim lighting, but there didn't seem to be a problem for any of the elderly or very young we saw. My husband carried our son on his back in a carrier. Be prepared for the cool air though. We regret not packing light jackets, so we rushed actually rushed through to avoid our son getting sick. We would have loved to examine the structures more. Nice experience overall!
very unique cave. the cave's lenght around 1,4 km. You will feel the sensation of cold air while down the cave. Don't forget to wear comfy shoes and jacket.
If u have  visited any cave in China, anyone of them is much better than this one. Since the one in korea only open a tiny portion to tourists

First time to see a lava tube. It was not the most impressive thing to see but it was such an eye opener for me! Learned a lot about this amazing geological formation. Information boards explain well the interesting features in the cave. The entrance fee (KRW 2000) is an absolute bargain. A must see in Jeju! Despite the summer heat, it was very cold inside! Bring a layer!

I highly recommend visiting Manjanggul cave while visiting Jeju island. It's a very interesting piece of nature that I was very impressed with. It's basically a lava tube formed from molten lava of volcano that pierced the earth surface and now is a long cave. It's very well maintained and open to public for about 1.5 km walk one way. When you enter the cave, you'll realize it's pretty "cool" as well as "cold". Definitely recommend bringing a light jacked if visiting during summer hours. Inside, pathway is quite rough to walk, however it's easily doable for adults while if your traveling with kids below 3, this might not be an ideal place to visit. Inside, you'll also find lot of information about the type of volcanic rocks formed that will refresh your high school geography or you might learn new information, if you've had not already. The whole walk can be done in 30-60 minutes.

I find this cave beautiful as it is made by nature. It is just 1km long, it is good for a short trip. The place is cold, that's why Koreans go here in the summer. If you get bored easily, this place is not for you as the cave doesn't have a variety of rock formations.Furthermore, if you do not like to walk in rocky paths, you may not appreciate this. This place is dimly lit to preserve the cave, so you have to be careful. Overall, a good place to visit if you appreciate nature.

although it just open 1/3 of area for tourist but there was quite big & long cave actually. slipping & uneven floor sometimes. light setting not bad compared with other country. it was cold esp for you need to take walk over 1hour if you don't do fast pace to finish it. actually, it has 1km. the rock & lava also impressive. good to take time for it.and i reached here at 11am, maybe the sunlight with cool air. i saw some spot light before went inside the cave. that was beautiful.
The lava tube is very interesting to walk around. It can get pretty chilly underground so prepare accordingly.

In my opinion, there are two world heritage sites that visitors to Jeju must visit. One is Manjanggul Cave and the other one is Seongsan Illchubong. Manjanggul Cave is unique as it was formed by lava movement thousands of years ago. It provides an insight into Jeju's geographical structure. The temperature in the cave could be chilly, so bring a jacket along. Visitors to the cave usually walked for about 2 km to reach the end, where photos with a large stalactite pillar could be taken. Other features in the cave include lava formations that look like elephant feet, turtles and book shelves.
Our first stop on was this place. the driver took a couple of photos and then we entered into the cave. we were thrilled. we took 40 minute to cover the entire tube.

I didn't know what to expect in a lava tube, and I was totally amazed and intrigued. We decided to make the trip by public transport from Seogwipo for the adventure, and we enjoyed every moment. There are good facilities at the cave entrance - nice toilets, two food outlets and an information centre. Extremely impressive . It is nothing like a limestone cave, and does not have that enclosed feeling. It does require some stairs to be climbed, and the floor is a little uneven and dark, but more cavernous than cave like.

It only costs about $2 to visit (separate from transportation costs).  Very well maintained site but still a rough surface that requires suitable footwear and it can be wet and slippery in some spots; also quite cool.  This is a very impressive channel to walk through and imagine the lava flowing and leaving the characteristic marks and artifacts along it path.  Dim lighting gives a neat eerieness that somehow makes it even more exciting to explore.  Various well constructed boardwalks with built in floor lights improve access.  The entire tour is about 1 km in each direction.  Very interesting experience.
In fact it felt almost chilly as we took the steps down 20 metres into the cavity.  Good for escaping from the summer heat.
We went during the spring festival where we had free entry to the caves.It was really amazing and with lots of details so a guide is not needed and you can enjoy at your own pace.

It was a little bit difficult to get there. We came by bus and had to walk 2,5 km from the bus stop, but luckily a taxi came by. We paid 4000 won to get from the bus stop to the cave entrance. It was even more of a problem to get out of the area, as all signs are in Korean, so it's impossible to find out how to get around. We decided to go to Jeju City to find a quicker way back to Seogwipo (it took us 1,5 hour to get there). There are only a few taxis coming to Majangul Caves and they charged 30000 won for a trip to Jeju City. We asked some other tourists to share, so 15000 won each. Was it worth it? Well, we liked it. It was a different experience, but interesting to see the lava formations, read the information signs and imagine the flow of the lava in the chilly environment. I'm travelling with a 14 years old teenager and she liked it too.Important: Forget about your flipflops and T-Shirt. Bring your jacket and a good pair of walking shoes.

You need to bring jacket that day we went even if its summer still cold inside, wear rubber shoes easy for you to walk, though there's not much inside to see, young kids will not enjoy for sure they will just be tired walking very long cave.

It is such a beautiful place to go! The scenery inside the cave is breathtaking and it is unbelievable for such a view. It is a bit cold and dark tho, but it has light installed along the pathway. A very nice place!
It's a lava cave, national herritage. Nothing special in there, it was dark and only rocks along the way. You need to be careful because the floor was wet and slippery.
History behind very interestingGood to see onceShort visitWay of making the visit more attractive

The cave is really cold and I love it. It's really good. And daddy put me on his shoulders. I was kind of scared. If you bring your kids to Jeju it will be lots of fun. It kind of looks like a mystery to me. The lava shapes are good and look like they are made by people. But they are really made by nature. I can't believe my eyes. The end. Done.

First of all the cave is not accessible by public transportation. We got dropped off the main road by public bus but it is still a long way in by foot.  My expectation was we will be dropped very close to it but it wasn't. The cave was ok.  Nothing special.

This lava tube is different from a cave. it is as big as the new york subway in headroom and width. runs for 7 over km but tourist are allowed to see over 1 km in a safe environment. The ground is most and uneven in some locations so wear comfortable hiking shoes. Entrance is very reasonable for this UNESCO world heritage site!

While it is not spectacular like other caves around the world that are open to tourists, they are worth visiting due to their geographical nature.They are easy for families to visit, no bending over or crawling necessary.The temperature inside stays around 16-18c all year round. It is always damp, and most areas are dimly lit.

It is a must visit place and I enjoyed it though I didn't spend as much time as I wanted.  It is damp and so a jacket is needed to keep you warm.  The ground is unlevel so walking with a good pair of grip shoes is a must as some parts are wet.I have been to the Shenandoh Caves in Virginia and though I must say it is more 'commercialised', I prefer the concept they have where you are brough down to the caves by their own 'cave guides'.  The guides would point out more interesting rock formations and though we did have our own personal guides, I think the ones by the cave operators would make it more interesting.It needs to be better lit as certain parts were very dark and there are minimal hand rails.  When we were in the Shenandoh Caves, the elderly were always upfront so that the other visitors could help them or watch out for them (mind you we were not from one tour group but individual members visting the cave) and one of them actually fell despite that.  That came to mind when I was in the caves too, that there was little light, a little brighter would have been ideal.  It was brighter lit nearer the entrance but not as you proceed further in.

The experience was exactly like what I read from reviews and so I'll just focus on key things.-If for youngsters,  no issues.-For people not used to visiting caves-*wear shoes that don't slip*bring a torch if darkness is a concern *wear a light jacket- there are unexpected water drops, huge temperature difference with outside -Using mobile phones, not easy to take good photos. What you see is better than what is captured by phones. Online photos look so much better than what we saw.-Flowers outside the cave are lovely. Good photo taking spots.

This attraction is one of the three UNESCO World Heritage sites on Jeju Island. We drove here in our rental car from Seongsan without any navigational issues. Admission fee of –2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry. Parking, free at all times, is plentiful in the area. The climb down into the cave entrance is via a large stairway and the surroundings get dimmer as you venture deeper. Only 1 km of this vast network of tunnels is open for public viewing. Take a walk through the cathedral-like cave to view spectacular rock formations, and weird and wonderful shapes of the stalagmites and stalactites, all formed from volcanic lava activity. These are not like the usual delicate works in limestone caves, but more rugged and robust. There are heaps of notices along the way which provides all the geographical descriptions and technical details for those who love the information overload. Conditions in the cave can be a little damp and cool, so watch your step and bring a jumper!

I'll start by saying I love caves, they've always fascinated me and this one doesn't disappoint. The Cave is a couple thousand year old lava tube with a really neat walking path through it. The tube itself is 7 km long, but the tourist portion is 1 km in length. The cave itself is a bit dark, but it also sets the mood of the cave. I went in the summer and the cave was at least 5 degrees C cooler than the outside and had some condensation (closed toed shoes a must). The only downside would be the crowds, but still didn't take too much away from the experience. Very much recommended if you visit Jeju Island!

This is a bit of a must see in Jeju. Its a walk underground in a lava tube obviously created by a volcano. The tunnel has some nice features but the payoff is at the end as there is a big lava colomn. Also if it's a hot day it's really refreshing as it is quite cold down there. A jacket or vest is recommended. The way is lit by lights but all in all a flashlight comes in handy but the one on your smartphone will do. The floor is very uneven so people who aren't that nimble might have problems. Finally there are bats in the cave who probably won't bother you but make the place a tad creepy as you sometimes see their shadow. Getting there with public transportation is hard drive or get a taxi. However the grey ones are cheaper than the black ones.

I enjoyed my visit to Manjanggul cave, however it was not my favorite place in jeju. What i liked was that they had signs and explanations for everything in English so you could learn on how it was formed. It is a little cold down in the cave, wear a jacket and comfortable shoes.

Bring your jackets, better to be water proof! Cave temperature is around 10 plus degree or lower. Also ground is uneven so wear good shoes and walk slowly. But overall fascinating to see how geography works

It's pretty difficult using public transportation in Jeju to getting around expect using car. But this one is ok because there is bus stop in the highway, but you need to take a taxi or walking 3km from bus stop to get this place
Nice place for a stroll, we had to turn around because our 6mth old got fussy, but we definitely enjoyed our visit. A little chilly inside the tunnel so bring a light jacket.

It was almost 1.5 hrs drive from our hotel but was worth it. It's the only 1 of the 8 caves (I think 8) that is open to public . Amazed by how mother nature ends up creating such beautiful sites . You can keep walking for almost a km in the cave where lava used to flow when volcano erupted . It has some signs describing the various locations. Tip: wear shoes and take a jacket if travelling with kids as it gets really cold inside

It was my first time walking through a lava cave which was an enjoyable experience. I appreciated the natural formation of the tubes and to think that lava once flowed through was exciting. Others might think it's just a cave and the first few meters is the same throughout which is fair enough but I loved it.

I think we paid KRW2,000 per adult for entry. Walked the lava tube where the temperature dropped by a few degrees. It was raining that day, so it was a good hideout from the downpour. The walk was rather long but many things to see along the way. Remember to wear good waking shoes tho! It can get slippery.

This is a natural cave and you have to walk down a stair at the entrance. It is dark inside the cave and be aware of your step as the stone on the floor are not plain. Better bring a jacket with you as the temperature inside is around 10-degree celsius only.
Fun walk through the lava tubes. We did this as part of an east side tour that included a beach and Sunrise Point and an English speaking guide

I went on a group tour around Korea last year and one of my highlights was seeing the lava tubes at Jeju. You might think a cave is just a dark place with little to no visual interest but this Unesco site is really cool because you're actually inside a tunnel formed by volcano pressure. There are lights that guide your way and handlebars so you don't slip. If you're into nature and on this island it's a must see because there are some extraordinary natural feats you observe and experience first hand as you explore these tunnels. It's very interactive.
UNESCO recognised scenic spot! Most of the part looks more or less similar and the best part is at the last! Better save time for the last part and beware of the slippery floor.
This was really excelent place and experience to walk in former lava tunnel. Just imagine thousands of years before here flew lava ...
It is attraction. You can see a lot of caves everywhere but not such long and big. It has safety signs inside.

About 1 kilometer of the lava tube  is open to walk through. You descend a long staircase into the cave. You will be walking on the old lave flow, so the floor is uneven & pitted, and full of puddles. There is dim lighting, so you really need to bring your own flashlight to see where you are stepping. The wall are fairly smooth & rounded, you will only be seeing a few small formations. If you are a nature geek (like me) you will enjoy this. If you want  lots of stalactites & large formations, this is not for you.

The site was the best part of an all day trip covering the eastern end of Jeju Island. Such places are always fascinating. As soon as you enter, the temperature drops to the lower double digits C.There is a one kilometer stretch you can walk. I like that it has not been jazzed up with a rainbow of colours. The floor is naturally uneven with some sectors covered in wood. The cave is 18 meters as its widest and  23 meters as its tallest. At the far end is located the world tallest lava column at 7.6 meters. When you appreciate the force of Mother Nature to cause such formations, it only adds to the visit.
Viewing of lavas in the cave was interesting.  But having been to other caves in other countries, like the Postjna Cave ins Slovenia, this place is rather boring.

Really cool and Interesting lava tube under the ground of Jeju island. It shows a lot of cool facts about how it happen and also how the island is formed like it is today. The attraction is both on English and Korean. The test is easy to under stand on the sign and pictures there are. Remember to bring some good walking/waterproof shoes or boots because there are water every were and the terrain is uneven because of the lava it self.

The bus ride from the bus terminal is near an hour and the bus stop you alight at looks like a bus stop in the middle of a highway. From the bus stop, walk 2km to Manjanggul cave. It's a very long walk and not if you are on a solo trip (my mistake as i thought there would be shops and things to see along the way!) as it can get quite scary. Cave is very dark, not well-lit, cold and vey wet. The floor and stairs/steps are very uneven with puddles of water so will suggest covered shoes. Will need a jacket or shawl as the cave gets colder as you walk further in. The lava/cave formation is amazing but I couldn't properly enjoy the sights as I have to keep watching out for puddles of water and the uneven floor to avoid tripping.Will only suggest this if you like to see lava formations, have a group of friends to go with and have transportation to bring you to and fro.

The cave and formation is very unique. Must go and it's not expensive. Only 2000 won per adultAs for transportation, we took bus 701 and waiting for bus 990. Note that bus 990 is not very frequent and be prepared to walk 2.5km. It's quite a pleasant walk though. So take note.

Down steep stairs and into the lava tubes.You can go in a long way or a little way.I enjoyed this unusual experience.I did not like the fact that it was wet and surface uneven so difficult even with good walking shoes.

I loved this cave! 2 km in and out. It was a very educational trip as you'll get explanations about what you see along the way. It's dark and wet and there's water dripping from the ceiling so bring a cap and good boots to avoid slipping. Don't wear a long skirt as it will get wet. A bit hard to take pictures though because of the lighting :/ But the ending and the way it was presented with the lighted walkway at the end was great!

We enjoyed this cave.  It's about 1 km to the end where the largest lava  pillar is located and then another 1 km back,  although the walk was relatively flat (no inclines) it was very uneven and slippery in places.  Wear shoes with good traction.  The cave is in a beautiful setting with many public toilets around.

I wanted to check what the hype was about. It did not disappoint. The place is huge and every few meters there is a guide which tells you what kind of lava formation is found there. I learned a lot about volcanoes. –

Visited this place in the evening after 4pm and was told its free entry.   Good for a short 1hr visit, but nothing really spectacular.  Good experience if you have not seen lava caves, just wear good shoes and the track has lots of uneven ground, as seen in my pictures.

At KRW2000 this was well worth the money.  Don't forget to wear a jacket or a warm Cardy though, I forgot and found it very cold.  Lots of people do this it's very popular.  We tried the restaurant there which was good enough.

I was traveling solo via public transportation, I arrived there 30 mins early before it opened for public that day. For it's 1st month of Spring (April), most of natural attractions were free admission. Good thing it was free, though I appreciate it, it's not really astounding as I though (well, as per my perspective).From downtown of Jeju, take bus 701 (East Route). You can ask your hotel reception of the bus stop. It would be easier if you have private car (especially for group traveler). Alight at Manjanggul Entrance, walk about 25mins, you'll pass by Gimnyeong Maze Park (roughly 15mins walk from bus stop). Not for a person who's kinda frightened to walk alone in a road of unknown :) You can wait for bus 990 the only bus that passes through Manjanggul Cave yet it isn't frequent.Just follow your path way back, if you're lucky enough, a taxi would offer you a ride for a certain price roughly KW3,000. You can negotiate the cost. In my case, I negotiated for KW2,000 which I think is reasonable enough. Yet when I'm about to pay, I only have KW50,000, the driver doesn't have any loose change, so he asked only KW1,000, I still have none, instead he just took the last coins I have, KW700.

Located in the north eastern part of the island.  Took us an hour from hotel.  The cave temperature is 5-10C lower than outside, so suggest to bring a jacket and don't wear your Jimmy Choos.  Is wet and slippery with uneven grounds.  (Not suggest for elderly)The open part in 2017 is the 2nd section.  which is about 1km from start to end. First you walk down a steep stairs 3 floors down and you start walking. When you reach the large platform at the end and see the huge lava rocks, take photo and then you walk back .Spent about 2 hours there.

We took a cab to the cave as we don't want to walk (think about 20 mins) if we are taking the bus. The cave is quite long and not so dark as there are small lights along the way. But it's good to bring a touch light. Quite cold inside the cave so better to wear a jacket. Walk till the end and walk the same way back to the entrance of the cave. Overall an interesting experience.

A veey dark and long walk with informative description on different formation of rocks created after cooling of the lava. Interesting and educational, no exit @ the end of the walk so would have to take the same route back.
1st visit in the cave tube. Really fascinated cold, dark, wet cave. The ground is uneven so walk with caution. It's good to walk in a group for safety.

I went with a group of fellow Taekwondo practitioners. The cave is an amazing example of this type of geology. Need to be careful as floor a little uneven due to the natural rock formation but well worth a visit if your in the area. We all did a little Taekwondo practice whilst down there so it made the visit even more memorable.

Entrance in Apr is FREE! My family had a pleasant time taking a bus 701 from Intercity Bus Terminal for 50mins and walked in 2km to Manjanggul cave.The cave was quiet and wasn't too crowded at the time we gone in. Just be prepared that it's rlly cold (around 5-10deg).

As all caves are, the interior is dark. But there is lighting along the way that is sufficient to show the wall and ground.The ground is not even, but one just need to be careful and pay attention when walking. A touch will help (I carried one). Wear sports shoes for easy and safe walking.We walk for about 30 minutes to reach the end, with stops to read the explanation posted along the way.
Really the Tubes are fascinating but a little redundant. Was a long walk in the dark for a six (6) year old BUT the park is well equipped w/ Toilets and a Local Resto & Taxi Cabs!!! Enjoy.

I'm glad I went, as I've never seen a lava tube before. Great multilingual explanatory signs. Four dots instead of 5 because even on the pristine day that we went, the wet, uneven floor made it mildly perilous and only a small portion of the tube is open to tourists.
Really enjoyed exploring this cave. Easy and convenient car parking. Great facilities. A must-see on your trip to Jeju.

The natural beauty of the lava tubes entertained my mother, husband, and myself for nearly two hours of appreciating God's creation. For only 2,000 kw per person, I recommend this highly as one of Jeju's most impressive tourist spots!
Good but it was freezing cold even though I visited it during the hottest month of the year.Visited it summer of 2015

We could not have gotten to so many attractions on our own in one day, so great time taking the bus tour from Yeha.  Wish we had booked more days in Jeju to explore other parts of the island such as Seowipo.  The cave is 1km long and a nice attraction to check out, especially for families.  Cold inside!  Bring an extra layer...

We took a local bus from Jeju City to Manjanggul Cave. It's 2,8 km walk from the bus stop to the entrance of the cave. You can hire a taxi, if you don't feel like walking. Just outside the entrance you can find a restaurant and a kiosk. The entrance fee was very cheap (2000 won). There are quite many stairs when you go down to the cave. The floor of the cave is a bit uneven, but still quite easy to walk on. The cave is quite dimly lit, moist and cold. I recommend bringing a jacket with you. All that said the cave isn't maybe a best spot to visit with small children or elderly people. For healthy adults the cave is a nice experience. There is information in English about the different formations and the history of the cave. There is only one entrance to the cave, so if you walk to the end and back, it's total of 2 km of walking. I recommend visiting Manjanggul Cave, if you're interested in Unesco heritage sties and natural beauty!
The place defitinely not suitable for elder people. Is too long walk for them and the long stair case. However, is an amazing place to visit.

Very enjoyable trek down the stairs and to the end of the cave and back but be careful when walking because the "ground" is not even as you'd imagine.Very cool inside.Great experience if you haven't done this before

The longest lava tube in the world was sitting in Jeju and I didn't even know! Stumbled upon it on my fourth trip to Jeju. If you like caves, geology, or nature in general this place is fascinating. If you aren't, it's simply an interesting/unique cave that stretches 7.4 km (1km of it walkable). It's a 30 minute round trip in and out if you don't doddle. If you take it all in, give it an hour. It's about 10-15 degrees celsius inside so it's warmer than outside in the winter and cooler than outside in the summer. Perfect place to get away from the elements either way. It can be kind of dark so mind your footing on the uneven lava rock floor!
We enjoyed walking until the end point.It is recommended during summer since inside the cave is cool ..

Quite long caves, but we do enjoy walking through it until the end of the caves. It was cold inside, feels like we are walking inside a room with air-conditioner. Lols. My friend do enjoy reading all those facts and information on the formations, and I find it quites helpful for those who are interested in geology thing. Maybe.It is quite large caves too. For those who are on tight budgets like us, you can take a bus and walk 2km to the caves. Not tiring at all as the view is very nice.

Manjanggul is one of the 10 longest lava caves in the world and deserves a visit. It is exhilarating to see the different formations due to the lava flow. As almost everything in Korea there are plenty info and it is very well taken care of.

We were very excited to visit Manjanggul Cave, and it did not disappoint.It is quite a large cave, and if you walk slowly and look around at the cave carefully, you can see the changes of the lava formation colours and shapes.Make sure you walk the entire length to check out the lava tube, I mean - when will you get another chance? Also make sure you wear comfortable shoes, as my recommendation of walking slowly is not just to check out the different sections, it also means you won't trip, as the ground is pretty uneven and the cave is quite dimly lit!

It felt spooky from the fog as it was really cold inside. Do bring a jacket if you visit this place. You could see firsthand how the lava affected the rock formations in this cave and it is interesting to watch for first-timers. The floor is quite uneven due to the natural rock formations so do be careful and wear proper shoes. It is about 1km walk to the end and you have to u-turn back to exit as there's only one entrance which is also the exit.

Place where you can consider one of the exercise from steps and all the way to the end to view the nature of Lava.You can learn about the Manjanggul Cave as there's information along the way. Cool weather as we went during the winter. Not sure if you go during any other season.Must come as you might not get it from your own country.
A cave without much special or interesting views. May not be worth it if you have limited time on jeju.

Definitely worth a visit, even if you only have a few hours to spare. This attraction my husband and I completed in just over an hour, there is no audio guide but there are informative signs throughout the cave. You return to the start of the cave the same way you came in, so take your time reading the signs but if you are tight on time you can read some of it on the way back. Being a natural cave/tube the floor of the cave is pretty rocky, must wear comfortable shoes. If you are driving around Jeju, and using the rental GPS, the telephone number to type into the gps system is: 7834818

If you are into rocks, earth and geology thing, then this place is for you. The visit costs you less than 5000won and would probably take you an hour to finish the entire route.Take your time to read all the usefull information and appreciate the wonders of nature

Manjanggul Cave is one of the top ten lava tubes to visit that was formed about 200,000-300,000 years ago. It is one of 7 Geomunoreum lava tubes of Jeju Island and located in the North East area.The visit can be done using either bus (another 30 mins or 2.7km walk to the entrance) or car. I'd suggest to rent a car while in Jeju because it will make it super easy to get around the island. If you drive, the number you want to input into the GPS is 7107903 :-).It was really windy and cold on the day we went to the cave. We walked for about 5 minutes from the free car park to the ticket booth but the temperature inside of the cave was very comfortable.The first lava related item that we saw was the lava column cascade. It would be there on the way to entrance, to greet everyone who came to visit the Manjanggul Cave. The entrance started with two flights of stone stairs that might get a bit slippery during the rainy or winter period. Even though you wear non-slip shoes with you, it's definitely worthwhile to hold on to the railing when going down and up the stairs.The cave was definitely not wheelchair friendly since the stony surface is always wet, rocky and covered with puddles. Water will occasionally drop from the ceiling of the cave but it didn't really bother us. We saw that some people carried an umbrella with them or wore the plastic rain poncho but since you'll be walking a lot, it would be too warm if you wear the poncho. Another suggestion is just to wear a hat/ baseball cap in summer and stick to your winter jacket in the winter time.I tried to take some photos inside but it was pretty hard because the cave was quite dark. It was a really enjoyable walk and we got to learn about how the lava stream formed the lines on the cave, stalactites and stalagmites.There were a lot of rocks around our path and we learnt later on that big and fragmented rocks fell from the ceiling during or after the formation of the lava tubes! There were a lot of lava columns as well that was formed when lava flowed from the ceiling to the floor of the lava tube.Manjanggul Cave closes on the first Wednesday of each month. Their opening hours is from 9 AM to 6 PM with last admission at 5:10 PM.

Again, freezing of winter time and slippery step stone has discourage our tour leader to let us go any further getting inside the cave furthermore. up to the point we stand inside there, nothing special.Hard to explain accept you are cave adventurer... tourists ? it is a No No No

This is a cave formed by molten lava melting the rock layers away over a very very long time. So expect a huge dimly-lit tunnel with uneven walking surface. The small museum does a good job of explaining the geological aspect of the cave. The 2 km round trip into the cave is not difficult but wear a pair good walking shoes and if you need, bring a small torch. This cave is located on the eastern part of the island so best to visit nearby attractions like the Ichulbong, Phoenix Island etc.Another tip: if you hated Geography in school, give this place a miss. LOL!
It was a nice trip. When in Jeju, try to visit here. You'll see interesting lava formations inside the cave. The entrance fee is KRW 2,000 for adults.

Surreal and spooky!! A must see place! Amazing place to see geological transformations and an interesting experience to enjoy. The caves were dimly lit and was quite slippery so be careful when visiting.

An interesting 2km round-trip walk through the Manjanggul lava cave in cool conditions. Was told by our guide that the temperature stays like this all year round. Really intriguing to see the various histotical lava formations and literally walk through a part of Jeju's history.

Be amazed how it was formed. Well maintained facility. A good place to visit for kids who are interested to know about rock formation and caves. It's a 7km in length, however you can only go up to the 1st kilometer.

With total of 2km walk in the tunnel (2 ways), you will be able to see different types of volcanic stones with good explanation notes in multiple languages. Not suitable for old people as it is dark and the walkpath is not even (all natural). Spend 1 hour.
manjanggul cave is one of the UNESCO World Heritage and it is one of the finest lava tunnel. it is quite cold inside the tunnel so make sure to wear a jacket!

For those who are interested in geology as my family is, this is a fascinating, and not too difficult, walk through a lava tube created by the molten lava. Worth a visit and the entrance fee is extremely cheap. UNESCO heritage.

KRW 2k for adults. Worth the 2km to and fro walk and all information panels in the cave have english. Not suitable for very old and very young. A lot of un even steps and walkways and high steps sometimes. Dark. Wear good tracking shoes.

This place is for geography lovers. You get to learn about how lava tubes are formed centuries ago, the history of the volcanic eruptions, how the lava flowed, how the lava stalactites are formed, how the different rocks are formed etc. The cave is very wet, cold and dark as water is dripping from the stalactites. You will have the chance to walk for about 1-1.5km into the middle section of the tube, where you will be able to take picture in front of the famous Lava Column. After that, you will U turn and return to the entrance. The whole journey takes around 1-1.5 hrs. The paths consist of harden lavas and steps, a really authentic experience. You might want to bring along your torchlight if you want to see the rocks clearly.

Well worth the visit, especially if geology is your interest.Plenty of stairs in and out of the cave so not too advisable for elderly, or families with babies/ toddlers. (though i did bring both!) Being a lava tube, the flooring can be uneven and slippery within the cave so wear proper footwear.It will be cold and dimly lit down in the lava tube, so bring your sweaters if chill is a concern.The walk long to and fro the end, so be prepared.After the first half to the end, it can get boring for some especially the kids. That said it is still a unique experience for many.

We didn't have great weather when we were on the island so couldn't climb the mountain. This was an alternative activity and glad we did it as it was really interesting. Make sure you go all the way to the end as you don't want to miss the lava flow. The ground is slippy in places and not suitable for small children, strollers or wheelchairs. If you're using public transport get the bus 900. Not the 701 as we did! The 701 has a stop called 'Manjamggul Cave entrance' but it's 2km walk away from the entrance!!
Walking down into the cave, walking on nature lava pavement looking at million years aging proof of volcanic activies that happen, create layers and layers of wall features- such experiance!

Visited Manjaggul Cave because it was a UNESCO Natural site, like Seongsan Ichulbong.  Unfortunately, beyond the concept of actually walking through lava tubes, the entire experience was rather disappointing.  It was dark, wet and cold. The ground was uneven and hence quite slippery with many puddles.  After the first few hundred metres, my older daughter lost interest but we insisted on walking further.  However, it was pretty much more of the same so we did not finish the entire course of 7.4 km (since it would actually be 14.8 if you consider you also have to walk back)!  So unless you are in the area and really into geography, I would give this a miss.

Manjanggul cave is world historic place of volcanic lava formation! The cave path is very unsmooth with bumpy small rock patches and wet so we had to walk steps by steps very slowly to the end! All along to the main attraction, there are small lamps and lamppost to guide us along.Took us one and a half hours to reach the main attraction of lava formation.We spent a few minutes taking some picture there and proceeded back out of the cave.I think I won't be going there again because I'm not interested in geography.
nicely labelled signs to explain the lava tubereally awesome to see the marks left by nature it's about a slow walk of about an hr, wear good shoes and a jacket as it gets cold

I am definitely biased as I lived in Virginia and there are magical caves all throughout the countryside.  Manjanggul just doesn't rank up there.  It is a fairly long trip to get there.  The inside is too dark to really see the cave details.  Just isn't a place I recommend to visitors.  There are soooo many more beautiful and fascinating places on the island.
Cave is big and long, take around 1 hour to come and back. Nothing much to see and it's dark so it's hard to take photo. Average compare to other caves
Brought my 7 yr old girl here and it was a good educational walk and eye opener for her. It's wet and cool inside, and unsuitable for wheelchair or stroller.

We just came back from the Manjanggul Cave this afternoon. There is an entrance fee of 2000 won per adult. It is quite a distance from the main road. We had rented a car so it was easy for us to go there with the GPS.The cave. It was dark, wet and slippery. It was really difficult to walk, not the whole path cos certain parts have raised platform, but generally the stones/ rocks are at their natural state which is not even. I do agree with an earlier posting that you have to watch your steps cos you may end up walking into puddles of water. You will walk 1 km in and the same route out, making it a total of 2km.The experience is however, - awesome. You are standing / walking where lave once flows. You have to go there to see how big the lave tubes are. The lave shelves, the staglamites, staglatites and many more of the geographic terms fully explained at the appropriate juncture in the caves. You have to take your time to read and understand the structures found there.

Along with Seongsan Ilchulbong, Manjanggul Cave is one of the two must-see attractions in Jeju, IMHO.There is a small information center building available with some interesting facts about the cave.  The cave itself is quite fascinating.  It is only 1 km in length, but it requires a very slow pace to traverse the entire cave.  This is due to the very rough nature of the ground that one walks on.  The cave floor has not been smoothed by man - unlike Micheon cave, so the ground is extremely uneven, sharp, and at points quite dangerous!  You definitely would not want to take a fall on the ground.  The ground is also very wet in areas.  Finally, the cave is not very well illuminated.  This makes it quite difficult for people who are elderly, have physical disabilities, or if you want to carry a baby.  In fact, for these groups, I would strongly advise not to visit the cave.The cave itself is quite large in height and occupies a large volume of space.  However, it is quite dark inside the cave and there's nothing too overly unique (when compared to something like Cave of the Winds) within the cave - other than it's very big and somewhat creepy.   I only made it through one third of the cave before I had to turn back due to time constraints.  There are a few man-made displays of interest providing more information on the cave and how is was formed.

The cave is very big, stairs at the entrance is quite steep, you might be a little bit out of breath here, but once inside it is manageable. The cave is spacious and well maintained, there is clear line for people to walk, there isn't much to see, after walking around 1km you will reach the end of the accessible part of the cave, people take pictures here and then walk back to the entrance. Whether you love nature or not, I strongly recommend visiting this cave. There is so much to learn on how the lava tube was formed and it provides you with a unique experience that is unforgettable. Really dark in there, gives a good feel of being in a cave.  If you want decent pictures in there. Must take tripod and use long exposure.
The cave is dark and cold especially nearing winter. If you are into cave exploration, then be sure to bring along a flashlight to brighten up. Be careful walking in the cave.

This was amazing in terms of the length and size of the lava tube. Explained very well at key points en route so understood features and processes . The Korean have sympathetically enabled the public to see an amazing site . Also very cheap.

It is worth a visit when you are in Jeju Island.We enjoy the two kilometres walking vv. please make sure that you have a comfortable shoes no  as the surface is really from the lava. This cave is one of three unesco heritage sites in Jeju Island.Nice and cool inside the cave and interesting marks of lava. We enjoyed it very much.

nice place to visit to see how nature works!!!....u can see how jeju was made thousands years ago.....beautiful cave!!!...but you must be fit to walk about 2km and walking in a slippery floor is not really easy in the dark....beautiful!!!!

Spent more time looking at the ground......., watching out for puddle of water than looking at the cave/tunnel. Do be careful if going with elderly and children as some parts are quite difficult to walk . It's quite dim and chilly inside. Nothing much to see....

I really enjoyed visiting this cave. It reminded me of the beauty of God's creation. I was expecting to explore the entire cave, but unfortunately, they only allow the public to explore the first 1 kilometer. Nevertheless, it was an eye-opening experience for me.Tips:-1. Wear comfortable clothes.2. Wear a good pair of shoes.3.Bring a cap.4. Bring a torchlight. You gotta visit this place if you are in Jeju Island!
this must be in the itinerary if you visit Jeju!experience the beauty of mother nature seeing and learning. this lava tube is amazing!

One of the highlights of my visit in Jeju - there's about a 1km walk in the cave which allows you to explore the after effects of lava tubes at your own pace; very interesting and spectacular. This is something different: a 2 km or so walk through an underground lava tube where molten lava has flowed several times over the centuries. A unique experience. Be prepared for a bit of a trek over uneven, rough ground, dodging puddles. It can be drippy and it's always cold so take a jacket. But it's good fun and just out of this world.

There is nothing much to see except of the cave. But if you spend time to read and understand the formation of the cave. Its quite educational for me.You will be more enjoyed if you slows down your steps and admiring the unique walls in the cave. Instead just walk, walk and walk until the end and took picture of the end of the cave then went back.
great place to go on a hot day as it is nice and cool inside and it is amazing to see how lava carved it's way through the rocks

This is the longest lava tube/cave in the word, so they claim, with a longitude of four kilometers. About one kilometer is accesible to the public. Interesting to see. Some explanations. Very dim light. The lava column at the end is impressive.

Was quite doubtful if it is worth visiting after reading some of the reviews.  Went for it and it is quite worth a visit if you are interested in works of nature or with kids for education purpose.  The place isn't too difficult to walk if you are with the right shoes as the floor is wet and could be slippery.
To be in a gigantic lava tube was something new and interesting. Recommended!  It's also near the Haenyo Museum which was very interesting as well.
Really fascinating visit to the lava tube. A bit disappointed that it is only one km open to the public, but the one km we got to see was worth the money.

We spent some days in Jeju and also visited the Manjanggul Cave. It is easy to find with car. Few parking places are available. Entrance fee is 2000 Won for adult and 1000 Won for child. We have seen much better caves but this cave was aslo somehow interesting. The cave is 1000 meter long. Walking through is easy but you shall watch your steps. It is quite dark inside and also wet.
