Wear comfortable shoes with good grip, tunnel is rather slippery and rocky.  On a side note, I think I enjoyed walking through the Manjanggul Caves better than the DMZ Third Tunnel. :)

We were taken to Manjanggul lava Cave as part of a day tour. I've never been in one before and this was pretty neat. Comfy shoes are a must. The feeling under your feet is a slippery one and one of many uneven ridges. The cave is dimly lit which does give it atmosphere but does pose problems if you are unsteady on your feet. The 1km tube takes about 25 mins to walk to the middle of where the volcano erupted. You can't go any further in. We thoroughly enjoy this fab experience and would highly recommend it. It is not suitable for people in wheelchairs or strollers. There are lots of information boards through out the lava tube giving you lots of nformation. The coloured lighting adds to highlight the different textures and forms of the rocks.

Although it was a long walk from the entrance to the end of the cave (and back), it was worth seeing. It was very educational and amazing to see the lava tubes. It was a good walk, just wear  good shoes and try to keep balance as the pathway was rocky and uneven.
excellent for people interested in such. wear comfortable shoes and carry a torch if you need though it is pretty much well lit. carry a good camera to get good pictures in the dark.

Nature is amazing and the lava tubes at manjang is worth seeing. The walk is about 1km in and same way out. Wear good shoes. Walk is not as tiring as climbing up other steep sites in jeju. Educational Signs in English are available. A bit chilly in autumn in the caves.
It will be a good place to visit for educational purposes. Nice to be walking in a lava tube. Not a must go attraction but if you have children, it will be good to bring them there.
Cooling cave and it was uneven and rocky. Wear comfortable shoes when visiting this attraction.Cost 2000 won.Not too spectacular but educational to see the aftermath of volcano lava.

Visited this place which is really a lava tube rather than a cave.  It is about 1 kilometer from end-to-end.  Inside the tube you can see different rock formations created by the lava flow, among them the turtle-shaped rock at 600-meter mark.  It is cool inside the tube and water is dripping everywhere.  It is recommended that you wear appropriate footwear while taking this tour as it could really be slippery and some areas are not so well-lit.  Maybe this is intentional to give the place a more realistic feel.

Never been to lava cave before..it's fascinating..the colour led lighting makes the cave more beautifull..to reach the end of a cave you had to walk for about 1km..maybe because it's rain outside,the temperature inside the cave is more colder..you should wear a long shirt and a long pants..

It is interesting but not quite a must-see in Jeju. If you miss it, it is still no grave regret unless you love geology. An extremely long volcanic lava tube but due to the number of tourists, I believe the condition of the cave is not as well preserved as the caverns in Europe. Careful walking in the first 100 metres... can easily twist one's ankles.

Caves are pretty common but first time walking through a lava tube. It is quite a walk (close to 2kms) to the end where the lava poured in (column like structure) but worth the walk. The cave is rather chilly & wet with uneven surfaces. Do come prepared. Decent lighting throughout however can get rather dark. Maybe a small torchlight or glow stick so you can enjoy it more.

after taking a few geology classes as an adult, it was exciting to see the lava tubes. Would recommend taking a glow stick or a small flash light if prone to having a hard time seeing in the dark. Plus, the glow sticks added some fun to the darkness.  Slightly cold like most caves, bring a sweatshirt is a good idea. This offered something to do when it is raining and could  be a great break from the sun if traveling in the summer time.
Good, worth experiencing if you haven't been to a lava tube cave before, but do watch your step. Uneven ground with deep cracks at some places

We walked the slippery, uneven and poorly lit path 1.5 km to the 7 meter column. It was again good to do some walking and the cave was interesting but how the cave was made was still a mystery after reading all of the panels (Wikipedia said lava flows of differing temperatures).
A place worth visiting. Found a new love for cave trekking. Beautiful lava cave, can see the tracks of nature.

It's just a 1km tunnel walk, feeling the chill a little.  Kind of dim, ground is uneven, therefore watching our steps took most of our focus, stopping occasionally for pictures taking. Nothing exceptionally awesome.

I was excited to go see the Manjanggul caves, and had an image in my mind that unfortunately didn't fit what I saw. The whole experience is pretty cool, the floor is uneven, dodging water droplets becomes a game, the lava flow marks are beautiful, but lack of light, lack of stalactite formations, and a lot of areas that are fenced off let me down slightly. However, cheap entrance, and the atmosphere is actually quite lovely. If you get the chance to go, try and do it.

This is a UNESCO World Heritage listed site. It is indeed one of the largest lava cave/tube I have ever seen. It is awesome, dark, wet and huge. Its floor uneven, wet and slippery. Artificial lighting is minimal and don't attempt to take photos as it is too high to be lit by ordinary flash lights. You need to watch where you are going. The result of a fall can be serious. Minor twist ankle is common. The experience is well worth the trip. Do not forget to take extra clothes and be prepared to have a thorough shampoo and shower that night as it drips everywhere.

This is a lava tunnel, NOT a stalactite cave. There is one huge stalactite at the end of the tunnel, but if you are planning to see many stalactite formations, you would be very disappointed. Nonetheless, there are many interesting rock formations here. The horizontal and vertical lava flow marks on the cave walls and dimmed lighting give an aura of an alien tunnel. There is also a stone that looks like a stone turtle. :-) The air is slightly chilly and damp with occasional water dripping from the cave ceiling. I would recommend a light sweater or a light scarf to make experience enjoyable. And wear comfortable walking shoes, since the ground is very uneven(but interesting).

We got there by bus. It was a rainy day and the walk was like 2-3 km so we took a taxi. 5 min drive for 4$ was a very good option vs getting all wet. This was one of the highlights of my jeju trip. Walking down those amazing lava tubes. You feel so small. It's midly cold and water drips from the ceiling so bring an overcoat. The ground is uneven but you can walk easily still. Saw old people with walking sticks along the way. Very cheap ticket entry for the marvel this is. At the end, there is a beautiful stalactite that makes a great pic. There are dim lights along the way but my headlamp made walking easier for me and people walking in front of me... You guys are welcome lol There is a restaurant at the entrance. Pretty expensive one. But if you cross to the joined convenient souvenir shop, they make fast korean food for a thenth of the price. They have soup, gimbap, mandoo and they are very good. Not the greatest place for souvenirs since that store is the only one around and does not have much. In between those 2 places, there is a small museum that takes around 10 min to cross and it explains the formation of the lava tube. Very interesting. A must do!

This was an exciting attraction. It takes about 1 hour to get to the end of the tube and back. The closer you get to the end the colder it gets. Also pe prepared to get a little wet, as there are drops of water falling from the top. You wont need an umbrella or anything like that. Getting here is tricky. As I was waiting for the bus to get here (990) I found a taxi and got him to take me for $4,000 won. This saved me a lot of time. It might have been too much but it saved me time, since the bus comes by every 45 minutes or so. There are restaurants at the entrance, they over charge for water so make sure you are prepared if you like to drink water. Definitely an amazing experience and a must do in the area.

You know that line movie critics love to use when it comes to B-grade chick flicks? "Have low expectations, then you'll enjoy it." The same can be said of Manjang Cave.The lava tube was not as spectacular as I expected it to be, but it did offer a few interesting sights here and there. Walking all the way to the end of the trail and back took about an hour, but if you walk quickly, you can complete the journey within thirty minutes.Take note that the ground is wet and rocky, so be sure to wear your walking shoes. Also, it can get quite cold, so a jacket would most certainly come in handy. For photography lovers, you may not fancy the fact that it's a bit dark in the cave, but there's nothing a few adjustments here and there can't do!Facilities include, but are not limited to, souvenir shops, toilets and lockers. Bear in mind though that there are no toilets in the cave itself. Tickets are cheaper for children, but you'll need passports for proof!If you're spending more than a day in Jeju, you may want to consider checking this place out. If not, you're better off exploring other places such as the Hallasan National Park.

Getting here was tricky, as you must take a bus from either Jeju or Segowipo and even then the bus stop is 2km from the entrance so usually taxis cruise past and you can do them a deal. It is pricey to reach and has an entrance fee (half price for youths under 25 with valid passport) but has full facilities such as restaurant, shop, toilets, lockers etc, It is a little cold underground so recommended to bring a jumper or warm clothing. It is incredible to be underground in a volcanoe and there are numerous info signs in various languages along the route as you walk underground to the cone. It's a little dark for photos but if your camera can be adjusted there can be some great shots. You must walk quiet far and it can be wet on the ground so proper shoes recommended and flip-flops/sandals avoided. I saw plenty of kids but obviously it is dark so may be a little scary, plus it's quite a fair walk so think through if you want to walk about a mile to the cone or just have a quick look. An interesting trip for sure!

If you love nature and have never seen any volcanic formation before, it would be worth the visit. Personally,  i enjoyed walking inside the cave and having a look at the volcanic formation.  It's like you can almost imagine how the lava flowed inside the tunnel a few thousand years ago :) i was in awe of how powerful mother nature can be. It was quite cold inside. Wear layers and proper shoes.  Can be quite slippery as well.

The idea is cool. I mean, yes, it's a cave formed from lava. But there's not really anything to see. It's cold and dark, and you walk for about 25 minutes to get to one end and then you turn around and walk back to the other end.The formation thing at the end is certainly the coolest part, but it wasn't worth the long taxi drive (or long walk from the bus stop - it's about 2.5km from the nearest bus stop) or the freezing wet environment. It had rained a lot on Jeju before we visited, so you definitely needed an umbrella inside the caves, or else you were going to get wet. We also really needed jackets. It was freeeeezing inside.

We reached the cave 45 minutes before closing hour and had to walk really fast in order to reach the end of the cave to see the Lava tubes. Many friends told us it's a must visit in jeju.  But my Cousin and I were disappointed as we felt it's nothing fascinating. Better time could be spent in other attractions such as the sunrise peak and Teddy bear museum.

Despite the heat, its very cooling inside the cave. Took a walk and I find that it was smaller than what I expected. Path is quite rocky and its good to wear proper shoes instead of sandals or slippers. It can be quite slippery too. Its good to visit but if you are tight on your schedule I think you can give it a miss :)

It was a hot day so felt great to get away from the  heat and descend into the cave. It felt about 10 degrees colder so be prepared with a light jacket. As with all caves, this has rocky wet floors that are very treacherous for those without proper track shoes. Very interesting signboards with geographical  information about the formation of lava caves too.

In the summer heat, Manjanggul is the perfect place to escape the heat. It's quite cold inside, and water drips from the ceiling. I changed into jeans and a light sweater before going in, which was perfect. The texture of the cave is fascinating! There are good informational English placards that explain how the cave formed. The floor of the cave is quite bumpy, so take care not to trip.It's a popular destination but getting there and leaving can be time-consuming unless you are with a tour. I took a bus from the Bijarim Forest to get to the cave, which dropped us off right at the cave. The bus leaving right from Manjanggul only leaves once an hour, so I recommend checking the bus departure times before you go into the cave and plan your stay accordingly. Otherwise, there are taxis but the drivers are rudely persistent, charge a non-negotiable flat price, and refuse to go by the meter. They kept pestering us the entire hour we waited for the bus, even after we rejected many times and had begun ignoring them.

It is smaller than I expected. Basically, it is a long walking path under the ground and it is about 15-20 degree celcius. It leads you to see different kinds of lava formation. And lastly it brings you to the iconic lava stack. It takes about 40 minutes by walking under the tunnel (to and fro) to end your visit.I walked about 25 minutes from Bus station ( Manjanggul Entrance) to the cave. The bus doesn't get you directly to the cave, but only the main road connecting to the cave. Plug your ears to headphone and listen to some good musics while walking to the cave. Scenery on both sides of the road is good. :)
I went to Manjang Cave. It  was really good place to see. It was very cold when we got in side and we can see you cave of Volcano, while you are walking the water drop down and very lively..
This is the must place to visit in Jeju island.Beautiful cave with very cold inside.The floor of this cave are total wet so when you walk please be careful
it's a long walk through the end..but it feels great when you are actually walking in where the lava used to pass.the fee is not expensive and this is a place not to miss when you are in jeju

You can go underground and experience the cold temperatures close to 12 degrees.. its like walking through an igloo.. Cold air everywhere and some parts are wet due to the precipitation though the soil. Reminder to bring a jacket and good shoes as floor is slippery and area is dark! Very good experience!

If you're into exploration and discovering a destination's unique treasures, this is one place on Jeju Island, South Korea not to miss.  Located in a beautiful park-like setting, Manjanggul Cave permits you to descend hundreds of feet below the surface in a cave system that was created by lava flows from a now-extinct volcano.  The cave system constitutes the largest lava tube in the world and is accessible by foot.  Wear comfortable shoes that have good traction (like hikers or sneakers) and expect to get a little wet as the interior has water dripping from the ceilings in places that are unavoidable.  Nevertheless, this experience is a must-do for anyone who likes adventure.  The floor of the cave can be wet (necessitating the need for footwear with good traction) and the temperature in the cave is approximately 55* year-round.  Dress accordingly.  There are many interesting features to see and experience in Manjanggul Cave.  Allow about 90 minutes (minimum) to walk the entire length and be able to see all that it has to offer.  Although you don't get to experience total darkness as in some cave systems, this cave is more than intriguing with the lava formations that remain and the expansiveness of the interior areas.  You might also encounter some inhabitants of the cave.  Anyone who enjoys nature would find this place particularly appealing.

Hmm... Where to start?Well, Jeju Island, being volcanic in nature, must really have places like this!Honestly saying, it wasn't something so jaw-dropping and spectacular!Just more like a place with rock formations due to the cooling of lava!The trek inside isn't hard and what I really liked was that it was chilly while we did it!It was a nice sidetrip nonetheless if you like walking and if you like all these geo stuff!If you're in Jeju, maybe you can give it a try
We did this as part of a tour.  It was a good way to end the day. Beautiful natural attraction and lots of interesting information is provided as you walk toward the end of the cave.

A cave system that can get in easily just by walking down the step.according to the tour guide, this special cave is cold during summer and warm during winter. By the time i go is summer, it is real chill inside the cave

Spent an hour exploring the cave first thing in the morning - very beautiful, unique and wasn't crowded. It started to get very crowded on the way out since the tour buses started arriving making walking a little difficult because it's dark and the path is uneven. Arrived in Jeju by cruise ship and this was the first stop of our 8 hour private taxi tour which I highly recommend. Saw the lava tube as well as 5 other attractions (Sunrise Peak, Seongup Folk Village, Haenyo Museum, and Jeongbang Waterfall). Our driver Mr. Kim Choong Kun (nytaxi5445@hanmail.net) was very pleasant, patient, spoke English, informative, and even took pictures of us.

We were staying near Seogwipo and took the two hour bus trip to the cave.  We enjoyed the cave but it wasn't worth a four hour round trip bus trip.  Would recommend if you are staying on that side of the island.  At the bus terminal in Seogwipo, most people spoke no English but the lady at the information desk did and was very helpful.

If you are interested in caves at all, this one is unique.  Easily accessible, this horizontal lava tube demonstrates the vocanic processes happening over 100,000 years ago.  Cool, wet and accessible with helpful descriptions in multiple languages and little anthropromorphizing of geological shapes.  A quick visit taught us a lot....and our 7 and 10 year old kids enjoyed the walk.  Modest fee.
It was freezing in the tube! There were puddles of water everywhere so be careful when walking. The stones were interesting and do walk all the way in. You've already paid,so why not?
Lava tube isn't something extraordinary. Exploiring just halfway (of the recommended in brochures) is enough

It's a natural wonder.  Amazing how lava can create a tunnel as large as this. Must visit when in Jeju.  Wear a pair of walking shoes and an autumn jacket as temperature falls to around 15 inside the tube. It'll take you at least 30 minutes to walk 1km in and then another 30 minutes out.  So,  it's pretty chilly if you are without a jacket. Floor is wet therefore walk carefully & enjoy the unusual sights especially the walls & ceiling of the tube. Walk until the end as there's a lava column in there, the only one.

So many stairs but a great place to visit.  There are places were the rocks get a little rough so recommend wearing good shoes.  It was raining outside and the inside of the 1 kilometer cave was chilly and wet.

This is just ANOTHER UNESCO Heritage site on Jeju Island. The designation doesn't seem to count for anything special. You probably will not see what you have seen in brochures or website photos because those pictures were taken with much better lighting than is presently available.It is cool but not cold. Like any underground area it is stable temperature all year round. Yes it is wet inside. There is some dripping and there are puddles. A good pair of sneakers will do fine. The ground is uneven most of the time. There are a few wooden walkways over the worst areas but most of it is in its natural state. There is no need for great physical ability to do the walk as long as you allow time to go carefully.It took us just under an hour to walk the length of the tube and back to the beginning including stops for pictures. I can't say that it was very interesting and the walk out was even less interesting since we had seen it all on the way in. The concept of it being a lava tube was interesting and the size of it was impressive. For this, I would say if you are in the area already pay the small fee and just go down the stairs into the tube. No need to do the whole walk. If you aren't in the area...don't make the trip.

it's definitely a unique place to visit but you should wear proper shoes as the 2km walk to and from the entrance has lots of rocky areas...the cave was dark,cold and wet but worth the visit if it's part of your tour.
I enjoyed it more than the group.  It's geared for those who are used to hiking.  Long lava tube - you don't have to walk the whole thing, but why not?  It is just 1 KM in and 1 KM out.
I was already satisfied with the other one in a park, so the impression was small. You don't need to see two of them, unless you are geographer.

I visited this sight with my brother yesterday and it was so cool! The lava tube was pretty intense. The walls were wide and the ceilings were tall. There were also lava shelves, balconies, etc, made from lava flows. It felt so cool to walk on the hardened lava, knowing that it flowed once as a bright and burning river of melted, hot hot hot rock!Stairs wind down from the entrance (an awesome gaping hole of an entrance), and it leads you down to the lave tube...It was about a 1 km long walk. Only 1 km out of the whole 7 km long lava tube was available to the public. Still, it was, an exciting walk. There are also signs along the way that describe the parts of the lava tube and brief you on how they came to be. I recommend you check it out whenever you visit Jeju Island! Thanks for reading my review!P.S. There is an admission fee, but it's inexpensive and affordable!

Great visit for the curious or those interested in nature and/or rocks. Nimble feet required. Numerous formations and lava sights to see and learn about.We took a taxi from Jeju city, around 22,000 won one-way. Very inexpensive entry fee though!The lava tube is more than 7 km long and 1 km is open to the public. There is modest lighting throughout though the footing is uneven at times. But hey, you're in a cave. We saw some Korean tourists carrying their infants to and fro inside! It took us more than an hour total to explore the whole thing.It gets really cool (temperature-wise) down there, so those sensitive to cold should bring an extra layer.

The park is quite large. Access to the cave is via two flight of stairs downwards into the earth. The temperature inside is colder than the outdoors, with the pathway often wet with water dripping from above the cave. Lighting is limited, and one has to use flash to take pictures, though a little tweaking of the camera could bring pretty good results without using the flash. There are written explanations regarding the lava layers. Because of time constraints, we were not able to finish exploring the cave to its end.

The cave is a must visit when come to Jeju. Be it winter, spring, summer, autumn... The temperate inside the cave stay the same through out the season. The rock inside the cave just so beautiful... Especially the one towards the end of the cave.

It's a 1 km walk from the entrance to the inner of the cave. Remember you need to walk 1km back, the place you enter is also the exit. Before you embark on your walk, there is a long flight of stairs to go down to the cave. If you have elderly people traveling with you, they may want to skip this place as the area is wet and slippery. There are lights to guide your path in the cave too but it is dim lit. Else, I would recommend this place for a great cooling walk, some geology insights for tourists too.
Uneven staircase down. Uneven flooring in cave. This cave is pretty natural and includes unusual formations. It's worth seeing but take a flashlight as the lighting is very poor.

Went there via a taxi tour which brought us to several attractions in Jeju during the day. It is a 1km stretch and you will take about 30-40 mins to walk to and fro. At the end, you will see the raved lava tube. Along the way inside, it is dark with dim lights. Nothing to worry about that. Information about the formations are also in English and it helps tourists to understand the formations. Good job on that.It gets colder as you walked deeper. However, temperature is still much higher than outside. We went during winter. Inside the lava tube is quite cosy-temperature.Nothing much to rave about unless you are really interested in geographical formations. Admission fee: 2000 won each person.

this is one of the logest lava tube according to the information stated there. i loved it so much because that's my first lava tube visit. i went there during winter so it's cold inside. Bring your jacket along because it is cold and water dripping from top. Very good experince if you never try it. I think this is only 1/4 (1km) of the length open for public. It will take you 50mins if you would like to take pictures.

The cave/ lava tube was interesting with many learning points The walk inside was about 1 km in semi darkness and wetness. Please wear the right footwear. I was using hiking boots so it was not an issue for me. If you are taking public transport bus 700 stops way too far from the cave about a walk of 3km or more...(after kimnyeong maze park, walk a further 500m) please be mentally prepared for a long, cold and uneventful walk (nothing to see along the way...maybe because it was winter). Cave was value for money though though you have to walk back 1km out of the cave from the same way you came in. Total 8km of walking if you take public transport. Take a cab or rent a car for greater convenience.

Manjang Cave is made of lava formation or lava tube as it is called. We walked about 1-2 km stretch of it only as not the whole tube was opened for tourist visitation.It is cold and dark. it is one of the longest lava tube in the world but it just is not my cup of tea. No  remorse on going into it but just was not awe blown away with it either. Go if you are a nature lover. skip if you are looking for awesome scenery to capture picture moments

Visit the lava tube only if you are easily awed by geological creations. 4 of us went, and not all were impressed as they thought it was just another cave. We read the description boards, and tried to spot the highlights to better our experience in the tube. As we went during winter, our coats were suffice for the low temperature within the tube. Wear sturdy footwear as the floor is uneven and wet.

If you like caves, then you have to visit Manjunggul Cave. It is simply fascinating! It is an extremely cheap entry fee and an easy kilometer walk inside the lava tube. Though the weather outside was rainy and wet, we thought the cave would be drippy and wet as well. It was quite dry. The interior is spacious and equipped with fairly good lighting along the guided route. For kids learning about volcanoes and the structures of the earth, this is a great field trip.

Chose to visit this attraction because it is UNESCO world heritage site. I and my kids went into the cave, make our way to the lava column, took some photos, then u-turn to make our way out. Nothing to see unless you are a geological fan. It is OK, just another "for the experience" trip.
If you have not experience going into a lava tube, you have to try Manjanggul Cave. A nice 30 mins walk inside the tube, and you will find a beautiful Manjang-gul at the end of the tube.

We originally did not schedule this visit as we have already seen Mulu Caves in Sarawak-East Malaysia.  But our hotel (TGG) told us that this is a very different cave (lava tubes).   The cost is not high at KRW2,000 and if you are already going to Seongsan Ilchbong, might as well make a visit.  We did not regret the visit.  It is really interesting to see how the lava flowing from Mt. Halla makes its way underground and forming the cave.  It is huge so you can see the magnitude of the lava flow.  Be sure to wear sturdy shoes as the ground is rather rocky and wet and you will need to walk carefully so that you won't fall.  I am amazed on how some ladies worn high heels!  It is also dim and cool so you must bring a jacket with you.  It is also a UNESCO site so definitely worth visiting.

Highly expected to visit this cave from the photo on the internet, because this site listed in the UNESCO as world heritage. But there is only a cave with stone that I don't know. Reach the end of the cave only big rock that from frozen lava. Maybe for cave lover you'll like it.Tips: bring jacket because so cold inside.

Good experience if you have not been to one.You need to have the passion in Nature and interest in Volcanology to appreciate the beauty, otherwise it is just a boring cave.There was this big group of young students walking and singing. When they reached the end at the lava column, they took some pictures and headed back. I guess they are too young to understand mother nature.

The stairs down into the cave system are steep and plentiful, so if you have trouble with stairs then you should skip it.  Also, if you don't like walking on uneven ground then you should skip it, because most of the cave floor is natural stone, so it's rough and uneven in many places.  There's also small standing pools of water in places, so watch where you step.  You don't have to walk the whole cave length, since it's very long indeed, so you can just do what we do and walk part of the way and then back again.  But you do need appropriate footwear, and no, high heels are NOT appropriate footwear.And remember, this is a natural cave system, not a fun park, so don't go expecting anything beyond what it is.
It is interesting to see the longest cave although it is a bit boring if you do it alone! I liked it and I learned something!

We were there about an hour before closing so there weren't many people in the cave. It's pretty dark and wet in the cave. The floor is also uneven. I must say that it's quite an awesome cave (different from the ones I've seen in NZ, USA & Switzerland) though I can imagine that it would be quite boring if there was no one to explain to you the different features of the cave.If you don't have a local guide with you and are not a Geography fan, you might want to give this a skip. But if you are into caves/rocks/Geography, I think you'd love it!

Dark cave, chilly, dripping water and uneven steps were all I felt for one hour journey in and u-turn out of the cave. Not much to see really unless you are acompanied by an expert or archelogist who can make rock and mud come alive and tell stories. I have been to few caves over the world and find this least interesting and dull.

Traversing through Manjanggul was nothing like my other spelunking experiences! This was more civilized and organized :) Manjanggul's explorable/walkable area is only 1km but it's already enough for you to appreciate how Jeju's volcanic origins formed these natural wonders for us to see.

Make sure to bring a jacket with you to the cave if you get cold, there is about a 10C temperature difference from outside to inside. So if you visit in Summer, it's a great break from the heat and humidity. It's about a kilometer walk, so give yourself plenty of time. Overall,a. Great attraction for all those visiting the island!!

Manjang cave in overall was really nice expierence, but we got a bit cold.When outside is more than 30 degrees, and you go downstairs, it's a bit...cool.And wet as well.But I won't whine about it, because the expierence you get there is more important!We were walking really slowly taking pictures of everything (if you don't have a good camera, pictures won't bet any good ://)They have diferent color lights and it makes cave more visitor-friendly.Only thing is that there is really crowded...Even though we went there on a weekday.So be prepared to see a lot of people there as well.

I went there because I have never been to a volcanic cave before. It was interesting, with lighted signs describing different rock formations, but overall, the experience is average. The cave gets colder the deeper you walk into it. It is about 750m one direction, a total of about 1.5km walking. The cave is cold and damp, so be prepared with a jacket and good walking shoes. Water drips from the top of the cave, and there are also puddles of water, so take care while walking in there, and wear a pair of good shoes that has good grip.There is no public transport that goes directly to the caves. We took a public bus, but after alighting, we had to catch a taxi for a ride to the entrance of the attraction. If you are going to visit Jeju, know that the attractions are all over the island, and it is not easy to get around on public buses. Most people join a tour, or get a taxi to bring them around for the whole day.

Jeju had a volcano that erupted long time ago, its lava flowed thru the Manjang cave leaving a lava tube that is about 4 kilometers long, The part open to public is about 1 kilometer with three entrances. Although lighted, it is still dark, wet and cold inside. Although it is an experience to go in, but be careful as it is wet and dark, the floor are not level, especially in the inner portion where there is almost no road. For the adventurous, bring along flashlight and wear rubber shoes. As for me, I just walk part of the way to feel it, as it's not worth the risk to go thru the whole cave. Again, it may help if there are better lighting showing important landmark within the cave like other caves in asia. Underground cave of Palawan, stalagtite cave in Halong Bay for example.

The cave is a mysterious wonder that Mother Earth presented to us. This cave is a long lava tube in which once lava flowed many years ago. You could guessed the history and patterns of how lava had flowed from the lines, colors and patterns on the wall of the cave. If only the whole 4km could have been opened to public instead of just the 1km. I believe that they are more wonders along the rest of the tube. I would spend the whole day here if I could.

Visited just because it seems that if you visit Jeju, you should visit one of its lava cave. I searched on the internet, and i think this lava cave is the most popular amongst the touristIt's a very big cave indeed. We were amazed by the size of the tunnel and imagined how was the lava itself that made the cave. But actually, It's a long, cold, dark, pathway for nothing. Yeah, maybe you can find some weird shaped rocks caused by the lava. Then what? your journey will be finished on some kind of a deck to see a big rocks standing in front of you and highlighted by colored lights. That's all. And the only way back is the same way you came in from. So boring!

Nevertheless, people always recommend us to visit this cave when we're in Jeju. what we found is around 2km long cave with cold temperature all the way. if you quite a fan for geology and similar, this cave is exactly for you.the 'main' attraction is located at the very end of the cave. nothing more , nothing less...come if you have free time.. but not suitable for older people due to steep stair and slippery.
It is just a long, dark, unending walk in a tunnel and nothing to see.Just a nice temperature inside. Don't bother and not suitable for older people...

Great place to explore, really. Worth a visit for sure.Before entering I would suggest though to visit the small museum, where some facts are explained before hand. We didn't see it before and then discovered a few facts after visiting the museum on our way out. Would have been better the opposite.I would also suggest to bring something warm and to wear snickers. As it is stated in almost all the previous review, it is quite humid and dump downstairs. No wheelchair access.

This was one of those places on earth that fascinates me... It was a rare opportunity to see and walk through a lava cave!  There is no place like this where I'm from, so I thought it was delightful! The day I went, it was hotter than Hades outside. Once we were inside, the air temperature immediately dropped. The farther down you went, the cooler the air. My hands were actually freezing cold.  Although its not necessary, I recommend you bring a light jacket and explore!

Very educational and interesting. How the cave was formed and the type of formation. It was nice and cool there. Be careful not to slip as the rocks can be wet and slippery. Some stairs with no wheelchair access.
It's definitely a different weather from the above, pls bring along jacket if you enter. The attraction is really worth for a kilometre walk.

Must see in Jeju. Biggest lava tube in the world. 2 km from the bus stop, close to maze park. Do not forget tripod to take good pictures as it is rather dark in the cave. Good place to cool down after summet heat.

Place is very interesting but gets a little boring sometimes especially if you don't see anything special anymore. If you are alone while exploring, the cave might bore you. But formations, especially the lava lines on the wall are very interesting. I just don't think if finishing the 1km lava tube is worth it. Place is very developed already compared to other caves in other places, especially in the Philippines. By the way, it's very cold inside so wear a jacket or gloves.

Before we visited Jeju, this was one of our number one places to visit. I must say, we were not disappointed. The cost was a couple dollars per person and we spent over an hour exploring the depths of the lava tube. A nice bonus was the fact it was nice and cool inside the lave tube which was a blessed relief from the heat outside! When we visited, there were a number of other visitors but not so many as to make it crowded. Walking through what once was a path of scalding lava is an interesting experience. The tube has a number of informational signs along it that explain the different formations you see and how they were formed. For someone uninterested in geology the cave could be boring, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Visiting this caves/tubes you can walk trough the geology! A huge tunnel made by lava rivers 300 thousands years ago, now accessible and well explained. A lot of lava stalactites and stalagmites and huge lava stones felt down from the ceiling. It is unbelievable how "untouched" their rest through the millenni. Nice job by the administrators of the park. It costs only 2000 won.You can also enjoy a free car parking and a small restaurant.

A geographical wonder and respite from the heat in high summer. Fascinating to see how lava carved out this cave which represents how the whole island (and many like it in the world) were formed. Recommended but also suggest you take a sweater or light jacket. It is cold and clammy!

I went their with my wife. I didn't find the place as interesting and exciting as other people claimed. My recommendation, unless you are a geologist this place has nothing substantial to offer. Take a warm cloth and comfortable shoes when you visit this place. The temperature in the cave is low(you feel cool even in summer) and the floor is wet and a little bit slippery.A person can have knowledge about lava tubes but personally I felt unsatisfied. The cave is very dark for anyone to figure out things inside. Information boards inside give information about the site. If a visitor has enough time to visit, you can drop by this place. But, if your schedule is tight you can skip this place.

It was an eye-opening experience as i have not seen a lava tube before. It is roughly around 2 km walk to and fro the entrance to see the lava tube. Along the way, you will be able to see the how the lava transformed the cave. Although i went during the summer period (Aug 2013), i would recommend bringing a jacket as the cave is really cold for me. Needless to say, comfortable walking shoe would be needed as the floor are uneven. The maze is rather near to the cave and both can be planned in the same day  itinerary.

I had never seen a lava tube before, this one is quite interesting. You can go 1k in and back, and it's very cold inside, a good break from the summer heat. Upon walking out, you feel like a melting ice cube. Like all attractions on Jeju, is missing some English-speaking staff - we forgot a beach bag inside and it was very hard to explain that to the staff, who kept telling us we cannot go back in without a ticket. The bus stop for this on the Jeju intercity bus by this name is very far from the actual attraction, fortunately a cab driver saw us and took us there - we would had to walk 3-4k and there are no sidewalks or anything.
I went during the summer months so that it really helps that the manjang cave was really nice and cooling in there. Really nice experience to walk through the cave

A lovely, lovely lava tube cave - totally different from the limestone caves with regard to structures (chambers, tunnels, columns, shelves, stalagmites etc) found inside. The lighting within the tube is great - kept to the essentials for safe walking and with no glaring colourful lights that makes the structures look artificial. The temperature within the lava tube is cool and very pleasant ... could spend hours here hiding from the summer heat outside.

Bring your tripod and dslr to take great low light photos of this lava tube. 1 km of winding and detailed textures of lava caves to challenge any photographer to take it all in. We came into the cave during the hot summer day but the cold cave temperature had pleasantly guided us through its many highlights. A must for any nature lover

it was just a super long cave that is really cold, perfect when you are visiting during the hot summers. Wear comfortable shoes because you will be avoiding water puddles, trekking on uneven rocky floors. Its just a super long walk in and out.

This was fun. it only took about an hour to go all the way through. there is a 2,000W charge. its chilly inside so if you bring the kids, pack their jackets. Its solid lava so it is not as colorful or full of stalagtytes as other natural caves but being in a lava tube is a unique experience and this one is really big. enjoy!
Lava cave. Big, huge cave. cold inside. can see the lines and cracks that lava form. The spotlight makes the rocks wall look beautiful

We go in the end of June , basically it is hot outside, but inside the cave is cold and a bit freezing, take along taxi ride from Soegwipo area, cause we travel in 5, 1 senior over 75 , 1 teenager ,1 children of 7,  so we decide to book taxi for 8 hours to explore Jeju it is more convenient and save time  than using bus , but a little pricey 120.000 krw for whole day, After reaching the cave and go down to look inside , my wife and mother in law surrender, cause it is to exhaust to walk 2 kilometer ( in and out )for senior and a bit dim,   Cave is big , but there is no living creatures like bats or others, I my self do not really excited at first,  but my 7 years son and my teenagers daughter really like to explore the cave, so we are not prepared and just go. A bit chilling but still bearable, no toilet inside so prepared your self , the light is dim but still able to see around, there is water dropping from ceiling but not too often ,the water clean and no smell, the pathway is not level and bumpy ,watery here and there in a few area the but still manageable and walkable ,  don't have to worry,  if my 7 years old can do it so can others , at last this is a pleasant and unique experience, a bit exhausting walk , but worth a try

this is  rare chance to walk down lava tubes and look at the odd shapes and formations caused by the molten rock. You can see different layers of lava that once flowed here and see how the laval squeezed through smaller passages.   Consider bringing an umbrella or a very light shell. It can be damp and sometimes water drips from the ceilings. Also, it's significantly cooler than outside.   All in all, a must.

I had never seen dried lava before (other than when hiking hallasan which was only the day before) so I thought this was super cool. There are tons of informative signs along the way too. Oh and it's cool inside--not humid!
A natural spot form by the volcano. It is very cold inside, recommended to bring raincoat as there as water dripping from above.

If you are expecting stalagmites and stalactites, this is not a place. If there were, we probably missed them. It s a dark underground cave and very interesting to see the lava flows. You can see imprints of such flows on the actual ground you re walking on. It s a bit nippy, so if you are prone to being cold, may want to take a light sweater. There is no bathroom in the tunnel (which my son figured out trying to get out halfway in the tunnel/cave. He had to run back the way we came to find one.) It s interesting. I just wished that there were more lights in the tunnels so one can appreciate it more. Uneven ground due to the lava flows, as expected. 2000W/$1.75 to get in, half for kids.If you've never been into one of these types of caves, you should.  If you have, maybe worth skipping.

Been to a lot of caves in my life but these are so interesting as they have been shaped by the lava flow. There are information boards throughout the caves telling you how certain things in the cave were formed from the lava - definitely a must see if you are going to Jeju!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater, Seongeup Folk Village, Oedolgae Rock, and finally Jeongbang Falls. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.
An eye opening experience to walk along a real lava flow cave! Bring along a small touch light; as well as a warm jacket as it can get a little chilly inside the cave.

It felt pretty surreal to walk through the caves, and I mean it in a good way! Definitely worth the visit.Just one advice - grab a cardigan when you go: even in hot summer days it is pretty cold in the cave! and also a torch can be useful so you can see better the shapes of the lava walls.

The lava cave was dark and spooky but then, that is part of the fun and adventure.  I took the long walk in the dark cave, looking at the various lava formations and reading the information that was provided about them. The cave is not completely dark, subtle lighting from lanterns are provided to show us the way into the cave. Some areas are brighter than others. The floor is very uneven, wet and rocky so you have to wear sensible flat shoes.  I got to see the Turtle Rock (Lava Raft), Lava flowstones and the 7.6 meter lava column at the end of the cave which is the highlight of our subterranean adventure. I saw a couple with flashlights and wondered why I had not thought of bringing one. I will definitely bring one next time.  It was a lovely adventurous experience at the Mangangul lava tube. I recommend it to visitors to Jeju Island because it is not every day that you get to see a geological wonder like this  UNESCO World Heritage site.

Ok- this place was pretty cool...but here is the deal-- it says "Cave entrance" which makes you think that a "Cave exit" will at some point present itself. It does not. You go a km to the end then turn around. It is bumpy and not well-lit. I am (relatively) young and surefooted, as were my companions, and we all noted that this place could never exist in the US: they would get sued in a minute...someone would fall and break their leg and it would be all over. It was interesting, but for one thing: we had unfortunate timing. We went in with like 5 busloads of extremely loud Chinese teens (mostly male). It was insane, annoying and...after a while, slightly dangerous (they started running past us). There is NO ONE from the cave to be seen in the cave (only an occasional phone...maybe 2 in the entire kilometer distance), so no one was there to even say anything about this. Not horrible, but got old after a while. Once we got some distance between them and us, things improved.Oh and they don't tell you about the spiders until the visitors center afterwards...This is not a place for kids or old people or anyone with unsure footing. I am not exaggerating when I say the ground is totally uneven...and there are random stone blocks scattered about to cover holes or water..it was rather rough walking-- at times it took away from the coolness of the cave because you cannot walk without watching the ground...

A lava tube showing the flow of lava and various natural formation such as the lava shelves or columns. Inside the cave is chilly (around 11c when outside is around 25c), dark, wet and slippery. Bring your jacket and sturdy shoe for this visit. Heels is a definite no no. Forget about your camera (too dark for photo taking) and just enjoy the brisk walk. To and fro takes you around 45mins-1hr.

This attraction was quite an adventure and somewhat scary at the same time. Throughout the long walk to the end of the cave, it was very dark, wet, slippery and bumpy. Make sure that you wear sturdy shoes(no sandals, flip flops), carry a light/flashlight, and something to cover yourself/head (jacket w/ hood, hat). The entire trek (roundtrip) took about let's say 45 min. to an hour- depending on your pace. Also, it's difficult to take a good picture due to the lack of light and darkness - FYI

We travelled here by bus and got completely soaking wet walking the 20 minutes from the main road to the cave. Unfortunately it wasn't worth the soaking! It was pretty boring and after 30 minutes walk up and down we were out in the ran again.I would only recommended visiting if you have a thing for geology or if you have a car and happen to be passing by.

It is a lava tube stretching 1km deep which means you need to walk 2km to get to the end and back to the entrance. It is a stunning cave and it's among UNESCO World Heritage sites. It is a popular site in Jeju and you won't be alone in the deep cave. It gets cold inside the cave and the floor is uneven so a coat and a pair of comfortable walking shoes/runners come highly recommended. The cave walk does not take that long, so it's a must visit.
It was cool and adventurous! It was an experience for my daughter and I... something she'll remember, very wet and damp w/lots of rocks and very cold temp...the acoustics were cool too!

I love nature but somehow Manjang Cave failed to impress me. I expected to see more so i was kinda dissapointed. Unless you're studying about lava formations, otherwise there was really nothing much to see. Wearing good sport shoes is recommended since some of the path is quite bumpy.

Coat/mittens/warm clothing, good walking shoes, and at least a small flashlight are a must.  The entrance stairs are steep and can be wet/slippery.  The lighting inside varies in how well it is placed.  The floor surface is uneven and can be wet/slippery.This is a popular tourist destination on Jeju Island and so there will be waves of tourists and school groups pouring down into the lava tube cave as their tour buses arrive, but if you are patient and can take your time, there will be periods of quiet and peacefulness in between the groups during which you can enjoy the cave - but if you don't wear a coat and are chilled, it will make it hard to be patient and wait out the hordes of teenagers and other tourist groups!

If you are a UNESCO World Heritage Site ticker, this is on the list. I m not a cave fan, so walking into the lava tube, taking a u-turn and walking the same way out in the damp and dark, jostled by rude kids on a field trip wasn t one of the highlights of my trip. In any case, no regrets going there because it would be weird not to go at all -- it s a Jeju landmark, and I would have wondered what I missed if I didn t come here.If you re checking out the Seongsan Ilchubong, it's pretty close by (if you're in a car). You should allot another hour for this. It s not too far from the Jeju airport, too.The thing is, once is enough   if I were to come back to Jeju and my friends insist that we go here, I would let them go ahead and hang out somewhere else.Like the title says, it's a cave.------Tip for parents:I tried to warn a family with a baby that it s not the best place if you have little kids, but they ignored me. Hello, it s dark, with water dripping and the terrain is uneven rock. You have to walk down some steep stairs for about half a minute to start your tour. There are a lot of people, and sometimes they bump into you because they can't see well in the dark. That family was going to take a baby stroller into this cave. Wah, suit yourself. It was so insane. If they trip in the dark, the baby could be hurt.
The cave is very cool and seems to go on forever.  There are informative photos with descriptions along the way so you know what it is you are looking at.

We went there after 5hrs cycling under the Sun at Udo Island.  The feeling was like, from oven jump into the fridge - it's definitely have a great cooling effect! It is very much different from Batu Cave @ Malaysia or Silver Cave @ China, Guilin.  As this is a Lava Tube.  Its long and not much of stalactite or stalagmite.  It is a long cooling lava tube.  I am very impressed by the way they develop and maintain it.  It is clean and 'safe' to walk (you'll need around 1 hour to walk in and out, and it is pretty dark and quiet inside) about, instruction & illustration are clear.  I would say it will be more fun if you imagine how this tube has been formed and even picture yourself in the movie :)  Wear sport shoes for a comfort walk.  If you have time then it is good to experience this. Note:1)  I bump into a group of backpackers from Hong Kong where they took public transport to this cave, and I was told that they need to walk quite a distance from the bus stop to this place.  So check properly if you were to go with kids & elderly that you might want to avoid such a long walk. 2) Next to the entrance there is a museum, there is a fun digital photo service there where you can choose the sightseeing background and snap the picture of yourself, then amend it, you can pay and print it out if you are happy with it or you can just re take as many times as you wish! It's all self services and I had fun here! It's not expensive tho, try it out if you happens to be here. 3) Nearby Manjang Cave there is this Kimyeong Maze park, just about 5-10mins walk away, don't miss this if you are around this area too.

Definitely a special cave. As it is a lava tube, the floor is also made of solid lava, aka uneven flooring. Bring good hiking boots as it takes at least 40 minutes to reach the end. Advice to use a tripod for good photos.

Having visited limestone caves in other countries before, what was different about this experience was the stalactite or staglamite looking structures were not made of limestone but lava.  The walking surface was very interestingly grooved unlike limestone caves but called for very careful walking at parts. The lava stack at the end of the section open to public was pretty awesome and is helpfully bathed in lights so one can see.What I wanted to point out is that we happened to visit at a time when many Korean schools send their students out on educational trips (we visited in early April).  So the lava tube was full of noisy teenagers who seemed more interested in shouting out to each other and seeing who could run through the tube fastest than in appreciating one of nature's wonders.  Seems like Korean teenagers are just like teenagers everywhere else!  So if you are going in early April, be warned.  If it is going to bother you then better give this a miss because you will be in a dark confined space where sounds are magnified.

Manjanggul is a nature creation which 1km of it is opened for visitors to walk through. However majestic it is, if you are not a keen learner of geography or stones and cave, this walk would be boring for you. If you are there in Jeju for a short trip, I would recommend you to skip this instead.
This is not a cave that was slowly worn away.  It is a tube that was created in a speck of time.  The unique conditions needed to make a lava tube of this size and length is pretty impressive.

Manjang Cave is near the northeast portion of Jeju, therefore if you are staying on the touristy south side of the island it will take over an hour to get here.The cave is part of a cave system that extends for kilometers that has been given some sort of UNESCO title (kind of like every natural sight on the island it seems). While the cave is indeed interesting, the allure of the cave stops once you descend down the stairs from the entrance and realize that you should have come more prepared.If you decide to embark to the cave, come with hiking boots or waterproof shoes and leave your Toms or Tori Burch shoes in the car because 95% of the cave is unimproved meaning walking along uneven surfaces filed with cracks and cold water puddles that may cause sprained ankles or ending up with cold and dirty feet is more than likely to occur.Also, the cave is dimly lit so unless you are Bruce Wayne or a vampire, you can't really see diddly-squat. So bring a flashlight or come hardcore prepared with a headlamp.Lastly bring a sweater or jacket because the cave is really cold. It's like being inside a commercial freezer but with cold wet feet. Not cool... I mean too cool LOL.As for the cave itself, it is impressive, but gets really repetitive and unlike the photos on the signs and pamphlets, the lighting is so bad you can't really see anything. Aside from "turtle rock" and lava stalactites, everything started to look the same. Would I return? Methinks not.The cost is 2000 won per adult, which seems to be the standard fare of most touristy spots on the island including the waterfalls and Sunrise Peak.

i never been in a cave before. so its all new to me. it can get chilly inside when you go deeper. you need to walk about 1km in to the iconic lava thg. is a really good geographic experience on how such nature create wonders. have a good footwear cause it has uneven and wet surface.
An interesting walk underground in a 1 km long cave. Some people would find fascinating, others might get abit claustrophobic.Very cheap, about 90 pence per person. Beautiful grounds on the outside.

It's amazing how the lava flows and make it one of the longest lava tube in the world! Its dark inside but it's interesting to experience the structure formed from the lava. However only around 2km of the tube is open to public but it's good enough for us to have a good memory of it.

I've never been in a lava tube before, but it was a lot like a cave. The formations inside are pretty interesting and the park does a good job lighting them colorfully. It was a nice walk. However, it is very touristy and if you've been to bigger caves in other parts of the world it's just cool, not extremely impressive.

It's quite exciting to walk down the huge lava tube and imagine the flow of lava melting its way to the ocean. You see the striped walls indicating different levels of the flow, each stripe has a bit different color. Glossy lava sinters, black, dark red and orange. Fantastic landscape of big and small stalactites and stalagmites. It's a shame, only a small part of the lava tube is opened for public. And the trail is arranged pretty dull. Nothing (except the natural beauty of the cave) would take your breath away and make you come again.There are many tunnels that branches from the main tube and go further and further after the end of the main trail. With a proper lighting and clever management it could be a fantastic place that would attract plenty of tourists and make them come again and again to explore this place.
Glad that I had flat shoes. It was pretty dark inside. Not warm during winter. Be better to go there during hot summer days.

If you love the nature, do not forget to visit this place. This lava tube stretches out to about 1km. Do watch out for your steps as it is quite dark inside, unnecessary to bring a torch light anyway.

For those visiting this cave expecting amazing cave formations you may be disappointed. On Jeju island all caves are more accurately defined as lava tubes. These vestiges from Jeju's volcanic origins are strange, dark, and geological wonders.Tips for visitors, expect Manjang Cave to be cold, dark, and rough surfaces to walk on. NO sandals or high heels! Hiking boots are a far better option. If you come into the lava tube expecting glittering cave formations you may not have a great time. However, if you want to explore a truly rare geological wonder, take this journey into the darkness to enjoy a unique experience.

Don't miss it. These caves are incredible. They stretch for miles. I took my students on a field trip and they all loved it. It's a Unesco world heritage site and an absolute must if you're visiting Jeju.

The Manjanggul lava tubes caves are amazing and the walk is well worth it.  Dont forget to take your flash camera as you will not see sights like this again.The sides of the cave are smooth from the flowing hot lava and show striations along the sides from when the lava level was falling.  The size of the tune varies from small to very large.  Lighting has been set up to high-lite many of the features.  Wear good waterproof shoes as the floor is uneven  and there are many puddles from dripping water
About 40 min taxi from the airport. The cave is a must see if you visit Jeju. Walk inside the cave, beutiful lighting. Amazing.

This is the longest lava tube in the world.  It's 7kms long and only 1km is open to the public.  It's rather spectacular to be in it, to appreciate the wonders of Nature.  For the cynics, you would probably ask yourself why you want to part with money to walk in almost darkness, through a wet and uneven surface, just to affirm yourself that you are visiting one of the UNESCO's accredited natural wonders of the world.  For me, it's a been there, done that experience.  Enough said!

this is the largert lava tube in the world (well, that we have found) and it's fascinating.  Really huge tube, interesting rock formations all through.  The walk is quite easy (a little uneven and damp, headlight recommended) and the informative signs are useful.  Not that expensive and well worth the trip.

We have never seen or heard of anything like this before. Probably its the only one in the world. The 1km walk each way, was full of facts about lava formations.We had wonderful time, and just loved what we saw & learned.

I had read the reviews here before my boyfriend and I went, but I am glad I didn't let the negative ones sway me. This place is really awesome. Just imagining the lava flow through as we were walking was mind blowing! And it's really NOT that dark down there. I mean it is a cave so don't expect the sun to be shining but I don't know what people were expecting! It's a really great experience and we loved seeing all the different ways lava forms after hardening. I highly suggest this! It was a bit wet down there so wear a hood or hat and some sneakers.

The Manjang Cave was one of the "must-dos" in my itinerary. I can only say it was somewhat a disappointment. It was not quite as spectacular as I have thought it would be. I was with my mum and dad both 60. My mum did not take the walk well and headed back halfway. My dad stayed behind to do some photo-taking, Here's the bottomline:- If you have never ever been in a lava cave before - go for it!- If you are traveling with young children / older folks / people with bad knees and weak ankles - give this a miss. The initial flight of stairs can be quite a walk. The floor of the cave can be wet and uneven- If you have been to lava caves before and if you do not have a mental benchmark - go for it if you have time- If you have seen the most wondrous lava caves and already formed expectations - skip it... more than likely this might underperform

I was hoping to see how magnificient the lava is in one of the widest lava tube before going into the Manjang Cave. It is quite disappointing to realise that the cave is not entirely illuminated. The lighting is minimal in the cave which made walking and lava observation really difficult. I was going with my mum of around 60 years old, it is really difficult for her to see clearly in the tunnel. And the fact that you have to walk for  ~1 km into the tunnel and then the same way back is not entiring pleasing. When I was walking down the tunnel, I always thought "there will be better illumination/rocks in the next turn". However, it was quite disappointing that this happens only at the end of the tunnel where you saw an illuminated lava pillar. I would recommend you to go to other caves if you want to see the lava clearly.

The longest lava tunnel in the world and designated as a natural monument.  Plan to spend a couple of hours here and wear study shoes with traction. Also bring a flashlight.  Walking in and out, over a mile distance.  Some light provided in the interior of the cave, but fairly dim.  The floor of the cave is rippled, uneven, sharp and unpaved, with occasional stepping stones placed in areas.  May cause injury, if you stumble, so you need to walk carefully the entire way in and out of the cave.  The entrance of  the cave requires you to walk down about 3 flights of stairs, which you will have to climb up to exit the cave.  Not reccommended for elderly, frail people and young children.  See some different lava formation along the way.

If you have an opportunity to visit these lava tubes, then make sure you do!   We have lava caves in New Zealand and I have seen the lava tubes on Hawaii, but these are giants in comparrison.  The grounds of Manjang Caves are well kept.From the carpark it is only a 3 or 4 minute walk along a concrete path to the entrance of the caves.   We were expecting big, but these caves are huge!There are a number of steps leading down into the mouth of the cave and then you are inside this amazing formation.   It was quite an eerie feeling as we ventured deeper and deeper inside the tube which measures approx 5meters wide and up to 10 meters high.   The temperature is quite pleasant inside the caves and it is a little damp.   Even though we all had good walking shoes on, we still had to be quite careful of where we walked on the uneven, slippery  floor.   It is true that there is not a lot of light inside the cave, but we felt that the dim lighting added to the atmosphere.   In hindsight, a torch might have been helpful.All in all, definitely well worth the visit and would highly recommend to all. I would recommend that this is probably not a safe place for the elderly and very young children.  My elderly parents waited for us at the main building where there was a restaurant, shop and toilets.

Good chance to explore natureof lava tube..I shall recommend for walk alley to be build along the way inside the tube..its to hard to walk on the slippery rocks.Hence to put more highlight inside the tube..its too dark inside

This is quite a long, dark cave with uneven rough ground surface so it's a bit dangerous. One must be careful with every step. However, inside is a treasure of lava tubes & our guide told us that each one represents a volcanic activity. At the far end is a unique rock formation or a stalactite shaped like a mother & child. Really amazing!

I was on my wear the Toms until they literally fall off my feet, and this definitely got them about there. If you do anything before going to this cave, make sure you have the right waterproof, grippy-ish shoes for the job. But really, this was cool, literally.  I managed to be hot and sweaty almost everywhere we went while on the island, but in the cave he temp drops to a comfortable 50something degrees. Just glorious! Is it worth the walk? I'm not sure. It was nice enough, and definitely cool to say I have been inside a cave at least once. So I guess I would put this on the itinerary if you are visiting the island for he first time. Would I go again? Likely not, I think once was enough!

This is a must if you're on the island - a great experience to be in the middle of where lava has flown from years past.  Best to wear footwear that will handle uneven terrain.  Tempature is cooler but not uncomfortable with a jacket.  Really great visual xamples of how lava changes the landscape.  It's very dark but the lighting in place is enough to get you through and keeps the mystery / awe.  The walk to the end of the tunnel is about 1000 m (and worth it).
Haven't been to any of these caves despite visiting many places in the world. The size of the cave was very impressive when you imagined how lava flowed through to develop such a cave.
I don't like much the environment inside the cave. So much water dripped off and dark. Nothing much to see. I liked only the cooling temperature.

I'm not a fan of dark hole underground but lava tube is something new to me, so I give it a go. Taking the eastern line bus (the orange bus) from Seongsan, it took us close to 1 hour to get off at the Manjanggul bus stop. Then we took a taxi for the ~2km stretch to get to the entrance of the cave. Needless to say, the tube itself is dark, the surface uneven as expected, drippy and chilly for me. They only open 1 km section of the whole tube, where we can see a quite nice lava formation at the end of the tunnel, still it feels like the longest walk in my life. I think that 1 experience is enough for me. Not for claustrophobic people. What I do like is the view between the bus stop and the cave entrance. It is beautiful.

The lava tube was quite dark all around,.... Except some light they provided... You be Able to see the natural lava tube formation and some feature like lava shelf raft etc... The journey is around 1 hour round trip.Note that the dark surrounding coupled with uneven rock ground,make it extremely tiring for the ankle... Could easily twist an anke or knee here and there....
This UNESCO cave is well worth it. It's a long walk through the black lava cave but fascinating. Leave plenty of time if you are a slow walker because of uneven surfaces.

The well-landscape beautiful environment surrounding the entrance to the "Manjanggul Lava Tube" enticed us into the cave which can be described as a hole in the ground.  As we descended the steps, we realized it was quite dark and the ground was not level.  Walking has to be slow otherwise we may slip and fall on the damp and watery walkway.  We also have to be careful that we will not be drenched by the dripping waters from the top of the cave.There were two or three highlights of the walk, one is a giant-shaped lingzhi (or mushroom) and the other is at the apparent end of the 'tube', two intertwined stalagmites growing to a hole at the top.The good thing about the cave is the cool temperate and although we were sweating from the walk, we liked it. So for those who fear the cold, take a sweater and also a cap!

Really enjoyed the place, great place to visit. As mentioned, more for casual visitors, not cave-experts. Can drip quiet a bit in places, so a rain jacket or hat can be helpful. Good shoes definitely a plus, though it is not a difficult walk and lit well enough. About 1km in, same way back out. Didn't feel too cold, pleasant.

A bit wet due to recent rains.  Luckily I wore a wide hat which was perfect.  Enough light to see where you were going without twisting an ankle.  Reminded me of the place where Phantom might have lived in Phantom of the Opera.
A nice break from the heat, it's nice and cool down there!You can walk 1km, I think we spent about an hour down there total.Really slippery, be careful!One of the coolest things I did in Jeju.

Having experienced caves in the USA, I was expecting a similar experience.  Not at all the the case on Jeju with the manjanggul caves.  This UNESCO site is self led, wet, slippery, dark and EXCELLENT!  Also, very cool in temperature which was very welcome in the humid conditions present on Jeju in July.

Cool not just because of the rock formations but also it is a great relieve from the temp outside on a hot summer day. This may not be the most spectacular of rock formations but it is cool enough not to miss.

I guess if you've been inside a really spectacular cave before this won't be much to you but for someone who doesn't go into caves that often, like me, this is a cool experience. the cave is nice and cool so it is refreshing on a hot day. It's also good to visit during a rainy day as it is underground. It's dimly lit and has a spooky ambiance. part of the walls look like they're melting chocolate. I would recommend it as it is one of the highlights of the island.

I would echo an earlier review that said that you should not bother with this if you have done any caving or similar - this is aimed at casual visitors not experts. It is a gentle wander in a cool cave that is appropriately lit, reasonably level and there is enough English signage to explain what you need to know. It is the fact that this was a lava tunnel that is not interesting and the signs do explain how the lava flowed, melted and cut down and through from other tunnels. 1) Wear sensible shoes.2) If it has been raining it can drip a lot inside though on our visit I did not think so.3) Some might feel it is cold - I did not
A place to discover the force of the nature, slighly cold inside the cave
This was my first visit to a lava tube or cave.  It was a great little walk through a dark and amazing cave.

If you've been in a real cave, you'll only be downgrading if you go to this lava tube. It is a plane tube with lots of lights. There is no cool dark places, and the only formation at the end is meh. I prefer a normal cave with formations and a tour in which everyone turns of the lights ^^.

We did a day trip covering Sunrise Peak and the Manjanggul Lava Tubes. It was a long drive though from the south. It was quite interesting to experience the vastness inside these tubes, imagining all these form by lava thousands of years ago. It was dark indeed and photography or videoing seemed very difficult. It was cool and moist, dark of course, not suitable for those in dress shoes or high heels. Be prepared to come along with proper walking shoes with good grip and some areas are wet.  Not a suitable site for family with young children. The end of the walk was a constructed steel walkway to see the "turtle". Not something to wow at, but just knowing that , that is the farthest you can go. Being a tourist attraction, food was easily availble.

It is dark inside so you need a good camera if you are planning to take some pictures. It is also cold so you might want to wear more layers of clothing. Through the tube, there are signboards that explain certain geological formations and structures (in several languages). Around 2km of the tube is opened for visitors and at the end, there is a lava column that is well lit for photo opportunity.Becareful inside as it is slippery, cold and a bit dark despite the lamps at an interval from each other.

Since it was a UNESCO attraction, I was expecting more. Like pillars or more rock formation or something. I was sadly dissapointed. There's nothing much to see. It was really dark and wet. I find myself concentrating more on finding my footing on the volcanic rocks then looking at the tube itself. It was relatively inexpensive. Only 2500won. So it's still value for money.

This is a lava tube, so don't expect magnificent views inside! Pitch black. and very cold! Do remember to bring along a jacket if you are visiting. Good footwear would be better (cushioned ones) as the walking surface is rather rough and uneven.Get to see the world's largest lava gest after a 2km walk, nothing magnificent, but I guess it's worth the 1000won entrance fee. I suggest you only visit if you're in the area though...

This was probably my favorite attraction - it wasn't a place where you go and just take pictures but also get to learn something. Throughout the cave, there are display boards highlightng the different lava formations. Plus, it's pretty awesome to be walking in a cave formed by lava flow. I felt like Indiana Jones! If you walk all the way to the end of the cave, you will see a pretty magnificent lava formation.Wear proper shoes as the cave floor is wet and being a jacket as it gets fairly cool underground.

Really interesting lava tube which is definitely worth the visit if you are in Jeju. Spent about an hour plus walking through the cave back and forth. Temperature was pretty cold down there so make sure you are well insulated and wearing good footwear for slightly uneven terrain. Beautiful lava formation with stalactites and other rock features. A must visit for geog geeks and nature lovers! youths get discount off entrance fee, just flash your identification card or passport.

This cave is actually a volcanic Lava tube, not limestone cave. So don't expect to see amazing things like what you see in Guilin and Yunan.Same as reviewer ggkoh, I visited there after a day of persistent rain. The cave is wet, filled with small pool of water here and there. The floor bed is rocky and uneven. So be equipped with a jacket comes with hood (or raincoat) and a good pair of track shoes.

Really cool volcanic flowlines and terrain.  Bring a rain jacket with a hood or umbrella and decent shoes.  Although I saw a woman in heels, but wouldn't suggest it. ouch.Take flash off your camera and use tripod for good pics.Does not take long at all to get at end and back.
Went a day after heavy downpour. Cave was "dripping wet" so we had to wear raincoat. Could not enjoy the view inside as we had to concentrate on our steps on the uneven rocky path.

If you are expecting something out of the ordinary, this case just isn't for you. No, there isn't any sign of life (bats) in it. It's just a natural cave formed, with tracks at it's natural state. Dark ambience, only with some help provided through man-made lights. But don't worry, the road before you is still visible.

There is not much to say about this: It's just plain boring; an unimpressive, badly lit cave. It isn't pretty either. Only recommended if you have a thing for geology: The history of a variety of rock formations is nicely explained.

Obviously, caves don't tend to be the most exciting things in the world, but Manjangul is a part of UNESCO's world heritage list (the Jeju Volcanic Island & Tubes) for a reason - it is pretty impressive.  Manjgangul is a 7km long volcanic tube, though you can only walk a small portion of it.  It is dimly lighted, with a few descriptive signs along the way (in Korean, English, Chine and Japanese, of course).  It's an interesting sight, a pleasant enough walk, and admission is just W2,500.

After hiking up some trails on Hallasan, we decided look at the Manjang Cave. Located on the north east of the island, one should know that it will take driving or riding a bus to get there.
