The Koreans told me this is the most beautiful trail up to Mount Hallasan, but this trail doesn't lead you to the crater. The landscape changes at as you hike up. Super stunning and beautiful. You must reach the "stop area" by 12pm if not they will not let you go till the end of trail and continue to descend with Eorimok trail. Start early, it's a tough hike but it's worth it! A must to visit!

I went to jeju island to see some view like this and i can say this Park was beautiful one . I suggest everybody to visit jeju island in fall season because u can see colours and feel great weather . Park is actually for hiking but if u don't wanna go till top u can enjoy forest before getting top , take some snacks and drink with ureself because there is not many mart nearby just one small and limit one down of park .

Hiked from the Yeongsil Hiking Trail Entrance (1280m) to Witseoreum Shelter (1700m). It was a total of 3.7km (one way) hike and took me 3.5 hours up.  Note that I do not exercise regularly and this was my first hiking experience.  I guess it is manageable for anyone as long you are determined to hike up regardless of your physical condition.  The trail was tricky involving a variety of tall rocks, wooden steps, pebbles and wooden planks, a tad steep at times.  My DSLR became cumbersome by midpoint that I've decided to use it at specific points for me to better soak in the sights and watch my steps at the same time.  The sights at various points are nothing but rewarding.A hiking stick and a good pair of shoes are definitely helpful.  Note that you have to bring your trash down after your hike!Bring more water and join the locals at various rest points with some snacks (eat what the Koreans do! Gimbap / tangerines / hard boiled eggs) and just immerse yourself in listening to their chatters while looking out far at the horizon!I would love to hike on the other trails of Hallasan again.

We took the Seongpanak trail up to the summit, and Gwanuemsa to descend. We agree with other reviewers that this is a better arrangement (gradual ascent, and beautiful descend - going up by Gwanuemsa could be a little too steep). It is a great idea to trek with a hiking pole - it is especially useful for the descending trek.Hallasan was a colourful parade of trekkers on October days - trekkers need to even queue up to take photo with the summit rock (with writing of Hallasan on it!) Less people descended through Gwanuemsa. It was a long, long way but there was no regret - this trail offered picturesque scenery. We even crossed two bridges.It is however, better to get the telephone number of the cab company on a weekday as it was not easy to secure a cab from the end point of Gwanuemsa (buses only ply the road during weekends). We were lucky to be able to carpool with 2 locals who were also heading back to Cityhall area, and they managed to call a cab only after they obtained the contact from another call taxi.

This is one of the highlights of Jeju Island. If you're ever there, you MUST go on this trail, unless outdoor activities aren't your type of activity. We took the Seongpanak trail up and down via Gwaneumsa. The pathway up was well constructed with wooden planks and shades for about 3 quarters of the journey. The rest of the path was quite stony. As the Gwaneumsa trail is relatively newer, it is not as well covered with wooden planks and a bit more slippery when you hike on the rocky trails. Both trails are as spectacular and offer different sceneries. On the way down, I encountered a deer sighting!Do bring along a wind wall as the winds can get very strong as you progress towards the peak. Also, it's best to start off as early as possible (we started at 6am) to enjoy the nature scenery as much as possible.

Please be aware to arrive early in the morning. Till 12.30 you should hike 7 km up the hill for approx. 700 m. It takes up to 3 hours if you're not trained, I managed to do it in 1h30m, but was exhausted. Great view from the top though.

Me and my bf did ＿깊肄 (Sungpanak Course) which is the longer but relatively easier course than the other one that goes to the top. Not counting the time we rested, we hiked 8.5 hrs in total round trip. It was VERY tiresome, but the view at the top was definately WORTH it!!!

While the hike was long it was definitely worth it. It wasn't too difficult, it was beautiful the whole way, and knowing I reached South Korea's highest peak felt like an achievement.It never felt too steep and even in the middle of summer the brutal heat didn't diminish the experience much. The only complaint I have is that parts of the path are covered with large, randomly distributed volcanic rocks that are a pain especially during the decent and my feat were pretty sore for quite a while afterwards.
I like the view of Halla Mountain and national park,easy going up to this mountain,every thing is perfect.

They have everything here from hiking, go karts, horseback riding, sky diving to airsoft. Buses traverse every half hour in one of the safest highways all over the world amidst a back drop of awesome scenic views.

Worlds'  natural heritage, really impressiveif you come to R.O.K and stop by Jeju island you must try!1950m high attitude, so no that easy course but comparing to Himalaya trekking, really easyso don't worry.If you are a beginner, it'll take around 10hours but if you used to go hiking, then 7~8 will be enough.If you like trekking, you must try.

My husband and I visited Jeju last November.Mt. Halla was out of the picture on this trip ( supposed to be ) bec. I am not an adventurous person and I thought I will not have energy to climb this mountain, but after learning that it is a world natural heritage park I finally gave it a go. I was afraid at the beginning of the trail but as we climb further, higher and steeper I was in Awe! I was literally inside the mountain. Plus it  was autumn at that time and the color of the surrounding was just beautiful, it seems so peaceful all you could hear was the chirping birds, gushing winds. It was tiring but i must i was worth it so sad that we didn't reach the summit bec we started a little late. But if i could go back I will strive to reach the peak, but I was still happy though because I've seen the best Autumn inside the mountain..It is really is the Climb!
We took the easiest hike trail and climbed up about 1.3km.It was tiring but worth the climb because of the splendid views from the top!! You can see the city and the Halla mountain.

Me and family went to Halla Park. I was 7month pregnant so I could not attempt the long Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trail to the summit. We picked the shortest hike Yeongsil Trail. It is about a 3.7k trail from Yeongsil Rest Area to the Witsae  Oreum Shelter one way which took me about 2 hours of gentle walk to get to the turnaround point. The trail was well signed and marked. It was a busy day on the tail with a whole school of high school kids out for an organized hike. But the view of the trail is still very nice. The steps were all well maintained so I had no issue of going up and down by myself. I will definitely come back to attempt the longer trail to the summit in the future.

It was a fairly easy hike up halla san but it would have been better if we have thicker clothes as it was too windy and cold when it's near the top. Such a beautiful view and we will definitely go back and challenge a different trails.

I came to this place at a rainy day, so I can't go until the top of the mountain, but I can saw, the scenery is very nice, with the sea under the mountain. I suggest you go there on the spring so ytou can walk to the top.

We definitely need to return as we didn't realize how much snow there would be. We were not prepared and so we just walked the 2.5 km to the trailhead along the road and returned. No hiking for us! There were tons of people who knew what they were doing though and obviously hiked with all the necessary snow gear. Live and Learn!

We didn't take the 3-hour journey but rather followed our tour guide on shorter route (approx 45 mins one way) to the top of another similar peak. It was bright and sunny with cold breeze which made a perfect day for hiking and photo taking. It's mainly "country view" from the top where green fields and moutains cover majority of your sight. You can also see the beach and sea far away with planes taking off and landing at Jeju airport. Overall, it's a nice outdoor walk and a place to chill out after a hectic journey.

It was the easier but longest route to the summit of Mt. Halla. Longest day of my life but it was so worth the aches and pain and sun-burns. Couldn't have done it without the constant encouragement of my partner. Reached the peak before lunch time and saw the beautiful lake and summit. Any later, the haze will start to come in and will ruin your pictures. Bring water and snacks and lunches while hiking. there is only one point where u can get drinking water. Pack light but sensible. Be prepared to spend a whole day for this climb and the next 3 days for aching thighs. So. worth. it. There are stalls selling food, drinks and ice-creams at the park. You can refresh yourself after the climb. Best to rent a car and start early.

If you like trails and hikes, this is it. Do it korean style and eat ramen at the top and even cucumber (take them along with you and even other snacks cause you'll get hungry). Plus, go in the morning, I want at 12:00 and thank goodness made friends in the way to get me back to my hostel. Around 17:00 there are no more buses and I would have been stuck there if it weren't for my new friends!

Before going there please be sure you are in a good physical condition because climbing up takes big efforts. In case you stay in Seogwipo city, it is better to start climbing to the top by Eorimok trail because it is shorter, and go down by Yeongsil trail. During th© trip the the Halla mountain you have a chance to meet a deer, enjoy fascinating view from the top and beautiful nature. To get to Eorimok trail entrance get bus No. 714 (if I am not wrong) from Jungnum (Seogwipo).

As a family of 3 it took us 11hrs round trip to do Seongpanak trail which reaches the summit. it can be done in 9 hours if u are a fast moving, experienced hiker with great gear. you have to start this hike between 5-7am or you will be forced to turn around before you reach the peak. there is also a place to buy kimbab at the base before you head up. its tastey too.  it is a gradual grade the whole way, so it is not too strenuous... All Though, you definately wanna wear the right shoes and bring your poles because 85 percent of the terrian is lava rock... big chunks of jagged uneven and slippery lava rock. be prepared to spend most of ur day looking down to watch your step. especially on the way down. i was so sick of the lava rock that i decided this was the least enjoyable hike i have ever done. i did however have a 2 yr old on my back which could have added the pressure to watch my steps so carefully. you do not get any views until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. the view is nice but if i had it to do over. i would have skipped this hike and spent the day seeing other sights. I highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong for a similar view at the top. if you have lots of time to explore jeju and you are a determined hiker, dont let me stop you. however, if you only have a few days to explore the island, you can get a lot more bang for your buck elsewhere.
It is very tiring to climb up the mountain. But the view here is nice. I personally like the shape of the mountain. Beside the sea, there will have the diver women show.

I hiked up Mt. Halla in the winter of 2007. It was my first hike up a mountain and relatively easy getting up to the first summit as a beginner. Unfortunately, I dont remember exactly what trail and how many hours it took but it was a day trip (up and returning down). The only downside with visiting during winter was that the snow and ice made it a bit challenging in some parts, since I didnt have proper footwear. My body ached a bit the next day, but spending the day at the spa made it all worth it!

6 hours to reach the peak, but it was worth it! Start your trip early as you need to be at the entry point by 12PM in order to make it to the top as everyone needs to start heading down at 2PM (depends on seasonality)...Certain parts of the hike is tough, but the feeling at the top of the mountain looking over the lake, is speechless!
The whole area is astoundingly beautiful and clean with spectacular views all around. Recommended to all as long as you don't mind a whole day's hiking. Spectacular.

Hallasan is the highest peak in South Korea (1950m) and on a clear day give you fantastic views over the island.  There are hundreds of parasitic cones which become clear from the top.  Breathtaking.  Good trail, and not too difficult.

We chose the "short" hike up the mountain (volcano) and it was all up. We are Coloradoans and hike quite a bit and this one was a bit of a challenge. The first part was through an oak forest and it was hot and humid. We sweat like crazy and things got better once we got out of the oaks and into the pines. It took us 2+ hrs to get to the rest station and a bowl of noodles and a chocolate bar. The hike was amazing, though with strange vegetation and a miniature deer, the only wildlife we saw along with many butterflies. We did not go to the top since it was in the clouds and starting to rain, but the views of the ocean and Jeju-si were as advertised. This is a must see place and there is an easier hike than ours, but takes much longer we were told.
This an excellent place to visit and photography lovers can enjoy the landscapes.

I did the hike in January, and it was amazing.  Parts were pretty difficult so you may need trekking poles or crampons.  The views from the top are stunning, but be sure to leave really early (before sunrise) as you'll be sharing the views with hundreds of your closest friends if you don't.
A nice panorama, 'enchanted forest' atmosphere, but very many people. Also be prepared for quite a bit of a walk.

We decide to go up the mountain on foot. It was a long way but worth it. The scene from the this mountain top is unforgetable and undeniably great. We could have stayed here all day seeing the nature changed if the weather weren t cold. Walking the way up was exhausting but the fresh air and the sights we saw at different heights really cooled us down.
The view is breathtaking. I wish we could spend more time there but it gets dark so you might want to head down before the sunset.
Make sure you have full clothings on as it is very cold out there. you will find lots of snow to play around. Adventurous people can trek as well.
Starting the beautiful day with sunrise on top of Hallasan Mountain. Refresh and restore yourself. Worth to hike~~^^
We went on a hike at Hallasan National Park and the scenery was beautiful. The park was beautiful and well kept.
Only did a short hike in the park but the views were amazing and I will definitely go back when I can.

It was a beautiful mountain as tree leaves were changing colors.  And there was many many people who came to sightseeing from all over the country & some foreign countries. The weather was perfect as well.

Halla mountain - Halla san (san means mountain) is spectacular in autumn with every hue of orange, red and gold. In spring it is the best time to climb the different trails but you must leave early enough to get to the top! Winter is a wonderland of white but hiking is trickier!

A trip to Jeju's and S. Korea's highest mountain is a refreshing experience. It is still nice and cool in the morning up here but no snow in late May. Oh well, may plan a winter trip back here for a more thrilling and chilling experience!

Is supposed to be the easiest trail up but does not reach the summit. Although a fairly challenging hike for those who do not hike regularly, it can still be done, even for kids as young as 4 years old. Wear good shoes for hiking.
For hikers this place was the good spot, but for some who doesn't like hiking you can still take pictures specially during winter and experience the snow.
We went during winter and there was nothing to see as the area is covered by fog and there was no snow as predicted by other. Nevertheless a cool place to be and surely more fun if there are snow.
On the way to the mountain, you can see some horses, the kind that can only be raised in the mountain. There is some snow but not enough yet.
Hallasan is the tallest mountain in South Korea. Your trip to Jeju island is not complete without climbing this mountain. There are several trails that have different difficulty.

Needless to say, Mt Halla was the highlight of my trip in Jeju. There was a good mix of clear sky and clouds during my hike up and down and the view is simply fantastic. I loved everything and every minute spent on this mountain.I went up via Eorimok trail and down via Yeongsil trail. Both trails DO NOT take you to the peak but to Witseorum Shelter. There, you can buy cup noodles, coffee and energy bars etc. but there are NO DUSTBINS - you must bring all your trash down with you. It was crowded when I reached the shelter around noon.I will not lie. You do need to be reasonably fit to hike up Mt Halla. You WILL have to do lots of climbing on rocks and proper walking paths probably make up 10% each on both trails. Many people recommend wearing proper hiking shoes but I went up and down wearing sports shoes and had no problem. It really depends on your personal preference and level of fitness.One last thing, toilets are only available at the start of each trail and at Witseorum Shelter. And make sure you have plenty of memory space on your camera for photos!

What a way to experience another side of Korea on an extinct volcano. The view at the summit was amazing. Suitable for ages, but a certain level of fitness is definitely required. The park is well maintained and well kept by the government. However, if you are looking for something more unpaved or natural this might not be the right trail as everything is already nicely laid out. (You will never get lost)

We hiked up on a cloudy day. I really recommend choosing the day for hiking according to the weather forecast. The hike itself and the views and people on the path made it an unforgettable experience, but after like 2,5 hours of hiking on a really quick pace we made it to the top and couldn't see anything. The crater was filled with mist and it was so windy that staying up there would have been quite uncomfortable. It doesn't necessarily take 4,5hours to get up and 4,5 hours to get down, if you don't stop every two hundred meters. But make sure to get to the last milestone (the place to take a break and buy ramen) in time to be able to start the climb to the top.I can only imagine what the trip and the scenery would be like on a clear sunny day.

The hike was awesome. Very scenic and nature at its best. There are a few different routes to the top. ( summit is out of bounds though) At the top, you can find a shelter with washroom and a small shop selling cup noodles. We drove there, so had to take the same route down. There are taxis waiting at the start points when we finished our walk(around noon time)
Beautiful and serene forest trails . Very good view but the walk up is not easy especially in a rainy day
Leave early as the final path to summit closes at 13 30 so I didn't see crater. Path is very clearly set out on wooden planks and steps. Very busy too.

We took the eomorik trail up - the first 1/2 or so was a tough climb, but through the woods so it was shaded. The second 1/2 was in open space - mostly on a Boardwalk type pathway. The path is clearly marked throughout the trail and there are signs to indicate how far you've come and how much you have left. The view was just average. It took us two hours to reach the top and we are not experienced hikers nor were we wearing hiking shoes, but we only took one short break for 10 minutes so we were always moving. We took the yongsil trail down and this was much more scenic with beautiful views of the mountains and rocks. Most of it was not shaded and most of the trail had steps so it was easy going down, but the look on people's faces as they were coming up showed how tiring it was to climb all those stairs! It took us about 1 hour and 15 minutes to get down. There were no taxis when we reached the bottom so we had to walk 30 minutes to the ticket booth to catch the bus. Since we just missed the bus and they don't run very frequently, we got a cab to take us back to our car at the eomorik entrance which cost about 10,000won.

I hiked the Seongpanak Trail which goes all the way to the top of Halla Mountain. In order to reach the top though, you must get to the last shelter before 12:30pm. The path is covered with uneven rocks and stairs so wear good shoes. I really enjoyed the hike but was underwhelmed by the view. Most of the path is shaded and when you do finally clear the trees it was cloudy and grey. The crater lake looked more like a big puddle of mud.If you like long, challenging hikes then the Seongpanak Trail is for you. If you're only in it for the view, perhaps try going in the early spring.
Whenever you visit it is AMAZING ! Boarded walks in many places and rough climbing for the adventurous. Clamp-ons needed in the snow but trainers fine in summer. Views from there are wonderful :)

Place is very clean and beautiful. No thrash bins around so do bring extra plastic bag to throw your unwanted things or drinks in it. It is a long walk up to the entrance. Choose the path wisely. Not advisable for those with joint pain and old injuries.
Gives an idea of how volcanic eruptions must have thrown Jeju out of the sea millions of years ago. Peculiar rock formations in a green landscape towering amid whispy clouds spell this Park.

For those who like to hike, this place is perfect! Make sure you have a proper map of the trails. Went during March so it was chilly and drizzled a bit but the climb was worth it when we saw the view from the top.

We walked the Eorimok Trail and it is a well maintained trail with signage all along the way that keeps you informed about how far you have gone, how far you have to go and categorizes the slope into three levels of difficulty (red=steep; yellow=moderate slope; green=gentle slope). It took us 2 hours to get to the tea house (Nambyrok Junction) from the parking lot at the base.  Even though we didn't go to the summit, there are beautiful views all along the trail. While this isn't a mountain climbers kind of trail, it is the tallest mountain in South Korea. My legs were sore for a week afterwards and I am in good shape. Be advised:  About 2/3s of the trail has big trees and good shade; there is no water along the trail; there are emergency phones every several hundred meters; and there is a single track 5-10m off the trail that looks like it would be used for emergency evacuation.

There are two lava tubes/caves in this park. The tubes themselves were quite interesting but having been to other massive caves before (e.g. Mammoth cave in WA, Australia), this is tiny. Nevertheless, it is a sight to see.The entrance ticket is quite pricey but the park is huge... And i guess the ticket price is more to sustain the park. I believe some may enjoy it more than us...
I like Halla Mountain.This mountain is very high but easy trekking.And FREE fee!I saw many people (Korean and Foreigner)
Very good hike, gorgeous scenery but this does not go up to the crater! Be warned only the Gwaneuma and Seongpanak go to the top!
Climbed it now proud. Most popular place to visit in jeju. If you are climbing the mountain bring foot snow sparks so that it won't be slippery.
We could not explore it much as it was raining. But we still anyhow manage to see horses in the ground.

When you get to the top theres the most beautiful view you will ever see. Im not an adult so if you are planning to go with your family just go, Jeju itself is really pretty but this mountain is exceptional, if you have the kind of teens/children that like challenges and adventures it is a must. I believe it is SO much better on spring or summer, cause i went on winter and the landscape is beautiful with all the snow but at the top its super cold and windy and the lake is freezed of course so you can not really appreciate it at all and it may make you think like you hiked all that enormous mountain(trust me the journey to the top is HUGE)  for just a freezed lake. Anyway its really amazing amazing, but i personally hated the way down, theres a trail for the way down opened all the year except from winter, so you have to go down the same way you went up and im just gonna say i fell 4 times. Go on spring or summer.

During winter time, it is surely different experience when you hike up. The view is totally different from summer. Can see icy plant. So beautiful that we wont forget. It might take about 45min to hike up if you are in good shape during winter time as it is not easy to hike up because of cold air.
Beautiful place. Had lovely weather on the day. Many tourists around, but didnt matter, as the place was gorgeous.

As we booked for a tour package in Jeju ofcourse Mt. Hallasan will be on the list. Experiences the thin layer of snow on the park which is perfect for strolling, walk a couple of meters and go back. And yeah visit the museum to see some photo gallery. Its worth to see.

Have you taken a trip recently? If you have not, go to Jeju Island in South Korea right now. There are two towns there with hotels of good reputation. Also, Jeju has a beautiful hiking trail called the  Olle Road . You can see a variety of sea creatures and birds there.   Olle Road takes you to the amazingly nice  Hanra Mountain . Hanra Mountain is a dormant volcano. Climbing to the top is a little challenging because the mountain s altitude is about 2000meters.  Also, Don't forget to go the big shopping centers for foreigners. The exchange rates are better in Korea than in your home country. So change your currency at the Jeju International Airport, or withdraw cash from the banks.    This place gives beautiful views. Visit Jeju Isalnd. You will have very fun time!

Be sure to visit even if you come to Jeju by only 3-4 days. Climbing is better to start early in the morning. At the beginning, some steep, climb to 1/3 after it enjoyed, leisurely walk along the gentle slope, wooded, narrow mountain road is very cool. Slightly sweating, big mouth breathing, anxious to put lung wash. I think is better shoes for climbing than sneakers because the rocks often.

This is my 4th time visiting Korea but this is my 1st time visiting Hallasan National Park. It is a great park, however do visit in the day time. Do note, Dec day time is short...do visit Hallasan National Park early.

The National Park is very peaceful by the time we reached in the afternoon. We tracked the shorter trail 9 stations point, as there is insufficient time for the longer trail. As we walked up the steped trail, enjoyed the woods, stones, freshness. Trail not recommended for those with weak legs - uneven steps. However,  you can still stay at the National Park to enjoy the serene park.
Good trekking course in great nature. But no confusion that there is only one way to see the lake on the top called Baekrokdam.

just walking distance to Jeju convention center is a vast scenic place complete with flowers, stone statues and the sea!There are also nice rock formations.There is an entrance fee of usd2 but it is so worth to see.
It is tiring but a nice walk up to the top. Nice view all round when at the top. Enjoy sometime up there before heading back where many good restaurants at the bottom.
it a must must to pay a visit while in winter season, it is awesome with beautiful snow and nice cool scene around. only setback will be got to try harder to climbed up.

This is the icon of Jeju island. We went there on a morning and started on the Seongpanak trail which happened to be the longest at 9.6 km. There are other shorter trails available from other start points. The mountain area is pretty cold with some winds. I guess it s the norm since it s November.The trail is a mixture of proper steps and stones. I wouldn t say it s easy but it s definitely achievable.A must go place in Jeju.
Climb up a little. love the view. easy trail to climb. the locals there climb it like a shopping trip or for leisure.
Amazing view in the autumn, especially u can see the peak at the end of Eorimok Trail and Yongsil Trail.
please take ur time to climb up the hill , you will never regret. the journey is not easy .you will need to walk about 1hour  to reach the top .
Must come to this place when you visit Jeju. We went here in fall and the view was astonishing. It took us about 5.5 hours for a round trip.
You should not miss Hallasan when you've traveeled to Jeju.  The scelery is very beautiful.  You can enjoy fresh air there.
Yeongsil trail said to have the best autumn views. Be prepared to walk 2.5km(along the road) from car ticket office ( No 740 Bus-stop ) or catch a taxi up to trail entrance.
Wonderful views and landscapes.  Excellent preservation of the trails and nature.  Well worth a half day.  Make sure you pack some food, water and enjoy this marvellous part of Jeju.

The highest mountain in South Korea.  Several paths and some are easily accessible by public bus.  I chose the one to the summit up and down.  Clear sign and a small shop before going up the summit.  Good view.  Can get a certificate to the summit in the park office.

We visited Jeju only for Hallasan mountain! There are two ways on top, one easier and one harder! We took the easier to get on top and the harder to get back down! Once on top you will have a beautiful view over the national park and the island! Take some good shoes with you if you want to take the harder trail! The park is easy to reach by bus

We did the Seongpanak walk to the summit. I am of average fitness and found the first half relatively easy going, although the rocky path and stairs after the last rest station were a little harder. It took just under 2 hours up and about the same going down again, with a couple of very brief rest stops.The views from the top are pretty good if there are no clouds. There's not much to see on the way up though, as you're in the tree line and there is little variation.The track is well marked and easy to follow. Most of the track is volcanic rock, although there are sections of board walk as well and the last 1km is wooden stairs. I didn't think that the distance markers were that accurate.The paths get very crowded - most of the walkers are dressed and equipped like they are attempting to summit Everest, but realistically all you need is good shoes and plenty of water. Most people were using walking poles as well, which became extremely frustrating as they tended to block the paths. The only people I saw fall were using these poles, they really are not required.It would be difficult to do this track in the rain, as it would get quite slippery in places. My advice would be to go early to avoid the majority of the crowds - the car park fills with tour buses by mid-morning. We started at 0700 and it was still relatively busy then. You need to be at the last rest station by 1230 to be able to continue to the summit and leave the summit by 1430.Overall - I wouldn't do it again, but if you had a free day on Jeju, it's a good way to burn off a few calories.

We hiked to the top of the volcano. The walk was pretty easy but long. Lots of information signs make it really easy to manage. The first part is in the wood, which means no view but shadows. The last quarter of the ascension is out of the woods but was really crowded what made the walk boring.The volcano is nice, but i think it may be overrated dut to the fact that it is the highest mountain of Korea.Anyway, it is a must do if you go to Jeju

Do this! I hiked to the peak with my sister and i'd say both of us are average when it comes to our fitness level. We took the  Seongpanak route, up and down and it took us 6.5 hours. When we got to the peak it was really chilly, so be wise and pack a light windbreaker/jersey. It's a beautiful hike through the mossy trees. Be prepared for too many stairs to count and hundreds of Asians taking selfies. You can buy yourself Kimbap at the start of the hike to fuel yourself or to eat as a much needed snack at the peak. There is one or two bathroom points on the way and a place to refill your water bottle. Entrance is free
It was a great day with clear skies for us to hike the national park! We climbed up the trails and enjoyed the bright sunny day!

If you come to Jeju island, Hala mountain tracking is No. 1 recommendation for you if you are health and have strong two legs. My recomendation is Yong-Sil course and it will take about 5 hours round tracking. It is totally different scene when you up to the mountain and never forget this memory.

Climbing Mt Hallasan was absolutely amazing, and I would recommend anyone going to Jeju to attempt a climb. If you re a bit unsure, make sure to research the trails before-hand and start walking in the morning   many trails close at 2-3pm.Bring lots of water and snacks (although in typical Korean fashion, there is a 'restaurant' at the 'top', where all the lower trails intersect. Do your research, take a car or taxi to the start of the trail (buses will drop you off much further down the mountain, and you'll have to spend time and energy walking up along a road before you can even start the trail). The views must usually be stunning, but on the day we went, it was covered in cloud/fog. Even so, I would 100% recommend it and I would definitely go again if I went back to Jeju.

We were hoping to climb up to the summit. However we ere told to be there before 9 am. We hiked the Yeangsil Trail instead. It was a great experience. The trail was as per the Trod advisor reviews. Make sure you have the right shoes with the right traction. It was not that hard except for some parts of the trail. We enjoyed it very much. We bought some snacks on the trail but had to carry the trash back to our hotel!! The trail is well kept and marked. Will go back again but before 9 am so we can go to the summit. The views were fantastic . We saw a couple of deer. It was worth the visit. Make sure you arrive before 9 am if you want to go to the summit.

The hike up Hallasan is fairly easy though a good portion of the hike is on rocky/basalt boulders.  There are long sections of boardwalks especially near the summit where there are a fair number of stairs.  Most of the trail is well shaded except for the last kilometer or so.  There are locations to purchase food and drinks along the way.  I saw families with young kids as young as six hiking thee trail.  It can get dairly crowded at times, but if you are fast people will kindly let you buy.  If you are an experiencex trail runner its a fun and slightlytechnical run.  Time up is about two and a half to three and a half hours, while time down is one and a quarter to two and a half hours depending on ability.  At the summit you will see a large crater.  Unfortunately you are not allowed to circumnavigate the crater.  Fun hike overall though a bit crowded.
had a great trip. used Yeha bus tours and the guide Joy was not only bright bubbly, she spoke English so one could understand exactly what was there

I didn't hike the mountain because it was so tiring. But, I really enjoyed watching the natural view. Moreover, there was an outdoor displayed pictures of the species found in Jeju. I enjoyed taking many pictures there.

We arrived and were surrounded by Koreans dressed in proper hiking gear and walking sticks. The day wasn't too warm and we made it up to the summit in good time. It was lovely to relax at a beach afterwards though.
Great hike! A bit demanding!Must get to a check point before 1pm to be allowed to go to the top.The descent route is often closed and the observatory is not fair if the lake is not full of water

I went with my boyfriend and his dad. We had our cab driver take us there at 6am from our hostel. It took us about 12hrs round trip. I'm not a experienced hiker, so it took a loooonnnngggg time because of me. View is EXCELLENT from the peak. You can see the entire Jeju-do. Hallasan is a stony mountain, so if you can, bring a pair of hiking sticks to help you, and wear hiking shoes. The rocks are pointy, and not all of them are easy to step on.

There are many pockets of great places to go to on this mountain. My family and I went on the Yeongsil trail and found it offered great views without being too difficult.We also went for a short visit to the Recreation Forest on Hallasan, which was a fairly interesting drive.

We did the seongpanak trail. Check the weather the day before embarking, and make sure you have proper hiking shoes as the climb is rocky and some parts are pretty steep. Stretch your muscles before the climb or you'll end up sore the next day (or you can tote along some muscle rub)! Bug spray is also recommended, for those prone to mosquito bites. Try to get an early start if you can; as you have to pass the second rest stop before 1.00pm if you want to make it to the summit, otherwise the staff will not allow you to proceed. On average you would take 7-8 hours to hike to the summit and back, depending on the number of rest stops you make. There are 2 rest shelters along the way (one selling food like cup noodles and choco pie, pocari sweat and bottled water). There are toilets at both rest stops, but no water; no washing hands or flushing systems. Generally, the climb path is divided into thirds - beginning (relatively easy, mostly uneven but flat ground) - first rest stop - second leg (rocky ground, with some portions made up of many steps) - second rest stop - final leg (fair warning it gets really tough for beginners, as the terrain gets pretty rocky and steep) - summit!

It takes about 6 hrs for hiking up and go back. The way back is rock path half of the way, so quite tough for me. But it's worth to hiking up. The scenery on the top is breathtaking and unique. I visited there on late May, which there were still some pink azalea blooming and it was very beautiful.Please beware of the weather and strong wind on the top.I'd rate it for No.1 attraction site to visit in Jeju-do.

We started with Yongsil Hiking trail passing through: Byeongpung Rock, Witse Oreum till the South Wall Folk and then to go down we followed the Donnaeko Hiking Trail. The way up is ok, the way down is quite difficult, ai recommend proper shoes.

I hiked up the Seongpanak trail, which was easily accessible from Jeju-si. It took only ~45 minutes to get to Seongpanak station on the 780 bus. It was crowded, but it was still a very nice hike (and luckily the weather was pretty good!). You have to reach the Jindallaebat Station by 1 pm in order to be allowed to climb to the summit. Then, you have to start your descent by 2:30 pm. Please note, the time may change depending on the season, but I m not sure (I climbed late April). It s a big hike, and I definitely recommend wearing good hiking boots and wearing a proper backpack. Bring lots of water. If you forget to pack food, there is some available at the Jindallaebat Station. The summit is breathtaking! I hiked back down the Seongpanak trail since the bus to get back to Jeju-si seemed more frequent than the other one. During the descent, I took a side-trip to the Sara Oreum and scenic view. It was just a good 30 minute detour, and well worth it! Once at the bottom, it was easy to catch the 780 bus back to Jeju-si.

The hiking trail is well designed and fellow hikers are courteous. There are multiple trails with varying levels of difficulty. Some parts are fairly steep. Stairs are installed in most parts of the trail that we climbed on, though I am not sure if this is the case with all trails. The midway station includes food and water facilities. There are no garbage cans anywhere on the trail, nor indeed even at the entrance to the trail. Make sure you do not bring too many things that require disposal when you climb.

I start my trekking 8.00AM at Gwanneumsa entrance and reach the summit around 12.30 and down to Seongpanak at 3.00PMPros : Magnificent various views(uphill), very easy downhillCons : No Hallasan view during uphillat this period, The weather is not so cold and the snow is still thick but robes and signs are intact. Good equipment is needed

It is a great place for families, whether you are just playing in the snow or hiking there. We intended to hike a bit, but we didn't have clampons on, we only did that for about 10 mins. On descend, we found out that they can be bought at the convenience store at the entrance. Otherwise, it would  have been a great place to hike

I hiked on Mt Halla on 24 Dec 2014, very beautiful. But I didnt have enough equipment, it was difficult for me to climb to the top of mountain.  I climbed at 7 km distance for about 4 hours and down for 3 hours.

I come there first time.And I am very exciting when I see a bigest mountain and very cool on December 2014. There provide a lots of coffee shop such as Starbuck , Dunkin Donut and Coffee Bean. If you go down to the small beach then You meet Ajuma who sell seafood. Dont forget to try it!!!
It is the highest mountain in South Korea with unbelievable scenery for all seasons. Each season - there are four distinguished seasons in Korea- you can experience differently amazing challenge.

Beautiful landscape, the trek is relatively easy to manage. Weather on the way up is was just perfect too, except it gets very chilly at the peak, so make sure you pack enough warm clothing up. The trail gets very slippery during wet days, make sure you have a pair of shoes with good grip. The route I did that morning - Seongpanak > Peak - Baengnokdam > Gwaneumsa.

I love hallasan so much, this is definetly the camp, although it was winter when we got there, but really its very beautifull .... I cant imagine , hallasan when spring ... For get in here, there is bus station 15 minutes walk from the foothills, but dont know exactly the number of the bus, because we hire rental car for only 20.000 won !!! Its amazing right ?? But sadly hallasan didnt have any restaurant or proper rest area for us to enjoy the view, or it because the winter season, i dont know ...
Visited the park when it was raining. Still very enjoyable and there is some sort a mini bird park in there. Very interesting and relaxing walk through the park.

Last weekend, I climbed up to the top of Hallsan Mountain and saw the crater on the top called Baerokdam. Hallasan is the highest mountain in Korea, 1,950m above sea level. It took 5 hours to go up to the to top, which means it took another 5 hours to climb down. Climbing was kind of fight with myself and I won! I'm really proud of it and the most unforgettable thing is Baerokdam itself. I can't express with a word. As it snowed for the first time this year, it was more beautiful.
Amazing views well worth the hike. Go up Yeongsil Trail and down Eorimok Trail. Best in autumn when it's cool and the leaves change colour.
It's a long hike but for me it's worth it. Its has different nature scenery from my country. Make it to the peak.

My family took the Eorimok Trail and the path is well maintained.  Remember to bring food and water along.  Recommend to start early morning as it gets hot at noon and early afternoon. It is worth the effort and a must see if you go to Jeju.

It took everything in me to make this climb.  But at the end of the day, my legs wobbling, I could say, "I hiked Korea's tallest mountain"Make sure to bring your food as the only thing available for sail will be ramen noodle, a favorite among Koreans.One tip, push through till you get to the area set up for sitting and eating.  Doing this instead of many stops along the way will definitely save you some time.

Great hiking adventure! A must do in Jeju! We took Yeongsil Trail and it was breathtaking. If you are have a chance take a different trail going down like. Also if you are heading to the summit make sure to have an early morning start.
Go before 2 if you plan to hike. Trail closes and is guarded. Enjoyed the scenes. Not a lot of parking.
Quite an experience! This is one of the harder courses, takes less time and its said to offer one of the best views of Hallasan. But note that this route doesn't go to the summit.

Hallsan is the highest mountain in Korea. You will have to hike up 1200m.  It is tiresome but it is not very tough, you can take your time. The time estimations indicated in the panels along the way are overestimated (specially if you have some hiking experience).Hiking up this mountain is like being on a highway with a lot of very noisy companions. It is packed, you will most likely be queuing up the mountain if you go in summer.If you are looking for a communion with nature, this is not the place. The hike up is almost entirely man-made, you will be walking up on wooden stairs and on wooden paths. Once you reach the top, it is so packed that you can barely enjoy. Views are excellent though.As you go up, there is a small path to the left to go to another lake. I will recommend this on your way down. Much much quieter as most tourists just want to go to the top.

It was just amazing. Though the path way is well maintained but  it might be tough for some foreigners because of its slope but for Koreans it seems to be an easy task. But once you go uphill it looks so beautiful, not to be described in words rather to be felt by heart. As usual in Korea, I saw that every traveler keep the way neat and clean from waste food materials and carrying poly bags.

Our driver drove us to the rest stop and from there we hiked about 30 minutes to the top. It had just rained so don't try it without solid walking shoes as it's easy to get a nasty fall. It was cloudy so we couldn't get a view of Jeju city but the feeling of being on top of the world was worth it!
If you are an outdoor lover, you'll enjoy your time there, take a little hike or have a little seafood snacks

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.

When I went up in July 2014, it was cloudy and misty, so no views to be seen which was a pity a heck of a climb up, but even though knocking 66 years old I made it (my pulse settled down after less than 15 mins), so it wasn't that bad for the oldies, once again shame about the clouds/mist.Worth a visit, on a good day.I marked it down 'cause of the clouds.

It was a nice hike, got really sore legs the day afterwards. You could even buy ramyeon noodles, water and snacks halfway. It is a trail all the way, more like a walk way made out of rocks than a hike. But still really nice!
The views were breathtaking, but do prepare a bag for wastes and do not fall back in schedule. 10 hr hike, worth the shot.
Halla San is a must do on Jeju Island - a range of trails to choose from, great views, great hiking and with the exception of Summer when it's super hot - a great place to hike anytime of the year.

Also known as the "Island of the Gods" and being marketed as the "Hawaii of Korea". They said going to this volcanic island (also favorite destination for honeymooners) is like going back in time. From the top, it offers scintillating views from coast to coast including naturally sculpted cliffs. It's an uphill battle to Mt. Halla made more so with hordes of tourists who come your way. Once up there, it's euphoria. Visited last Sep-12 during "Experience Hyundai" Trip.
Very lovely place to go. The veiw was fantastic. You have to go up to the mountain.
high but beautiful.you have bring some food and water.

It was different then I expected it to be. It was more organised and less of a real nature trail.But when you arrive at the top, walking the Seongpanak trail for 9.6 kilometres, then you're proud! The trail is walked by many, many people (we went on a Saturday). And most of it is steps or wooden walkways. So it is accessible for a lot of people, even if you're not a real mountaineer! Mind that there are only two trails leading to the top!

We choose Yeongsil Trail as it's the easiest but too bad in less than 1km we had to turn back. We were there in early April 2014 and the wind was blowing like crazy and it was very cold. Reason for turning back? We spotted ice and in no way wearing the suitable clothes for the climb. We even saw the waterfall freezes. Astounding and beautiful. The trees were all bare and yellowish. Don't expect greenery at this time of year.
It's a serious walk, lot's of steps. Not sure I'd do it again. Limited refreshments at top - just Pot noodles.

We hiked up the Yeongsil trail. The trail is very well maintained. The views are amazing. However, if you expect to see the crater lake, you should consider one of the other trails. Start early because hiking is very popular in Korea. On our way down, we encountered a steady stream of hikers.

If you are fanatic about nature then you would probably really like this park. However if you enjoy nature but are more swept away by breath-taking scenery then in my opinion you will be really disappointed. We did the Seogwipo trail and for the effort involved the reward was just not enough. The trail took around two hours each way, and part of that was over some extremely difficult terrain. It's not that step, but walking over really large stones and boulders for over an hour can get really tiring, especially when there is no view to distract you, you are just surrounded by trees, There is nothing to see at all for the most part! At the end of the trail, the mountain lake and view of the valley is nice, but nothing that special or amazing. We were there in low season and even then it was extremely crowded, so you never have the feeling that you are really hiking a mountain. I wouldn't do it again.

We hiked the trail at Seogwipo Recreation Area.   The cost is 1.00 US per person and 2.00 per car.The trails are very well marked in english with plenty of stopping stops along the way.   There are also a number of bathroom faculties along the way.   be sure to get the trail map when paying admission.
Great view, average difficulty hike.Be prepared and do your research before hiking will make everything go a lot more smoothly.
Super great!! It was a really fantastic climbing for me! It takes so much time and makes you tired but it is great enough!

We made a side trip to this attraction and thanks to our guide, we were able to experience a very refreshing afternoon hike and enjoy the beautiful colors of autumn.  There is a walking trail and it's  an easy hike even to non-hikers. It was late October when we visit and i just love the foliage in this mountain.

Breathtaking view of the surrounding landscape. A good way to discover by walking at leisure. There is so much to enjoy what the nature can offer right in front of you. The place is well kept and it deserve the UNESCO world heritage site. A must in your itinerary to Jeju. Only regret - could not climb as high to see the the peak of Halla due to time constraint.

I visited this place because of friends' recommendation. In the end, I was glad that I made it. It took me 3.5 hours for the whole trip. During this trip, I met a few friendly Korean people, which gave me a great company. there are lots of birds and greens along the away.In the summer, pls put sunscreen on your skin before/during the trip. Otherwise, you will get sunburn easily.

Beautiful, serene and breathtaking views. A mid-level challenge to hike up and carrying extra water was mandatory in the heat. It is the highest peak in South Korea and the geographical centre of Jeju. A most worthwhile wander.

Only managed to do the shortest of 6 trails. Despite the rain, the view from the top of the Eoseungsaengak Trail (1.3km of upward climb) to the summit of Eoseungsaengak (an oreum) was wonderful once the rain clouds cleared. Worth the effort!
Took me 11 hrs to complete as I am a amateur. It is important to start in the early morning. Advice to take the seongpanak as it is easier for beginner.
Make sure you take time to see the mountain when you go to Jeju! You can't go wrong heading there to get great views of the Island.

Great natural parc. We've done the trek suggested by the lonely planet guidebook. Going up from eorimok and down yeongsil (which is really breathtaking). It was a little hard, but we succeed though we aren't particulary trained, thank to the stairs and timberworks all along the path.
Should be rather pretty when all leaves turned brown and golden. However, colors had just started to change slowly at the end of Oct.

Be prepared to climb flights and flights of narrow stairs to get up to the top of this mountain (felt like a 40min walk up and a 30min walk down). It was really windy when we reached the top and very crowded with tourists.

This is the first thing you should do if you visit Jeju. The tallest mountain in South Korea and you shouldn't miss it. Climb to the top if you can for awesome views of Jeju and its surrounding oreums. Locals recommend winter and spring but autumn is beautiful too especially along the Gwaneumsa trail.

I like that you can kind of 'customize' a trail to suit your time, difficulty and type of view you want. Views of the peak are spectacular with it's craggy face and the raised wooden trails make walking a breeze. There are fresh natural-water springs along the way, so drinking water is in good supply.
Hiked to the very top and back for 12 crazy hours. Incredible experience!!
Beautiful views from Hallasan. The climb up was temporarily marred by rain, but we continued up with an umbrella. Quite a work-out, but worth the effort at the top. Beautiful!
Whenever i visited Jeju island alone, i climbed the mountain. I already visited Jeju  more than 10 times, climb the Halla mountain is still a speical event 'cause i could meet nature itself

In April, watch the weather. Aim to get to the trail head around 7 to 8am. Make sure you wear good hiking shoes it is rocky in most parts even though there are stretches of boarding. It is windy up top so you might not stay atvthe summit for more than 30 mins but the views are breathtaking. This is not a boring hike as some may say. It is a classic in these parts

We selected yeongsil trail since we rarely hike in own country and it is recommended for beginner. We started our hike at 9:30am and it took us 3 hours to reach the shelter while 2 hours to come down. We used back same route to come down since we drove there. The cup noodle shop was closed when we reached the shelter, grateful we brought some biscuit and roti else we will starving after long hike hours. We didn t expect still having ice on mountain since it is turning spring. This get bit challenging especially to me as my shoes a bit tough to walk on the ice. But luckily a korean lady offered her stick to me and hold my hand to cross the ice path. It really make a different with the stick support. It is really recommended to get prepare self well with good hiking shoes, enough water and food.

Just did the hike on 30 March.Trail: seongpanak up and gwaneumsa down. Goes to summit. (highly recommend to do this trail Cos going up by gweumusa is really steep though the view is nicer for gweumusa) Time taken: 4.5hrs up and 4hrs down (please go early and check the time that you need the reach the shelter and summit by.  Think should be by 1230 reach shelter and by 2 to leave summit) Weather: good.  Cold in the morning but as you hike,  you will perspire and definitely need minimum sweaters. I was only wearing teeshirt and windbreaker. In the end only tee-shirt cos it's getting warmer and you climb and when the sun is out. Need crampons?  Yes!!! It helped alot especially at the icy areas both going up and down. Not too sure where you can buy it but I managed to rent it from my hostel. Though I did see people without it,  and they did just fine.  I was wearing track shoes kind. So crampons helped alot!  How to get there: I went there from Jeju city and took bus 281 from bus terminal to seongpanak bus stop. Coming back from gwaneumsa trail: took bus 475 back to jeju  national university and change bus 360 to Jeju city.  Please check with bus driver or use kakao map/bus to help as Google Map doesn't seem to help much with he routes. Bus 475 have some timings going back. You can always find out from the visitors center at the gweumusa base. It is situated at the left side as you make your way down passing through the car park.  Shelters and food: not sure if I did miss it..  But I didn't see any food vendors, drinks stall as I hiked up and down. So I was really thirsty as the end of the trail. There's a small restaurant and a convenience store at gwaneumsa trail end. So please bring ALOT of water like at least 1.5L. Bring along food to eat up there and also plastic bag to put your trash and there are no rubbish bins around.

We went to Eorimok trial thinking that we can go up with normal tracking boots. To our surprise, there was snow even though it was in the middle of spring. Due to the snow, we cannot go up the mountain without crampons. We still enjoyed ourselves at the carpark area as it was beautiful.

Love the amenities at the place. Clean and functional. The view is breathtaking and there is ample area for picture taking etc. before the serious business of hiking.Make sure wear and bring proper gear and supplies as there are limited item at the sole shop at the base.

I was hesitating to climb the mountain in the winter, but it is definitely a must do! It was so amazing with the snow. The path itself was 'easy' to walk and to follow. Tip: buy crampons at the start of the trail (12,000 krw (I think) for the cheap ones).

I woke up really early to get ready for this hike. I took the first bus 281 from the old bus terminal in Seogwipo leaving at 6am. We arrived at Seongpanak trail entrance about half an hour later. I did this trail mid January and you need crampon for this. Personally, I don t like slippery surface so crampons really give me the confidence. But I saw people on the hike didn t have crampons. Some other people hiked in their running shoes. Snow was thick but you basically walked on top so I guess You don t necessarily need hiking boots. Unless you go off trail, the snow will be knee deep. It was such a nice feeling to see everybody get up and early to start the hike when it s still dark out. The hike up was not very challenging and it took me about 4.5 hours. I m an extremely slow walker. Keep in mind that there is cut off time. If you start too late and couldn t get up to the last shelter on Seongpanak trail before 12pm, you are not allowed to go to the summit. The view at the top was so beautiful. It was very windy though. I took Gwaneumsa trail down since I wanted to change views. That was challenging. My knees hurt so bad even though I already wore knee braces. It s shorter than Seongpanak trail but it took me almost the same amount of time. There was one part quite steep and I didn t notice the rope which you can hold on to, I slid down and broke my trekking pole. Apart from being slippery, the trail is quite rocky and by the end of the day, after a beautiful sunny day, the snow started melting and made the trail very slushy. There was time I almost gave up, my whole body hurt and I started to get blister on my toes. When I got to the entrance of the trail, I took bus 475 for 10 mins to a university entrance station then changed to bus 281 to go back to Seogwipo. I guess you can take 281 directly from Gwaneumsa to Seogwipo but I didn t know where it was so I followed the crowd. I totally recommend this hike.

The road brings you to an altitude of 1100 m close to e Mt. Hallasan which with 1900 m is the highest mountain in South Korea. They have built a walk with wooden planks that brings you to nice trees without getting wet feet. The walk takes about one hour when taking Pictures, if you rush it is only 20 minutes.
I am thinking of driving up the mountain, where would be a good pit-stop to enjoy some view with snow?

For 1st time hikers climbing Mount Hallasan, take note of the different hike trails AND the closing time for each trail. This is especially if you drove on your own and parked at 1 of the 5 (one of the locals told me there are 5 different car parks at different foot of the mountain)If you are climbing Mt Hallasan to reach Baengnokdam (the crater top), do not take the Eorimok trail as it does not lead there. I made the 1st mistake taking this trail and the trail ended 3 quarters way up the mountain and you only get to see the side of the mountain top. I made the 2nd mistake not watching my time and could not descend Hallasan from the trail (Eorimok) where I came as apparently it closes at 2pm, and there was a park warden stopping me from taking the trail back and kept ushering me to take the other way (towards Donnaeko trail) to descend. The descend took 4 hours and the trail was treacherously full of rocks. You could tell that it was a trail less taken as there were over-grown bushes covering parts of the trail. Your only guidance of where to go was a      thin cord string tied from tree to tree and red strips of cloth tied on the string. If you weren't too careful and lost sight of the guiding string, you may actually go off tangent of the trail. There are no lights, very few signage and are all in Korean, so if you are like me with no understanding of Korean, good luck. And that wasn't the end. Donnaeko trail actually ends up at Donnaeko cemetery. So when I got to the foot of Hallasan, it was pitch dark (6pm+ and no street lamps), by myself, and I had to walk for 1 hour through the cemetery to get to Donnaeko car park (which was 30 mins driving distance away from Eorimok car park where my car was T-T).

The mountain is extremely busy with tons of people and older koreans are not always very friendly toward foreigners, but the rude people are exceptions. In general the hike is wonderful, just very long. There is beautiful scenery and forests to enjoy. Take a jacket for the top as its cold and start early.

We travelled from Seogwipo by bus to Jungmun Elementary school.  Thereafter, we were supposed to hop on another bus to the stop nearest to the entrance of Yeongsil Trail.  However, we did not read the bus schedule careful enough to notice the change in the schedule during winter.  The bus starts later and ends earlier during winter.  We ended sharing a cab with the other 2 tourists who happened to be there earlier than us and were heading to the same destination.  The guy who mended the convenient store near the bus stop was so nice that he helped us to call the taxi.   It was a blessing in disguise since the taxi actually sent us right to the door step of the Yeongsil Trail entrance in which otherwise, we would have to walk up for about 2 km to the starting point of the trail.  Should you travel with baggage, the park office (which I guess so) can keep them for you.  I m not sure of the storage capacity or if lockers are available, or this is just an additional service provided for those who happen to travel there with their baggage.It took us slightly more than 3 hours to hike up to Witsoreum Shelter since we re quite slow and took plenty of photos.  The Koreans took 2 hours only.  The wind was very strong, so do take care of your scarf or anything which is light.  Witsoreum Shelter is where you can opt to go back down with the same trail or by another trail, Eurimok Trail.  However, the other trail was closed on that day.There s a canteen and restrooms at Witsoreum Shelter.  The canteen sells instant noodle and simple snacks.  After eating and disposing the residue of the noodle, you have to bring the trash back for disposal.  Plastic bag for keeping your trash is provided but I find it rather thin.  However, we brought some plastic bag along with us for this purpose as well since we had some snacks while hiking up.The fog was building up when we left at about 1:10 am.  It took us about an hour and 40 minutes to descend.  Overall, this was a good experience.  We were just on time to catch the last bus back to Jungmun Elementrary school (if I recall this destination correctly).

Mt Halla is known as Korea's jewel. It is its highest peak. And well worth the trip to Jeju. We left Seagwipo very early (around 7 am) and took bus 182 (181 also goes there) to Seongpanak because we wanted to climb up to the peak. We got to the mountain around 7:45 and started the hike. The weather was super nice when we left, and we planned it that way, because we wanted to at least get some nice views of the city, and while at the summit. This is a long day of hiking, so be prepared. Bring snacks (and a trash bag, because you have to carry everything back down), and water. There are 2 checkpoints along the way that have bathrooms. The last checkpoint sells ramen for about 1500w with hot water. This is the checkpoint you have to get to before 12:30. We made it there around 11, and up to the summit before noon On the Seongpanak trail, there is also a lake with an observatory that's worth the detour.The last part of the hike up to the summit is pretty steep and rocky, so watch your footing, especially because you might be tired from walking up. Wear adequate footwear, make sure they are sturdy and comfy!Unfortunately, we didn't get that lucky with the weather as it because overcast as we were getting up there. I guess it really depends on your luck (the next day, it was super clear! Damn you Mt Halla!!) hahaha.We took the same trail down (from the summit, there is another trail, but no buses stop there. And this is where your comfy shoes are a must. The hike up was not bad, but the hike down, was torture! Our feet kept hitting the front of our hiking shoes, so we were bruised and hurt by the time the hike was done. We were also sore for the next 2 days (and we're pretty sporty, but we rarely walk for 8 hours) Overall, it's a great hike. The trail up is covered by trees, so it is cooler than it seems, but there are still some great views, especially with the fall foliage. We'd be surprised at the range of people walking the trail, old and young love to hike up this trail, and we understand why!

If you live on Jeju you have to do it at least once. I'm from the West where the mountains are huge so, when I saw Hallasan it looked like a piece of cake. How wrong I was. Mountain trails in the West take you up by switchbacks but the tail up Hallasan goes straight up  and straight down. There are no switchbacks. Only about a million steps to climb. I'm not saying that there is anything wrong with that......just be prepared. Start early and take water.When I went up I thought I was going to die. It didn't help that there was this grandpa in flip-flops who passed me on the way up and then he passed me again as I was still on my way up and he was coming down and then he passed me again going up as I was still on my way up. How embarrassing was that?????? Very embarrassing!As far as the climb went, it was great. I felt like two cent going up but once on top I felt like a million bucks. Clean air and blue sky. Views of the whole island.One good thing about going down is that it's all down hill. I do a lot of complaining about it but I've been up there five times now so  there must be something I love about it.If you do go up and you see that grandpa tell him hi from me. He passed me so many times I feel like I know him. ;)

So we did minimum research on this thinking that the trip up would be somewhat difficult but we were way off that. We made it to the top but we had to push through it. Highly recommend bringing lots of water and snacks.

People who visiting Jeju island is to see its nature (except those to Casino), Hallasan is a must go to me.  Together with the family, we opted for the route of Yeongsil (shorter though not to the top and unable to see the crater), where we could easily accessed by self driving from Seogwipo city.  Along the hiking, we experienced the sub tropical environment in the bottom, then a much cooler environment after 1.5km of steep uphill.  The view is great though not fantastic, we spotted few wild deers having grass in the mountain.  The first 2-3 km was quite steep but mostly on boardwalk and constructed staircases, the last 1-2 km was rather flat.We ended in the point with toilet and food supply and then back down on the same route, due to the last section was closed.  An interesting hiking day to experience different climate, weather condition, meet locals, spot the wild animal, and do physical exercise.

Halla mountain can be hiked in 3-5 hours easily. I have hiked the Seongpanak Trail (on the east side)  and the Gwaneumsa Trail (on the north side). These are the two trails that go all the way up to the summit. If you are fit, these runnable, but Geaneumsa trail especially gets very steep at the end. Get to your trail of choice early to miss the crowds, and also note that the half way points of each trail close around 12 (depending on the time of year it is sometimes 12:30). Een when it is foggy it is beautiful, but, of course, it is best when you can see clearly down to the crater lake and across off of Jeju to the ocean. Pack a lunch and enjoy it on top of the mountain! (Or instant ramen is the traditional food to pack).My favorite time to go is in winter when the top of the mountain is covered in a few feet of snow! Make sure to bring crampons for your shoes (simple ones are OK, you aren't hiking K2!)

Disclaimer: Not a seasoned/experienced hiker. Was done on a cloudy day with a scattered drizzles.I had high expectations for the highest point in South Korea and a highly rated tourist attraction on TripAdvisor but was greatly disappointed by the experience.The reason I am giving a score of 1/5 is because there is a long hike (approximately 3-4 hours one way) with very little to see along the way, with ultimately what I would consider an "okay" view of a "crater lake" up the top. In addition, whilst walking the unpaved bits of the trail (rocks, which account for about half of the trails we walked) you will need to focus hard on walking to ensure you don't slip as it can be quite slippery. This means you don't have the luxury of looking around at the scenery/surroundings while doing the hike.It is not that the view up the top is objectively poor. It is actually decent. it is simply that the effort (3-4 hours one way) to reward (the view up top) ratio is terrible.The group of us hiked up the East trail (Seongpanak) and went down the North trail (Gwaneumsa). The hike down along the North trail provided a handful of views that were decent - better than the East trail.My experience at Mount Hallasan was preceded by Seongsan Ilchulbong the day before which to me provided a much much better experience. The hike was a lot easier and the view was much superior, offering a beautiful view of the Jeju City skyline. I personally would highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong over Mt Hallasan and would recommend against doing Mt Hallasan, unless you are someone that personally loves hiking as an activity anyway.Summary: Long 3-4 hour one-way hike (7-8 hours return) to the summit rewarded with a decent view, with a lot unpaved trail which can be slippery. Not good for people with bad knees, those expecting plenty of beautiful views, and those wanting to enjoy scenery while hiking.

The hiking was great.  I decided to stop and buy a few bottles of water at the last rest stop/cafeteria and quickly used them to replenish my water-backpack.  I then gave the empty bottles back, and the attendant said take your own garbage down!  The way I see it is I bought the water NOT the bottles and I was in no mood for his sarcastic rude remakes.  If you are selling food and water THEY not ME should have a garbage disposal system, even if it costs customers a bit more money.  I found they were very selfish and demining to me, and I would not recommend buying anything from them.   They only are encouraging people to pollute and dispose of there trash  along the trail.  As for me, I hid my trash in front of their exit door to prove a point.

My family with two boys 10 & 12 hiked up the Yeongsil trail to Witseoreum and back down by visitor center near Eoseungsaengak trail. We made a mistake of getting dropped off at the ticketing office by Yeongsil trail and not at the entrance of the trailhead.  It added another hour to 4 hour hike. But the walk was nice nevertheless and we saw a snake and a giant snail to compensate for it.         Trails were very well maintained and clean. But be prepared for ankle twisters and knee pains. I sure wished I had my walking sticks with me. I had to drink some Hite(Korean pale beer) afterward to relieve some pain on my knees. My two boys had no problem for them being young and all.  A little one did the whole trail on sandals but I don't recommend it as there are sections of trails made up with volcanic rocks. One wrong fall and one can easily get a nasty scrape.  Oh yeah, don't forget to bring, snacks, bug repellent, bandaids, medical tapes for your toes and heels.          I enjoyed the cupnoodle at the Witsoreum.  It was only $1.50. I think coffee was $0.50 or 0.60. There are few other snacks offered at incredibly low price considering the location. They give you a plastic bag to carry all our garbage down the mountain.         One thing I really love about this place is the variety of landscapes. It felt like going to several different national parks at once.         Few things...there are no bathrooms between trailheads and Witsoreum.  Be sure to use airgun a the trailheads to blow away the ticks and other insects off your body and clothes.

I chose Seongpanak as the starting point from 7am, I managed to arrive the top before noon. I took Gwaneumsa to go down. This track is difficult than previous one but the view is beautiful. Make sure to bring lots of water and your own food.

My husband loves hiking and the great outdoors. Me? Not so much, but when he told me about the opportunity to climb a very old volcano in a day, I couldn't say no. We chose to do the Gwaneusma trail (8.7kms one way) which is considered steeper of the 2 trails (that reach the summit). I was initially worried that I wouldn't make it to the top because of my poor fitness level, but we did it with zero meltdowns from me. For those who are concerned about the difficulty, ask yourself if you can climb stairs for about 2-3 hours continuously. It was definitely a challenge but I've come to love the mindfulness that comes with hiking. Although, my muscles screamed on the way up, I found it easier to climb up than climb down. The reason for this was because a lot of the path is lined with uneven rocks, so you have to have pretty strong ankles and good foot placement. I managed to roll my ankle 2kms into the descent. Fortunately, I could still walk on it (just!) and we made the very slow climb down. We watched as many people just seemed to fly past with their walking sticks and strong ankles (I'm so jealous!). Moral of the story is, it's a wonderful hike, but be careful!!

We had quite an adventure that could have ended disastrously for us but for the amazing kindness of a family that stopped to help us and the team of park rangers who helped us down and refused to take a penny from us. The trail we chose to climb was supposed to be the easiest route up to the crater lake and indeed, the trail was well laid. The different parts of the trail were graded based on steepness of the gradient. There were rails on either side most of the way and steps as well. The toughest part of the trail for us were 2 boulder fields that we had to cross. My husband got careless when we got to the easiest part of the trail, slipped & twisted his ankle. Unfortunately, this was close to the end of the trail, less than 1 km from the crater lake. We had to turn back and our daughter tried to help him get back down - another 2 hours when one is fit! It was soon evident that we needed help & soon. The sun would set in another hour, we had forgotten to pack food or water, warm clothes. All along the trail our signs with emergency phone number & a number to indicate location. But we had not coverage & knew no Korean to communicate. Just as we had begun to despair, a party of 3 ladies, a father & a daughter stopped to help us. The 3 ladies told us that they would alert the rangers when they got down. The father & daughter stayed with us, helped my husband lie down on a mat they had brought, elevated his foot, called the emergency number. I had some alleve with me & they gave us some water. The rest & the alleve brought down the swelling some & they helped us proceed   a little more down the mountain till the park rangers (a team of 5) met us. The park rangers iced my husband's foot, sprayed pain medicine and bandaged it. A pair of them supported him down the mountain. The father and daughter stayed with us & climbed down with us. We could not have managed without these incredibly generous, compassionate people. The park rangers would not accept any compensation. They told us 'it is our job'. Regarding the trail itself, the route is absolutely stunning beautiful - rhododendrons were in bloom, one could see virtually the whole of Jeju island and the small islands beyond. Well laid out & marked trail with railings & emergency signs, warning signs everywhere. Our accident was due to our own carelessness.

This is a very well maintained mountain park as expected of any Unesco World Heritage site. My wife and I visited on a Monday and it was packed with people. We climbed up from Yeongsil and climbed down to Eorimok. It's impossible to lose your way. The hike is moderate and you don't have to be very fit to do it. Trainers or tennis shoes are adequate in May. You can do it at a leisurely pace or try to break a speed record.
