This park is huge! it is divided into different areas with different themes. It has a great variety of plants and birds. There are also two underground tunnel caves which enrich the overall visiting experience. There is also an area with seasonal flowers.  Great spot for photo-taking. Highly recommended for family with children. Allocate at least two hours visiting time here.

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.

Hallim Park is quite a beautiful park. There are so many things to see, and the flora is really quite spectacular; however, the living conditions of the animals in the park killed the whole experience for us. The turtles are in aquariums that are much too small, and the aquariums don't contain any kind of natural vegetation for the turtles. In fact, only a few turtles had only a single rock in their containers. If that wasn't depressing enough, the living conditions of the peacocks were, quite simply, inhumane. Although some lucky peacocks got to roam around in an area that was relatively open, most of the peacocks were living in small enclosures and sharing those enclosures with up to 13 other peacocks. There was hardly enough room for them to move around, and the birds seemed to be living in quite stressful conditions.  Then, there were the ostriches. All of the ostriches we saw had a terrible looking skin condition, and most of them were going bald. Compared to the flora in the park, it just seemed like the park put no effort into properly caring for the animals at all. If Hallim Park would put a little more effort into making sure their animals are properly cared for and provide better living conditions for the animals, I would recommend going to this place. However, with the current living conditions of the animals, I absolutely cannot recommend anyone go to this place.
The park is quite big and there are many interesting stuff to see. There's a bonsai garden, a small hanok village, bird park etc. It's quite an interesting place where you can spend a good 2 hour.

Hallim Park has everything you would want to see. It has a big and beautiful flower garden, stone and bonsai garden, caves you can explore, a folk village, and a wonderful cactus garden.  It also has a bird garden and reptiles in cages.  You can spend at least half a day exploring everything.

Hallim Park is located at the West part of Jeju island, approximately 20 minutes drive from Jeju City. The park is pretty large as it has a wide range of gardens (cactus, bird park, flowers) and it also has a couple of lava caverns. The park does not have spectacular sites but it is a great and cozy place to spend time especially for families. Do wear comfortable shoes.

Hallim Park is really a variety of interesting elements of Jeju Island rolled into one. The cave located within Hallim park is one of the main attractions. Other attractions include a multitude of gardens, some animal exhibits, and even a small recreated folk village.If you have more than 3-4 days on Jeju island, I would highly recommend Hallim Park. It can be combined with the excellent Hyopjae Beach located close by. Great day for families. If you are staying less than 3 days, it would probably be best to focus on the main natural attractions Jeju Island is so famous for.I enjoyed exploring the park, taking some pictures with my wife, and then relaxing at the beach.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

I read a few reviews saying how it s just a park with trees and birds but I love this place! The greenery is beautiful, the air is fresh with a cool breeze and the cave system is entrancing. Being from a concrete city means all this is actually quite a refreshing change of environment for me. I don t particularly care for the animals and birds being kept in too small enclosures though. But the scenery alone is enough to give it 4*.

Spent approximately 5 hours walking in the park. The park is sub divided into different sectors with different themes. Didn t go to all the different sectors because some didn t appeal to us. What I found nice and interesting were;1. The Caves2. Cultural Village3. The Bonsai & Stone Garden4. Seasonal Section - Ume FlowersWhat I didn t like;1. Birds and reptiles in captivity2. Wild Flowers Garden - area seems to be poorly maintained. I didn t get to see anything except grass and weedsBe prepared to walk and walk so if walking is not your thing then u better reconsider. Limited restaurants on site, so it s best if u bring your own food and drinks.

While in Jeju - we booked the Yeha bus tour and this is one of the places included to visit.  We really enjoyed our time here and our guide did an excellent job of recommending how to see everything in the time we had allotted.

Hallam Park is one of the best botanical gardens we ve visited. The paths are clearly posted and friendly to foreign visitors that don t read Korean. We loved it. The restaurant at the entrance is only a good choice if you like Korean food. The barbecue spot inside might be a better choice for western visitors.

Allow for at least 2.5 to 3 hours to walk around. There are a number if different areas, my favourite being the bonsai trees. The park is very well kept and very tranquil. There are a couple of places that sell snacks and one restaurant on site.
The park is a very big park to cover specially in a hot summer day .Has many different sections and it is easy to get lost without a map .It is a must see place
Great place for kids to have fun.  Kids were searching and hunting for hermit crabs.  There were also some fishermen the kids were interested in.
A great variety of exotic trees & flowers, marvellous birds, unusual sculptures,charming waterfalls, traditional symbols of  Jeju Island.  Beautiful inspiring day.
Hallim Park look older , inside not much fun , and tickets expensive too , inside some area was not clean !

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. However the enclosures could be done better for more visibility of the animals. I read some reviews that they were ill treated but I didn t see any evidence of this. We have very good displays of succulents at Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and Yeomiji Botanical Gardens was also more impressive than Hallim park. For April, I would recommend to skip Hallim park and go for Yeomiji instead for a better visit in general unless you really like tulips. Have to admit the tulips display was very beautiful.

It s about an hour s drive from the airport. Entrance is KRW11,000 for one adult.  The tulips and cherry blossoms were in full bloom. So lovely!  A surprise was the caves. It s so cool!  Really worth the visit.

I can't make of this place. It has plants, caves, a folk village and greenhouses. Yet none of the attractions was really top rate. I would give it a miss and visit attractions with more focus on any one of the above.

My only concern with Hallim Park is the condition of some of the animals they have there. The 'cages' or 'presentation units' seem quite small for some of them, and some of the bigger birds didn't seem particularly happy. I don't want to give this an 'average' review because the caves are incredibly unique, the diverse array of trees and plants is also very special. But full disclosure, this place may not be for everyone.

Fortunate we are able to catch the cheery blossom even during mid April. Nice place to walk around, similar to The Garden of Morning Calm. There is a beach across the park, very nice walk and beautiful scenery. Bring your jacket if you are going during early spring, ITS COLD!

we visited two parks in Jeju. Hallim and Spirited Garden. ticket price was almost the same for both but Hallim was by far much better and bigger with good design and a lot of different and amazing trees and some birds too. It is really a must visit for Jeju visitors to spend around two hours enjoying the park.

We went here mainly to see the cave network formed by Mt. Halla's eruption. It was really cool, literally. The temperature was about 17degrees so it was a nice rest from the 34 outside. There are about 3 sections to all the caves....It was very quiet when we went so not many people about which was nice, but it does get a bit hot walking around all the gardens as we went in the summer. We probably only stayed for an hour or two.

We entered this park with great expectations - the gardens themselves are great, the bonsai area stands out as superb, and the Lava Caves offer some welcome respite from the heat.Everything in the garden was destroyed by the horrific and unacceptable conditions of the birds and other animals.  There was a smallish section with parrots, a few other birds, a monkey in a tiny cage and a few other small furry creatures.  It was filthy, some of the animals had no water, the temperature must have been 35 degrees.  There was one small animal that was clearly suffering greatly (in one of the cages with no water). I emptied the contents of my water bottle into it's water bowl, and reported its condition to a member of staff - who did nothing.We went on to see peacocks and ostriches, yes in slightly larger enclosures, but with no shade, no vegetation, and 13 peacocks in a tiny cage.  The birds were in obvious distress with obsessive grooming and clear skin infections.I've travelled all over the world, and been to many places like this and never, from the poorest, to the richest countries, have I seen animals kept in these conditions. I rarely, if ever, write reviews, but I am so angry at the conditions here, that it's important to be aware.The gardens are immaculate, the conditions of the animals are disgraceful, and should be an embarresment to whoever runs this organisation.Do not visit!

This is really a large park with plenty of places to visit inside. It is recommended to visit this park at spring or early summer so you can watch more blossom flowers. I visited it in October so there is only few flowers. It is still worth a visit though as you can visit the village, the stadium, the bonsai, the caves, and even a bird zoo inside.. must come.
Went with my kids and parents. We explore every part of the park. From Caves, cactus to folk villages. We enjoy the plantation at the park and flowers definitely. Must visit
An decent park to spend 2-3hrs.Nothing great just decent.Lots of tourist thought, so don't expect a peaceful walk unless you go at odd hours.The park close at 6pm.

Hallim Park is so big, we didn't even get to see everything. Spend at least 3 hours here (I think). That should be enough time. I loved the caves, the bonsai garden, the cactus garden, the cherry blossoms, and the tulips festival! Lovely park to visit.
Gardens were not well maintained (except bonsai garden good) but it broke my heart to see the conditions of the animals in captivity. Completely turned me off.
Opposite to Hyeopjae Beach, it is an old fashioned park with almost every element in Jeju. Caves, plants, mini zoo, and even a folk village. 10000 krw entrance fee is not cheap though.
Scenic park with many photo opportunities. Restaurant inside the park (not the one at the entrance) served the most affordable black pork in the region.

This is Actually botany park with some few nice spots , i really don't recommend it because there is many more to see in jeju better than here and not worth to paying 10$ to seeing something u really don't understand , most of park is designed for professional botanist not for normal people .

Hallim Park is privately run, which would explain the cost, which is 5x the cost of entrance to Sunrise Peak, a must-do in Jeju.There are many parts to explore within the park. The most interesting sections to me was the albino peacock enclosure and the rapeseed flower garden. The cherry trees at the cherry blossom section were okay (we went during the cherry blossom festival) but why would u need to pay for that when the rest if the island (and Seoul as well) is full of cherry blossom trees.The tropical plants, wildflower and grass garden section were disappointing. There were lots of potted plants which looked unhealthy and unkempt. I really couldn't tell if the garden was supposed to be manicured or wild.Overall, I think the park is quite passable. I wouldn't visit it again, nor would I strongly recommend it to a friend.
I really liked this park and would recommend it to anyone going to Jeju. It took us about 3 hours walking quickly around it and at W9000 I thought it was defiantly worth it.
Nice pictures can be taken in the park, I most liked bonsai part of the park. 2 gorgeous beaches close to the park entrance.

Went with my son and husband on a very hot day! Park well laid out with several drink food and shade stops on way round! We spent a few hours to see it all! Caves were a highlight - very interesting and cool!! Reptiles and birds ok - not my thing! Enjoyed water area especially cold showers we could stand under :-)) overall a good place to visit and see a range of sights! Easy to get to on main coastal bus route Enjoy
Well set out with a large variety of natural features although we felt a bit sorry for some of the reptiles and birds in confined cages. The highlight is possibly the two lava tubes.

I got a public bus from the Inter-city Bus Terminal at Jeju-si to this park at only Won 2000. 1 hour required.  This is the last activity of my trip and upon leaving, luckily I met an American man at the bus stop who agreed to share a taxi with me heading to the airport, otherwise I may be late.Time is rather limited for me and I took a quick and rough walk in the park after taking a 45 min lunch of seafood pot at the restaurant at the entrance.  Yummy!  Seafood is to die for in Jeju.  I like this park as it's well gardened, clean, cozy with some souvenirs shops and two restaurants inside.  And I did not meet groups of tourists which is a PLUS.  Visitors decent. Next time when I come to Jeju, I should spend plenty of time in this park.There is a famous beach opposite to the park entrance so you can have a walk there as well after leaving here.

If you really have a short time available at Jeju and that you want to have a glimpse of everything, Hallim Park may be your solution.  In there comprises of a tiny folk village, two lava tubes of smaller scale, water park, beautiful gardens for you to enjoy for a few hours.  One couldn't admire the courage of Mr Song who spent 40 years of his life developing Hallim Park from NOTHING.  He literally sweated & toiled through the barren rock into something magical that's been visited by dignitaries around the world.  For someone like myself who came from New Zealand, natural green is something that I have taken for granted but one would have to give Mr Sung encore for the grand vision that he did, to build a tourist attraction for Jeju when tourism wasn't a happening thing just yet.  Just like from the movie, Field of Dreams, if you build it, people will most definitely come!

Love Hallim Park! My expectation was a quick walk around an outdoor park, but it was so much more! Easily taking an entire day if you want it to, you can meander through under ground lava tubes, fruit orchards, small animal zoos, bonsai tree forests, etc.! Highly recommended.
Working hours from 8AM (or 9?) till 5PM.Spend 2-3-4 hours there, many flowers (in season), animals, folk village inside, two interesting caves. Just nice! :)
Entrance Fee 12,000 won. Very wide park. Enjoyed each part of the park.. Not so many flowers are blooming.. Peacock were left free roaming at the park.
This is a great park for the kids, next to a beautiful beech. Loads for the kids to do. Great place for a picnic
Pleasantly surprized that there are varied natural creations to view. Caves, Bonsai, fruits...Delighted with the free calender.

Hallim Park is huge and divided into various sections. You can spend almost a day slowly strolling through the different sections for plants, animals, cactus and you can even visit underground caves. You can also visit a very small old village modelled after the olden days of Korea. It s a place suitable for all families with kids or senior citizens. The entry ticket is on the expensive side for Jeju.
If you like bonsai, tulips and great landscaping, this botanic garden is for you. I particularly loved the hundred year old bonsai trees delicately nurtured to inspire visitors of its natural beauty.
A lover of plants and trees would love to spend hours here in this park. The lava tube may be a new experience for some . . . .

We should have just come here on Day 1 instead of on our last day in Jeju.It has the caves, stone statue, flower, cactus, bonsai, reptiles, birds,  etc all within the park. Even though it was winter, we still enjoy the visit. There were no beautiful flowers but we could still see cactus, birds, reptile, tropicals ferns, etc. If you enjoy botanic garden , stress free walk, you will love this place. It is huge place so we find ourselves rushing to try to see everything. I m sure there are more beautiful gardens and caves in other countries but in jeju, i consider this good. This park is near to 2 beautiful sandy beaches so you can spend a day innthis area. There are restaurants, cafes, etc near the beach but cos winter most were closed.If you are driving just drive along the coast to see the beaches. Our first trip is a touch and go but our hext trip, we will focus on one  or two main areas. We could not do the hiking cos it takes time and better with an overnight stay near the base of the mountains.

This was one of the most popular things to do in jeju and we stayed close by so was a no brainer. Cost $11,000krw to get in, and had heaps of different plants and flowers from different parts of the world etc. overall not too bad, october is the off season to go so was very quiet. If you love plants you ll love this if not properly not the place for you.
We saw birds, ostrich, peacocks and various bonsai trees. You need at least 2 to 3 hrs to enjoy the place. There is also a cave with paved walkways.

If you can't make it to Manjanggul caves, there are caves here too. There is a lot of English signage for the trees, which is great. There is a cafe and restaurant on site. I really enjoyed the  afternoon out, lots of lovely different areas to explore.
Hallim is a beautiful place where you could see a little bit of everything (cave, flowers, village etc). Each sector is small, but it does deserve a visit while in Jeju.

I came here by accident thinking it was simply a nice local park.  The entrance fee was $11,000.  I took a bus and taxi to get here so I went in anyway, thinking I d just stay a short while. I stayed for hours.   There are all types of plants, flowers and trees organized by type.  There are also turtles, snakes, lizards, birds- and peacocks y can see walking about you. There s an area showing old living accommodations in Jeju.  There are real lava caves on the property.  There is just so much to see.  I also got a delicious chocolate ice cream cone for 3000.

Its a beautiful and quiet park to visit. Enjoyed the bonsai area and birds area alot with my 5 year old daughter. There are bonsais as old as 300 yrs old! Signages are clear to indicate the different areas in the park.There is a restaurant within the park itself at the folk village, serves korean food and also small food outlets selling convenient food, ice cream, drinks and beer. There is also a herb cafe in the park, selling herbal teas.A place that is away from crowds to spend an afternoon leisurely with your kids.

Tulips are great. But cherry blossom are ending. The tropical garden is very impressive. If only the other parts of the garden were better maintained. I would have rated this place 5 stars. The caves was very interesting. From hot garden to cold caves. The follow by waterfall. It s very nice transition. One must spend about 3-4 hours to fully explore this garden and use the guide to walk through the garden. I really enjoyed walking this garden with many different theme. Keep up the good work and hopefully with your increased price you can do better maintenance.
It is a very nice park and a lot of attractive scenery and nice place to take pictures snd so on. Strongly recommended!

It s a very big place.. there are a cave, garden, mang kind of birds, trees ans flowers.. i think it is a good place to visit in jeju.. you can see many things here.. but it is difficult to find a bus to here and the bus is not ontime..

Pretty big park with 2 caves that you can go through. Many school trips come here so don't be surprised to see flocks of students in the weekdays too. Nice peaceful area but there are quite a few other Jeju attractions I would see first if you're on a time limit.

The place is big but there are many places that are not well maintained. Tall grasses in some places and many of the plants are left to grow without some serious planning. The caves are nice though, clean and doesn't have the smell of bat urine. The bonsais are quite nice too.

The caves are amazing, well maintained and secured, very clean.  I am just wondering why other tourist doesn't want to go inside. If you visit hallim, don't ever miss passing the caves before going to other attractions of the park.  The second thing that attracted me most are the wide bonsai collection and the stones. They are really beautiful, picture perfect.

We spent the afternoon at Hallim Park and thoroughly enjoyed the statues, the bonsai garden, the rock sculptures, the caves and the traditional village.  The grasses section appeared to be very dry and in need of some immediate cleaning up.  We were shocked and saddened by what we saw in the bird section.  The ostriches were clearly in distress as they had lost many feathers and were showing signs of balding.  They were enclosed in an area devoid of greenery and appeared to be desperately seeking out food by nipping the air.  The enclosure did not allow for these beautiful birds to run and get the necessary exercise.  Yes, there were food dishes in various locations however they didn't seem to meet the needs of the ostriches.  The peacocks were also showing signs of stress as their plumage was rather thin.  They were enclosed in an area where the floor was of interlocking brick.  This is as far from a natural setting as possible. Our visit ended on a sour note and it is our hope that the dire situation of these birds will be addressed by those in charge.  We highly advise anyone who visits this park to make his/her concerns known as it is the only way to rectify this sad situation.
Fare was expensive but nothing to see inside almost flower and tree ,some place was not very clean ..

This park includes a variety of sights including two lava tubes, an aviary that includes a variety of peacocks, ostriches etc, a small traditional village, strange little rock people sculptures, and a very impressive botanical garden with outdoor sections around a pond and several green houses.   Some strange combinations in the outdoor section with large palms mixed up with various types of cacti and other random mixes of fabulous plant specimens from all over the world.  The greenhouse plants seem a bit more organized by regions or types (e.g., large cactus collection in one greenhouse; palms in another), with live animals interspersed between the plants (impressive boa and python collection, also some special turtles, and lizards such as nile monitors, iguanas, etc.).  In between plant viewing, I enjoyed a nice cool cactus juice relaxing in the herb bar.

At Hallim park, there are a few lava caves that are interesting, and very cool (temperature).  The flower gardens are very nice.  The bonsai garden has trees that date to 300 years ago.  They are constantly trimmed to keep them small.  There is a restaurant at the entrance, and a rest area with a gift shop in the center of the park.
If you are a family with children, it is good to visit. But if you are alone or couple, you would not be interested only with plants..
Very beautiful park with flowers and cultures, exotic animals and a continued paved walk through a number of cool dark caves.

There are several things to visit and see inside the Hailim Park.  This botanical garden includes bonsai artwork and garden, a Jeju stone, a Jaeam Folk Village, an underground Hyeopjae & Sangyong Cave, and a zoo.  Well worth a visit.  Best time to visit is in the spring especially during the cherry blossom season.

first advise don't travel juju alone ... tour and tour buses become a necessity ... as i was travelling by public bus it took almost more then an hour to reach there .... was already a bit tired by the time we reached ... We were lucky that we visited during cherry blossoms season, so it was an added bonus.  Only caution is don't go there hungry.  Food there is terrible and expensive. Walking between different kind of plants. It is nice for who love nature. Also I love folk village, cave, and Bonsai tree. It was 20,000 Won Taxi cap from Jeju Lotte Hotel, and you don't have to keep your taxi waiting for you because there are many taxi in erea.
Hallim park is part botanical garden, mini zoo, and culture center. The majority of Hallim is mediocre, but the jewel of the park is its rich bonsai collection.An hour is okay

Great place for nature lovers to soak in multi themes and explore the Hyeopjae & Ssangyong caves in one location for admission price of KRW10000. Park is wheelchair friendly and is a great place for friends and family to spend a few hours together. The park does not feel overly crowded as it is spread over 80 acres. Visitors still enjoy tranquil surroundings even though the park is crowded.

This Hallim Park is a big area with the palm tree, tulips, cherry blossom, etc.  They also have some cave and near to the sea.  They have Historical Story since 1971 if you see the website.  We need to have 2-3 hours i think to go arround.  When i visit here last week, we still can see the tulips.

Pro: Great caves, delicious hallabong icies, beautiful water liliesCons: Quite expensive, a little bit dated, the peacocks look sickly

It's a mixed review.  The ticket price is 10,000KRW per adult and since other natural attractions are around 2,000KRW, this park should be well worth it.  Highs: The caves are really cool as well as the Bansai and Stone Garden. The park is easy to walk and has shops and toilets easily available.  Transportation is also easy as it's just the 702 bus from the Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal for 1 hour. Lows: The park is dated, like late 90s with its signage and information cards.  The bird exhibit, stone exhibit and flower garden are average at best.  While the park trail is easy to walk, you do walk through gift shops for the next exhibits (so a bit too tourist-y). Overall, it makes for a decent easy afternoon, especially with kids or elderly.  The park needs some updating to be worth the ticket price, but it is close to the beach (just 5 mins walking).

Nice park, relaxing. The Lava Tubes within the park were nice and cool. Try to go on a cool day. The grounds are nicely kept. The ostriches were not taken care of very well. The rest of the birds were ok. Bonsai garden was interesting. Only the hydrangeas were in season, so no flowers. Only spent a couple of hours there, then headed to the beach across the street.

Hallim is mixture of small zoo,botanical garden, lava caves and stones. We arrived     In morning after rain,park was quiet, with not many visitors, relaxing. I liked walking through volcanic caves, beautiful bonsai garden with some trees around 300year old. And completely white peacocks, I did not know before such ones even exist.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.
Had a really good time walking around the park. The gardens are beautiful and the lava caves are cool too! Worth a visit if you're passing by.

A larger version of Bontanic Gardens. Provide rental of prams for babies/ toddlers. The weather was good when I was there, hands nice and relaxing tour. They have cactus, flowers, plants, water park, caves, birds etc

Stay in touch with nature and culture with this big park. Take time to appreciate the caves and read about the stories. I especially like the bonsai park. During spring, make sure to check out the rape seed canola flower beds and the cherry blossom trees on bloom.

This was our first attraction after arriving in Jeju-do. It was recommended by several locals including our taxi driver. We had a mixed aged group with us (4 year old active little boy to my 70 year mother) and everyone was able to enjoy what the park had to offer. My mom and aunts were amazed by the plants, especially the hundred year old bonsai trees. My two kids loved the caves. First time that I have ever seen white peacocks. The only thing I found rather odd was the petting zoo that requires another fee.

You could easily do 4-5 hours or even a day trip at Hallim Park. The first part of the gardens is uninspired, but persevere and head to the lava caves, tulip garden (late March/early April), bonsai gardens and beyond.
I like the ume flower garden, canola flower field, mini traditional folk village and greenhouses of cactus.

I like the way they have put up arrows for you to follow around the park so you won't miss anything.  But if you want to take short cuts and look for the peacocks, it will be pretty hard, as there is no guide and the people there can hardly speak English.  I got lost looking for the peacocks even though I had a map.

If you have limited time, I would highly recommend this garden over the Yeomiji Botanic Garden.  There is so much to see and with the very helpful signs, there was no anxiety about getting lost.  The garden is designed for 1-way traffic so once you enter into one of the many feature spaces, you can't decide to opt out but have to continue until the exit point.  We did not know just how vast the garden was and wished we had allocated more time.  The bonsai and stone garden was really outstanding.When leaving the garden, do consider taking a scenic drive along the west side of Jeju Island and head towards Jungmun.  This stretch of coast was truly out of this world beautiful.
Lovely park. Went with a tour group so was a rush. Would have been better to spend more time there. The caves is a must see.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and "rare" factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). We just did a cursory walk around the park and made our escape after an hour.I seldom recommend my own country to other travelers, but if anyone wants to visit an interesting garden, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore is so much better than the gardens at Hallim Park. I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.
We liked this place very much! Natural, beautiful and wonderful park! Definitely worth visiting and spending the whole day. I liked the caves best of all )

We decided to visit one of JeJu s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.
This relaxing adventure is full of all kinds of beautiful flowers. I have been here 3 times. I recommend going in the spring when many flowers are in bloom.
The park was full of nice gardens and i was really impressed by the caves. Was only 10,000 won entry and i think it was worth the visit

A nice botanic garden with interesting elements. I particularly like the bonsai garden with lots of areas to sit and admire the specimens. Since we only had a very limited time, we were not able to see the other areas.

Me and my husband visited Hallim Park, the beach just outside the park is beautiful so make sure to allow some time to check it out. The park itself consists of about 7-8 different theme subsessions. It was a lot bigger than I expected. The park was very well signed and designed with lots attention to details. Of cause it is not comparable to the natural beauty of Jeju but for a man made park, it is a great choice for an outing with family for 2 hours.

caves, bonsai trees, birds, nice gardens, restaurant in traditional style, and very well maintained area, the owner really has a passion to gardening and pride for his homeland. worth to visit at anytime, in summer you can also enjoy magic sandy beaches on the other side of the park

This park has a collection of 7-8 sections of different type of plants and sights, such as tropical plants, cactus collections, bonsai collection, wild flowers, cave systems, folk village, small cave system etc. You could easily spent 2 hours at this park. The park is nicely planned and appropriately signed to guide the exploration of the entire park. We really liked its cactus collection and roads lined by famous Jeju-harubang (stone human-shaped statues). We definitely recommend visiting this fabulous park.

My husband and I were staying in the Hallim area and our taxi driver mistakenly took us to Hallim Park. Especially since it was a bit chilly and an overcast day, the beautiful green houses and occasionally covered areas were a nice break from the weather. The park itself is nothing overly spectacular, but it has a little bit of everything with a nice mix of Jeju style to your typical botanical gardens type park. Plants, flowers, animals, exhibits, and fun!

This is one of the best place we visited in Jeju. Various things to see such as flowers, plants, birds, small reptiles, lava cave etc. I love the cactus garden most. Great for photo taking and a slow stroll with family members! I did not fully explore the place due to time constraint. Guess it probably need around 2-3 hrs to slowly explore the park.
The park has birds area , flowers area, caverns with lots of other attractions probably you need 4 hour to see it all.We like the caverns more than anything else
so many beautiful flowers, with mini bird park. also caves where you can learn about geography. there is an entrance fee but cheap. so just enjoy the beauty!

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.
Extensive botanical gardens which include some caves. Well worth a visit to explore. Allow plenty of time.

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

Heaven on Earth - volcanic stone sculptures abound - every tree a bonsai - cedar, pine, maple and more.  Azaleas were in full bloom and a delight in colour.  The birds, in particular the white peacock who posed displaying all his feathers fanned out.  Then onto the water garden with its lotus blooms, fish and waterfalls.  I would do anything to have a garden like this in which to spend my days.

Place for everyone - Solo, couple or with family.Garden has multiple theme garden build in. Botany students can spend days. Best one is Bonsai garden. There is exhibition on garden formation with pictures but everything is in Korean. Tropical garden is beautiful too.Note: Tropical garden is built one way street   you go in and come out after long walk. You might get lost.

The park is a great snapshot of what the island has to offer. There are bonsai exhibits, traditional korean village exhibitions and even an aviary.  Very neat and pleasant way to spend an afternoon.

This place is just great! I love Hallim Park especially the caves! they are so mystical!! the parks has most of the natural attractions. The park is huge and you may need to spend hours in it to enjoy everything that they offer. It was so relaxing and very nice.
Visited mainly to see the lava caves. Walked past the bird enclosure on the way out and was shocked to see the crowded small bare enclosures they are kept in.
Unexpected place. Really huge. Good for family visit. Fun time with the kids. You may need to spend the whole day in the area.
To put it simply one of the best garden parks Ive ever been to. A magical place which  peacocks roam around. very professionally done, a must see while here.
The park is located close to the beach, it s entrance fee is 12,000 won, it have a variety of plants, a cave, birds and some reptiles. A great way to spend a few hours.

This is just a park with some trees, caged birds, caves and bonsai. Nothing very spectacular for the krw120000 of entry fee. The signage was insufficient to the various sights so I walked around quite a bit but still didn t find some key sights.

This is a very nice park with some diverse points of interest. The lava tubes were interesting. Especially stunning is the walk through many, some quite old, bonsai. What was an aside visit for us became one of the highlights of our trip. I d suggest two hours at least.

Nice stroll around the garden, the lava tunnels are cool and most waterlilies in bloom. Nice, but not spectacular. Not an absolute must.

Must come when spring season on early April. There will be more flowers especially cherry blossom and tulips.

The park is nice and had a good size. Not much to see, looked a little bit worn out to me. Any way its nice if you have extra time on your hands

I was so surprised of beauty this park. I walked about 4 hours here to watch all places.in this park you can find beautiful birds, gardens, waterfall, caves, etc. to spend day here is amazing cause you feel that you in a forest with many trees and other signs of nature.
big enough & diff topic in park. you could see the flower, bird, cave etc,,,,not too crowded when i visited, good place for spending time

This place is a garden and there is cave and lot of birds, literally this place has everything. It is worth the visit, I like the cactus garden and the bird feeding area. I will definitely come back again with my family. I made a vblog during my trip, come and see if it is worth the visit.Search by title :#3 TRAVEL BLOG DAY 2 JEJU - NATURE - GD CAFE

Pleasant wander around here. 2-3 hours with a stop for lunch. We took our little dog on a lead and no problem. The water garden and Bonsai were my favourite. Reasonable admission for the amount to see. Definitely a must do!

Wow-this place is huge, gorgeous and meticulously maintained. Spent 3 hours there wandering aimlessly, just loved it and the calming vibe. A nice park with nine different ereas. The only important ones in my mind ofcourse is the caves and the Bonsai garden. The other partd you can find in many places.
This is a very good park. You can see a lot of varieties of flowers, trees, and birds in this park. Also, you have a chance to see two-dimensional caves.
Enjoyed wandering through flowers, and bonsai trees. Interesting look at the folk village and some gorgeous peacocks. Takes a couple hours tops but a nice place to visit
This park has 9 zones, botanic garden, caves , flower garden, water garden....We spent a present day out in the park.
It's a beautiful park to stroll around in the spring time (that's when I visitors Jeju) and given the good weather condition, walking around is just refreshing and calming. A must visit place

Interesting! There are quite a few things to visit like Botanic Garden, Bonsai Garden, Folk Village, Lava Cave, Bird Garden, Water Garden etc. Recommended!

It was a nice walk around Hallim Park especially if you like Bonsai trees, folk Village and more...We had a great walk aroundthe area and the weather was so freshly cold . Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

To those unfamiliar with bonsai trees, they may just be miniature trees; but to those who know the value of these works of art, these bonsai trees are literally priceless. In fact, it's almost unbelievable how openly accessible these trees are to the guests, considering their value and need for extreme care.If you're planning on visiting, briefly study the artistry before your trip to enhance the enjoyment. This is a one-of-a-kind collection.

We took a Crystal Lines cruise ship tour from the JeJu island port to Halim Park - about 45 minutes. At the park, I really liked the stone sculptures, the Bonsai gardens and the diversity of things to see (cultural village, diver statue beside waterfall and the small cave). The park was relaxing and there is a quite a story about the founding. Key fact:  the park was built on volcanic rock back in 1971. This provides perspective on just how great this park has become.Even more interesting were the statues of the JeJu female free divers.   For generations, many women of JeJu   called the Haenyeo women - free dive 60 feet or more into the freezing ocean to gather shellfish, octopus and abalone. The divers hold their breath for up to 10 minutes. Naturally, these ladies are respected for their stamina and courage. Over the years, these women have found other lucrative dive sites as far away as Vladivostok, Russia.  Alas, the tales of courage are dying out as only 5000 free divers remain active, two-thirds of those are over 60. Young women just want to have more fun, I guess.Overall, high marks.

The park was established on barren land in Hyeopjaeri, Hallimeup, and covered with tons of earth and began planting assorted subtropical plants in early 1971.

They sprinkle in some reptiles and birds to keep the kids interested.
