My friend and I took the 781-1 bus there from Jeju intercity terminal at 6.40am, cost 1800W. Get off at the Seongpanak stop, approx 30-40mins. We were happy to find that the walking is free and we got a good map (incl english) from the counter where you pay for parking (which we didnt need to pay for given we got the bus). It took us 4 hours (incl breaks) to get to the top. It's well sign posted and there is some food and drink at the stop before the top. I'm usually a solo female traveller and it would be totally fine to do on your own as it's so busy and we'll marked. Footwear ranged from Converse (!!!) to sneakers to full on tramping boots. We wore sneakers and were fine but if you have weak ankles, sensitive feet, or its wet then I'd wear boots. Take a wind breaker as the summit has a cold wind, otherwise casual walking gear was sufficient for us in Oct. We walked down the Gwaneumsa track which was great as there were hardly any people and much better views, it's also 1km shorter. On sat/sun/public holidays there is bus from Gwaneumsa every 50 mins (the timetable is in korean on the side of the parking lot entrance pay station booth) but as we were there mid week, we just walked 3.7km to the nearest bus stop (facing the road/with your back to the track exit, turn right on the main road and just follow the road to the main junction then turn left to the nearest bus stop). This was ok as we had already walked so far, it was only another few km, and it is all downhill, the only dodgy part is that you're walking along a road with not much of a shoulder to walk on when cars fly past. But, don't be afraid of Gwaneumsa! Bus from there to Jeju is 1200W. A long and tiring day but definitely worth it.

We were dropped by a taxi at the beginning of the Seongpanak trail (a little way up the volcano), but you can catch the bus there if you prefer and there is a bus stop right near the entrance. The track is 9.6km (19.2km return), and took us about 6 hours return walking at a medium pace, including breaks at Sokbat shelter (4.1kms up - toilet facilities only) and at Jindallaebat shelter (7.3kms up - toilet and small kiosk). We had initially wanted to walk up the Gwaneumsa trail and then down the Seongpanak one, but were too tired to get up before 6am to achieve it in one day. Walking the Seongpanak trail up and down was a great experience in itself, even though it is apparently not as scenic as others. But, because it's one of the easier ones, it is packed with tourists, most of whom are not seasoned walkers, so be prepared for being held up a fair bit (and witnessing some pretty avoidable but hilarious injuries!).The trail is quite an easy one in comparison to other hikes we have done - no really steep bits or actual climbing - more of a gentle incline, with boardwalks in parts, dirt paths and as you get higher, rough rocky paths. The only strenuous thing about the trail is that it is long  It will take you all day, and you have to start early so you reach the Jindallaebat shelter before a certain hour (changes depending on the season, but in September it was 12:30pm) or the ranger won't let you continue - for obvious reasons, there's no lighting at night to climb back down, so he doesn't want to come and find stupidly lost tourists! You can check the times on the official Hallasan website. You don't really need proper hiking boots/other equipment for this hike (we did it in light walking shoes), but if you have weak ankles I would probably recommend wearing hiking boots with ankle support, especially for the walk back down the rocky paths. Take plenty of water and snacks - don't rely on the shelters like the Koreans do, they may sell out/be extremely busy, and you have to get to Jindallaebat by 12:30! We just bought some muesli bars, fruit, WATER and energy drinks like gatorade/powerade at a 7/11 before we left Jeju city in the morning, and were almost the only ones who had thought ahead! On the way back down, the Jindallaebat shelter will be quieter, so it's the perfect opportunity to then buy some of their hot ramen noodles or a chocolate bar. I would also recommend bringing a light rain jacket, and a waterproof backpack/cover for your backpack - it showers sporadically within the fog. I also took a plastic bag to put my camera in to keep it dry.When we began our walk, it was quite chilly at the entrance and the local walkers laughed at us wearing shorts - but by the time you get a few kilometres in, you'll be stripping off layers of clothing, so totally wear shorts if you want to - it's quite warm in the sun on the summit, so everyone will be peeling off their layers anyway! There was a thick fog hanging low over the volcano for about 2/3 of the walk, so it's a bit muggy, but the side of the mountain is lush and green, an eerily quiet forest. As you get higher, suddenly you notice you're climbing above the fog - feels like you've popped out above the clouds, on top of the world! The last part of the track is quite windy, and you can see how the wind has beaten its wooden steps, which are strewn everywhere. Be careful in the last part and beware pushy tourists! But, once you get to the summit, at Dongneung Peak (no facilities on the summit, by the way), the view is breathtakingly beautiful - like nothing I've ever seen before! The crater when we were there was overgrown with vegetation, with a small crater lake. Such a wonderful experience, and most definitely a highlight of our trip to South Korea! You must hike Hallasan during your stay at Jeju-do!

I am a complete beginner to mountain climbing but was there thankfully with an experienced climber. We took a taxi from jeju city to Seongpanak visitor centre and the journey costs around 20,000 krw and approx 40 min. I was there on 7 December after a snowy night, and the trails were covered in snow. Poles, proper hiking shoes and crampons are absolute necessity as the snowy paths were hard to walk.  Gwaneumsa, the popular trail for descent after reaching the crater summit, was closed that day as the snowy trail was too dangerous, so it was pretty rough to get up while people are trying to get down. Especially since the trail was already made quite narrow by the snow. However, the view is great and it's like a winter wonderland all the way up. The last stretch to the crater summit was hard for a complete beginner like me. It was however considered easy for seasoned hiker like my friend. On the whole a great experience and certainly worth the trouble for the views but would recommend complete beginners like me to do some training before getting up. The rest stops are well stocked and constant announcements were made (in Korean only) to keep the hikers moving up before the gate closes at 12 pm and down before it's gets dark. Note: we were staying in Jeju city before the climb and the weather was grim with lots of rain. The weather on Hallasan was however completely different. Sunny and pleasant for climbing.  Be sure to check the weather forecast on Hallasan and not Jeju!
the views were beautiful from above, but had slightly hard time getting there. we enjoyed our time there
this is a wonderful nature trail with breathtaking view. One of the best places to visit while in Jeju.

I hadn t hiked in years, but thought I d give it a try at a friend s suggestion. I dressed in layers as the weather was still cold, but knew I d get warm on the climb up. I didn t use crampons and there was only a small amount of ice in some places, it was easy to avoid. I did use poles, which I ve never used before, but was thankful to have them, especially on the way down. The terrain was rocky, but there are lots of stairs and ropes as you reach the summit. It was much colder at the summit and the view was clearer than I expected. The crater is impressive. I did see a deer and a couple red squirrels. The hike down was much more difficult. My legs were in so much pain by the end of the day. Bring lots of food and water. Many people have picnics at the summit. I arrived to the trailhead by taxi and found a taxi at the trailhead when finished. I had to wait around a bit for a taxi to show up.
this is one of the 2 trails that leads to the peak of Hallasan. beautiful view especially the last 2-3 km stretch towards the peak. Try going on both trails as they have different views.

Long trail relatively easy.. specially the first 4 KM .. are flat basically The rest is a hit steepThey will give u a certificate if u take a picture up for 1000 wanBring ur own food.  And water.. In the winter wear ur gears as its super sleepery dont go with out gears i went in april. . And in the last 1/3 of the road i slipped and injured myself many times.. Fantastic hike.. Definitely recommend it

I've done the hike from the trail head at Seongpanak parking lot to the summit of Halla-san 14 times.  The hike is about 9 KM to the top.  The trail is very rocky and vertical.  There are a few drinking water sources on the way to the summit.  As you get near the top, the trail becomes a series of wooden stairs.  The trail becomes seriously vertical about 7KM from the trail head.  It took me between 2 and 2.5 hours to go up and about the same amount of time to return to my car.

Might not be very tall at 1950m but it's no walk in the park. The best part though is that the path is clear and generally easy to walk especially when there are planks. Otherwise walking on volcanic rock and boulders are not so comfortable for the feet. Great views at the top and as we went in spring, flowers are in bloom.

See other reviews on rubbish, food, clothing, water etc Travelling from seongwipo - take bus 782 (stock up on snacks/lunch at the convenience store nearby if haven't done so already as your options are limited once you get there). Bus Tickets cost 1800 won per person one way. Purchase tickets from ticket office or bus driver (take small change) and the trip takes around 30mins, dropping you off right at the entrance of the walking trail. (take bus 781 if travelling from Jeju city). Take the 781 bus to return to seongwipo.

My wife fell on the mountain due to lack of safety equipment, and had to get a ride down...  I am former Army...  I ran the 2 hours down the mountain to beat her there...  asked a staff member where I could get water... showing a drinking water bottle...    instead of pointing to the store where I could buy drinking water, he told me to drink from the toilet...  I took his picture....  Sad!  Meanwhile, another, much better employee was helping my wife down the mountain in their train of sorts...  cog mono-rail...  was pretty cool!  Her knee is better now, but this attraction is a serious hazard and needs to be put on an advisory of some sort!!!

We took bus 182 early morning reached there around 7.30am and started to hike about 8am. It's good to bring hiking stick as there are lots of steps up, with a hiking stick it's easier to move up the rocky paths. It was very cold at the mountain so it's good to wear in layers and can remove the jackets if it gets too warm during the hike. We managed to reach Saraoreum shelter before 12pm where we ate and took a break before moving on to the summit. After 12pm no one is allowed to move on up to the summit from the shelter as it gets dark very early during winter time. We reached the summit just before 1.30pm. The ranger already chasing people to get down. It was very cold and windy at the top and it started to drizzle. So it's important to bring a raincoat too. I could'nt get a good view as it was very foggy and windy. We did'nt get some rest and started to descend. It took a long while to descend too as the path is very rocky and slippery. Lucky i have my hiking stick with me. Half way down it started to get dark we needed to use our handphones as touch light to guide us down the path. Very happy we are all able to reach the summit. It's a nice experience.

Hiking Mt. Halla was on my bucket list for a long time and finally i did it. There is a time restriction and you cannot enter the gate before 6:00 am during the winter time. You have to pass 'Jindalaebat Shelter' before 12:00 pm to continuously hike up to the summit. The park keeper will not let up pass the gate of Jindalaebat if you arrive after the noon. It took about 2 or 3 hours to get to Jindalaebat from Seongpanak gate, and another 2 or 3 hours to get to the summit. It took me 4 hours to get to the Baekrokdam, and took another 5 hours to get down to Gwaneumsa temple. I highly recommend to hike from Seongpanak because it is easier to walk and you are too tired to look around. Then, walk down to Gwaneumsa direction which has a really good view and nature. (Gwaneumsa route is shorter, but definitely harder...super stiff)You will see many people lining up to take a photo with a monument, and I didn't understand why people want to take a photo with just a rock. I learned that you will get a certification of Mt. Hallasan hiking if you show the picture with the monument. All you need to do is go to the ticket office, pay 1,000 KRW and show the picture. I've seen many people hiking with sneakers, but I recommend wearing hiking boots since you have to walk on rocks for 8~9 hours. I heard that you need to be luck to see the summit because Hallasan is always foggy and cloudy. I was lucky and weather was just amazing!! I also heard that it is slightly easier to hike when it snows. There are buses that you can use and I strongly recommend hiking Mt. Halla!!!!!!!

I have always wanted to climb Hallasan so when I got the chance to visit Jeju, I included it on my itinerary. As I wasn't an expert hiker, I have opted to start my ascent at the Seongpanak trail. I wasn't disappointed. It was only a moderately steep climb for most of the trip. You will only have a more difficulty from the rest stop. The scenery wasn't as good as Gwaneumsa but if you want a more relaxing climb, I'd suggest to take this trail.

We ( mostly) enjoyed our hike up Hallasan. It is a moderate climb despite being the highest peak in S. Korea. Important to note that you still need crampons to climb right now. Our hotel went and told us we didn t need them as there was no snow left...well they were wrong! The steepest slopes on the trail are still sheer ice and it is quite treacherous without the crampons to help you grip! Other than that it was a good hike. Crater at the top is pretty cool. Also note that even on a clear day it was really hazy in the distance so the view from the top wasn t as expected. Still worth it though. I recommend starting very early, get the first bus in the morning. The trail becomes quite crowded later on.

Seonpanak is known to be the more difficult route, however both to the summit have their difficulties. Seonpanak definitely has nicer views than Gwaneumsa, thats why we chose to walk down this trail, as your back is facing the beauty on the way up. This route has TONS of rocks which make it hard to balance and hike without the proper shoes. There are 4 or 5 base camps, only one offering water, and one with (disgusting) squat toilets. It took about 3 1/2 hours to hike from the summit, to the bottom. My legs are KILLING ME. But, it was worth it!

We wanted to hike to the summit of the Hallasan mountain, and decided to use the Seongpanak trail.It's roughly 9 kms from the parking lot to the summit, and it took us around 2h50m at a constant pace with few stops. This is a very scenic hike starting in the middle of the forest, and close to the top through prairies. The hike is properly maintained with stairs and paths, but some parts have many rocks, and thus proper hiking shoes are highly recommended.The views from the summit are spectacular!

Went on a day hike up and down the Seongpanak trail! It was a gorgeous day, about 18C and I couldn't have asked for better weather. It took about 10 hours round trip. Started around 8:30am and made it down by 6:30pm. Luckily the sun didn't go down until 7:15ish so I had plenty of light to guide me.Now, I am not a hiker by any means and this was one of the toughest hikes I've been on. To be honest, it wasn't because the trails were all that difficult - it was actually quite pleasant through the woods and there were 2 rest stops along the way. The first stop is basically a bathroom break and the 2nd had some food available before heading up the last (somewhat steeper) trail to the lake up top. Oh, by "food" I mean some cup ramen and snacks. They also sold water and sports drinks. It would be helpful for you to bring food of your own. They also have no garbage cans so you need to carry and dispose of your own trash once you get back down.The reason why this trail was difficult for me was because I simply wasn't ready for a 20km hike! By the last 5km of the descent, I felt my feet and legs were going to fall off or give in to becoming jelly due to all the stairs and rocks. Make sure you have proper shoes! All in all, I'm glad I did this hike - it was worth it when I got to the top and was able to experience amazing views and clean air. And the flowers!! It was simply beautiful. Just expect to have sore calves for a few days following :)

It was supposed to be sunny day according to forecast but the rain started the night before and it just won't stop. I was about to give up the plan but my friend insist on going and we ended up on top of the mountain :) it was rather a different experience hiking under the rain. The only disappointment was the fog on top which basically cover the beautiful view of the lake.
It's a long trail... the track is quite easy at the beginning but become more challenging to the top. But the view its worth it... But if you can, avoid go on the weekend. Too many people on weekend.

My wife and I were rather underprepared for this hike. And the terrain is not for someone who had never trekked before.Nevertheless, taking it to summit on the 3rd day of November was an interesting experience. From temperate zone to the frosted summit, the temperature and views changed dramatically. Thumbs up!

Seongpanak is excellent trail, but no need to compare it with other places in other countries, you need to appreciate it as it is, it's the trail to reach the highest crater of Hallasan in South Korea (there are only two trails to do it and Seongpanak is easier than Gwanumsa), you will find couple of nice views close to the top, otherwise most of it's more like an exercise hike, don't expect too many nice views on the way, it's mostly forest walk. For most Koreans it's an easy hike, there are really fit:) so be prepared for serious hike.I found winter hiking the most exiting, but you need to be well prepared: jackets, gloves, hats, crampons etc as well as get more information on difficulty rate not overestimate your level and timing.

Myself and wifey and our 2 boys aged 12 and 15, decided to walk this mountain, and arrived just after 9.30 in the morning. This trail is supposedly the easier of what are now 3 trails that take you to the summit. Because it wasn't the weekend, there were fewer people, and this was a big bonus, as the whole way up is sectioned off with guide rope, and is either wooden stairs or stones and rock. The few times we came across people, you were held up a bit until you came across a widening where you could overtake them. I can imagine this being very irritating on a weekend, and also you lose that feeling of being out in the wilderness.On the way up we met small groups of older Koreans, who offered us cucumbers and oranges, and we greeted all we met with " hello" or " how you doing ?" in Korean. This was mostly met with a smile and a happy reply.The downside with this trail, is that you are surrounded by trees the first 8 km up, and it is not until the last kilometre that you actually begin to get an appreciation of the views. In some ways it is quite beautiful, but like I said to our two boys, the bottom of the hill is nearly like the top, because you can only see the trees- okay different formations, but no view.At the top, you have the crater sectioned off, and you can peer down into it and take pictures. Because of the distance, we rate this quite a hard going trek,and there are many loose rocks that you could easily twist your ankle on, wifey did!!We used 3 hours up, a little more down, because we had to stop for a while, so wifey could swear at me when she twisted her ankle!!
This is really a challenging hike for me, but it's worth the time and effort. I'm so happy I reached the summit !!!

We choose a day with the best weather forecast, during our visit to Jeju island, to take a walk to the peak of Hallasan. We choose west trail   it doesn't lead to the peak, but is much shorter. It took us 3h to get to the highest point of the trail and 2h to get back to the next bus stop. Everything was very exotic, as we are used to hike in Alps or Carpathians. It is worth to remember, that the temperature drops about 1째C/200m, so it should be 10째C colder on the peak than on the sea level. And it was. More surprising was that there are no possibility to buy food or drink in the park. Fortunately we took lot of water and some fruits and sweets (old habit from "real" mountains). The trail was very "civilised"  mostly steps, easy and very safe (however with ice or snow it's for sure not a pice of cake). More walking than climbing. Not so much people (May seems to be off season), but we were not alone. The view from the trail and the peak just beautiful. In my opinion it's worth to spent half a day on Jeju to see it.
We went this trail up and can recommend it surely for everyone who is in doubt of their stamina. It was a steady elevation with nice stops on the way

Am not much of an active person who trek but managed to finish the hike.  Pretty easy to find alternative transport instead of cab.   I took a cab to Jeju bus terminal and ask for the bus to seongpanak hallasan.  There are announcements and signboard to alert one for each stop and hence I manage to align at the seongpanak stop with no difficulty.  The trek was okay for the first leg (pre-rest stop) and got more challenging at the final leg.  Not knowing much, realised that most of the hikers have their hiking stick while I was on my own - then again I survive the hike abit limping for the long long hike :). In all, I enjoy the hike with not regrets

Not only was the view after climbing to the top of Trail no. 2 breathtaking, the track up the steps and steep trail will also leave most breathless! There are markers that state you are at 2-1, 2-2 etc., the 2 in front meaning trail no. 2, but none tells you how much higher you must climb! Incidentally the top is 2-5. Its quite a struggle to reach the top but if you take it easy and take regular breaks along the way to admire the fauna & flora, take some photos and generally get your breath back, you should reach the top in about half an hour. The journey down is much easier and faster. The view on top is magnificent and definitely worth the climb! The fresh cool mountain air was great too. Highly recommend you try. PS : There were two ladies in their seventies from San Francisco who completed the climb and decent at the same time as my group. Two thumbs up to them!!There is also a museum and sculptured garden at the base of the mountain where you can sit on park benches and enjoy the air and general view of the Hallasan mountain and its surroundings.

We take this trail to climb Hallasan. This trail is very popular but the longest trail. It could take approximately 4 hours to climb to the top and 5 hours to climb down. if you are visiting in winter time, please prepare your crampon/ice cleat, since the trail road is slippery and covered by snow or ice. You could buy cheap crampon at E mart or Lotte Mart with the price less than USD 10, but it is very use full.

It was very good and origin. I though I'd given up before I even start, but the quite,the white of the snow amazed me, I kept moving head. Lost of local people climb on the last day of 2014. and I have to say is they climbed so fast,we were passed by many followers.

This is a long but fairly gentle trail up Mt Hallasan. It was extremely busy with people going both ways and most of the path is on wooden boardwalks and steps or basalt rocks. The later are uneven and I'd recommend hiking boots for comfort. There is a place to refill water bottles about half way up and the second of two shelters does some basic foods - noodles, but better to take everything you want with you. The toilets are grim. The crater at the top was rather disappointing with a muddy pool of water at the bottom on the day we went, but there were some splendid views across Jeju Is over all the parasitic volcanos. The lower slopes were very pretty with fall colours at the end of October. However, I've done better hiking with far fewer people in other countries.

The Seongpanak Trail is the easiest, though the longest trail to hike up Mount Hallasan (bit over 9km). It's a beautiful path with a gradual ascent and some steep sections. The difficulty in this trail is the surface, as the majority of the time you are walking on volcanic rocks that make your footing uneven and it does wear you out. I hiked in Chaco sandals and was ok, but I'm used to it. I highly recommend wearing comfortable shoes. I also suggest getting an early start, before 8am. Because it's the most gradual ascent, this is also a busy trail with hikers constantly going both directions. Bring snacks and plenty of water. There is a re-filling spring water station a bit more than half way to the peak. Highly recommend if you are an outdoorsy person and can handle long walks/hikes.
It was nice place but I did not find it as the 7 new nature wonders of the world. Also it was too crowded. lots of tourists made the area very noisy and all the scenic views were blocked with people

We did this hike by end of March 2014. The first part is indeed a kind of forest walk. Half way we were indeed surprised to see some snow on the hills and later on lots of snow on the path, Since we did not have those clampons it was pretty tough. At the 2nd shelter we did indeed buy those clampons whereafter the hike was more easy to do. The view from top was not that good due to the upcoming mist. We were amazed though to see so many RAVENS waiting for food.

I took Gwanuemsa trail up and down with Seongpanak. I find that there is nothing much to see from this trail as most of the pathways are rocky pathways with trees all around. There are 2 stations which provide toilet facilities, and one at the higher level sells called jindaraebal shelter also sells food and crampon. If you are coming in winter, do check the weather. If the pathways are filled with snow, it is better to bring along the crampon as the path will be really slippery.

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. The Gwamneumba trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre.. And not to mention the fattest and most active flies inside and outside the cubicle..We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa. Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved. Yes it is a mountain, and I hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan which did not put me through the physical pain without much reward that hallasan did. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope!Enjoy!

My wife and I ascended Mount Hallasan in April. While it was cool in the morning, we soon had to tie our sweatshirts around our waist. We weren't sweating as much but we're winded trekking 9.6 kms. While that distance may seem daunting, the Seonpanak trail was not too difficult, even for non-trekkers like us. There are steps and wooden walkways but in parts you have to tread carefully as it gets rocky. The difficulty level steadily increases as you move upwards. But if you take little breaks and keep proceeding, your effort will be rewarded with breath taking views from the peak. Well, the Crater lake didn't match our expectations or the pictures we saw online as it had dried up. However, we were well above the cloud level and there were green and brown hills as far as the eye could see. A word of caution - there are no sources of water on the way up (although it says there's portable water at the half point) and no shops once you start the trek. So carry energy drinks and bars, at least 3-4 big bottles of water (per person) and Jeju oranges. You can get all this from the shop at the base, at the start of the trail. Go on, enjoy your trek and discover pine trees, maples trees, black Chipmunks and much more

I went there too late so I cannot reach the top of the mountain. This route is 9 km and the walkway was pretty bad because it's all lava rock and it's raining before. We have to reach the shelter at 6 km by 12.30 but we can't so we had to go back when we reached the first shelter. I think you should try other route if you have a little time like me.

This was defiantly a must do event for Jeju! We thought it would be easier than it was. Towards the top it gets very steep and with all the snow and ice it can be quite challenging, especially since we were only wearing regular footwear and no crampons or even hiking shoes!We made it and 3 days later our legs still hurt but was worth the struggle! It took us 3.5 hours each way including stops but not including the time at the very top, which was almost an hour. So 8 hours total!

Hike this 19.2km return path *9.6km one way on a rainy and cloudy day is definitely an unforgettable experience. Rocky paths have turn into flowing streams. Took  9 hours non stop to reach the peak and return. Thick fog on the peak most of the time and only manage to get a glance at the lake. Great sense of achievement when reaching the top

Living in Hong Kong we're pretty used to tough hikes - this one is a little difficult but manageable for anyone who is reasonably fit or has some hiking experience. Whilst the incline on this hike is never that steep and the first part of the trail is easy with paved walkways, the terrain for the second half is pretty hard going with lots of rocks and boulders. We managed in trainers but hiking boots with a sturdy sole would probably be better, and some may feel more comfortable with poles. But it's ABSOLUTELY worth the effort for the view. The crater lake is quite impressive but more stunning is if you look back on Jeju from above the clouds. Took us about 6.5 hours up and down but bring plenty of snacks as there is only one point where you can buy water and some dubious looking packet noodles. Oh and there are no bins so bring a bag for your rubbish. If you are in Jeju and like hiking, you must do this as it's a great sense of achievement when you can say you've hiked S Korea's highest peak!

If you're unfit like me, please be mentally and physically prepared before embarking on this "hike", 4-5 hours upwards, another 4-5 hours downwards. The view at the top is great but that highly depends on the weather. Don't be surprised to see many elderly Koreans in their 50s or 60s even at the peak. And oh yes, please bring along good hiking shoes for this trip, it will definitely help you a lot.

This hike will make a great day trip. Make sure to leave early as you're likely to spend a couple of hours on the mountain, either walking/climbing or admiring the view. Wear proper hiking boots/shoes and layers of clothes. Bring sufficient water. Toilets are very clean.

just a well maintained hill track. More like a plantation than a forest though we spotted a deer. Crowded with people going in a hurry to complete a formality. No great scenes on this trail.of course we did upto Sara Oreum only. May be the other difficult trails must be having better sceneries. If you want to go to summit better start early say by 8 am since there is no permission beyond the upper shelter after 12 noon. Not good for someone with weak knees. Avoid on rainly or cloudy days.

This trail takes about 2 hours to get to the top, if you walk fast you could do it faster. It is uneventful and going to the top the first 70% you can only see trees. At the top there was too much fog/pollution so you could only see the crater, which had almost no water in it. There are stairs and wooden platforms so it is more like taking a simple stroll through the woods at a bit of an incline.

A relaxing trail with picturesque scenery. I went during autumn and the climate was just right. The leaves turning brown was a breathtaking sight and if you're lucky, you will be able to catch a glimpse of deers along the trails.Do be careful along the steep slopes during certain parts of the trail as a missed step could result in some pain. There are water points on the trail though located a substantial distance from each other. Do bring your own food or you can buy it from a store near the summit. Bear in mind that you will have to bring along your trash and don't leave it on the mountain! (Bring along extra trash bags!)

We climbed Seongpanak Trail on the Saturday of a 3-day weekend and it was crowded as hell. On the way up it didn't feel like a hike but more like a line of people marching. It was not a huge deal for me. I've never seen a mountain for hiking so well equipped. There were 2 rest areas, one about a fourth of the way up and another 3/4 of the way up. The one 3/4 of the way up is where many people have their lunch and can buy snacks/ramen (less windy). The toilets are horrendous and I had to tie a scarf around my face but it was so strong. About halfway up a mountain you can take a left and for a 20 min walk in & out you can see a nice lake (it may be foggy).This was DEFINITELY a worthwhile experience. The hike was quite easy because there were many man made walkways. When you are approaching the summit it can be very windy. I had to grab the rope a few times to prevent myself from being blown away (I am only about 50kg). We went in October so it may be less windy and cold in the summer months. The clouds move quickly so we were able to see and take many great pictures. Please do this if you enjoy hiking and want to stand among the clouds!

Highest mountain in Korea.  Beautiful area.  The wife and I went in midweek hoping to beat the crowds.  Forget it.  masses of cars, buses and people.  At 10 am on a weekday we sat in a line of cars for approx. 80 minutes just to get a place to park.  Once in, the hike was pretty strenuous.  Bring a hat and sunscreen.  We got approx. 2/3 of the way up (in a horde of people) before the park employees turned everyone back saying there was a "big wind coming".  It was a nice sunny day and no visible weather to be seen.  Oh well.  I will probably try again when I come back.  But I will be sure and get here at daybreak and try to beat the crowds.

I don't know why people get surprised about the length of the walk or about the presence of rocky steps to get to the top of the mountain:if you're not trained stay at home!! You can easily get info on the web about the trails,so don't complaint! The trip is hard,but only from a physical point of view,not technically. We took the Seogpanak trail:19 km round trip but it's worth it. Unfortunately at the top it was cloudy but I'm sure that with clean sky it's spectacular! Btw,I think that stairs are more than rocky steps.

took our family of 3 about 11hrs round trip. it can be done in 9 if you ha e the right gear and move fast. its gradual grade, so its not strenuous but the terrian is terrible. it is 85percent big rocky jagged lava chunks. if you are prone to ankle injury, this hike is not for u. you have to watch your feetthe whole time  which is fine since there is no view until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. so all in all i do not really recommend this hike unless you have lots of time in Jeju and you really wanna say you climbed Koreas highest peak.

After nearly two years spent in Korea, I can quite easily say that Hallasan is the most beautiful place I've visited while here. Dramatic scenery, including sprawling vistas and interactive cloud-cover made this an exhilarating climb. Don't expect an easy journey! I took the "easiest" trail and it took us a good 5 hours to complete, and the hike up the mountain itself was via a crowded and steep staircase.The sheer variety of landscapes you experience as you climb up is really impressive. When you reach the mid-point, there's a rest stop where you can buy water, coffee and ramen noodles (oh, Korea!), but bring your own snacks because you'll probably be up there for a while.

Jeju Stone Park is a vast area with everything stone related.  With Jeju being a volcanic island, the lava stones are everywhere from the Harubang statues to the walls surrounding houses.  The park is divided into three courses which would take about an hour each at a leisurely pace.  The first course has mostly rock statues (including the Harubang statues) that most likely had some religious significance.  The second course shows how the rocks were used for more practical purposes (tombstones, tools, housing, etc) through the different eras of Korean history.  The third course specifically shows the different Jeju style housing made with mostly the volcanic rock walls.  It s probably not the best place to be in the middle of heat in the summer but when the weather is nice, it s a fantastic spot to spend a few hours.
Beautiful, haunting, natural. An absolute must if you're based in Jeju city (can be accessed via the city tour bus) and is amazing value for money (just 1,500 won). A definite must.

We were coming from Hamdeok Beach to the Jeongbang water falls and happened to directly pass by this place on the highway and I remembered it was one of the top places to visit in Jeju so we decided to pull over and enter.  We're very glad we did.  We spent about an hour there but you could easily spend more time.  It was awesome to see all the man made stone statues and their significance or their meaning, one of the main ones  being the mother who had 500 sons.  The museums were pretty cool as well and you could learn a ton of geography.  The setting was very picturesque with Mt. Halla in the background and the surroundings looking like you were sort of in a savanah.  We took some awesome photographs and learned a lot of information.  I think if you're able to rent a car and drive there it's a must see in Jeju.

I am not able to visit this park because of the bus. We went to the airport by bus in order to take the 131 bus for the park. To confirm this info from our hotel receptionist, we asked the airport tourist info counter. Correct, and we were directed to gate 1 and begun to wait for the bus. We missed the 1240 so we decided to wait for the 1340. The bus didn't come until 1400 and we went to double check with the info counter. Then we were told that 1340 is for the number 132, which is grouped together with 131. 132 doesn't head for Jeju stone park and we were told to wait for the 1530 bus. Isn't it amazing our bus waiting experience? I am sharing this as a gentle reminder for all. Plan your bus schedule properly especially for venues outside the city. Cheers

From Segiowipo (Jangung rotary) the park can be reached in a little over an hour on the 231 bus which will drop you at the front of the park.   Fare 1200krw. Park admission is 5000krw. I spent 2.5 hrs here doing course 1 and 2. I think you might enjoy it more if you were an artist but I liked it all the same. The stone museum, which is the first stop on course 1 tells you all about how lava rocks are formed, their different types and would be a geologists dream. After that you'll walk around the park and see the different stone sculptures, most of which are natural,  some manmade. There are also a couple of replica traditional jeju houses and local pottery too. The Obaek gallery has some driftwood on display along with 1 hall of art but it is mostly empty. I thought there would be more info on the local traditions and how they lived but the park is still a work in progress. Its not due for completion until 2020. Rug up because it seems to be colder here than other areas of the island and you will be outside most of your visit. Recommend you go on a sunny day as this area gets very heavy fog too.

The initial part was fine. There are 3 routes within the park. Route 1 was ok. Route 2 was getting creepier as one approached further into the route. What they didn't tell you is that this is a graveyard from the ancient times and we were walking around the graves.

There are lot of naturally formed stones from volcano eruption. There is also a museum where they teach and share about volcano eruption and a nice place to take pictures with the stones where they have arranged it nicely.

I quite enjoyed this place. It takes a while to walk around so don't go if you are in a hurry. If you take your time there is plenty to see, ancient tombs, traditional housing/tools, stone statues, giant stone towers, etc. The museum was also good and I learnt a bit about volcanic rock formation that I hadn't seen before.
Great place to see and explore.... Highly recommend. Beautiful place with many great outdoor sights to see. Also an indoor museum of rocks but not as interesting as outside.

It was such a pain to get to but I loved the Stone Park. The main reason was to see the Dol hareubangs - the stone sculptures which represent Jeju. There was information about the mythology surrounding the formation of Jeju which was at times mind-boggling and contradictory. There are different routes around the park and there is an indoor exhibition which features the volcanic rocks and Jeju's origins as a volcanic island. I preferred the outdoor sections where the use of stone in Jeju was highlighted - used in things such as tombs/ shrines, walls, icons of spiritual beliefs etc. The largest sculptures are near the exit and the Dol hareubangs were awesome. They all had slightly different expressions and quirks which was cool. There are plans to expand the museum grounds and I would defo like to go back again in future. It was quite quiet when we were there and we only saw a few people except for a group on a guided tour at the end. Such a shame there are not more visitors but good for those who made the effort. Recommended visit in Jeju!

My husband and I went to the Jeju Stone Park to see the guardian statues (Jeju stone heads) but found the park to be so much more than that.  It's a large park (and they are still enlarging it) with an emphasis on nature.  The museum and historic buildings are interesting but walking around the grounds was the high point.  Rocks in their natural shapes are placed throughout the grounds and if you are quiet and observant, the connection to nature just seeps to your being.  We found the place strangely intriguing, calming, and uplifting.
Nice walk around to see different carvings of stones which we took lots of picture with. Not spectacular, but nice to see. There is a small entrance fee.

I got the bus here from Jungmun - a couple of hours in total but it was worth it. Really good value, lots to look at, peaceful place to walk around, beautifully done and looked after. There weren't many other people there so it felt as if I had the place to myself. I had lunch in the restaurant and that was also good. Make sure you take your camera. Hugely recommended.

We went to the park by a convenient bus form jejy city. If you are a scientific or a stone-lover, this is the place to go !!If this is not the case (as it was for me), I would also recomment the park as you have a few impressive stones !

This is the place you must visit if you want to understand why stones especially volcano rocks are so important to the people of Jeju. This place provides all the history about Jeju Culture as well as nice scenery for photo-shoot. The place is well-kept and huge. But, the trail is nice to walk with lovely autumn weather. Admission is only krw5000. Take bus 720 from intercity bus terminal.

Jeju stone park was rated A by Korea Ministry of Culture and Tourism, in recognition that this park is excellent in term of its specialization in the theme of stone, differentiation from other facilities, and characteristics relating to mythology and the life of the people in the region.Get the map at the entrance and follow guided park course. Don't miss out the Jeju stone museum to know how the formation of Jeju Island. After a short nice walk from the entrance,the museum is just located in the basement of a building opposite the Sky Pond. Follow the map to look for Jeju traditional village with thatched roof houses. Before at the end of course, drop by the unique Gallery in the park which you may find artworks of domestic and foreign artists.It is indeed best travel Korea during Autum because even though it was sunny day, but the breeze was so cooling and the air was very refreshing. It is a museum as well as an ecological park. It is a very remarkable cultural park which sublimating nature in art ,really very fantastic.

i went here in heavy rain. not much to see. but im having good time here with my friends. there are a lot of stones sculpture here. and also theres a museum regarding jeju.the museum tell us about types of stone. and the jeju itself formed by the volcanic activity happened before this.

A must see really - seems a bit underrated. Almost no people when i went. Take a gorgeous stroll through the park to see different lava stones. Get educated about the geological activity. See some traditional houses.

This is a pretty big park that has a little bit of everything from history folklore and stones.  I had to convince my friends to check it out and only won when i told them it was like 15 minutes from where we were staying.  However they both were quiet happy with the decision since it was empty and just a lovely walk through nature with some great smells.  Even the trash cans are made out od stone pits.  I thought we would only go for like 30 minutes but ended up being there for an hour and a half.  Other bonus is that for the month of may there is no entrance fee!

It's been several years since we have been but I can't stop talking about this place. Definitely worth the stop weather it's for half the day or half an hour a walk around this place will not disappoint the outdoor enthusiast or even the person who likes a causal stroll around a park. There are many different things to check out. All around an amazing site.

Half science, half art. A museum dedicated to the formation of the igneous rocks in the area, tectonic plate movements, volcanic eruptions, formation of lava tubes, and various methods of making craters. Extremely interesting!Then rock art. Lots of interesting rocks from around the island, arranged in a way that makes them just so fascinating.Budget a couple of hours here for a leisurely walk through these sections. Add a couple more hours to see the historical village section (which we didn t go into as we had seen these elsewhere already).
Jeju Stone Park is interesting. There are lots of great spots for photos and there are also lots of stone exhibits which infuses some aspects of history, culture and art.
Definitely you need to visit this Stone Park so you could understand how Jeju people develop. Very nice place to visit.

we took some interesting shots. cool place to spend some time outdoors, it's not too big and easy to walk around. definitely worth going there!! in fact, we thought this was pretty much the most interesting thing in Jeju

Built on a reclaimed land-fill site, this vast area of pathways, statues, displays, museums and traditional villages is very worth a visit if on Jeju. From the impressive stone structures and flat basalt 'floor' at the entrance of the park, I was blown away by the vast array of statues that are displayed, explained and on show in this area. There is ample car parking that is only a short walk form the entry way. A small fee is required and then you are free to wander the area that included a massive and spectacular 2 store (below ground) museum that outlines the geographic development of Jeju along with many interactive displays, a short film with subtitles, examples and galleries of 'stone art'. A gift shop of course, provided a range of traditional and specific items and there are amenities spread throughout the part. Water features, a traditional village, an art gallery and a vast array of stone sculpture will give you hours of things to view and read as you wander through the park In my humble opinion, not to be missed!!!

You can easily spend 2 or 3 hours walking around the stones and getting to know the  past lifestyle of the island population as well as the geological history of Jeju. Volcanic rocks are exposed as real art pieces in a museum, allowing you to have a different look at them and admire the work of nature.
This is an unexpected indoor/outdoor museum. To be visited on sunny day. This museum depicts the stone culture of Jeju island with lots of interesting structures. It is entertaining for the kids.
This is an amazing collection of natural and men made stones in Jeju. In addition it has an outstanding water instillation and an indoor unique museum. Truly worth the visit

this is a very interesting park, they have at least 3 sections; a museum, 2 parks and smaller exhibits. If you like stones and interested in how they are formed and how they look like and appreciate by the people of the past and present, do visit. some stones have interesting tales like: Goddess and her 500 Sons. The whole park is pretty big, it can take up to more than 3 hours if you go through all the writings and descriptions. do go after a meal.

We agreed that visiting the Jeju Stone Park in the snow was one of the most enjoyable experiences we have had in Korea. The stones, sculptures, houses and other artefacts, as well as the lovely walks are beautiful in the snow. It also meant only a few people were visiting, so it was very peaceful and serene. The museum was excellent, very educational, and we really appreciated how the different lava types were displayed as sculptures. They are beautiful, nature s art!

We travelled using the Jeju City tour bus and stopped here after visiting Jeomul Natural Recreation forest . There were other stops but we did not get down to visit the other places due to time constraints. Initially, we planned to only visit for an hour but the park was surprising large and interesting and we ended up spending over 2 hours here.  It was time well spent.  We saw lots of stone statues and products in all shapes and sizes. The displays of rocks and rock formations were scattered all over an extensive outdoor park as well as an indoor museum. You need to wear comfortable shoes, wear a hat and apply sun block. Toilets were clean and strategically located around the park and clean drinking water was available in many places.  You only need to pay a small entrance fee and it was well worth it. There was even an air-conditioned resting hut with hot/cold water and seats just outside the entrance.  In our opinion, we think this is the most interesting stop on the public tour bus circuit.  Highly recommended.

We also went to Jeju Stone Park. Easy to find and approach with car. Parking places are available but during peak season the earliy bird .....Entrance fee with 5000 Won for adult and 2000 Won for child. It is a nice walking area with a lot of big and small stones. Dont forget your camera to bring. Inside there is also a huge museum with history of vulcano eruptions and of course with history of Jeju. Mainly in Korean but it it is definetly worth to visit. It is a very nice place and we would come back again.

Visited the Park based on TA reviews. Extremely well done with extensive museums and stone displays. Allow at least 3-4 hours for the visit. Enormous work has gone into the development of the Park. Should be in the Top 5 attractions in Jeju outside the beaches.
beautiful park with small huts with various traditional items in.  Stone grandfathers are the best bit.  Lovely receptionist called us a taxi after our visit.

Rocks & stones everywhere.  Beautiful landscape.  There are nice traditional houses in the park.  No need to go to the museum which is quite far in.  Just explore the area near the entrance, see the traditional house, go straight to the exit area.  Lots aboriginal statues near the exit.  Statues are like those found on Easter Island.
This is a strange wonderful mystical place. A work of art on a grand scale, a hommage to the volcanic, mineral nature of this island, and also to its ancient gods.

A great place to learn about history and culture of Jeju. Stone museum is a must-see for those who are interested in geology. Views of the Sky Pond reflecting nearby mountain are fascinating. There is a small traditional village. You can borrow an audio guide at the ticket office for free.
it is a good place that you can learn about their history of Jeju. Jeju is formed into beautiful islands because of many rocks around it.

Most of the park is outdoors, and we went when it was raining, so that wasn't that good. But the place is beautiful, with trees and stones lined up. There's also a museum about volcanoes as well as statues of historical figures. Very nice place although it is only accessible by car and very difficult to get a cab.

We got a local bus to this park. When we went there it was quite windy so take a sweater.The park is very large with lots of stones to see. There is no cafe so take water or food. It is really worth the visit.
Initially we weren't sure what to expect here but it is a very pleasant park but you will need around 1.5 hours to complete the whole circuit.  Worth a look.

This is the best stone exhibit on Jeju island.  And the best part of that is the museum itself.  There are many, many very interesting stones shapes, all collected from Jeju (I think).  If you like geology, there's a great explanation of lava types, stone formations, lava tubes, etc.  Also there is a nice drift-wood display with very unusual, artistic shapes.  Outside, there are many carved stone artifacts used by Jeju islanders from ages past.  The Obaek Jang-Goon Gallery has a nice drift-wood display in the basement.  Park is big, but except for the museums, just a walk-through is enough.  I spent 2 hours in the museums -- the best part!

Stone park is a must see one. It has big outdoor. There are a lot of big stone shapes. This park is good for natural lovers, people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. Near this place, miniature park and Eco land are there. All these 3 places can be seen in one day.   So book a taxi for these 3 places.  My Taxi driver charged me 90,000 KRW for 11 AM to 6 PM.  Bus doesn't come frequently to these places.
just do the first route and get out unless you want to endless tombstones. dont miss the sky pond though.

This is an amazing place. The museum is absolutely first rate. All the exhibits have explanations in perfect English.  There are lots of interactive displays. If you are interested in the geology of Jeju you should come here first and expect to spend several hours. Outdoors there are 3 courses (walks) with exhibits of life in old Jeju. The exhibits are well done and English signs are excellent.  This place is huge and amazingly you will have it almost to yourself. It has an entry fee of about $5. That is the bargain of the century!   Don't skip any of it. It could easily take a full day if you are intellectually and esthetically inclined. It was the best thing I did on the island. I spent only about 4 hours. I would suggest you bring food and water with you. I had a few apples and tangerines.

The grounds are HUGE! It felt like a nature forest walk, a geography and history field trip all rolled into one.I don't know if it's windy there all the time, but when we were there, it was freezing when the wind blew when we were in the shade.We had a tour guide who explained the various rock features and how/why people carved the stones for use in the past. But honestly, I was bored after awhile. This place had rocks/stones galore. Considering that there are so many other things to see/do in Jeju, I would give this place a miss.
Gimme a good information about korean people in the past. The wind were killing me! It would be better if you come not in the weather transition.

My boyfriend and I just visited the Jeju Stone Park last weekend. The park is huge with lots to see! Plan to spend a couple hours here. The history and legends are so interesting and the sights are really gorgeous around the park. We took a taxi from Hamdeok Beach but were able to catch the bus very easily back to Jeju City for only 1,000 won. The only thing I'd suggest is making sure to eat before you get here or bringing food! They have a restaurant but it's closed and looks like it will be for a while. Other than that, really great park!
Beautiful "Stone Grandpa" displays in multiple setting. A nice walk around the park and also learn about the local culture and history.

This place exceeded my expectations, it is definitely a highlight of Jeju, it is perfectly organized to be a journey itself. We spent around 3 hours walking around ( it has 3 different routes well explained in the map) and simply feeling the nature was already healing. The entrance is 6.000 Korean won per person. They have drinking fountains and toilets inside. You can reach it by bus!

Jeju stone park was not part of the regular sightseeing itineraries and do we opted for a customized private tour to visit Jeju stone park. Requires atleast 3 to 4 hours if you want to walk along the trails to cover entire area. A visit inside the museum to understand the volcanic activities and formations will help in understanding the nature of the island better. Good to go with a local guide. Interesting statues and rock formations

Massive ground. A full walk about will take 2hrs easily. Even though all the stones look similar after an hr, it's a very effective way to understand the folklores of Jeju. Cheap entrance fee of only 2K won.Some places near the museum are still under renovation when we were there.

The Park is quite a distance away from other major sights but it is different in that the star attraction are those "grandfather stone sculptures".Be prepared for lots of walking on easy trails.  There are small pebbles everywhere so do watch the kids and carefully navigate those wheelchairs and baby strollers.The underground museum near next to the water reservoir/water sculpture is definitely for those interested in geology.  It is a good place to take a break and use the restrooms as there is another set of lavatories near the car park.

We were staying in the Seogwipo area (near the International Convention Center), so it took us about an hour by bus to get to the Stone Park. It was interesting, with some unususal lava formations, but the drizzling rain didn't help in enjoying the scenery. The "museum" is OK, but nothing spectacular. When you (if) select a sunny day!

Hi all!, we visited this place on 1 July, 2017. It is indeed a good place. when you are almost fatigued with seeing big big places such as Seopjikoji, Seongsan sunrise peak, you can visit this place while returning to Jeju si. the entrance is really amazing. Lots of tall and large stones will welcome you. We took lots of pictures there.  There are different carvings of stones of different types. There is a gallray of stone-made sculptures. We also noticed a nice water reservior type of thing. Really nice place.
An outdoor gallery of stone sculptures. You can find a lot of Jeju stone icon, as they call it "Grandpa Stone".  The park is very large,  and not many visitors.  An interesting place worth visiting .
Not worth the entrance fee and time spent at the park. Unless you really have no other attraction sites to visit.

We're her during the off season. This was a great Museum for a cold day- on the inside. The outside was beautiful and would have been great to explore on a warmer day. Loved the lifestyle displays of ancient Korean life (kitchen, agriculture).
This was a very relaxing walk, not strenuous and  a good place to take lots of pictures.  I enjoyed it immensely.
Juju is a volcanic island. From pre-history it's peoples worked the stone. The park concentrates, in a beautiful setting, works from all periods.Free entrance for senior citizens (over 64)

So, one might think that this is a great place to see artifacts or historic pieces, but as far as we saw, everything was a replica. To include the replica lava tube entrances. Sigh. They couldn't even be bothered to completely thatch a straw hut- they had concrete roofs with thatch done at the top and edges. They do have quite the array of carefully placed rocks and replica stone statues, but seeing as how none of it was real (the whole thing was built on the site of a landfill) there are more real things to go do on Jeju. The price is cheap. Spend it looking at the columnar basalt on the beach. At least that is real.

Nice park and a great way to know about the history of the island.amazing grand sight of the rock formations.Rocks & stones everywhere. Beautiful landscape. There are nice traditional houses in the park.

We didnt expect much from this park but was taken in by the amazing grand sight of the rock formations. There is also an interesting folk tale behind these formations. The scenery was beautiful and there was many small trails to explore within the park.

You might think a stone park is boring. But it turns out not quite right a statement. Not too many people visit it. You can enjoy 3 different routes. Very calm area with increadible examples of what the nature can present.

I find it as an average, nothing special ... better to walk around outside the stone park,the surrounding is quite nice with traditional hall nice traditional look toilet (no hot water, water is icey cold) I came last month (early May)
A must visit in Jeju. Nice park and a great way to know about the history of the island. I joined a tour to visit this place as it is more convenient to travel privately than the public transport.
Definitely a lot of stones on this island! Discovered and are displayed and arranged beautifully. Thanks to Korean holiday week, our visit was free of charge.

This is a big area in the outskirts of Jeju city, need to car to get there. There are many stone formations around the park and there is story of an old grandmother who had 500 kids and was finally cooked in the porridge and the kids ate her as they didnt know. There is a nice stone museum that explains how rock formation on Jeju is formed and all about volcanic activities and some weird looking rocks. Educational place for kids!
Great place to visit on Jeju. We loved the path 2 at the village part. But actually  all of it was amazing.

It is definitely a park full of stones, but it is actually quite interesting.  There is also a museum in the park which is worth checking out.  It shows some of the history of the island and the different types of volcanic rocks that can be found on the island. If you aren't interested in parks or rocks this probably isn't a place you would enjoy, but my husband and I really enjoyed it.  Naturally shaped rock sculptures, carved rock sculptures, stacked rock sculptures, etc.

Jeju has a park or a museum for just about everything. And so it is with Jeju Stone Park. It does have some interesting rocks.You know, some people think that Halla san is the volcano on Jeju. But, really the whole island is a volcano. If the volcano erupts again you will not have to worry too much about the lava flowing from Halla san because lava will be flowing from every little mountain on the island, which a lot of them are closer to where you live than Halla san. So, just about anywhere on Jeju you can find interesting rocks.especially along the coast. Even though it would be a nice walk around the park, you can just look out your window to see interesting rocks you don't necessarily have to go to the Stone Park. But, if you don't have anything to do and want to spend the day outside and see part of Jeju along the way, Jeju Stone Park might be a good way to spent the day.
The museum is excellent. you get to understand how Jeju island is formed and the geothermal activities.The ground itself is hugh. It takes about 1-2 hours stroll.It is cold and windy in Dec.
Plenty to see here including traditional houses, a museum and plenty of... stones. Nothing special but a nice place to enjoy a walk.
We've been here on a cloudy day which gave a nice touch.It's a pretty wal trough the park and they show as well some old korean buildings.It's more nature than the eco park next to it...

Beautiful scene to be seen. Very natural. 20,000 stones of different verities. Natural as traditional village houses in India. Toilet facilities are everywhere. Very clean. Dogs and cats are not allowed.Water fountain is there. very good place for peace, health and meditation.Thanks.
Spectacular. Jeju is known for it's coastline, but Jeju Stone Park in the interior is an absolute must-see.Words can not do it justice. Just see it.
rockbig stonevery good art jobthere are artficila lake made by bronzewow~

I loved this seemingly unassuming place that I would have never really thought of visiting.  It was one of the most interesting and beautiful places I visited in Jejudo Island.  It is definitely a "must do", as they say in Disney World!  We would have loved to spend more time there.  It's not just a park with a bunch of rocks so don't miss out!  It's like a natural museum/art gallery of indigenous Jejudo volcanic rocks with a splash of the island's history.  Highly recommended to spend a minimum of 3-4 hours here!!

My rating for this may be a bit harsh as I really don't know what I expected of this. It is quite literally dedicated to stones/rocks. The museum is quite a stark architectural building reminiscent of cold war Russia, flat and straight lines and all concrete. Having said that there are some really informative exhibits on the tectonic shifts and volcanoes and this general area of geology so if I had an interest I would have scored more highly.It was an experience and I was glad I did it but it's not for all.

This place is huge!If you like nature, do visit Jeju Stone Park.  The English audio guide was excellent.  The exhibits were really interesting.  There were indoor and outdoor exhibits.  Do be selective if you have limited time.  One could easily spend up to half a day at this place.As we were a bit short on time, we browsed through the indoor museum rather quickly and still managed to pick up some interesting information.The outdoor areas were really nice and comfortable.  When we were there, the weather was cool and nice and we really had a good time walking around admiring the stones. It is a park that combines nature and art.  We like it a lot.

This museum is interesting if you have the keen interest in geology & history of jeju volcanic past. The entire park is very well maintained and its advisable to bring an umbrella if you're those who can't really take the sunlight.For couples who would just want to take a quiet stroll, this place is strongly recommended as crowds here are lesser as compare to other tourist attraction in jeju.

You want to know about volcanoes? This is the place. The museum is interactive and informative. And not to mention it houses some of the most beautiful natural volcanic sculptures around. There are three courses to follow in order to see what the park has to offer - taking things at a leisurely pace, this can easily take 3 hours to complete. It is well worth it though - with the some of the paths in course two taking on an enchanted forest appeal. The entrance is 5000 won, and you can get to the park on the Jeju City Tour Bus. The stops are just outside the park. A good poncho will serve better during rainy weather than an umbrella here, as there are parts of the course with low lying foliage (and the wind can be a little ferocious at times too).

The museum is quite interesting if you're interested in geology.  It's nice to get a decent scientific understanding of how and why the other things you'll likely be seeing on Jeju (Hallasan, Seongsan Ilchulbong, etc.) are the way they are.  If geology bores the heck out of you, then skip the museum, but don't skip the park altogether.  It's really quite a beautiful place to walk around, especially if you're in the mood for something somewhat quiet and relaxing.  Major crowds can make some of the the other sites on Jeju quite the opposite of that, so it's nice to find a place that's legitimately peaceful.

What a GREAT place to spend the day. Entry was $5 and I did not expect much. We intended to spend 30 minutes here but ended up spending most of the day. Take a picnic and bottle of wine and enjoy the serenity of the park. For a full video review of this place check out my YouTube clip https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LlgzW0VCQHw

Admission fee: 5000 won each.Went during Feb 14 which is winter. It was snowing where we were there and everything was covered with snow!The whole park is really huge! If you want to walk slowly and understand everything, it might take 2 hours or so. Most of the signboards are covered with icing and snow and we couldnt read it at all to understand.Of the whole time that we were there, we see no one at all until the end, we saw 1 person. After reading the reviews i was a bit reluctant about visiting the park but i am glad i did. For only ~$5 this is a nice park to spend a few hours if you want to slow it down and be in nature.

Entrance fee 5,000 won and free for senior and disable as this place is not wheelchair friendly. Thank God my aunt could walk a little so those part that cannot be pushed on wheels.... she had to walk slowly..

Jeju Stone Park exceeded our expectations.  So much space and everything well laid out.  The museum was particularly interesting with some absolutely amazing pieces of lava, and microscopes set-up, which my 9-year old Daughter loved.  They also had an interesting photography exhibition (temporary).  If you are a geologist and/or simply interested in volcanoes and rocks, then you will probably spend all day here.  Appreciated the water machines everywhere but the restaurant was closed (just in case you are hungry).  We all enjoyed it immensely.  Children less than 12 are free and adults are KRW 5000 (very reasonable).

Keep in mind, the founder, Paek Uncheol, is quoted " Visiting the park is intended to be a journey through the mythology of the island, entering through the ear of Seolmundae*, progressing through the body and exiting at the feet. It represents the journey of life and death.  Taking a journey that ends in death, even if it is a metaphoric (mythical, mystical, mind-boggling) death, may not appeal to everyone, but it could be transformative if you're open to it. Allow for hours of contemplating stones, thousands, tens of thousands, of stones, natural, carved, authentic, replicas - millstones, mortars, volcanic bombs, boundary markers, 2000 ceramic jars, fossilized tree roots - locals thought its creator, who collected these stones for forty years, had gone mad. Three courses to follow, each taking one to two hours. *Seolmundae Halmang, the grandmother of Jeju Island.
We spent over 3 hours in the park and exhibition building.Gives you a perfect view on the history and evolution of mother earth. We really enjoyed and learned a lot.

The park is a unique in the sense that it is dedicated to stones in Jeju culture. Lots of statues, pavilion with the history of volcanic activity, some traditional houses, old sculptures, big and small. Large space, a lot of walking.

This attraction would be hard to describe. A huge park with magnificent exhibits of boulders and rocks. The park was so silent but the exhibits made their statements loud and clear.  An enjoyable afternoon just to immerse in the natural beauty of something as common as rocks, pebbles and such. Who would have imagined that such an outdoor exhibit could offer so much. There s even a mothers  nursing room within the park itself.

I traveled in early December and sea side wasn't a priority, and then I found this park. The monuments you are going to see at all kinds of markets of Jeju all come from this park. I have ever seen best museum .. design of museum is really has deep sense of existence .. stone s story and Jeju story are melted in the same pot.. enviromental style is exiciting.. authum s color bring good sense.. I exactly advice..
Nice stone formation and park. It maybe very hot during summer time. But worth a visit. I went there via public bus and you can also visit ecoland just across the street

It is a museum as well as an ecological park related to stone culture in the lives of Jeju people.  It is huge and you are required to walk a lot.  It is about 40-45 minutes drive either from Jeju Airport or Seogwipo area.  You need 1-2 hours to go around the complex and the museum.  Opening hours: 0900-1800 hrs.  Closed on first Monday of the month unless it is a holiday.  Entry fee: KRW 5,000.  It should be a MUST in your itinerary of Jeju Island.

The park is big and have many to see, especially for people who don't know the culture of Jeju. It would be also good for family but since it requires lots of walks I wouldn't recommend elder people who can't walk for a long time. The weather of the day we went wasn't quite good, but the drizzle and fog made that place more mysterious which is quite special because we saw different type of scenery from those pictures you can find from the Internet.
One may think that stones and rocks are boring, but not at Jeju Stone Park!It is fascinating to learn about how Jeju is geologically formed and see these amazing sculptures.
My six (6) year old son's imagination could really run wild here. We had a blast, plan for a 1/2 day. Chicken place across the street for the hungry.

The park covers a vast area. One has to decide how far you wish to explore and watch your time. A map is given at the ticket counter and we did not expect it to be so big. There are scripts on stones to tell you about the legendary story of this stone park.
