It is a quite tough for elderly to walk to the place in order to take great pictures (the usual spot that tourists will take pic). It is so windy and nice actually. You can see how the locals get the fresh seafood from the sea and consume it. Thou it is very fresh but I am not a fan of raw food hence, I pass! LOL
This is really amazing. I loved the view. The place is well taken care of. The walk is of moderate intensity. We had wonderful weather. Recommend this place

While it is not the only waterfall in Asia that falls into the sea as many think (I've seen them both in Indonesia and Philippines), it is definitely a cool waterfall to see and they are relatively rare. I would definitely recommend seeing this waterfall first if you're planning to check out all of the waterfalls on Jeju. It is very accessible and a great viewing experience.
This is my second times visit, the water fall still strong and powerful. Feel the fresh of the fresh water from waterfall while enjoying the breeze from the salt water. Amazing place to revisit.
About 5mins down the long flight of stairs and you get upclose with the waterfall. Helpful to come with proper shoes as you can walk closer the the waterfall on the rocks to get a good photo.
Jeongbang waterfall has water flowing into the open sea. One of Jeju 7 wonder on the island . Ladies divers for oysters to sell as fresh seafood .
Love this place! Admission is 2000won per adult and parking lots are available.  Glad that the weather was good!
Short visit but the scene is beautiful. Steep climb is not recommended for old folks though. Really like the waterfall that goes into the ocean!

This waterfall lies in the southern part of the island, specifically in Seogwipo. Pay an entry fee of 2000 KRW and you can experience it up close for some photo-opportunity but just remember to wear a good air of shoes and be very careful when walking around or climbing over large rocks for a closer feel of the cool breeze. It's worth the trip.

I think this is the better of the two main waterfalls in the area.  It is more natural and a little less touristy. There is a second waterfall shown on the map around 1km along the coast path but this is not worth going to.
This scenery of falling water is really very amazing. An appropriate place for photography. There are many other beautiful places near it.
2000won per adult. A 3min walk down the stairs and you'll reach the waterfall. Love the weather and sun during autumn.
Good photo opportunity. Visit during high tide to see majestic falls flowing into the ocean.Visit during rainy season to see more water crashing down.

We saw many people taking photos around the waterfall. It's not the tallest nor grandest waterfall so I'm not sure what's the fuss about.Entrance fee is only 2K/pax. It's a short climb back up from the waterfall, ie very suitable for family and elderly.The rocks around the waterfall are rather pointed so please watch out while taking your selfies.
Entry fee equal to USD 1.50Nice waterfall. A lot of tourist though. Nice for short photo stop. Must climb stair.

The entrance fee was 2000 W per head and 1000W per car . After buying the tickets , you descend about 5-6 flights of stairs onto the base of the waterfall . There you can clammer on the rocks for better photos of the waterfall or catch the sea waves crashing upon the rocks . After which you climb back up and then one can see stalls selling iced water with ice .The stalls also sold orange juice and ice-cream. Overall expect to spend about 45!minutes here .

This place is a must go place. It's a picturesque place for photos and videos. It's quite a small place for many tourist. Lucky for us, we went as early as 8am, we managed to escape the swamp of other tourists.

I ve visited many waterfalls during my travels but this one is unique as it is not located within a lagoon or by a river or along a forest but this is one that goes out to the ocean!! A unique experience for me :)Definitely no swimming here but you can actually walk up close to the foot of the waterfalls for pictures and such. Wear comfortable shoes as there is a significant amount of steps to climb up and down.

Beautiful waterfall near the ocean. The water is icy cold. You can't swim in all the waterfall in jeju. Too bad as the weather very hot and I really wish can dip inside here to cool down my body. Entrance fee of 2000won.
Remember to go with sandel or any footwear that makes going into the water easy and comfortable.   You won't regret as the water is icy cold & refreshing under the hot sun.

With a 2,000– fee, this waterfall is well worth a visit! It's a short walk down from the parking lot - not hard to get to at all. You should, however, wear comfortable and supportive shoes because you need to balance on rocks in order to get close to the falls.

Steps down to the waterfall are well constructed and have seats along the way. It is mostly shaded on the way down if it is hot like when I went. You can see women selling abalone on the rock shore, I have tried it, because when in Rome, but I don't like the texture.There are little shops selling souvenirs, and drinks etc. There is also a tourist information point near the car park exit, and they are very helpful. You can walk to the harbour, or to the other waterfalls in the area in around 30 minutes along the seashore and there are a few gardens along the route.
it is Only waterfall in Asia falls directly to the ocean. Not that interesting, easy to walk down, a lot of kids and old people can visit.
Breathtaking waterfalls with crystal clear blue water.  The walk to the waterfalls takes you through a pathway surrounded by trees and shrubs.

Its definitely one of the most impressive waterfall I have been to. Its only a 5 mins walk from the parking lot and you see this strong waterfall. The water was nicely cool. I wish I had my bathing suit with me.  Its a small area.. we only spent like 30 mins there.
Beautiful waterfall with an amazing view - can recommend buying a drink or an icecream before going the stairs down and then chilling on the big stones

Entrance fee is 2000 won which is not that bad but again, the waterfalls are not that big. There are other falls on Jeju with greater magnitude you should consider instead unless you stay in Seogwipo as this is literally just on the outskirts of the city.
The waterfall is very close to the ticketing booth so there isn't a need to walk for a long distance to get to it. It is generally quite nice but not super impressive.

2000krw to get in.    Walk down stairs to get to a very rocky area with the waterfall coming down right next to the sea.  There was not a huge amount of water flowing down.     Some souvenir/food shops around.
This waterfall is amazing, but be careful, it's almost dry in summer!! Only negative point: we need to pay to access to it.

Very scenic place to see a pretty high waterfall flow directly into the sea!! There is an admission fee of $2000 Korean won entrance fees per Adult. Short walk from the ticket booth with steps reaching downwards to the waterfall. Interestingly if time permits, one can walk to the end of the big car park in front of the ticket office and there is an Olle trail near the sea that leads to a Castle of Shell and a smaller waterfall!
We went there in the morning. 2000krw for the entrance fee. Nice scenery view. Watch out for slippery rocks if you wanna take photos.
This was so beautiful! I went during April and there was a lot of water going down the falls. Such a picture perfect spot! I highly recommend it to all visitors.
great view of the waterfall and the sea, you can see the locals there selling crabs coconuts, oranges and other stuff like souvenirs

This waterfall is not very big as compare to other but the view is breath-taking as the water falls into the edge of the cliff at the sea front. One can feel the mist of the water fall spraying onto the face as one walk closer to the cliff of the water fall. However, be very careful while walking on the rock towards the waterfall as the rock gets more slippery as one get nearer to the waterfall. But it is definitely worth the risk and the slow walk as the pictures that comes out from the shot is gorgeous!

As my country does have lotsa waterfall, this short walk for the scene just a ok to us.  Well, the difference is since we are tourist, so we visited the place. You can skip to pay the entrance fee if you are not keen on waterfall as it can be viewed and spotted before climb down for a nearer view of it.

A short walk to these falls - low ticket price at the entrance and then about 100 steps down to the base of the falls - quite rocky and need to watch the step - fortunately we went on a day without many tourists. Could feel the refreshing cool spray, nice when in the sunshineI love the fact there s no littering here - helps maintain the natural state

We need to pay for the entrance fees but it is not that pricey and worth it. You need to take a few stairs to finally reached the waterfall area. The view is very sceneric and worth to take a picture on every angle of it. A must visit place when you are at Jeju Island.

It's worth our climb n walk to the fall. Please wear warm enough to prevent same thing as us. I just wear a sweater and T-shirt inside yet the wind breeze can make you freeze. Worth the long walk and stairs taken to reach the destination.
The waterfall is beautiful and takes only a mere 10 minutes to go down. There were people stacking stones, which also made the environment look more aesthetic.

Came here by using waze , there's parking , entrance fee 2000 won for adults , 1000 won for youth , walk down the stairs leading to the rocky waterfalls , got to be careful when walking around the rocks .
It's a impressive waterfall in Jeju Island of historical significance.Should not miss this site, if it's your first trip to Jeju Island.

This was the only waterfall we visited on Jeju island. It was worth the visit although somehow not terribly exciting for me. I think it would be  nicer in  the summer time when you can put your feet in the water. There is a small entrance fee.

Nothing spectacular in terms of size other than the water is running into the ocean. It was a nice walk to get there and the view is nice from the rocks along the sea.  Ladies selling fresh seafood on the rocks.
Nice place to visit. Wonderfull waterfall nice place for relax. My son enjoy this place so much. We took public bus to come here and its quite easy to find.

The scenery was nice. The driver told me it is the largest waterfall feature in Jeju area.  Lots of tourists when we visited.  The rocks were quite slippery and could be dangerous for young kids and elderly.  Overall a nice place to visit even if you only have 30mins to spare.  The entrance fee was cheap.
Not so great but for a small place like Jeju .....good to go if you have a day to spare. Lots of eateries around & cosmetic shops as well.

I ve never been this near to the base of a waterfall before.  No railings, just the raw power of a thunderous fall.  And a rainbow!  The kids loved jumping from rock to rock.  This may be a little precarious on a wet day, but we were lucky with the weather during our visit.You do get some splashes.  So if you have very expensive camera equipment, you may want to protect it?  The walk up was a little tiring, but not overly so.Absolutely love it.  A must see!

Getting close to the waterfalls looks easier than it seems. However, that adds to the thrill of getting nearer to mother nature. It is tricky manuvering around the wet, slippery & sometimes unstable rocks & boulders in cold weather. Many a times, you find yourself balancing precariously on the boulders or have your feet stuck between the rocks as you slip or slide from the smooth rocks. You will also find visitors around you lending you a hand to help you get back on your feet. Such spontaneous camaraderie !  For the young & agile, it is fun watching them jumping from rock to rock, like Tarzan in action.  It is a thrilling on the rocks experience not to be missed !  And you get rewarded by the beautiful sight & sound of a great waterfall!
One of the most beautiful waterfalls in Jeju! I didn't ecpect it to be so nice! Definitely worth spending 45 minutes there. Good spot for photoes, too.

Went here on a cloudy morning and loved it. Lots of steps to get down to the falls so grandmom stayed at the top. Pretty impressive and the bottom and it s neat to see a waterfall so close to the ocean.If you have time, don t forget to walk along the path along the coast to the  Castle of Shell . You get to the boardwalk path from the other side of the parking lot and it s not well marked. It leads to a house on a cliff and another small waterfall. This place would have been a 4 but this extra trail makes it a 5. The cost for a family of 5 was 7,000 KRW.

This waterfall truly was magnificent to see. I recommend going early in the morning (ticket office opens at 8:00 am). It was 8:30 am when I visited and there were a few people. At one point they all left and it was only me and the waterfall. Truly amazing. Definitely go before before all the tourists get there!!!
This is a fun place to visit, as apart from the waterfalls you can walk around the area and see many different attractions.

I visited this waterfall very close to the closing time. I reached there at 530pm but it was more than enough for me to wow at this waterfall. The air was refreshing and having the water coming together with the sea was amazing. It was a pity that it was too cold for us to take a dip but nonetheless we did not regret making a trip here!
tough climb to take pictures at the waterfall because of the rocks and uneven ground. but the sight is well worth it.

You need to purchase a ticket at 2000won each and then take 130 steps down a flight of stairs to get to the waterfall. Comfortable shoes are recommended if you want to get closer to the waterfall. It is advisable to use your feet to check for the stability of the rocks before stepping on them as there were some loose and moving ones amongst the pile of rocks. The rocks nearer to the waterfall are wet so be careful if you want to get even closer to the fall. The waves crashing on the shore are also rather strong, so be more cautious if you re moving nearer towards the shore.
I really like this waterfall. It adjoins the ocean so its pretty unique. The climb is pretty steep. Wear comfortable shoes.

If you like nature then this will be a wonderful experience. It is a spectacular waterfall that connects with the ocean. It is quite busy, but the area is big enough as well. There are many steep steps to get down to the falls and back up again

Its really easy to reach this attraction. Parking is free however you are required to pay a minimal fee in order to view this waterfall. Walking on the stairs is easy but if you do wish to get close to the waterfall , a good pair of shoes with good grip is required as you have to walk on the slippery stone/rock. There are some women selling fresh seafood by the waterfall.

Take your time and enjoy the views. After rain, the waterfall is very pretty and worth the walk from the car parking area. Vendors sell drinks and traditional snacks at various spots and there are many photo spots.

a cliff beside the sea fell with fresh water. Thre is a historical legend about a staff of the 1st great empire of China that he wants to be immortal. The story is also about the name of this city. sea woman inside the park.
Nice for some lovely photos. Beautiful scenery all around and even some super fresh seafood caught by the locals available here.

It's a short walk down to the waterfall. Very doable and not tiring. We went early in the morning after breakfast and the pictures turned out lovely.  Also saw real Hanyeo women actually diving tirelessly.

This waterfall is a poor second to the nearby Cheonjiyeon Falls. If you want to see everything Seogwipo has to offer then pay a visit but I much preferred the other falls for both the actual waterfall and the surrounding gardens that give you access to it.
We went here to see the waterfall. The stones were very slippery but otherwise it was okey. The easiest way to get here is by taxi I think.
It's a nice walk to the waterfall, but from land I suspect the view is not as nice as from sea. Consider doing the boat cruise of the area to give a better perspective.

When we arrived we were a little surprised at the ticket price to enter. There was quite a lot of steps to get down, as we walked down you can see the waterfall. when we got down to the rocks by the waterfall there was tons of people it was so crowded. but the waterfall was very beautiful and was very nice how it was all open without any barriers keeping you from the waterfall.
Fantastic view and cheap entry maybe 2000 won ($2.00 us). Cheaper for students high school and below.But a nice scenic hike and a fantastic view. Well worth it.
Stand nearer to the waterfall for some refreshing sprinkle. Nice view and a must visit. Stepping stones to get to the waterfall may be a challenge for some.
This is a place with a great view, you just need to walk a few minutes to get there from the enterance. There was some people that sell raw seafood snacks if you want to try.
It's relatively easy to find this place. We need to pay 2000 won for entrance fee. If you have more time, take another walk to the parking lot, there is also beautiful scenery.

This is a very beautiful location and in a good location. You can visit here for any length of time that you would like. It is great for a quick stop on the way to other attractions on the south side of the island. Don't miss this one. Even if you have many other things to do there is time to put this on the list.
Easy climb down to see the waterfall. If you are adventurous, go navigate across the rocks for better photos angles and also for a challenge. A simple waterfall for photo ops and a light stroll.

The waterfall is not as impressive as it was advertised and there is an admission fee.Frankly, I don't think they should charge for admission as there is really nothing to do except to see the waterfall. If you have time to spare, visit other attractions.

The only waterfall in Jeju that drains directly into the ocean is worth stopping by for around half an hour. Ample parking space, free admission, good accessibility and the ability to get quite close to the waterfall even if it isn't that tall.

Interesting way they hide it from free view, but a  nice drop and fall into the ocean.  Careful clambering over the cobbles and boulders to get your shot.  Looks like local vendors selling raw oysters of sashimi down by the shore.  Other souvenir shops align the entrance and exit.

Interesting sight, w lots of tourists. Only 2000 won per adult, not expensive.There is another waterfall 40 mins away but other than that not much in that area. So plan well before making a trip there esp if you are going to use public transportation.
Enjoyed how easy it was to walk from parking lot down to the waterfall, ws not expecting such a short walk! A waterfall that goes into the ocean, two awesome things in one!

A good short stop to see a waterfall. There is a few steep steps so not recommended if u are bring a baby or toddler. The waterfall is not extremely fanciful though.  There are some old ladies trying to sell the usual seafood.

Walked over from our hotel to the waterfalls and enjoyed the view.  Absolutely gorgeous. As a group, we enjoyed climbing up and down stones to get closer to the falls for pictures or over to see the fishermen (and women) slightly further away from the falls.

A popular hotspot and parking can be a problem. The waterfall is nice but not very spectacular. Can stand on the rocks bottom to catch a better glimpse of the waterfall but mind the slippery rocks. Wear a sport shoes with good traction or simply walked bare footed on the rocks.

This waterfall was a 15 min walk away from where we were staying. The trail which led to this waterfall is amazing with great views of the ocean. Waterfall itself is pretty amazing and great opportunity for few pics.

Beautiful weather with wonderful scenic view. Took a bit of time getting to the side of the waterfall due to uneven rocks surrounding it after going down the stair for about 10 mins. Once you get past that, have a great time snapping away and find your best angles  though you have to take turns with other tourists who are doing the exact same thing. Snap away!
Beautiful Waterfall. Because it was April there was no charge to see it, liked that part. It was sort of hot so it was refreshing to be  near the fall

Waterfall is easily accessible from seogwipo town and surrounded by lovely parks. Entrance fee is 2000 krw but no one was collecting fares when I was there. There is a stairway down to water fall but you can see it from the top easily. Nothing spectacular if you have seen other water falls.

The Waterfall is very close to Seogwipo, within walkig distance.  It costs 2000eon adults to enter but you can get very close to the Waterfall.  There are even seafood being sold next to the cliffs so you can eat seafood, watch the sea and enjoy the waterfall.  We took a few pictures and then   left because the downside is that there are a lot of people.

This is a very accessible waterfall. Kudos to the local government for making it as easy as possible to enjoy the natural landmarks on the island. A flight of steps down and a very short walk brings you to the waterfall. There are large rocks to climb over and also a rocky flat "beach". Young children will especially love climbing over the rocks and exploring the pools of flowing water. I have a sturdy 4 year old and a 5.5 year old and I think the waterfall impressed them less than the natural rocky playground they happily found themselves in. Do keep a very close eye on young children as the rocks are sharp edged and uneven, some even loose when you step on them.

As someone who loves walking on rocky surfaces (yes it does sound weird when I type it like that), I really enjoyed walking down to the base of the waterfall. You don't have to walk the rocky part to get you to the waterfall though - the steps from the carpark down to the base will take you close enough. Someone the rocks are slippery so be careful. Along the way I think there were haenyeon with their very freshly caught seafood. Loved this place; would come back in a heartbeat.
We tried the seafood that they sell at the seaside. The seafood taste horrible, everything so hard. It is so fishy, sea salt taste.
Well, another water fall, again! haha, its nice, give it a try if never bit there. Photo look nicer tho, actual scene you might feel that the waterfall is not as big as you imagine.
Beautiful waterfall with nice view.Kids love them n lots of pics taken.Tired part is to climb up the stairs n big step..
Everyone loved it!Make sure to bring your selfie stick and sunblock.Will definitely revisit.Visited in Summer of 2015

It's a waterfall that goes directly to the see. Not many like that so you should visited it at least once. The road after the stairs was rocky, so you have to be careful. There's a woman diver, so there' s some people that ate her catch near the waterfall.

Our family spent much effort taking a nice family picture near this waterfall - and it turned out GREAT!! Hahaha... Nice place to go, for the sight, the EXERCISE!!But it can get quite crowded though. Older folks may find it hard to climb on the uneven rocks but they can get near enough for picture with the waterfall at the background. To get REAL near to the waterfall, leave it to the young ones!

One of the best waterfalls in Jeju that flows all the way to sea... Spent a wonderful time in our free and easy trip around Jeju island with a rented car! Will go to Jeju again for the third time again!
If you are ona  relaxing trip and just want to see some nice scenery then this will fit the bill.  Its by no means spectacular but nonetheless very pretty, especially with the local plant growth.

Really gorgeous view of the waterfall which flows right into the sea. A little bit challenging to go near it as you have to walk and hop on big rocks but you could still see it clearly just by standing near the stairs. Sat near to the waterfall and my shirt got slightly wet by the water splashes. Cold but refreshing. Do wear proper shoes if you intend to walk on the huge rocks to go near the waterfall.
This waterfall is very tiny but really difficult to see the water itself because it dries up time to time. You must checkout the season before visiting this place.
It's very scenic and a good location for photography, it's near to town and easy to reach. The entrance fees is affordable
Magnificent view. We spent an hour taking lots of photos. There are some locals selling raw sashimi of abalone, octopus and top shell if you keen to eat them fresh (or rather I should say alive)

Set out from the M-Stay Hotel for this attraction, and well worth the walk!  I think it is a bit better than the highly-enjoyable Cheonjiyeon Falls, with a wider view and a spectacular drop into the adjacent ocean.  Found this site to be more open and therefore afford a bit more solitary viewing than its aforementioned neighbor, though if you have trouble doing stairs than this site would pose a far greater challenge than Cheonjiyeon; here, you have to walk down steps to get to the falls, while the latter affords parking and access from the base of the falls.

It is my first time seeing a waterfall by the sea... The view was spectacular! Experience the breeze of the sea combined with the breeze from the waterfall. The majestic waterfall is already quite impressive itself...

There is a standard entrance fee of 2000krw. After you buy the ticket you will proceed into the entrance and you can see the waterfall infront of you. Hang on to your ticket because somewhere along the route, they will check your ticket. Most people will walk to as near to the falls as possible to take pictures. It was quite crowded on the day. The rocks / boulders are not so easy to walk on. So we stayed near the staircase. Yes, there are stairs to climb down to the falls and then you have to climb up again.I would say it is quite a normal waterfall - just to tick off that you have seen it.

It was a short walk from the entrance to get to the actual Jeongbang waterfall site, but was a grand sight to behold - you get to see the ocean from the waterfall! I also like that you could make your way closer to the waterfall by stepping on the big rocks around it.Between Jeongbang and Cheonjiyeon, my vote goes to the former. For the latter, the walk from the entrance was longer, the view was not as fantastic, and you can't get nearer to the waterfall even if you wanted to.

Located on the beach, you must go down and walk on lava stones, it's a nice place, many people take photos in front of this waterfall that comes out from the massive right on the beach, this place is connected to story of a Chinese traveller speaking the elixir of eternal youth, he hoped to find it on Jeju

This is a very spectacular waterfall plummeting down into the ocean. The boulders add to the fun of the attraction clambering over them to see the waterfall more directly .Very well organised walk from car park down to waterfall area. Some interesting stalls at the entrance. Again very cheap to visit.
If you choose one fall out of 3 in this area, choose this one.  It has the best view, and no platform which really ruin any natural beauty.  This is one one the best waterfall I have seen.

This is the largest waterfall in Asia that falls into the sea, and one of the only ones that is not fenced up at the bottom. Usually, when you visit waterfalls, it's always staring at it from a distance, where a viewing platform has been built. This is different, you get to walk ALL THE WAY to below that waterfall, and if you are open to wading through knee deep water, go touch that waterfall.The spray of water is refreshing, and the scenery rocks. You'll feel one with nature.
It sets you with AWE where you could see the waterfall meeting the sea.  You could experience the good ion in the air and listening to the music of the sea.
nothing special, just a waterfall. spectacular? not really, but it is special as it is one of the few waterfalls that directly falls to the sea
This place is really amazing. The waterfall is falling directly to sea and it is a treat to eyes.. The best thing is we can enjoy both of them together here.. Was really astonished by the view.

In order to reach the waterfall, you need to walk down many stairs and using the same way back. But worth it as the view is beautiful as it directly flows to the ocean. But be careful since the area is rocky.

One of 3 famous waterfalls in Jeju, along with Cheonjiyeon Waterfall and Cheonjeyeon Waterfallis but apparently the only waterfall in Asia to fall directly into the ocean.  Definitely worth the short climb down to get as near the fall for nice shots and a sea splash. If lucky, you might even catch a rainbow over the fall.  Walking shoes recommended to navigate the rocky boulders.  Do come early before the tourist horde arrive.  Adventurous hiking enthusiasts can continue to the Olle trail from the carpark entrance.

We visited the falls early afternoon, only minutes away from our hotel. It was worth the short climb down the views are amazing and it was not at all crowded, that maybe due to time of year. This was much nicer than cheonjijeon waterfall as you could get close and take nice pics.
visited 3 more popular waterfalls in Jeju and this one is the best.  best visit time is summer so that you can enjoy the splash when you walk close.  Imagine it would be too chilly for winter though.

We paid our entrance fees and simply stayed on the top to get some good pictures. There were hordes of people down below so I don't recommend taking a long walk down and then back up just to get some pictures of other tourists.

I was in a rush so I briefly stoped by this fall to enjoy its amazing views.  It is simply amazing how it looks, I guess if you like nature, this would be one of the must see places.  I am a nature lover.  Take your time, and you can possibly have some of the fresh conch caught by the ladies by the bottom of the fall.
You have to go down to get the waterfall. Entrance fee is 3k won. Crowded with people. The waterfall is quite beautifull as it

Ofcourse is a nice waterfal but i think it was a little overrated. Like everyplace att Jeju you have to pay a small entrance fee (2000 won) and then its just what it is, a waterfall. For sure you can take some nice pictures but thats it.

Very rocky do be sure to wear appropriate shoes. Lots of great angles to take photos without having lots of other tourists in the shot. Go around dinner or lunch time as they have some local women selling freshly prepared seafood (I'm a vegetarian and didn't try it but looked good).

If you have time, I would definitely recommend coming here. After coming to this waterfall we decided there was no need to see the others as this was so beautiful. There are a lot of tourists though, so you may want to come earlier. Quick and easy to find the location, with only a few steps down to the waterfall. Definitely worth it!
Might not be worth the $2 entry fee. If you walk behind the first ticket counter you get one of the best views of the falls. There's another ticket booth that they punch your ticket at.

It's a good stop if you're in the area. I get the feeling there's much more to do around but it was raining. Anyways it's cheap and easy to access. It's also right in the city so ot won't require you to travel far. Really nice spot for photos.
Nice waterfall, but nothing too special except it was pretty big. It was right after the typhoon so lots of water flowing down.

Jeongbang waterfall is impressive for its sheer size and also the fact that it falls directly into the ocean - apparently the only one in Asia that does. You can climb over the huge rocks in front of it to get a better view beyond the hoards of tourists taking selfies. Worth the visit!
Jeongbang Waterfall is a very nice waterfall with a great view. You have to go there if you travel to Jeju Island.

It is known as the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly into the ocean. The view is breathtaking, the most beautiful waterfall I have seen so far. Definitely worth the visit. The entrance ticket is 2,000 KRW, it is only 1,000 KRW for teenager.

So the water level in South Korea is low right now due to an unusually dry rainy season so the falls were not as grand as they usually are however it was still an impressive sight and one I wont forget. BTW take a swim trunk with you and go swimming in the water at the bottom of the first falls its cold but amazing.
Really nice waterfalls. Awesome view of the beach from the top. Entrance is just 2,000 KRW with 50% discount for military.

Of all the waterfalls we visited in Jeju, this was one of the ONLY that you could actually play in!  The others are beautiful but this one allowed visitors to swim and play!  Not many people did but we had a BLAST enjoying the cool water on the hot summer day!

My friend took me here because he said it was beautiful. Indeed, a waterfall next to the ocean is as picturesque as it gets. We took some dope pictures and dip our feet into the cool and refreshing water when I saw my FIRST EVER DOUBLE RAINBOW. Life is good haha
This is a cool waterfall. With 35 degree heat the splashing from the powerful waterfall was a nice way to cool down. Of the many waterfalls in Jeju, I feel that this is the best one.

The waterfall is in walking distance from the center of Seogwipo, even if there are a fee steps to get to the waterfall it's worth the visit!The view is fantastic, and the vapour coming from the waterfall is refreshing (especially in summer).Beware just of the last few meters because are on rocks, and sometimes slippery.

The only (or so I'm told) waterfall that falls into the sea in Jeju Island.  Easy walk down stairs to the bottom of the falls.  Able to walk around on the rocks and view the falls.  Really gorgeous and totally worth the visit.

Nice wiev, cold water. Not that big but worth going in hot summer days. Easy to reach, wide car parking. Entrance fee than stairs to reach sea level. Fun for kids, if you dare:...... get into the water!!!
I loved it! You could come real close to the water fall and get water on you as well. I prefer this one over the other one definitely.

A few dozen steps down to the open rocks at the base of the waterfall.  And then you are rewarded with a beautiful scene and welcoming and cooling mist.  If you have good balance you can walk on the rocks for some beautiful pic of the falls and the waves crashing on the rocks.  Gorgeous!

It's not the most huge waterfall, but its certainly the closest distance you can have with that beautiful waterfalls. Brace yourself with the beauty of natural creation. Must visit whenever you go Jeju.
Amazing view. Undescribable scene. You can stop by the small shop for fresh orange juice or an orange in your way.

Of all the waterfalls we visited, which included all the major ones, this waterfall takes the cake. How to get there:It is easy to reach, a quick walk from anywhere in Seogwipo to the shore. Taxi's help.Once you get there you pay entrance and climb down the steps to the beach.What we liked:Waterfall falling into the sea.Nice way to cool down in the summer heat (water spraying everywhere, cold sea water).Busy, but not too busy.There are much appreciated ice creams and cold drinks at the top of the stairs.What we didn't like:The idea that we looked as silly as everyone else with our selfie stick. Would we recommend others to go?Yes
Although really busy... what a beautiful sight! You do need to be able to climb steep stairs to access but well worth the effort.
A short walk from the parking lot. This waterfall is also connected to one of the Olle trails which you can explore from the car park area. It gets quite crowded though.
This waterfall is so beautiful. Showing your ID/ passport and if you are below 24, you can get discounted price.
nice and beautiful scenery, not very crowded easy parking and ticket were only 2000 won, around 2 dollars

It's close to the main centre of Seogwipo, easy to find with street signs posted in English around the place, it only costs 2000 won to enter, and it's not only unique but a spectacular chance for photos. Do as the Koreans do, they sure do love a waterfall selfie.This and the nearby Cheonjiyeon Falls are two must-visit attractions in the area.I'm not sure if you can walk too close to the actual waterfall, or what the rules are for swimming in the waterfall pool, but on a hot and sunny day I seriously considered it.You do get a bit of spray from the waterfall, so keep that in mind when taking a photo so as not to get your camera too wet.
Unique setting near the sea-shore. The water flow was good, take tangerine from market outside the falls and enjoy water sprinkling out of the falls.
It was amazing to, after a very short walk down stairs, be able to walk/climb so close to these spectacular waterfalls. Just lovely, safe, accessible, great!
There are a number of waterfalls in Jeju, but only one deserves your time. It's amazing to see just how close the water flows directly to the sea.
Definitely one of the key sights in Jeju and not to be missed.  This waterfall is just 50 meters from the sea and the view is amazing.

This waterfall is beautiful in that the water falls all the way to the rocks in the ocean unimpeded.  You have to scramble on rocks to get closer or you can remain on the landing at the bottom of the steps and get a pretty good view.

If staying in or visitng Seogwipo, this is a must. It's no Niagra Falls, but the quality-to-price ratio of this georgeous waterfall is difficult to overstate, as it costs only 2000 won (less than 2USD). A short walk down several staircases, passing shops along the way, will lead you to a stoney beach and the nearby waterfall. You're free to get as close as you wish, but, as many other reviewers have pointed out, the myst created by the falls makes the rocks slippery. So, wear shoes with decent treading and proceed with caution!

Staying in Seogwipo we were lucky enough to be able to walk to these amazing waterfalls which fall into the sea.  We descended  down some wooden steps to the beach and clambered over rocks to get close to the falls.  There was a great atmosphere there with many tourists all happy to help take photos of each other with the falls behind.  Well worth a visit.

A bit difficult to find, but a gorgeous location.   The waterfall flows into a small pool and then flows into the sea.  It was pretty crowded when we went, but still worth going.  The rocks are SLIPPERY.  Be careful when moving around on them as we saw a few people fall.  There are a few shops selling snacks and Jeju treats at the top and a proper coffee shop as well.

You can get right up to the falls even as it empties into the sea. Where sneaks that day because there are a lot of rocks. Be careful and take lots of pictures. A taxi or bike ride is preferable but you can easily walk to the entrance it is just out of the way of the town
The natural waterfall in the raw form and walking in the rocks is fun. The surprise was a fresh Jeju orange juice nearby, the seller was honest and nice.
Such a unique place as the water falls directly to the sea. Not far from the city centre, definitely worth to visit.
The location is close to town centre but the fall is not grand. It's special in the way that it directly falls to the sea. Anyway very convenient to visit.
Such a great waterfall in Jeju island, it's good to be able to take photo with this Mother Nature. You will not be regret to climb down and up to the waterfall. A place that must visit.

I found this place by accident. One afternoon as I was shopping at Seogwipo market area, I happen to see the sea at a distant. I thought I'd just take a walk towards there. It was a lovely surprise, as I managed to get to this very much talked about waterfalls. The water actually drains directly into the sea, and not another freshwater reservoir as more commonly seen.There is an entrance fee and plenty of souvenir shops and eateries here. It's a beautiful sight and even better sound.... the sound of the water gushing down into the ocean. The mist from the pounding of the water is so refreshing. Be prepared to walk along some steep steps...not many but quite steep.

It's got a high ranking but I was disappointed,  this was the 3rd waterfall I'd paid an entrance fee to see,  it's nice to see but nothing spectacular we hooked it onto the end of olle trail 7 after cheongjiyeon falls.

This spectacular waterfall is worth the visit. Parking is easy and there is a small fee to walk down to the bottom of the falls. The bottom is all rocks so it could be difficult to maneuver for some. At the top is a lovely art gallery and cafe.
The water was cool (it was a hot day), we went on a weekday so it was not too crowded. Take off your shoes and frolick.

Interesting if short visit. Not too well signposted, but once found, plenty of parking and a short climb downn to the beach. Depending on the season entry if 2,000 Won or free. Demonstrates well the islands volcanic cliffs.

It was my first time experience in Jeju Island, but with 3 days and 2 nights , has been provided with a pleasure vacation with my family. For those who are planning to go to Jeongbang Waterfall, it is actually in Seogwipo, and you can cover two famous waterfall in this towns and most probably you can cover in a day. For this Jeongbang Waterfall, please take note that it is closed at 6.00pm and whereby the another waterfall in Seogwipo is open during nightime. Thus, last time during our visit, for Jeongbang we visited early morning, and that the best time you to go, because not that many people and you can snap a photo alone instead of a lot of people.My tips:1. Go early i.e. 8.00am2. Get photo as much as you want3. Each season the waterfall will be different, if winter, you may get different panorama and landscape of the waterfall.Thank You.
This is in my opinion the best of the three major waterfall sites on jeju. It wasn't overly crowded and the surrounding coastline makes for great photos.

The Jeonbang Waterfall was breath taking and is the only waterfall in South East Asia to flow directly into the ocean. The views are great and the waterfall looks so majestic. This is definitely one waterfall you should check out in Seogwipo.

Beautiful, according to our guide we hired he claims that the this is the only waterfall in South Korea that is sea side. The place is touch crowded and a bit of walk downhill from visitor location. Otherwise, totally worth the effort.

To be honest, I didn't expect anything from this waterfall, but once we got there, it was pretty nice. It wasn't big like the one in U.S (Niagara fall), but this is only waterfall I know that flows right to the ocean! We paid about $2 to see the waterfall. We took some pictures and left there within 30 mins. Was this worth to see? It's a toss up but I'd say yes.

Although the waterfall itself was very beautiful to see we only stayed for a few minutes if that there was a lot of people there taking pictures and sitting on the rocks once there, there wasn't much stuff to do. But on the bright side it was really nice to see.

Jeongbang Waterfall itself is beautiful.  A bonus to see the Haenyo (women sea divers) set up camp at the base of the waterfall selling fresh sashimi from their morning's catch.  The entrance is a bit touristy with a small market trying to see you all the typical Jeju fare (famous hallabong which mine were deceptively switched to regular tangerines, hallabong flavored everything, grandfather statues...).  But what makes the stop worth it is the "other waterfall" just a few min walk down the Olle trail at the same entrance.  That one isn't nearly as tall but way more impressive in my book.

Our guide added this to our itinerary and we were glad he did. It's a beautiful location and the waterfall itself is lovely. It can get a bit busy with Chinese tourists, so you have to pick your photo taking opportunities when you can, but well worth a visit.
need to be careful walking on the rocks, the water is very clean n clear, a lot of tourist here so have to be 'skillful' to take photos and move about on the rocks.

There is a fee at the entrance. It takes only 10 minutes to climb down the steps to the waterfall. There is no proper footpath so you have to walk on jagged rocks and stones to go near the waterfall. Wear proper shoes and tread carefully. It's really a majestic waterfall and you could get really close which adds to the experience. We sat down in the shade and enjoyed the cool mist and sounds of the waters. Took a lot of photos of course. A sight not to be missed!
This was one of our most favorite waterfalls in Korea. Amazing to see. Lots of steps down and up but worth the climb.

This is in my opinion the best waterfall in Seogwipo. I don't know if it's the biggest or the tallest, but it is truly unique, as water falls down into the ocean in the middle of a pebble beach. I visited it on a rainy and windy day, and because of it it might have left a stronger impression on me. I could really feel the forces of nature. Also, since the water falls onto the beach, you can take pictures really close to the waterfall. Overall, it is a must see waterfall if you come to Seogwipo, even though it doesn't get more than 20 minutes to get a nice view of the fall and its surroundings.

This could be a quick stop or you could spend time enjoying the view.  There weren't too many people when we were there but of course it could be busy.  The falls are unique in that the fresh water falls directly into the sea below.  You have to take stairs to get down to the sea level.  You can't get right up to the falls but you can get close enough to feel the spray and hear the roar of the water.

A very nice place to admire and get close to nature but do be in the right footwear as the steps down can be quite slippery. You can get really close to the waterfall and that was what many people were trying to do so it was difficult to get a nice picture without any photobombs.
Although the weather wasn't perfect for a visit this afternoon, however, it hasn't spoiled a positive impression. Lots of tourists anyways, and it leaves a good feeling of connectedness with nature.
This was one of the highlights of our trip to Jeju. We took an afternoon trip to visit and the falls themselves are beautiful as is the view over the sea.
Quite pretty and relatively easy to get to. Granted you have to go down some steps to get to the falls. Entrance fees are KRW2,000 per person.
Beautiful Waterfall to visit while in Jeju island. Make sure you are wearing the right footwear and are fit. Many steep steps to get down to the fall.

A waterfall which falls right into the ocean, one of its kind and unique. Suitable even in rainy weather but take caution on the slippery rocks leading down to base of waterfall. The best of the 3 famous waterfalls around Seogwipo
It's crowded but the view is amazing. If you're a first timer, I personally will recommend this than the other waterfalls in Jeju.
On sunny day, beautiful rainbow and  really blue sea you can see. you need to walk down some steps, but it is valuable experience to take time and effort.you don't want to miss it ^^

Was surprised to learn this is a UNESCO listed site and once I got there just loved it. It's one of the few waterfalls where the water falls straight into the ocean. There were alot of tourists when I visited but definetley worth a look!
We went in July end and found this waterfall good.It was loud,nice place to get some snaps. scenic beauty is good.Recommended for family.

This is, so far, the best waterfall I have ever been. You need to go down from a lot of big rocks to go near the falls. That is what makes it exciting. Wear comfortable shoes and I recommend to wear pants.

Just try to get past all the tourists and walk down to the waterfall, bring a rain proof jacket :) went in November and waterfall was relatively small, probably more awesome after period of heavy rain. Great selfies ;)

went to Jeongball fall, the view is amazing. and the fact that it faces the sea, it suits me alot.there is 1-2 ajuma selling live seafood. can enjoy the excellent sea view with fresh seafood at the same time. But not for the weak tummy.

Take the step down the cliff and you will find yourself a unique waterfall that is near a sea. Usually you will find waterfall upstream of a river not close to sea. The force of the water is quite huge so you can feel the breeze when you nearer to the waterfall. There are other cultural stuff nearby the waterfall as well.
Worth seeing, and I liked that it was within walking distance of our hotel. The beach area was really pretty although it is not a place to go if you want a beach and not a waterfall.

This waterfall provides loads of great photo opportunities. We liked this one better than the cheonjyeon waterfalls. You can get very close to the waterfall. You can also buy fresh seafood at the site.

The falls are really beautiful but extremely crowded. I would recommend taking the first bus you can to the area to be there as soon as it opens if you want to try to get decent pictures without hundreds of people in your photo.  We arrived around 11am and the sheer numbers of people detracted from the beauty of the falls.
Cool falls near rocky coast.  Walk down into rocky coast and get sprayed by the falls.  There are women selling freshly caught seafood just near the fall. Great place to visit.

The best waterfall to visit! Don't waste time to other waterfall, this is the best one. I managed to see rainbow at the waterfall was simply amazing! Made the whole trip worthwhile! Just wear the right shoes there as there are some rocks to walk on before getting close to the waterfall
a rare waterfall that falls directly into the ocean its a sight to behold. can go quite near the falls for a good picture.

This waterfall is so tall and you can stand near it to take a picture. The water is so cool and refreshing.There is a stall selling orange ice-cream near the exit- really delicious and thirst-quenching.

What a amazing waterfall. I heard that there are olny few waterfall forward the ocean in the world. I had seen several waterfall. If anyone ask me what waterfall is best in your life time, I will say Jeongbang is the best. It is not that big like Victoria or Niagara, but it make feel me cheer up.
If you can get pass all the uneven boulders, you can get really up close to the waterfall and it's pretty impressive and majestic!
Several nice waterfalls around here. This is one of the nicest. Swimming is not allowed, but you can cool down anyway, so nice for kids as well!

The lack of barriers and many signs makes this a very pleasant and natural-feeling sight. If you're alone, someone will be more than happy to take a photo with you in it here, as Koreans come here with photography very much in mind.
If you have been to Niagara, don't bother to visit this one. It's not a roaring high waterfall. Also when it's crowded, you have to be careful, climbing up the wooden steps.
This is a lovely waterfall, but try to avoid the peak season otherwise it's a bit busy.  Beautiful how the water flows right next to the sea.  Good for a paddle as well.
Pretty, but not necessarily a must see. The weather was terrible when we visited so maybe that contributed.

Falls is very beautiful.  You walk down 100 steps or so, then across big rocks to the bottom of the falls.  Wear tennis shoes or flip-flops for rock hopping!  Lots of water spray, and nice wading in the cool water as it runs across a few rocks to the ocean.
it reminds us of tropical islands in the pacific. its an excellent location ideal for a picnic. Very beautiful and romantic feel.
It's one of the only water falls in Asia which goes directly into the sea.You can get very close but you will het wet.Is as well worth the 2000 Won entry fee.

This was my favorite amongst all the waterfalls I have been to as you can get pretty close to it. You can even wade in the pool if you want to as it's quite shallow. Very nice place to take photos. Took a short trek to Sojeongbang waterfall from the same parking area. For those driving you can enter the phone number 7331530 into the gps. Admission fee is 2000 won for adults. Make use of your youth ID card if you are below 24 years old! It's half the price and can save you a lot if you go to many attractions. Closes at 6pm though so plan your itinerary properly!

Absolutely stunning location. Great place to sit on the beach and relax while the waterfall sprays you! If you're travelling from Jeju City, make sure you ask for directions before you try and find this waterfall (there are no buses that take you directly there so you have to walk for 15 minutes). - Guess that isn't the waterfall's fault though!

If you only see one waterfall in Jeju, I would see this one. It is beautiful how it goes into the see. We visited it during a taxi tour along with Cheonjiyeon Falls. They are very close to each other so there is no need to see just one but if you are short on time I would go to Jeongbang. For 2000 won each it is a bargin. Bring shoes you don't mind getting wet and can climb over rocks in, if you want to get close to the waterfall.

It was a short walk of about 10 min but we took longer than usual as we were distracted by the locals selling raw abalone... decided to try out the raw abalone... Dont really know how to appreciate them... Too hard and chewy for me... But the locals are very kind... They even offered us soju...
It's a shame that water is toooo cool because  the first reaction on a water fall like this is to go inside the water and don't come out ;-)
It is easily to reach from the downtown area.  Next to the Seobok Park, at the coastal rim.  You may enjoy a nice view on the coast-front.  Good for the family for fun.

Beautiful Falls. Also its rare to see falls directly in ocean apparently only one in Asia. It said that the dragon's spirit is contained in the water which can cure diseases and bring rain during drought. Easy to access. Make sue you wearing comfatable Shoes, it does get slippery. We had some lovely click out here, spl couple ;)

We took airport limousine bus 600 and got off at Paradise Hotel, the second last stop, and the journey took us 90 minutes. At the bus stop, we saw the sign pointing to Sojeongbang Falls and started walking there. Reaching the place, you need to go down the staircase to see the waterfall, the little brother of Jeongbang falls, as it is not as high. Feeling satisfied, we followed the pathway and continued walking to Jeongbang falls. Paying an entrance fee of 2000 won, going down the stairs, stepping on rocks of all sizes and shapes, we reach the waterfall that had been discovered in 219 B.C. Seobok was ordered by Emperor Qinshihuang to find an elixir of life with a big fleet of over 3000 people by sailing to the east. He chanced upon this waterfall and he had inscribed on the rock near the fall stating that he had passed here. The waterfall is 23m high and very close to the ocean. This is one of the waterfalls to visit in Jeju.

It is easy to access the fall for those who dislike climbing steps.  It was only a short distance from the entrance via some steps.  Nice feeling to get up close and personal to the fall however just gotta beware of wet ones which at times can be slippery.  Smaller rocks tend to move when you are stepping on them so be careful.

Great waterfall, not very high but impressive nonetheless.  Spend a while looking about and then try some of the seafood brought up by the "haenyeo" [ladies who free-dive for shellfish].  Fresh as can be, washed down with a glass or two of soju.
This place has a very nice view. The waterfall is beautiful and the water looks pure and clean. But you have to climb all the big rocks around to get closer to the waterfall.

went there on a rainy day. Was't hard to get down to the waterfall but it was a little difficult trying to balance myself on the rocks while holding on to a camera. Was crowded but still manageable. On my way down, I found the lady divers selling fresh catch of the day and it was awesomely fresh!
Scenic view by the sea and we can see lady divers on that day diving for their catch. We also tried fresh catches on the spot sold by Ahjumma and was a wonderful experience. A place not to be missed.
Impressive and memorizing. Love the view. Can also have some fresh live seafood. Definitely worth going. One of the best waterfalls in Jeju. The rest are not really worth seeing.

Cool and refreshing. The rocks just at the foot of the waterfall are difficult to walk down. Not recommended for old people.I could not find the inscription which this waterfall is famous (go check out the history/story behind this)!

We drove up to this attraction easily via an English GPS. No prams or strollers are allowed in there because it's mostly stairways and lots of rocks. You'll need to navigate across some amount of rocks to take a nice picture with the waterfall. There're a couple of old ladies selling seafood with a small fire burning nearby - we didnt buy anything coz they don't speak English. Not a huge waterfall, but the kids love it (not of the waterfall, but the rock walking experience) - if you're not careful, you can easily sprain an ankle or even break some bones.

This is the only waterfall in Asia which falls directly into the ocean. Admission fee is 2000 won. You'll need to climb over quite a number of rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. Be careful of the slippery rocks if you go after raining. In my opinion, Jeongbang Waterfall is worth to visit than any other waterfalls in Jeju.

Took a Taxi to the waterfall from Cheonjiyeon Waterfall. Plan to get wet if you get close to the falls.Better get there before is closes. Admission of course. Lady at information desk was very helpful. We took the Airport Limo bus for 11000 won bus # 600 to the Cheoniyeon Waterfall. Since I wanted to see as much of the south end as I could before dark I am glad we got to see these areas. Go to KAL hotel and take the Limo Bus back to the Airport for 11000 Won.

It's a beautiful waterfall. As described by another reviewer, there is a flight of stairs you have to descend to reach the waterfall. At the bottom of the stairs, you will have to carefully traverse across rocks if you want to get nearer to the waterfall to take a good photo with it in the background. Be sure to get good shoes to avoid injury as the rocks can be slippery. Not recommended for pregnant ladies or old folks, especially so when the rocks are wet from rain.
Must see stop in Jeju. Very scenic place, not too crowded. Have a museum nearby, not worth the visit
Waterfall falls direct into the sea. You can get so close and almost touch the waterfall. There's a little tent nearby that sells fresh seafood.

This was a great view. I was able to do it in less than an hour. Its a small descend( you will have to go up these same stairs to leave) to the actual waterfall. There were women selling seafood on the side. You can hear the waterfall when you get in the area. At the entrance there is food. And a 3 minute walk further there is an art museum. The waterfall itself was amazing. There was a lot of water coming down. And you can see it go directly to the ocean. Opposite the waterfall is the ocean.
Very easy to walk to. Eating places nearby. Very beautiful.  We had breakfast at Dunkin Doughnuts nearby. Cost is 2,000 won to see. Unique shopping near location.

This is the only waterfall that falls into the sea and it's awesome. The steps down can be a bit slick when you get  near the waterfall, but in the rainy season the waterfall is massive and a great view.

This was my 3rd waterfall visit in Jeju and my favourite, probably because the waterfall goes directly to the sea. Also, we saw some haenyeo (female divers) there and they were selling fresh sashmi seafood on the rocks next to the sea. It was definitely a very unique eating experience!
Liked: The waterfall was nice and good value at $2 entry.Disliked: It was VERY busy and you were not allowed to swim here!
A crowded place to visit during the summer but a lovely waterfall with clean amenities for visitors. Very family friendly, reasonable prices on tourist goods.

Walk down to the falls is quiet and serene. A couple of local women were offering the fresh seafood they have just caught for sale. One just need to pay small amount and the woman will cut up the seafood and serve it with some sauce. People will just eat it fresh like sashimi.To get bearer to the fall, one need to navigate through rocks. Care should be taken else one may fall or drop your camera of smartphone. We were lucky to spot a rainbow at the place where the water splashed on the rocks! This is real rare and definitely made our day.

We enjoyed our walk to the falls and took great pictures.  It is a beautiful area that is a national cultural heritage. There is a sidewalk that takes you close to the falls.  The waterfall drops 23m into the sea, this is one of the 3 major falls on JeJu island.  Well maintained, very clean and well worth a visit!
Our taxi driver brought us there and be our camera man, this is the only waterfall that meet directly to the sea water.

We enjoyed the experience of transversing the rocks to get to the falls. It can be a challenge though with young children. The feel of water vapour sweeping through your face and sitting close to the falls was great. I can't compare it with the other nearby falls as we didn't have time to visit those but we were satisfied with this fall. While heading out, there are a few hawkers selling stuff and bought boxes of Jeju chocolates and biscuits at really good price.

There are a lot of negative reviews basically saying this waterfall is just average. It may not have that 'wow' factor but one should not visit if they are expecting the niagra falls. The one valid complaint are the stairs, slightly steep, and the rocks that need to be traversed to get closer to the falls. One has to be careful when hopping and stepping from rock to rock. Also, it can be a bit crowded with picture taking tourists.I found Jeongbang to be a modest waterfall, but nonetheless very charming. Great pictures can be taken on approach and up close, right next to the pool where you can feel the freshwater spray. Turn your back to the waterfall and a nice ocean view greets you, with two small mountain isles off in the distance. For the more adventurous, there are rocks of all sorts to be found closer to the sea. Most visitors snap a few pics and leave, but hanging out by the sea for a spell was also quite enjoyable.  While the rocks won't be confused with the rainbow, it was fun to pick out unique looking rocks from the saltwater, but watch out for the waves!

The waterfall is not so large when we came, so we can walk up near to it to take some pictures. It is only a short walk down from the entrance, but be careful when walking on the stones as it can be very slippery and very crowded at times. The falls itself is very unique as it flows straight to the ocean and it cost only 2000 won to enter.
the waterfall is not huge but we can walk close to it. we saw 2 women selling raw seafood nearby which is a nice experience to have the sashimi near the sea.
This was a nice place to visit with the waterfall flowing right next to the ocean. It's a very short hike down but it's worth it to see the nice waterfall. It cost 2,000 won to enter.
Very nice place, quiet. During my visit not much of turist there, located within the city. I woul like to know, how is there durin rains...

Not spectacular but unusual that it flows into the sea. You can walk across the rocks to get really close and many did for pictures. Be careful though. Some women selling freshly cut abalone, sea cucumber, snails - raw! Just 200m away from the base of the fall. Ticket is affordable at 2000 won even for foreigner which is the good part about most of the sights unlike some countries which cost double or more for foreigners.Don't see any restaurant so drive into the city seogwipo food street for plenty of choices.

Went there in the morning via taxi. Not many people. Admission: 2000 won each.There are flights of stairs to climb down when you first reach, so imagine the climb back up once you are done. To get nearer to the waterfall, you have walk over many many many rocks. Not recommended to go after rain as it will be super slippery. However, I love this waterfall more than Cheongjiyeon waterfall. It is nicer actually and you can get closer to the waterfall (of coz getting passed the obstacles of rocks).Love it actually but no way near magnificent.
Don't waste your time on this one. Parking was bad, then most of the stairs were destroyed. I don't know if they fixed it but ask around for more information before you head there.

Jeongbang Waterfall was near our guesthouse and it was the first stop of our trip to the east of Jeju. You can climb through the rocks and take a photo in the middle the small pond, in front of the waterfall. The water spray catches the light and acts as a prism to scatter the light into rainbows..pretty
Cheap entry but a huge fllght of stairs to access and a "beach" with huge boulders. best to view from up top for free. Cheonnjiyeon Falls are much better.

Personally, this is my least favourite falls in Jeju.  Nothing special about it except that it is a fall that flows directly to the sea.  The walk down the steps to the falls are fine but I do not recommend walking on the rocks to be nearer to the rocks.  Kids and senior citizens should not attempt that is it is rather dangerous.  You can still see and take photo of the fall from a further distance.  Not worth injury during your holidays!

I saw this on a map that the tourist center at the Airport provided. It was within walking distance from Ocean Palace Hotel and was very nice with walkways, parking, souviniers, food, stores, all for W2,000!

I've never been able to go up so close to a waterfall that flows directly into the sea. You'll need to climb over rocks to go up near to the falls. I loved being so near the waterfall and the sea at the same time!If you only have time to see 1 waterfall on Jeju island, go to this one. Cheonjiyeon & Cheonjeyeon waterfalls were quite unimpressive in my opinion.

This waterfall apparently is the only waterfall in Asia to cascade into the sea.You can get up close to the waterfall, unlike Cheongjeyeong and Cheongjiyeon. Do remove your footwear and have a dip in the cooling water. I personally preferred this waterfall out of the few that we visited.
A nice venue to visit along your way - didn't see the divers but a pleasant stop off along the way as part of an overall tour.
This is to me the nicest waterfall in Jeju, having visited four in total as you can get close to it and see the waterfall right into the sea...Not grand but nice...

Located in Seogwipo, it is the only waterfall in Asia that falls straight to the sea. You may cool your feet in cold river water (or even the whole body if you brave enough). There are 3 women divers who offer to try raw seafood for 20 000 won.

The waterfall is said to be the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly into the sea - although it seems to fall into a cove, not directly into the ocean.  The spot is very touristy and busy, but is a nice waterfall in itself.  You can paddle in the water to cool off and kids love playing on the rocks.
It is supposedly the only waterfall in Asia that falls into an ocean. It's not spectacular but the setting is very beautiful and it is fun to play around in the cold water on a hot day.
it looks just like any other waterfall. this place can be skipped if you have other interesting places to go, or you can just stop over for a short while.

Jeongbang waterfall is a marvelous sight where you could see the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly to the ocean. The only minus point is how I couldn't manage to walk or hop well from one rock to another so that I couldn't get to near to the waterfall. Other than that, everything was good.
awesome view, loads of walking so be sure to be in your comfy shoes. loads of picture taking & as usual loads of tourists

I went there early morning on a sunny day - perfect for photo-taking. The wonderful view of the sea from the walk down was just a prelude to the beauty that was to come later. I was delighted to see that little rainbow at the bottom! If you're more gutsy (and have a good sense of balance), you can make your way nearer to the waterfall to feel the cool mist and enjoy the grandeur and the surrounding scenery. Not a sight to be missed!!
There is an hour long boat tour that shows you many of the sights, but was the best way to see these falls and get pictures for these Hallasan weary feet.

Have to climb down the stairs with 3 kids. Very challenging task & we need slowly go down the stairs. It s not that far. But the view & surrounding is worth it. The waterfall falls right into the sea. And i must say it is among the amazing sight in Jeju Island. You need to be very patience to get a good angle & picture. Need to get as close as possible & i think it s worth it. Pro's : Amazing waterfall (can take good picture)Con's : Crowded & need to make sure nobody in front of you (to take a good Picture).By the way you need to Pay for entrance.

Best visit in summer or late spring when there's more water in the river. It would have been more magnificant. Historical evidence shows that the entourage sent by the Emperor Qin to search for the longivity medicine passed by this place.

the view of the waterfall is great! however, many will get closer to the waterfall by walking through the very rocky area from the stairway. kids and elderly need to be careful and also to secure your belongings, if things were to drop into the rocks, may be hard to retrieve. ensure you wear proper footwear!
The water fall was rather small but the good thing is we can walk on the big rocks path and take an up close pic without getting wet.

Nothing really special to me as I don't really know how to appreciate small waterfalls :p Interesting as it's the first waterfall I've seen that falls directly into the sea. Took about 10 minutes to walk down to the falls. Be sure to wear proper shoes as it's a rocky shore, all loose stones. Spent less than an hour at the place.

Climb down stairs to reach this waterfall but the place is hard to reach cause no ground at all, have to walk on different shapes and size of stone to reach the waterfall. Only need to spend about 15 minutes here will do. Natural scene than Cheonjiyeon Falls that with man made paths.

A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.

there's nothing much to do. just walk a bit and you see waterfall right down to the sea. they said this is the only one in Asia. i did spend few minutes here. people who love nature and photography will love it here.
The waterfall that falls direct to the sea. Although not as majestic as I thought. But you can see rainbow where the water is falling, in a clear day.

It is a pretty waterfall, though not as majestic as I thought but the walk to the waterfall was not too difficult anyway. It is possible to do the 3 waterfalls in Seogwipo in one day - Cheonjeyeon, Cheonjiyeon and Jeongbang.
We viewed the falls from afar and the tide was out, so it wasn't so dramatic. We were glad we made the detour to see them anyway.

You will be enchanted by the beauty of this place. It's quite unusual to see the shallow stream meeting big ocean waves. You can come very close to the waterfall to feel the power of falling stream. Or cross the stream and walk along the shore, it's fun to jump from one rock to another. Or just sit on a big smooth rock and watch the sea.

This is the only waterwall that flows directly into the sea. To give another better reason to see this waterfall, you'll catch a rainbow where the water is falling, but only in clear sky mornings. It's beautiful sight to behold so it's a must see!
If you like to see waterfall falling into a sea, you cannot miss this waterfall. The place is rather crowded though... try going around the sunset because the scene is really beautiful.
This place is pretty kool, it's great during a hot day, cause it's a little cooler around the area, and it's pretty
The waterfall is amazing, but the steps to the waterfall are steep and slippery.
Worth a visit to this waterfall. The waterfall on one side and the sea on the others!

The Jeongbang Waterfall is one of the "Big Three" on Jeju. This one is particularly stunning as the water falls down over the cliffs to the beach below. You can get very close to the water (your camera will get wet) and get some stunning photos. There are good facilities at the top and the walk down isn't too strenuous.
the waterfall is the only waterfall that flows to the sea directly.
A waterfall at the ocean. Easily accessible. A 5-minute hike down from the parking lot. Can get crowded, have patience.

If you dont mind being slightly wet due to the splashes of the waterfall and the breeze from the ocean wind.. Well! that the place to go! you can get super close to the waterfall to take photos. why visit? that the place where the water flows from the waterfall directly into the sea!

The unique thing about this waterfall is it's by the sea. Do wear proper shoes as you would have to climb down stairs and rocks if you want a closer look at the falls. Like most attractions in Jeju, it was awfully crowded. Ap, one doesn't really get a chance to sit and enjoy the falls, which is a pity.
Well worth the walk.Words are not enough to explain the beauty, the sounds of thunder and the vision
Took cab from Seongsan Ilchulbong. Beautiful site for sea and waterfall. A bit crowded but worth it. About a 30 minute walk from hotel Little France.
Lovely view.  However u need to clinb endless stairs, which was horrible for me as I was using a babycarrier.  Nonetheless, everyone should visit, lovely views.

Well worth the small trek down.  Do a little rock/boulder hopping to the base and you can get a nice spray.  If you catch this waterfall during the rainy season or after a good rain it will be much more powerful.  Take the time to visit this place...maybe a little crowded but plenty of space to find your own spot.
This is 1 of 3 waterfalls on JeJu Island and the only one that enters into sea in Asia
Worth a visit if you are on the island. Beautiful.
Spectacular waterfall tumbling over the cliff edge into the sea

What can I say...I loved Jeongbang waterfall soooo much. I went there on one of the hottest summer days in July and it was absolutely amazing. On my way down, I was complaining and whining the whole time because it was too hot. But once I got down near the waterfall, it was really windy..almost chilly!!! Cooling winds lovely views...I'll go there again before I leave Jeju!

Impressive sight withthewaterfall ending directly into the sea, walking down to the foot of the waterfall can be challenging with the rocks formation and without proper path, so don't wear heels!!!If you want to get near to the waterfall, be prepare for a shower of blessings

Jeju 4-3 Peace Park educates visitors thoroughly about the Jeju 4-3 Incident which was really almost a genocide when Korean government and US military killed over 30,000 Jeju residents and tortured many more.  With Korea on the brink of dividing into two, Jeju residents wrongly suspected of being Communists ended up being victims.  The government didn't even go public about the incident until the late 1990's and only officially apologized in the 2000's.  The museum describes the build up to the incident and depicts all the horrible details of what the Jeju residents went through.  Having gone through grade school in the 1980's when the incident was not public knowledge, this was a very educational experience for me.

The museum and park are both really engaging. We learned a lot and enjoyed a family discussion on history and human nature. The park is really gorgeous and the entire experiences as moving. A highlight of our trip.

I went here on Friday 31.05.2019. The front desk staff were very helpful, the museum is really easy as there's arrows on the floor directing you where to go. There is loads of information in English, it's easy to follow and very informative. The island has some really sad history, for anyone interested in history, and the impact of splitting Korea, this is a must do. The information does not make easy reading, but you will never forget this story, and it's an important one to remember. The gardens have lots of memorials, and outside is a nice space.It's not a pop in memorial/museum, it's bigger than expected. I'd recommend 2.5 hours to do the museum and outside. Unfortunately I had to rush as I got there late in the day and wish I'd had more time, but I'm pleased I went, and got most stuff done. It's accessible by bus. The museum closes at 6, last entry 5, but I'd suggest you get there no later than 3.30pm to do it properly.For clarity, this is the 4.3 peace park on the east side of the island, as there is one on the west side with a similar name, I've no idea what that one is like.

This well set out and very informative museum recounts the history of how many of the Jeju islanders were killed and repressed during the late 1940s and early 1950s.  The visitor passes through a series of rooms, each explaining in Korean and English a different stage in the tragic events.  Apart from the actual events themselves, two things shocked me most.  Firstly, that I had never before heard of the April 3 Uprising, although some 25-30,000 people were killed by Korean government forces and their supporters.  Secondly, that even well into South Korea's democracy the events continued to be hushed up and only relatively recently has the truth begun to be told.  Just a few years ago, mass graves were discovered near jeju airport.  The museum provides such a valuable insight into the island's past that I think no visit to Jeju would be complete without coming here and learning about the events and their aftermath.  Entry is free of charge.  The peace park around the museum provides a place for contemplation after visiting the museum.

This museum is EXTREMELY well put together.  It is not often in Korea where you will find proper English translations.  This place does not disappoint.
