There is a wealth of knowledge to be found here for those interested in the sad history Jeju people have had to endure.  ProTip:  Make sure you take time to explore the outside part (the lands and the memorial wall). ProTip:  You do not want to rush thru this.  Make sure you give yourself enough time to really walk around and read about the history.  The museum covers almost 6 years worth of events and details!

The Peace park serves both as a memorial to the victims of the April 3 uprising as well as the long period of persecution of islanders that followed. The museum shows the background of the conflict, connected to the division of Korea, in great detail. It could benefit from more signs in other languages. But it does give a detailed and balanced look at the period and also mentions reconciliation in the future, in contrast to many other memorials in Korea, which only look at the suffering in the past. Well worth to get to the out-of-the-way Peace Park.

This was a very informative and extremely moving experience, which helped me to gain a greater understanding of the Jeju people, and why, even today they see themselves as 'other', having a separate identity from the rest of the \korean people.
Jeju April 3rd Peace Park  - really a peaceful place to visit. Walk through the small exhibitions to understand it better.

I was there to lead a Sacred Circle Dance event in memory of the 4-3 Massacre, which was the most touching and powerful experience of group dance and solidarity. The following day I witnessed an amazing dance performance (Kim's troupe) as part of one of the services offered that week.- also touching. The level of art is very high. The architecture of the buildings speak loud and clear. Not to be missed - approach with reverence, and you too will be deeply moved.

Jeju is not only beaches and shopping malls, but has also a really interesting history ! This memorial is part of this history and helps you to understand the island but also Korea better.They have english translations of most presentation boards in the memorial, so you don't need to be able to read Korean to understand this visit.The explanations and the context they gave about the uprising of April 3rd are really captivating and well presented.I highly recommend to go there !

I moved to the U.S. (from Korea) 26 years ago when I was 15. I have been coming back to visit almost every year in the past 15 years or so and visited Jeju five times thus far. I don't get to take long weeks off from work, so I always try to pack as many activities into any given trip, so I squeezed this one in on my way back from a day trip to Udo (which is my favorite place in Korea). I wanted to pay this place a visit because I came to learn of what 4.3 incident last year, and I didn't want to pass up the opportunity to learn more about it.The memorial hall was very well organized with plenty of pictures, exhibits, and videos to see. My 16-year-old kid, who almost never bothers to read through anything at museums, was taking photos and reading through the exhibits, which I found impressive.My appreciation for the island (and its residents) grew tenfold after the visit to this memorial hall. Government run, the Jeju Peace Park is set out over a large area with a variety of things to see. The main building contains a movie theatre, a cafe, information desks, and amenities as well as the main museum. The museum itself contains not only an amazing arrangements of information, exhibits, artworks, detailed memorabilia, personal video stories and recreated scenes of important sites, but also photos of the lost, current excavation efforts and modern artistic representations of the era. There are several other building that house additional memorials and scenes that are both emotional and historic. It is very worth a visit or two and should be given the time it deserves.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying "oh my god.." I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.
It is very sad history has in Korea.But, it is a been boarding.I like this place.Because I can know Korea's history and first time I feel said when I touring Jeju island.

This was a building to commemorate those who perished when an uprising was brutally put down.  It is part of Jeju's history and should interest history buffs. As we're not history buffs, we just paid a short visit here in October 2016. The building was of fair size and the surrounding park was quite big, but not much to see. It has a serene atmosphere and a solemn place and reminds me of a cemetery.  We saw lots of local school children visiting when we were here.
Not on the main tourist route but this is worth a visit. Offers a look into the history of Jeju and it's people as well as a beautiful park.

I  read about this peace park in Lonely Planet and asked to go there. Our local guide had never visited there before but said he would definitely take people there now. It took us a while to find the right way to go in- lower floor. On the first floor there was a beautiful photo exhibition but the museum is the real attraction. It tells the story of post World War 2 Jeju and  especially about the massacres by different sides of politics. While the museum focuses on Jeju it provides a real insight into the sources of the 1950s Korean war and the division of the country. The USA and its military commanders certainly contributed to the problems and the terrible suffering of the Jeju people.   I highly recommend Westerners to visit this place and the labelling in English is very good.

The Peace Park is very spacious and beautifully laid out.  (Shouldn't compare but it reminded us of  a smaller version of the National Memorial Arboretum in Staffordshire, UK.)  They were still working on some landscaping while we were there.   We were lucky enough to catch the excellent art exhibition that is on at the moment and the museum display is very well laid out and informative - lots of English  so we learnt a lot about the Jeju's history around 1948.   We were there about 1.5 hours but could have stayed longer.
An interesting museum that was extremely well catered for English speaking tourists. A part of history that we knew nothing about and was moving to hear it from the perspective of the people of Jeju.

This museum is well worth the trip and it's FREE to the public. Very informative and emotional. This museum will not disappoint. I was so impressed with the honest representation of Jeju history. This museum incorporates works of local artists to help tell the stories and are very well done and effective. The staff was very kind and helpful. You also get a great book for free when you visit. My visit here was very moving and I would recommend it to everyone. Very impressive!

You can reach this place with Jeju tour bus - if you're going to the Roe Deer Observatory as well, I suggest you go there first and then walk downhill to the Peace Park (less than 10 mins). If you do it the other way round, you'll have to trek uphill. The admission for the Peace Park is free and everything is in English. The museum offers a comprehensive account of a controversial point in Korean history: some exhibits are quite chilling and upsetting but I think it's important to understand the history of this island: Jeju is not all about tangerines, erotic statues and kitschy teddy bears.

It was a piece of history on this beautiful island that evaded many visitors. Thankful for the immersion tour so I know a little more of the Jeju islanders on their pain & their desire for reconciliation & peace!

The Jeju Uprising/Massacre (or simply 4.3), with up to 80,000 villagers killed by the military, took place just prior to the Korean War but is relevant today as South Korea re-militarizes the Island of Peace. Go to the museum, then witness the current hot protests against a naval base being constructed in the fishing/farming village of Gangjeong (between Seogwipo and Jungmun), along the Ollie Trail.

Went there because I heard it's a good place for silver grass view, and I was welcomed with a full mountain of beautiful silver grass! Wear comfortable shoes as the oreum is quite steep. Below the oreum are some food trucks selling snacks, good enough to fill your tummy after the steep hike. It might not be easy to locate this place, as the phone numbers I key in the GPS failed to bring me to the correct place. Finally able to find this place by searching for "Everis Golf & Resort" phone number, and managed to see "Saebyeol Oreum" at the highway signboard. Try searching for Everis resort if you can't locate saebyeol oreum, as they are just next to each other.

We really enjoyed this hike with our family. It is steep, as the reviews noted, but it is very fast. Our five-year-old and seven-year-old had no problem doing it on their own. It has nice views, isn t very difficult, and it s right next to an interesting coffee shop (you can see it from the parking lot) that has been converted from an old horseback riding resort. The coffee shop also has a bakery with some delicious treats for after the hike.  Easy to find and plenty of parking.  Overall a great little outing.

Sabyeol Oreum definitely has lots to offer especially for tourists/foreigners. The stunning view from the top of the hill is obviously something worth to be explored, and the best part of it is that you don t need to pay anything to experience such aesthetic view! It is a flexible place that offers different kind of experience depending on the seasons, and it does not take much of a hiker to climb it. Not only does it not take long to climb to the top, the paths are also significantly safe. Near the place, you can also see some horses without having to pay for it, and there are lots of places where you can take good pictures! If you are coming to Jeju, I believe it is a must visit place that you should consider in your itinerary!

I first heard of Saebyeol Oreum when watching Hyori's Bed & Breakfast, and I really wanted to visit this famous oreum. The hike was insanely steep, and we huffed and puffed to get to the summit (520m above sea level). The view from the top was breathtaking, and the eoksae (flamegrass) covering the entire oreum was absolutely gorgeous. We were lucky to catch the magnificent sunset, and it was a great end to our Jeju trip. Highly recommended!

This is one of my favorite oreums (volcanic hills) on Jeju!!It is not exactly close to anything so be ready to travel quite a bit.  It is also a steep hike, but each step that takes your higher gives you more and more of a view. I am telling you the negative up first but I am also telling you...it is worth it.  *On the weekends (depending on the season) you will often find coffee trucks parked at the bottom parking lot.  You cannot count on this as they come and go...but if they are there, it will be a nice treat for you.*This oreum is also host to my favorite festival in Korea.  Jeju Fire Festival.  Thousands and thousands of people come to this oreum to say goodbye to the past memories and to welcome spring.  It is a seriously amazing event.  Fire, fireworks, food, beer, shopping tents, performances.....absolutely a fantastic event.

The Jeju Fire Festival (now renamed the Field Burning festival) takes place every year and is a huge celebration, with music, dance, enormous quantities of food from many different places. It is on The last evening that the Oreum (hill) is set fire to.Allow plenty of time to get in and park (shuttle buses from Jeju city are probably a better idea, as it can also take an hour or more to get out with your car afterwards.

Well, I think in fact if you go up the pathway at the right it's easier. But in fact you are supposed to go up on the left side and come down on the right. In any case, if you are able, it's quite an experience going up and should try it the tough way! It's beautiful throughout, up you'll have a magnificent view.

If you like quirky and somewhat kitschy glass sculptures, you ll love this place. If not it s not worth the relatively high ticket price. It s a nice outdoor area and some lovely walks. It ll be also fun for kids I guess. But it was a bit too much kitsch for my liking.

My kids loved this place I was sort of disappointed in the gift store I wish that there were more of the things displayed that you could buy, but the actual displays were quite amazing lots of good photo ops.

I visited Jeju Glass Castle last winter. I went there twice while I stayed in Jeju for a week. The first time I visited, the weather was good and so my family walked around the museum with joy. We were very glad to be there. The second time, I was very thrilled to visit again, but unluckily, it was raining. Our family struggled to see the sculptures that were placed outside. I recommend that you go to Jeju Glass Castle when the weather is good.

This place is such a gem   literally – awe found it by accident and were blown away. Seriously one of the best parts of the trip! Highly suggest as a couple or with friends. (Solo is fine too, honestly)

amazing trail in the woods like walking through a fairy tale! lots of glass ornaments, lighting,  this place is probably most beautiful and vibrant in the sun with all the reflections; we were there during a rain, but still very cute

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though very floral and colorful girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts,  I am in Jeju!  or  I am in Korea!  for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.
Pretty to kewl to check out what they did with glass. Still fascinating to see them make glass art work right in front of you.  Got to see numerous glass art work from different countries...

We visited the Glass Castle with our grandchildren. They had a great time running through the forest full of glass flowers and animals, there was a multiple mirror room, It is a bit kiche, it shouldn't work but it does beautifully.

It is quite expensive with 12.000 won per adult, but you could easily spent 2-3 hours and it is nicely set up. Of course the glass castle has a lot of romantic photo ops for newlyweds. But also their little hiking trail is nicely decorated and I loved all the wind chimes. You could do glass blowing or get your picture in glass. They have snacks and a coffee. Overall a nice little theme park.

The Glass Sculptures are very beautiful and creatively made. I've never seen anything like this before, so, it was worthwhile. Couldn't believe that they were all made out of glass. Recommend visiting this place if you've never been.
Only the nude glass sculptures were interesting. They saved the day. All the rest was quite dull and boring.
there are display of recycle glasses. Glasses are recycled and made into flowers, fishes and others.

There are beautiful indoor and outdoor displays of blown glass in a variety of formats.  The indoor display includes masterpieces, many by the Italian master, Signoretto.  The outdoor displays make for a great walk about through a beautiful park-like area.

This was a first time visit for us...and we found it to be cheesy with a capital 'C'. However, who would have thought that CHEESY could be so COOL!!!!Yup, we had fun here...the place was amazing. Nature in harmony with recycled glass and plastic. it's very well maintained, good to spend a few hours here taking pictures...as well as soaking in the various exhibits on display. I particularly enjoyed the walk in the Enchanted Forest, a bit creepy though...as it was secluded from the rest of the complex, and this added to the excitement of being in the forest...talk about a vivid imagination!They have a shop selling souvenirs as well, clean restrooms and a cafe. I would recommend those looking for some fun to drop by here, and just let your inner child run free!

I have been here several times, I really do enjoy it.  It is just an easy and fun way to spend a day. Lots of photo opportunities.I see they occasionally offer glass blowing classes. I have never done this, but it is on my list of things to try!ProTip: There are 2 stores filled with glass items for sale.  Some tacky, but mostly rather reasonably priced gift ideas. Plus, lots of  cool looking jewelry.

The entrance fee is 11000 won . Worth a visit if you are in the vicinity . I particularly like the salmon Swimming upstream , the glass flower garden and the Pinocchio like town in the dark room. The glass forest panel is also unique . This place will look fantastic if visited at night.

I don't think anyone is taking care of the vanue well enough. Everything seems to be dirty so the glass is not shiny. You really have to be into glass to enjoy it. Kitsch is the king here. Not worth the ticket (11.000 won)

Was not so keen on coming here in the daytime as I wasn t sure how the glass sculptures will turn out. Was really glad that we came after all. It was really amazing how the artists are able to sculpture glass into so many different sculptures and with colour. Some of them do not even look like glass. The glass was well designed with meandering paths which showcases the sculptures in different settings. Well Worth two hours or more of your itinerary.

Our trip in Jeju was turely a great one.  We had an excellent driver.  Mr. Kang from Jeju Day tour ( Hi Jeju Taxi tour) provided us with amazing taxi service. He also recommended good places with reasonable prices. He is very friendly and patient with us.  We were all satisfied and will surely go with Mr.Kang if we happened to visit Jeju again. Highly recommend. Thank you.

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.
The ticket entreance fee is 11,000 krw!!! Please do go if you dont want to regret. Too expensive with nothings special there. Its juz only like a forest with bad maintenance. Too dirty.

I thoroughly enjoyed the Castle. I got to try my hand at glass blowing  (I'm not very good) and found the detail in the pieces amazing. You can wander around at leisure, take as long as you like (I was there for 2 hours). There's a short 500m walk at the back you should do if able, there's all sorts of surprising pieces hidden in the woods.

For 11000krw entry per person, we expected an eye opener and an attraction different than most. Upon entering, we can see from the number of glass exhibits on display that this place would've been a great place to visit for couples or families.Beautiful display with intricacies that you will need to understand to appreciate. The displays look quite challenging to maintain as there are so many glass objects that could be dulled due to weather conditions. Aside from that, we appreciated the effort it would've taken to create this glass wonderland and enjoyed it extremely. Even in the wintry snowy condition we were experiencing, although this is an outdoor exhibition, we enjoyed it!Would recommend 1-2 hours at a slow walk pace with many photo opportunities.
The displays are nice and beautiful you can also have a personalized glass item with your name and picture which can be delivered to your hotel for free.

Place kinda small, outdated. You will probably like the outdoor more than the indoor. You would walk through glass sculptures illuminated at night. So recommended to visit at night. There is a workshop where they will help you to make your own glass work. It is also a great chance to learn glass work.
This is the special place, have more glass decoration. But the decoration almost look old. if you have time you can go to see.
A very nice place to visit, beautiful installations that are perfect for photos. Will be pretty warm if you visit during summer since most of it is in the open.

Soooo pretty! Absolutely stunning glass sculptures and the trail through the forest was an absolute highlight of my stay in Jeju. The glass tangelo trees must have taken FOREVER to complete and they were so well done. Loved the little farmhouse in the forest and the huge glass spider webs. So peaceful looking out at all the colours across the lake. Definitely recommend this place for something a little bit different.

Jeju Glass Castle houses collection of glass arts. The glass arts are tastefully arranged in different areas of the park, most of them outdoors. The forest trail is the most interesting area. Best to be visited in good weather.

After having been to quite a few of Jeju's museums...this has to be the most boring and way overpriced.  It should be charging 2000KRW entry. ..not the KRW11,000 each we paid!  All the extra stuff you can do inside costs extra, you can only see so many glass flowers and glass baubles before it becomes boring!  We went in the day time.  We had lunch there first.  I would suggest that people get lunch in the nearby restaurants .... much cheaper!  The food was good but not a great choice and double the price you'd pay locally.  Perhaps this place is better at night but even if it was the price is still too high.  I wouldn't bother taking kids here either.

This place of interest has a very large estate in which you can almost spend close to an hour walking all of it.  It was interesting to see how glass can be made to be all kind of artifacts.  The place is located in a area where other place of interest are closely located too so add this to one of your visit if you can.

Small confession: it's the only museum we've visited in Jeju so I can't compare it to others and say it was better, BUT the museum is great. It was something new and an interesting experience even for my parents who are in their early 50s. Overall, I do recommend you to go there. FYI: there aren't places there where you can refill your bottles with fresh water.
The entrance fee was quite expensive, plenty parking space, have a few interesting activities for visitors to try with fees.
This is a very lovely place. I really enjoy it! Especially all the outdoor display. Feels like being in a fairy tale story.

The place itself is huge. We went before lunch and it was a good time because the sun was up. Being a glass museum, most of the art are made of glass and having the sun at its brightest made the art look even more amazing. It's nice to look at the reflections made. There are different signs in Korean, Japanese, and English. They also have shop where they sell little glass artwork. You can bargain with the sellers too. They're nice and friendly.

I was staying last week at the Shilla in Seogwigpo, and this was just a short cab ride away. Despite the slight morning drizzle, it held the attention of my 20 year old son! There were enough wow moments - spider web, Jack's beanstalk, mushrooms, football, dinosaur eggs, slippers... all made of glass, of course. I'm sure they would have looked even more impressive at night with the lights on. The cafe was worth a stopover -- you must have the freshly squeezed tangerine juice there. The souvenir shop sells some nice pieces of glass jewelry and ornaments.

The exhibits were pretty interesting actually but as mentioned in the title, it's a mainly outdoor venue! The glass sculptures look better in the day time or at night when the lights are on.. SO..! If the weather is not helpful, save it for another day! It's pretty far out, so if u are gonna go, do the O'sulluc tea museum and this together... Don't leave too late coz it's terribly difficult to get a cab, unless you have a pre-arranged driver. That said, the staff there really are very, very nice.. We were actually the last few patrons out and we were stranded without a cab, in the bloody freezing rain.. We had 3 ahjussis trying to help us call cabs and eventually one of em offered to drive us to the nearest bus stop instead coz no one was responding, and FYI the nearest bus stop is abt 10mins out too..

This is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall, garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These are six themed model parks jn which over 250 models are exhibited. These include glass qrt masterpieces by international famous artist from Italy, the Czech Republic, Japan and more.At least one hour explore the entire exhibitation garden. Visit at night as the place is well litted and less tourist.
we went in the evening and i must say it is really beautiful to see the glass sculptures lit up at nightnear the dinos, there's a forest walk... super exciting in the dark

I am a resident of the Seattle metropolitan area so I have to compare it to the Chihuly Garden and Glass museum.  The Jeju Glass Castle is very different in concept as it also focuses on small to medium sized glass items.  Conversely, Chihuly Garden and Glass focuses on large scale items produced by Chihuly in small quantities.  That's not to say it was disappointing, but it wasn't that impressive in the sheer quality of the items.  However, you do get a very large variety of glass items from throughout the world so it does make it up in quantity.  Unlike the Chihuly museum, the glass castle is a very large complex.I did notice the museum seemed a little run down in a few areas - it really did seem it needs some upgrades to its infrastructure.  However, there is a maze, nicely manicured gardens, glass shoes, and a large variety of other takes on glass items.  There is also a nice trail to walk that showcases certain glass items as well.Perhaps the most interesting part of the museum is near the entrance.  You'll find a glass making room there with windows you can look through to see glass artisans at work.  It was quite interesting to see these people create glass items by sculpting it, putting it in the oven, and more.

Jeju Glass Castle is the famous place at Jeju. When I first went inside, I just like walk in an unreal place. Since the entire thing is made by glass. You can see glass everywhere, such as the flowers, the trees and the artworks.One of the special things in this castle is an artwork that calls  a moment of musical concert , this artwork show that the moment of a band that is performing. The entire performers have different emotion and music instruments. It is very hard to do this, because each performer s face is smaller than a coin.Here also have some funny place, such as Glass labyrinth and distorting mirror. Be careful, maybe you will lose in the labyrinth, or become a fat boy/girl in the distorting mirror.Finally, I suggest that you need to be very careful in this castle, if not you will break the glass.

At 10000 KRW/entry (+ discounts, if you know where to find the coupons) it can be a bit pricey for some.But I personally liked the place. It was just full of beautiful glass sculptures. Almost everything on display was glass. It required a certain amount of walking, but it was definitely worth it exploring the compound. There was even a short pathway through a mini "jungle" that had a Dinosaur theme to it. Weather that day wasn't too good and it drizzled quite a bit, making it a rather gloomy day to go about, but there were so many pretty, sparkly glass sculptures to see, so I felt that this trip was worth it. Only the area was more open-space with very little cover, so we had to stay indoors for a bit.

We visited on a dull wet day but even then there was plenty of sparking glass to see.  Everything you can imagine made of glass.  I loved the mushrooms and pumpkins and some of the weirder sculptures.  On a sunny day it must be even better.  Great place to take kids and, except for woodland walk it is all accessible for people with walking problems.There are examples from different parts of the world and you can watch craftsmen making things - and even book an experience to try it yourself.

For only $10 (10,000 KW) you can spend an afternoon wandering around a carefully manicured small park that exhibits outdoor glass work. As you walk in there is a place to watch professional glass blowers blow bottles in the traditional way, and if you are taking a school group there, the kids can have ago at making something, and then return the next day to pick up their handiwork. After that you follow the path around the exhibits until you get to the other end.In this mainly outdoor museum, there are glass plants, flowers, and an eclectic collection of glass made curiosities that make a very pleasant way to spend a couple of hours. There is a small cafe in the middle of the exhibition, and the gift shop just before you exit. The bathrooms are at the entrance exit, so go before you start!
it memorable experience in my life, seeing things all made from glass, and get to see glass roses, glass the ring,cinderella shoes, and carriage.. a special moment in my life
It is interesting place. There are nice garden from glass. But I think it would be better if you visit at night so the color of glass can shine more. It would be nicer.
This might not be for everyone, though if you like stained glass you'll love this place! Lots of stained glass and other glass art. Very pretty and playful.
Very nice place to visit with kids. Many nice background for photos too ;) i would recommend this place for visiting.
Excellent place for picture taking. People who loves picture taking will enjoy here. I love the effects of each glass/sculpture/exhibit

It is a park consist of many statue and also plantation made from glass. Yes. Glass. Also museum where we can learn the making process. It is quite nice as this is my first time but I don't think will revisit.

We went here on our way to south jeju.It was a nice place where we can see the various art forms possible with glass.A sculpture of a horse made with glass was displayed, which was really looking cool...

My 6 year-old girl loves this place sooo much. We enjoyed walking around & taking photos of all the cute things. Too bad, we didn't have enough time for the activities like glass painting, glass blowing. (We spent around 30 mins walking around the place.)

When we arrived at Jeju, we took a taxi to Jejueco and left our luggage with time since check-in time was in the afternoon. From Jejueco we took a cab down to Glass Castle and managed to reach there before 5pm.As its name suggests, the Glass Castle is a glass art theme park that consists of an exhibition hall and garden with everything made out entirely out of glass! All in all, there are 6 themed model parks with over 250 models exhibited: they include the world s largest glass ball and largest glass diamond, a glass stonewall, a mirror lake, and a glass bridge etc...The exhibition was definitely a breathtaking sight to behold: glass displays made of all kinds of shapes and sizes! We couldn't help but be amazed and ended up taking - pictures of all the art pieces. For more on the experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/glass-castle-jeju.html

Jeju Glass Castle is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall,garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These includes glass art masterpieces by international famous artists from Italy,The Czech Republic,Japan and many more. This theme park suitable for all ages. Very cold due to winter season,do put on more wear as you need to walk round the outdoor.

Jeju Glass Castle is a must see museum. It has outdoor which can be seen with in 2 hours & indoor as well. There are a lot of glass shapes. This museum is good for people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. The entrance ticket is little bit expensive.

There's an entrance fee, that's one . It's very far away from where we stayed (Gujwa-eup), that's two . A pretty large castle with grounds littered with many colourful glass decorations of animals etc. If you take a walk into the garden, you will also find colourful glass figurines of insects and animals nicely arranged in the park to create a fairy-tale like experience for the kids.

It was just perfect vacation for me & my friends. We always dream of cruises holidays amnd just had a blast on superstar gemini cruise. Entrance Fee is 8,000KRW but our driver manage to get some discount for us.The idea is creative and brilliant. Everything is made of glass and its really beautiful. You can't stop but keep taking photos in every part of the place.

A group of us, 22 in number, visited South Korea from 13- 20 April, 2014.  One of the highlights of our visit was to Jeju Glass Castle. We went to the Glass Castle on 15 Apri;, 2014. Also, they have quite limited displays and very few look special to us. We managed to see all displays in about 20 minutes! Overall, we were completely underwhelmed by this place. If you are interested taking photos, there are opportunities for some nice photos. For others, there is nothing to learn and experience anything new here. There are other nicer museums or sights to see in Jeju, so this can be safely avoided.

It's good for what it is.  Some people have been calling this place a glass museum - it's not.  It's a theme park for glass.  I say theme park, but if you're thinking rides then you're wrong.  What they do have is lots of things made out of glass to see.  It's pretty and often colourful.  My female partner enjoyed it more than I did, and there's nothing there that would make me want to go back.  I think children might get a little bored by the place, although girls would probably enjoy it more.  As far as adults are concerned, if you think it sounds like a place you'd enjoy, then you probably would.  But if you think it sounds kinda boring then you wouldn't enjoy it.

A unique theme park to visit. Just love the colorful displays of glass.  This theme park has an outdoor and indoor displays of everything made in glass. The park has 2 parts..indoor and outdoor.It just like walking around a garden that full with glass sculpture. Nice view. Worth a visit.
Love the theme park.  It has exhibits of glass sculptures indoor and outdoor. The whole place is so colourful. You can enjoy all the glass work in this beautiful theme park.

One of the best location that i went to while i was in Jeju. Highly recommended for theme park lovers and those with kiddy heart hehe. I love Jeju so much for the uniqueness of this castle. Fancy, colourful and happy place to be!

We went to the Glass Castle in spite of the 9000 Won entry fee simply because of all the hassle we had gone through to get there. If you have young children forget it, there is almost nothing for them to do without spending additional money for them to make a glass craft. The crafts are neat but spendy. Lots of cool trinkets to get for gifts and souvenirs - of special note are the hand painted, hollow, personalizeable, crystal balls. If you are up to the trip and willing to pay the cash to look at glass art go for it. Otherwise, there are other more interesting things around to do.

After the Jeju Love Land, w/c is a X rated (for adults) theme park. Funny, unique, it's a theme park that you will never find in any other country... This is just a regular museum with a small collection of glass from different parts of the world. It is far away from everything and not worth the trip. I would skip it.

I though this show was good but expensive.  It has lots of energetic routines and was fun but I wouldn't choose to see it again

This is my second time I see this Nanta Show. The first time was in Seoul couples of years ago. Each time it never failed to amaze me. Very exciting and energetic show played by 5 showmasters. My cousins and I went traveling through South Korea and while we were on Jeju Island and we decided to go see Nanta! I had bought tickets 2 weeks prior to our trip from TripAdvisor. This is one of the best shows i have ever watched! My family and I enjoyed the show so much. I think its really worth the time and money spent! We took VIP tickets from Jungmun Tourist centre  at 50 percent off. The show is very entertaining and involves lots of interaction with the crowd. The show was hillarious and interactive. It is so entertaining. You don't need to know korean to watch this show. Mixed between acrobatic, dance, comedy and music

Very entertaining and funny. They perform with body language so we can understand the story easily. Recommended and must see when you visit Jeju.
I visited with a large group of teenage girls and we ALL loved it :) The performers were funny and because it is action there is no problem with not understanding this Korean show.

This is a must see! An awesome show in Jeju that is very popular around the world. It has Korean culture involved which makes it even cooler. Hardly any talking but you can totally understand the story throughout the entire show! This show had my attention the entire time! Don't want to give to much info to ruin the surprise but I would definitely recommend this if you visit Jeju.

This show is highly recommended as it showcases the traditional beat and a fun show which can be enjoyed by the entire family. A shuttle service can be arranged at the ticket office after the show for only 1000KRW. There's a nearby park which you can visit before the show.

We caught the Nanta show in Jeju and it was such a fun night for the family. It is a combination of comedy, musical, martial art and drums. My family and I watched this show only knowing it is a non-verbal performance and wow! It was pretty good! I think little kids to the elderly will enjoy the performance for it is wacky, straightforward and attention grabbing. Would recommend to anyone and everyone.

It's a great show and worth to have a visit if you are going to Korea! The show is very interesting and you may have many chances to interact with the actors if you are sitting nearest with the stage like me. Great & awesome show!

Nanta is like the korean Pride nonverbal performances. It's fun and defiantly great if you have kids. It's not the best nonverbal performance out there, but Jeju has regular showings and the tickets aren't the pricey.
The ticket is a bit pricey, but worth the show you get. Entertaining, funny and universally understood.

Get the VIP seatings as a 10,000WON (10 USD) is well worth it.Engaging and entertaining, but priced a little too steep for the "random sound making" performance.(: However, do still recommend and definitely added smiles and laughter to the trip!

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.
Very awesome and funny hahahahaha!!!! Can't stop laughing becauae of this show. Once again it is very amazing!!!! Spectacular!!!

The story lines are the same, but the performers changed since my last visit in March 2013. However, I really enjoyed this show again! Heard that NANTA Jeju is better than the one shown in Seoul but I cannot justify that.

Saw the show with a group of friends, one of whom was selected for the audience participation segment.  This increased the enjoyment for us, but the show was entertaining anyway even for non-Korean speaking people.

Worth spending the money and time to have a good laugh. Even the kids were laughing loudly. Not much talking but many actions. They speak good English so not a problem to understand.I was even being selected to go on the stage to perform with them!! Unforgettable!
The team who entertained us were the yellow team. I was thoroughly entertained by them. They were able to engage with the crowd.

This is a fun and interactive show that would be great for families with members of all ages.The VIP seats are more expensive, but you have the chance of being picked to participate in segments of the show. If this is not important to you, choose the regular seats as the theater is not very large anyway. You can get a 5,000 won discount if you reserve tickets through YEHA Tours. Then pick up the tickets on the day of the show.Instead of an intermission in the middle, a cast member does some interactive clapping and stomping with the audience.The City Hall downtown area is a 15-minute walk away from the theater. You can find restaurants and shops there.

This is arguably the longest running South Korean LIVE show ever!  Now, it is branching out to other popular tourist destinations such as Jeju Island.  You needn't understand Korean language to appreciate the show, which is leaning more towards physical action and slapstick comedy based on timing.  It revolves around cooking.  Nanta show is leaning heavily towards satisfying tour groups and the day I was there, two thirds of the theatre was filled up by tourists that came in bus loads.  Nanta is interactive too, with occasional involvement with the audience.  Children thoroughly enjoyed the show.  It was pure 90 minutes of unadulterated fun and enjoyment.  In terms of price, you can get cheaper price booked through YEHA website.  Commendable fun:)

We paid for the VIP seats, KW10,000 more than the standard seats. When we entered, noticed that VIP seats were in red right in the centre of stage, while standard seats were on both left n right sides of the VIP seats. Worth paying the extra to be at the centre. They also choose guest from the VIP seats for participation on the stage. Show was hilarious, enjoyed by both young and old. Even my 4 year old child was laughing all the way to the end. It lasted 100 mins, try to catch evening show instead of night show during winter a the hall would be freezing at night.If you have not seen this, include this show in either Jeju or Seoul.

We were glad we could catch this show in Jeju as time in Seoul were simply too precious for shopping. It's funny and you don't need to understand Korean to enjoy it. All 3 of us including our 4 yr old enjoyed it. It' a plus to have that cute lady in the show as well. Show time is 90 mins but not a dull moment. We got our taxi guide to reserve the tickets on the same day and only manage to get the VIP seats at w60k each. It would be better if you can reserve the ticket days in advance.

A fantastic show a must see in Jeju. Lots of laughs and you don't need to understand Korean. We brought our tickets at the show, which was full by the time of opening. They were very talneted actors. The show has been done in numerous countries around the world
It make us so excited! We love it and hope to see it next time! It is the most fantastic show I have ever seen!!!
it's a value for money show, the performers were 찼ll out' during the show, u can feel their passion & fun, not be missed
As the only show in Jeju (while in Seoul have 3 theatre) so always full. Interesting, Fun & a Must see Show.

Performance was mediocre and unprofessional, did not meet up to expectation. Theatre is small and unimpressive. Also, no food and drinks were allowed in the theatre when the show is during dinner time.

Nanta Show was like a famous tourist attraction. I decided to see it while in Jeju since there was nothing much in Jeju anyway. The theatre wassmall but cosy. I seconded the previous review that 80-90% are all China tourists - They were noisy and some even tried to leave before the 90-min show ended. But we were here for the show so please yourself as the show was really entertaining.
Theatre is small.  No much spectator interraction. 90% of the audience were from mainland China and we felt like we were in a China Theatre as they speak very loudly.

These cliffs formed when Hallasan erupted and lava flowed to the sea. When the lava hit the sea, the contrast in temperatures caused the rock to form hexagonal columns, giving us this beautiful view! This is a really neat sight to see, but you don t need to linger. It s a great place to stop on your way to the waterfalls. Parking is cheap and plentiful.

Jusangjeolli Cliff, designated as a natural monument of Jeju Island, is the largest columnar-jointed lava in South Korea. It was formed due to the sudden cooling of lava from the Hallasan Mountain, which erupted into the sea of Jungmun, thousands of years ago. Witnessed a picturesque view of the sea and the cliff. I recommend not wearing any hat or cap when you visit Jusangjeolli Cliff as the wind is strong there.

I've visited this place many times and every time I love it. So pretty, the best view and a really nice garden as well. The only downside is the strong wind so I don't recommend any hats and warm clothes!
The best part of my entire trip, this attraction was so beautiful, calming, and overrall an amazing site. The view was amazing, and it wasn't overly crowded.

We were amazed by the hexagonal shaped columns of the cliff here. There are well-maintained boardwalks that one takes to the cliffside. We were there around sunset and the views out into the ocean is superb.
It was a cold, sunny day, but the landscape in this area was just awesome!  There is a boardwalk lookout point where different landscapes could be viewed on each end.  Definitely worth checking out!

Another spectacular volcanic rock. Is a beautiful nature creation. Cold and Windy when you visit this place during winter. Nice places for photography. Is also the filming scene of the famous Korean drama "Dae Jang Geum", where Lady Han of Dae Jang Geum passed away.

Magnificent view formed by molten lava.View is nice when high tide, crowded during noon, so try to reach there early to avoid crowd.Discount for youth (need to show passport)There is also a pampas grass field, situated at your right side once enter the booth of Jusangjeoli cliff parking lot, can walk in the field if you have no time to visit Saebyeol Oreum

This is a geological wonder of Jeju - the cliff is a volcanic rock formation made up of vertical pillars shaped in cubes of hexagons. Amazing view as you walked along the trail. Tickets are at 2000 won per adult and 1000 per child/youth. Also do explore the area at the foot of the cliff - just take the left trail at the main entrance (no tickets required for this path).

The cliff was very beautiful and unique, and is definitely worth a visit if you re looking for nice sightseeing views in Jeju. However, other than viewing the cliffs, there was nothing much to do, so spending an hour or less there would be sufficient. Do head down the viewing platform to the bottom of the cliffs, where you can get a magnificent view at sea level, with lesser tourists there. Overall, if you re looking for a short sightseeing trip, these cliffs would be a good option to explore the wonders of Jeju.

You must pay for 2000KWR/ adult for entrance. It has natural beautiful. Comparing with Ghenh Da Dia in Phu Yen, Vietnam, It 's not as good as Genh Da Dia. But i think it's still a good place to experience in Jeju. It nears KPOP Play, TeddyBear Museum and so on

I was staying at the Lotte Hotel in Jungmun and decided to go for an out door walk to enjoy the beautiful weather. I was walking along the coastline and it eventually lead me to this attraction. Although it is wonderful to see these unique rock formation, this attraction is rather small.
We enjoyed the visit to the cliffs because they are such a unique geologic Geologic. There is a beautiful view of the coastline and a statue garden.
This attraction is located minutes drive away from Jungmun Beach. Slow down your pace as you admire this amazing natural cliff formation.

Beautiful views of the coastline and the cliffs.Part of the walkway to the viewing platform was closed due to the recent typhoon, so a lot of visitors were gathered on the main viewing platform. The park itself was not very big, making it a pleasant, easy stroll.
The view of the row of natural stone is very good. The scenery around is also very beautiful. This place is worth a visit when you are in Jeju island.

Very interesting cliff!Maybe a bit overpriced, however.Main cliff access with fee, but you could also may view a similar cliff for free from left side of the park.Better to be there as early as possible, otherwise there will be many visitors and you'll spend a time for to make nice photos or selfie.Good park at left side, for free and nice - just walk by track by coast and you'll always see the sea.
Nice cliffs, but wouldn't go to this part of Jeju just to see this by itself. I'm not sure what the 2000won goes towards as there's only 1 crowded viewing platform.

The cliff itself is really pretty, blue water crashing on rocks looks nice, but there is no nature experience there, you walk on a concrete path, see the cliff from a platform and that's it! Not sure why you have to pay for it (entrance fee and parking). Maybe if you have never seen a cliff before this could be a nice experience.

Spectacular geological formations and scenery.  It really is quite unique. It's easily accessible and there's a nice small park around the top.  There's a path that can take you to the portion of the shore which is nice and not many people go to.  Jeju let's nature take center stage and they do a nice job getting you access.

The cliffs are beautiful and wondrous. Be sure to go very early as there will be less visitors then. Once the tourist buses come and go it will be difficult to move around. You can get there by walking from Jeju International Convention Centre and going out the back door into the park and walk towards the left side of the park for about 10 minutes.

We were staying in the Lotte Hotel Jeju and it was not too far to walk to this sight from our hotel.The view is a nice one, probably not as impressive as the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but interesting nonetheless.Definitely worth a visit for the coastal scenery but doesn't occupy much time.

For 2000w you can walk into the park. The lookouts for the rock formations allow great photos. Similar natural rocks to those seen in Ireland. The park has some Jeju stone statues otherwise not much else to see. The parking was free.
A counterpart of Giant s Causeway. It s part or along the Olle trail of Jeju. The viewing place is not that big, but if you are visiting Jeju, it is worth visiting.

Must Go - Don t Miss this. It a Great View - The topography is amazing, Make sure you have the Fresh Orange Juice which the stores prepare very refreshing, actually there is a lady who sells fresh oranges if you are lucky :)
A must go place as you can see how the lava formed meeting the sea. Be prepared for strong wind but spectacular view

It has a beautiful view,only a short distance though.But overall very pretty However when we were there,there were a few bus full of tour so it was a bit cramped.However still beautiful though,there were also many attractions around. It opens from 9 so don t be too eager and come at 8.
With cool weather.Like a park with natural occurrences.With a romantic atmosphere.Going with family or boyfriend is very good.Is an interesting tourist destination in Korea.

Jusangjeolli are stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju Island. Jusangjeolli Cliff was formed when the lava from Hallasan Mountain erupted into the sea of Jungmun. There is a admission fee and parking fee to enter this place. We reached there by car the other day and it was an hour journey from Seogwipo city.
It's not an easy feat, walk about 2 km round trip filled with stairs. There is a 2500 Won enterance fee. 3 waterfalls and a huge bridge
This was part of our Yeha bus tour - South Course - and it is a beautiful cliff formed by lava.  Such beautiful views!!
Well made wooden stairs lead you all the way along with the cliff line. Octagon shaped stones are amazing over the clean blue ocean. You ll be taking tens of pictures over there!!

One can have a magnificient view of basalt stone pillars formed along the coast due to sudden cooling and solidification of the Lava which flowed into the sea. The sudden contraction of molten lava due to the cooling effect of water has resulted in these rocks splitting into polygonal columns and forming a coast of almost 2 km long.This attraction is worth the visit and can be reached directly by trekking from Cheonjeyeon falls or taking a bus and pass thru the garden (Jusangjeollidae Promenade) and then reach the cliff at the end.Walking around the garden would be relaxing and one should not miss it. Wooden Platforms have been built to reach the end of the cliff and for a better view of the coastal line.
What makes this cliff so unique is the hexagonal shapes of the cliffs. Unfortunately, you can t really get close to it but admire it from a distance.
Another natural wonder in Jeju. Easy access from Seogwipo city. This is close to the Seas Resort& spa

I had to see it for myself to believe this natural geological occurrence. There were diagrams and explanations at the site to describe how these lava hexagonal structures were formed. Hard to visualise the geologic event but simply amazed at the outcome.

Went there with the intention to educate my kids on how lava could flow to the sea and came up with beautiful natural shapes such as those seen there. Great to have educational information nearby to explain the formation.  More should be done to explain how small stones also play a part in eroding pitfalls on the rock surfaces It was an easy walk from the carpark.  Some local snacks were sold at the entrance and tickets could be bought via a machine.
3 km stretch of cliff showing lava columnar along the coastal shoreline . Lava columnar rise in a speculator manner .
The rocks are beauty made by nature. It is formed by lava flows but the shapes will leave you to wonder on how it is formed. There will be some steps to climb up to view the cliff.
Geography lovers, don't miss this!  Just awesome...very beautiful!Those driving, the gps number that leads you to the convention center is wrong. Choose one that leads you to coast (not buildings).
This landmark is very well maintained with beautiful structures. Very instagram friendly. Location is also pretty near many places like teddy bear museum, several waterfalls and casino resorts.
Well maintained and a good place to visit. View is phenomenal. There is some climbing to do so be prepared.

The cliff is formed from lava flow. Hexagonal basalt columns like those in Ireland. It is interesting if you have not seen this kind of formation. It will be interesting if you could visit during high tide and high waves as the crashing waves may reach all the way to the top.

We went there twice on the same day as it is within walking distance to our Seaes Resort.First we went during the general time when other tourists all come the same time, which was still ok for us because we somehow could find a good spot for taking photos.Tips: don't wear black or dark grey or another other dark colors if you want to pose in the photo, unless you want to disguise as a rock formation yourself.After checking out the place we decide the best time is to return at around 6pm to tke the sunset view which was truly amazing. We visited Ireland and the Giant Causeway in Iceland before and must say the sunset here in Jeju is much more likely because of the weather, and is so much easier to visit (although the scale is smaller).More tips: When we arrived at 6pm, one would be intimidated by the tourist crowds at that time but hang on to it and stay longer if you can. The crowds probably were restricted by their guide and car, just quickly left just BEFORE SUNSET ( tours!), or some individual visitors also left right away, leaving the spot empty for a truly memorable experience.  I did my yoga there freely in the sunset until the door guard finally swept us away, about 20 min after sunset

This is my second time here. On my first trip, we can't get close to the cliff because of strong waves. This time round, I finally get to see the unique rock formations that made this a unesco site. A few photo spots in this area. I think 30mins viewing time is enough.

This place is really good. You can see the cliff right beside the sea and it s really safe to walk at the walk area. The view is really nice but there are a lot of stairs. So it s kinda hard for old people and for family who use baby strollers.
Would not take up much time here as the viewing area is very limited and congested with travellers scouting the area to take a good spot & photo. Worth to visit.
A must visit to this attraction . Entrance fee is 2000W . Short and easy walk to the cliffs . Expect to spend around 30-60minutes here if you want to take photos .
The attraction is not very large. There is a charge of 2000 won per person, which I feel is expensive as compared to other natural wonders in Jeju. Still the views are nice and unique.

We walked to Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff for almost 30 minutes from Cheonjeyeon waterfall. it was worth it. We can witnessed the picturesque landscape of the nature. We had to pay 2,000KRW for the admission free. Easy access to the lavatory. Easy trail for walking.

The place reminds me of Cliff of Moher, Ireland, a famous movie scene from 'Leap Year' movie. We went during summer, it was pretty hot however, the breeze did balance the heat. This is a must to go place!
Recommended to visit when you go Jeju Island. The view is amazingly breathtaking. We booked for a private tour for 1 day and bring us to different tourist attractions and good foods as well.
The Jusangjeolli Cliff is a beautiful geographical site with lava rock formations against the beautiful ocean. Great scenery for pictures and a relaxing stroll along the boardwalk.
If you're new to volcanic rock formations, this would be very interesting. It helps that the view of the sea water lapping against the rocks is beautiful too!
A very enjoyable place to walk around and watch the waves. If you have limited time on the island, it is definitely one of the places that's worth visiting and doesn't take up much time to see.
Special geographical zone & it is interesting to visit.  But, if you have been to other bigger lava column sites such as The Giant Causeway, you may skip this one.

If you've never seen hexagon rocks [I don't know what they're called], this is a pretty neat place to visit.  There are stairs and viewing platforms with smaller platforms you can stand on to get a better photo.  There's also a big park at the top where you can see the rocks from different angles and just enjoy the park.

One of the more outstanding attractions on Jeju Island. It was raining almost everyday while we were on Jeju Island, but the day we visited this cliff, the clouds lifted and we had a beautiful view of the cliff. The entrance and the rest of the park (the area surrounding this cliff) were very unassuming though, and to a certain extent, poorly maintained. Don t waste time hanging around those areas, just head for the cliffs straight away!

God s beauty with unique rock formations and the waves crashing. Short boardwalk to see the beauty. We bought a bag of oranges and explored a bit more on the side paths but it was so hot, we didn t enjoy that part as much as cliff viewing.

Amazing rock formations. We spent about 45 mins at the park. Its a very well-pathed park with some stairs; suitable for most people. We went in July and it was super hot. I'd recommend going either early morning or an hour or so before sunset.  The adult tickets are krw 2000 each. I think it's a fair price.
Breathtaking! Enjoyed the walk and picturesque view. Really enjoyed the view. Entrance fee about 2000 won for adult and 1000 for kids
A vista point for your Cheju trip. Showing the typical rock formations. Photo opportunity you should use.

The hexagonal basalt columns are similar to what you see at the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but you can't actually walk on them unless you try accessing them from a park further down. There is a well laid observatory path which takes you through the best view points to view the structures. Very touristy when we were there so it was a bit of a mad house but worth visiting when in Jeju.

Perfectly symmetrical columns of rocks stack on top of one another. Must see for geology/volcanology students ( columns were cooled-down volcanic lava). Located within few minutes walk to the Changjeyoun Falls.

Although there is not a lot to do here, it is a short walk from the parking to see this absolutely beautiful view!  If you take a few minutes to watch the water swirling around the cliffs it will mesmerize you, so pretty!

It is interesting to see and then read how did these lava columns came to formation. It s worth a quick walkaround. Place is not big so it gets pretty crowded but people are understanding to disperse so that you can have a chance to take some pictures too.

The day I visited Jusangjeolli Cliff, the place was crowded with group tours particularly students on education trip, so had to virtually jostle for a good spot to get some views of the cliffs, which were really a classic example of Mother Natures numerous works bringing us all her beauty.
In this place you can see the interesting formation of stones, made by the volcano. The place has a beautiful view of the sea, and also has the juices of the oranges of Jeju .. a good walk.
The place is very scenic, enjoyed the blue ocean view and hexagonal stones makes it a different experience.
This is a great place to visit on your way to somewhere. Worth about 30 mins of your schedule. See the formation and learn how they are formed.

This is a nice place to have some scenic shot. The natural volcanic formation is indeed unique. The walk from the carpark to the scenic view is just a short 10 Min slow stroll. There are amble carpark but there are many tourists too. If you don t stay at the cliff to absorb the nature then the entire place can be done in just 45mins. So if you are here, don t rush so that you can enjoy the wind and listen the waves hitting into the cliff!
This place is amazing. I was awed by the dark rocks and the beauty of the sea as it splash to the rocks. They also have a park where you can spend chatting and picture-taking.

Ah what to say, it s an okay place to visit but not that spectacular and you have to cue and wait to be able to take a picture. It s interesting too see the rectangular pillars in the sea but you can t enjoy it really because people are pushing to take a picture. I was a little hungry so bought some local oranges there, 10.000 KRW for 5 oranges from a very unfriendly lady. I guess you can expect that at touristy places but it does not particularly make you happy.

The place is very organised with well created pathways to see the rock formations. However, the place is really quite crowded and it is hard to take photos because of the amount of crowd there. Everyone was just walking along the path and there isn't much space to move around. That being said, it is still quite worth it to pay it a visit.

Very nice spectacular views of the scenery. At times it was truly majestic.We went there while on the walking olle trail. Had a nice walk with some amazing views along the way.However as usual, there were quite a number of tourists but still manageable. Had to pay 2000 won entry fee

Its still raining in Jeju when we arrived here. No regret walking in the rain and climbing the stairs when the view welcomed u so wonderfully beautiful. Spend at least 1 hr here to absord the view inside ur mind and take it home with you. Also try the grilled octo sold infront of the entrance. Yummy!

We went on a very rainy day so there weren t many people.     The white seafoam crashing against the rock was amazing.     The formations were breathtaking.     Information given in English about how they were formed.      It doesn t take very long to walk the trail, no more than 30 minutes.     There are toilet facilities and a couple shops with limited food and other items for purchase.   On a nicer day, there would probably be a lot more vendors.

The place could get quite crowded, however, the rock formation was awesome, take a slow walk and enjoy the breeze. I visited this place with my mother, there are some stairs here and there, but it is an easy track, she doesn't have difficulty at all. Amazing Scenery

The main attraction is just a short walk from the car park. Tickets can be bought from a machine so you don t have to queue. The walk takes one through lovely art structures like dolphins, boats and conch shell. There were canola flowers just before the entrance of the walkway. It has to be the right season or you will not see them. The cliffs themselves are amazing. They look like sculptures done by the hand of an artist. A row was cube like, another was like honeycomb. At the other end were corrugated pillars. Be careful not to sit on the parapets as the wind is super strong and there are large crowds, you may fall to your death if you are not careful. Hold tight to your umbrella or headwear. Best not to use any. Young children and old folks will be able to handle this attraction, the walkway is constructed well and not hard to climb up or down. It is also very short. Good view of the ocean and pines.

It is an excellent trail which allows one to have a breathtaking view of the sea and the rocks formation that is created by the nature. However be prepared for the mosquitoes attacked for those who are prone to their bites as there are army of mosquitoes during the autumn when we visited in October 2017. But the view is worth it as we are also able to take fantastic photos of the sunset view.

It was a bit difficult to find the site even asking a hotel staff for directions.  I was not prepared to pay admission but did so since it was minimal.  Took a lot of pictures of the ocean and lava rocks
An excellent walking area with beautiful views and interesting seascapes.Trails were accessible and facilities were clean and pleasant.

I really cant say much about this. I believe that the being the largest columnar-jointed lava deserves a much better critique, but sadly not from me.In this trip, I realise something about myself which is i am just not a person who likes rocks, which is quite ironic when Jeju is known having abundance of rocks. Lol. So if you like great sea scenery & rocks, pls, do come here and be awed by nature.
scenic and windy. crowds were in the hundreds so it can get squeezy. good place to go for pictures if u have the time
Special view on how the cliff formed in square and you will amaze with the nature beauty of this place as so far I didn t see the same in countries I have visited.
Came here around sunset and it was beautiful. The lava columns looked very impressive with the sea waves hitting it.
It's a great place with great view. The breeze bring peacefulness. You can walk around and enjoy surroundings as well. Nearby attraction is reachable by bus.

We need to pay for the entrance fees, but it is not that pricey. Then, we need to take a walk to the main point to see the breathtaking view. It is very beautiful as we barely describe it. It is really a wonder of nature. The view and the pictures that we take there is really worth it. Highly recommended and we will surely repeat to visit this place again.

No admission fee is required. The weather was sunny with a little breeze during my visit in end of winter season. There is a walk way to the platform that bring you to the cliff. Scenery is nice and you will be amazed how nature created such beautiful cliff. If you taking public transport, take any bus to Jeju International Convention Centre (the local call it ICC), from there walk about less than 10 minutes by the road side you will see the sign board to the cliff at a T junction. There is a park and is a good place to picnic with your friends or family.

This is a beauty to behold. The site is really breathtaking! We visited the site after our lunch, it was a sunny day yet it was very cold due to the wind. The site is famous destinations, many tourists come and flock to the cliff, that is why patience is very important if you want to have  good solo and group photos. My Jeju visit was complete due to this wonderful, amazing and lovely cliff. The blue sea is just so enticing. The sound of the waves was mesmerizing and the arrangement of the stones in a unique and beautiful shapes are indeed a beauty to behold. This must be part of the bucketlist for every tourist who will come to Jeju.

There's parking place but there's a fee to pay around 2000 won for my rented Kia Sportage   , Entrance fee was 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for youth . We walked around the park nearby the stairs leading to view the cliff from here .

The cliffs are interesting to see, but the site is very touristy. It can become incredibly busy even in the winter season. It s 2000– pax to get in and you have to pay for parking depending on vehicle size ( you pay when you leave the site). It s not really all that much money and keeps the site clean. This is a quick stop on Jeju probably 20-30 mins and worth it, but if you have seen Giants Causeway ( Ireland )  or similar rock formations in Iceland or NZ I would skip it.

This place is extremely beautifully especially during sunset. The rocks are carved by water to different shapes. Nice view of the ocean with a well maintained garden. It is 5 mins walk from international convention centre.

ON the winter time it is better to go in the morning as the sun still arise. It is beautiful. There is some ahjumma who dived looked for seafoods in the cold water. "Daebak" Cool!! as the temperature could be below 0 degrees or even minus. My eyes even already tear up because of the cold wind. Overall I loved it!!

The place shows very nice rock formation, although it was eroded after so many years. It was still awesome. Nice view with a boardwalk to the observation point. We were lucky and saw some Haenyeo diving there. They could really hold their breath.
My 10 yo daughter and I enjoyed walk-in around and taking pictures of the beautiful scenery and ocean. We spent about 45 mins here. Cost 2000W to get in for adults and 1000W for children.
Blowholes were small as compared to New Zealand s Pancake rocks. But view is beautiful, a small park outside with shops around. Many attractions like Teddy bear museum are just a walking distance.
I would recommend others to spend an hour or so in this site. Spend good time with wife strolling the path and of course, took some beautiful pictures.
It was awesome to think that nature created these remarkably artistic cliffs.  Sure, you d have to jostle a little with the crowds to get a good selfie.  But it was worth it!

Beautiful view from the cliff and surprising rock formations. Went on a rainy morning so we took our time and walked around a lot too. Snacks from the vendors near the front gate were tasty. The entry fee and parking was 8,000 KRW for a family of 5.
There is really nothing more amazing and intriguing than nature. How could such shapes come to being? It was just amazing, incredible.
Lucky to visit on sunny day, was slightly crowded but still managed to still the cliff. The volcanic structures were very interesting and you can see the clear blue water.
This is where you get to see the volcanic rock formations by the ocean! It is beautiful and stunning. The walk was nice and breezy. Would highly recommend for anyone who can walk.
These rocks are truly remarkable and will make you feel grounded and very in touch with nature. Be careful of the tide!

This place is quite overrated when the cliffs aren't as majestic and huge as can be seen in pictures. These are lava columns that hardened upon meeting the sea and formed into pillar-like structures. Going into the platforms was easy, not too much hiking but after seeing it, there's not much to see or do. Beware of the shops nearby and try to haggle before buying.

This compact section of Jeju's coastline has lots of pillar rock formations (similar to the Giant's Causeway in Ireland). The walking path was crowded but people moved quickly so it didn't take long to see. Don't miss taking a pic with the massive shell by the entrance!

Very interesting sight with polygonal rock columns from cooled lava. There was a platform for viewing and a thrilling jet ride and sailboat rides. We probably spent only at most 15minutes there. An easy and quick climb.

Advisable to go in the morning as it can get very crowded with tour groups by afternoon. The walkway above the cliff area was a little narrow, where only 2 rows of people can walk at the same time. However, the view was breathtaking. It was an amazing experience to see how Mother Nature created such an intricate formation with volcanic rocks which is similar to that of a beehive.
