My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs   Jeongbang Waterfall   Oedolgae   Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw   it s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform  railings We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

There are so few places in the world which offer this columnar basalt formation, and even fewer in such a scenic location. This is the best spot to view these gorgeous formations along the stretch of coast and nothing bets watching the surging ocean smash against the rocks - it's hard to believe this is simply the result of rapidly cooled magma and not some otherworldly creation. My heart still tells me mermaids have something to do with it! Make sure to take a snack and just sit and be humbled, it can get a bit crowded on the viewing platform but everyone is in such a hurry if you just sit back and take it all in you will find you have this wonder of the natural world to yourself in no time!! An absolute must do!!
We went on a wet and rainy afternoon. The cliff was dull and unspectacular in such weather conditions. We parked at The Seas resort carparked and strolled through their beautiful landscaped grounds.

We took bus 600 from the World Cup Stadium. This bus is also the Airport Limousine. We got off at Jeju ICC and walked from there towards the sea. The geometrical volcanic rock formation simply took our breath away!  Who cut/shaped the rocks this way? A fantastic work of art created by the Master Craftsman. Another wonder of nature. The geometrical shapes were amazing! This is - must-visit site!

Once you walk up the stair, you will see the local shops which sell food snacks and fresh oranges.   You need to walk inside pass the garden then you will find a stair and walk way to see the scenic view and the stone point which it's the attraction there.For me it's too crowd with people with limit waking space. Since there were many tourists there. The view is not but not much interesting. It's good for one time visit. And it's just a corner walk to see it and back. I'm not sure it's worth to come in case you stay far from this area

Overlooking the cliff from the viewing platforms, the formation is indeed unique and a beauty. Walk along the surrounding path, we get to see the different angle of the cliff and the formation.However, you can omit the park. It is just an added attraction due to the price paid for the entrance.
This place was amazing because you can see the real volcano stone. We saw this on the boat and so great.

We followed Trip Advisor's map and was brought to a small hotel garden area. We were iniatially confused but the hotel staff pointed the way to us. It wasn't very far already. We took our time walking, and to tell you the truth, I was glad we came the way we came. We found a way down to the rocky beach and climbed a little right to where the waves break. At that point the rocks aren't geometrical, just normal. Afters we walked thru a garden, which was a good distraction, and finally arrived at the cliffs. To my disappointment we can't actually go down to the rocks. And then there were a few shops selling fresh seafood, postcards, ice cream, mandarin oranges and to my surprise, some hallabong oranges. I got it pretty cheap too, compared to other places that I went after that

Rock formations on the coast with goemetric patterns as though machine cut by man!Nice at sun setting into the sea. Walkable from ICC and we just stumbled into this place when we went for a stroll! Pleasant surprise indeed.

A nice stop on the yeha bus tour, a lot of tourists so it easily gets overcrowded as the observation platform is small. Nice walk nearby with a small park next to the ocean. Pentagonal and heptagonal rock formations from lava cooling down. Enjoyed it and do recommend if in the area!

The volcanic cliffs are nothing spectacular. Just some natural formations with fixed shapes. It s a been there done that thing. Worth a visit if you have never been there. The entrance fee is not expensive. Think it s $2,000 Won per pax.

Okay so we went to the address given by Tripadvisor, and to our astonishment it was just a small garden behind a hotel. The only reason I can think why it was set to that address - is perhaps there's free parking? Dont give up if you're there! Because the actual site is only about 800m further down. There's a walking path (goes uphill from the hotel garden) along the coast, so simply walk along that and forgo the stone garden (needs an entry fee). The actual cliff site is open to public and free for viewing..Path is quite family-friendly.
It is wonderful and interesting with rectangular stones and beautiful landscapes. Interestingly, you may find woman divers nearby and you may like to each fresh raw seafood there.
The cliff is amazing with a nice park to walk around. After the stroll, we visited to ICC duty free shop for shopping.
It is really amazing to see these formations.  Small fee to park and see the formations, but still super cheap, and well worth it.m you can see it all in a half hour.
Though the sight may be spectacular, the site of the cliff is actually very small, but it's nice to walk around the park.

My view is totally different from the rest of reviews on trip advisor.I actually wonder if I had went to the right place. I was expecting a entrance fee, but we were free to walk around the hotel gardens for 10-15mins till we reach the edge where u get a clear view of the coastal line and jungmum cliffs are.This jungmum cliff is supposingly behind a hotel garden, so if ur GPS brings u to an hotel like my 2 GPS (provided by car rental company), apple map and google map did then I got the right place.I saw some cliffs, strong sea waves smashing against it....... Eh huh???? There were 2 other couples (one from HK, another from China), all of us was having the same reaction... This is it????? .Was quite a waste of time especially after I drove round and round for almost 2 hrs looking for it, didn't knew it was behind a hotel garden.

We were dropped by the bus at the parking lot, and had to walked through a beautiful park where seashell statues and boats placed along the path. We have to queue for about 20-30 minutes before we could really see the amazing nature-sculptured cliff.It was very beautiful, especially at sunset.
Formed by volcanic ashes, the cliffs were indeed an interesting place for a visit.  The surrounding park added to its ambience for a pleasant stroll.  Worth a visit.

If you have been to Giants Causeway in Northern Ireland,  you will want to stop here too. Same hexagonal basalt columns that are only found in a few places around the world. It's a quick visit as you view from a platform and walkway.  Entry is only 2000 KRW. Even the people in our group who have not been to Giants Causeway enjoyed it.

Jungmun-Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff is beautiful place where, look at huge waves crashing against volcanic rocks, one can experience the power of nature. With so much to do and so much to see, the Jeju island is certainly one of the most prominent tourist places in the world. Just about an hour's flight from Seoul, it's a paradise for nature-lovers and surfers. There are countless world class museums offering education and entertainment based on themes like Glass, Ice Sculptures, Trick Art, Folk Lore, Health and Sex, War, Art - the list is endless. Best way to explore the Island is to take taxi tours with a driver who speaks and understands little English. They ask for W150,000 for 8 hours, however, you may beat them down to W115,000 or so. For sightseeing, 5-6 days should be enough.

This place is a must visit. We visited this place in late afternoon. The viewing deck was awesome as you really can view the rock clearly. There are  information display on the viewing deck explaining the rock formation...very informative. At the time of our visit the wave was high...and unexpected by us and the rest of the visitors who were busily taking photos.. the wave  splashes on the viewing deck...making those near the deck  wet...it was fun though :-). Though a bit wet we really enjoy the view and the amazing rock formation...It still amaze me how the rock can be form like that naturally...
its really diffiicult to believe that they have been so well carved by nature. a beautiful natural wonder.

Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.
Nature's art. Rocks cut as if by a human sculptor. The place is nice, Well organized. Well built wooden decks and bridges bring you to excellent viewing and photographing spots.
A beautiful spot of commanding good view of the sea and the rocks of special shape lava formed on cooling.

The ocean waves against the beautiful volcanic rocks are just so amazing. The island is gorgeous and so much to see and do. We enjoyed going further down the beach to go into the water as well. The pineapple & tangerines are awesome.

The hexagonal shaped rock is crystallized lava.  For some reason the literature doesn't state this.  It is very hard material and when the waves are big (e.g. a typhoon passing by), the waves are fascinating to watch as they crash and interfere with each other in the U-shaped channel.  Tourist boats don't come near for obvious reasons!  Best is to see the park itself.  The formations are visible in places for several kilometers, but this is the best single place to see them.  They are very tall -- tallest I've ever seen.  The park is government operated, so the entrance fee is just 2,000 KRW (about $2).
You can have a very picturesque sight from special viewpoints.But unlike in Vietnam Ganh Da Dia you can go down and be closer.

Very cool place to take some nice pics.If you leave the area where you have to pay and walk torwards east you will have different coast lines where you can acces the lava rocks and walk around on them and as well take some pics they look like you landed on mars.

I and my family visited during late June 2015. There was a little bit of rain that day but the path to the cliff was still accessible with problem. It was a scenic walk. You can reach the main entrance from the Jeju ICC by walking about 5 to 7 minutes. There is a cheap entrance fee to pay to go inside the cliff. Even under the light rain, the view was so magnificent. We stayed there for about an hour before leaving. If the weather was better, I bet I would stay longer.I probably will visit again next time in Jeju.

we visited this place with little or less expectation as many friends had said it too overrated but to our surprise is pretty awesome. Maybe because there was strong wind and rain the waves were very strong. The waves were hitting almost the observation point. We bought rain coat outside the cliff entrance for 2000wons (2$) and trust me its best decision we did. We were showered with water like anything as there was rain and wind. maybe in other season you dont need to worry aobut it. the phone number listed on site took to the parking lot the resort next to cliff, had to walk a bit to reach it but got to see the resort common area with some nice garden and statues!
Very easy and accessible walk. I wish I had more time to enjoy it, but since I got there about 30 minutes prior closing I had to rush.
Arranged to visit it in the day but our tour guide suggested in eveneing... when we reach there in the evening, I can totally understand why... The sunset is beautiful...

Had an awesome day here last week, awesome place for walking and photography. It was so nice to get out of the city and see some of the countryside. I think this is one of the most rugged areas, my kinda style of image. I dropped business for a few days to come here and it was worth it. If you have the change, like hiking or are a photographer. Go!

Bet ya you have never seen this before! Its real touristy but well worth the walk. From the convention centre on the east side the first road down to the sea. You can't miss the busses. Taking pictures is best in the morning because of the sun. We went at 16:00 and the sun made it impossible to take good pictures. Got a crappy camera so that could also have something to do with it. Another tip is to follow the olle trail to the east from here after about a 1,5 hour walk (through beautifull orange plantations and up and down tracks paved / dirt) you'll get to the Yakcheonsa Temple. Get from there to the 600 airportbus back to where you came from.

It was a dream come true to see these beautiful hexagonal columnar formations made of lava. Also, seeing some haenyeo (women free-divers) at work near one of the lower cliffs was a nice addition. After walking along the paid promenade, we ventured down a steep paved hill to the left of the entrance (where you'll see a big conch shell sculpture and some big maps). After going down the hill, we walked along the large stones to the right, then up the large lava formation, and saw the hexagonal shapes up close and personal. What a cool little gem to find! We were the only ones there!

While in Jeju, another worth seeing place is Daepo Jusangjeollidae, where stone pillars (columnar joints) are formed like cubes or hexagons of various sizes due to volcanic lava and are piled up along the coast. One can walk down to the special platform to take pictures of the stone formations, but it was crowded with tourists when we were there. The view of the sea was breathtaking and one can see the waves hitting against the stone pillars. Truly a unique and wonderful experience!While we were there, we saw a local man ordering fresh sea cucumber from the lady seller. The sea cucumber was sliced and then eaten raw with chilly sauce. It seems like it is a common practice among the locals to eat raw sea-food such as sea cucumber, abalones, shell fish and sea snails in Jeju.  There is also an information counter inside a building near the park and one can request for a Tour Map of Jeju (Jeju at a glance) with information on tourists attractions, shopping in Seogwipo Olle Market, the Intercity Bus Routes and contact numbers for tourism information and transport information.

Jeju Island is indeed a unique island with so many gorgeous scenery, i had a great time travelling there in Winter, a low season with lesser tourist gives a different experience from visiting it in busy Summer. I have seen pictures about Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff ( ъ＜©₩由) and was amazed by the neat shapes of hexagon stone pillars formed by volcanic lava, i totally recommend tourist to spend time walking around the nicely design olle trail in the beautiful, as well as to visit Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff during your trip in Seogwipo or Chungmun area. you don't have to plan for a long stay, a good two hours should be more than enough, as it was just a viewing spot rather than you can actually walk-in and visit. Don't worry about the transport, bus services are available (in fact it is very convenient to reach most of the travel spot around Jeju island), just drop by Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and walk about 15 minutes to the park entrance, bus drivers in Jeju are very friendly and can basic communication woudn't be a concern. there is a entrance fees of 2000won in the park.there are steps to walk down to have a clearer view, description board with picture will explain how the hexagons shapes are formed, you can take amazing pictures and enjoy the sea view too.speaking of the weather, i have quite an experience, it was sunshine at first while i was taking the bus, and soon it become heavy downpour and even snow flakes begin to attack me during my walking! i think an umbrella or raincoat is necessary for either bright sunshine or unexpected rain. i gotta say, Jeju Island's weather is unpredictable! although this is not a spot to actually feel and touch the pillars, it can be quite boring to certain people who expected more attraction, but seeing the amazing cliff, the neat pillars, it was totally worth it to witness it by your own eyes, even the finest artist surrender to this piece of art, isn't it?

After a fulfilling breakfast, the first stop of our Jejueco tour was the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱©₩由щ ) along Jeju's Jungmun Daepo coast, columnar joints (stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju island) which were formed from the volcanic lava from Hallasan mountain. The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱©₩由щ ) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱©₩由щ ) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. So if you want to exercise and take in the scenery at the same time, this is one scenic route you can take.Read more about my experience and photos at my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/jusangjeollidae-columnar-joints.html
You can see the rocks near in the beach and enjoy riding the horse. Maybe 20,000 won for 30 minutes.

It's a dramatic coastline, just like blocks of puzzles stacking on top of each other. It's a unique sight. The entrance fee is KRW2,000 and the overall walk is easy, takes maximum 15-20 mins including photography. The sea water is clear and you can actually see the formation from below.
You would believe these rocks are the art work of mother nature until you visit it. We saw heayon (women diver) in action near the cliff. Good place.

I always wanted to visit the Devils Postpile National Monument in California. It is a surprise to find Columnar basalt on the seashore of Jeju-do, South Korea. One can walk behind the Sailboat ladders to take a closer look at the Columnar basalt. If you have time, you can stroll along the park to enjoy the beautiful seashore.
Unique rock formations, but you will see them quite from a distance. Too many people around. Good in Summer for a short walk, nice breeze from the sea.
A definite must-see when in Jeju. The columnar formations were absolutely gorgeous. Unfortunately it was a little too crowded when we were there but the view was gorgeous with the crashing waves!!

This is a very interesting coastline with hexagonal rock columns shooting from the water. It is very unbelievable that nature created these columns, since they actually look man-made. It is 2,000 won per person for entrance fee, and it is totally worth it. The only regret is that it is so famous, so it is packed with tourists. The endless blue ocean, dramatic coast line, and the unique stone pillars make this one of my favourite attractions in Jeju.

This was seriously one of the coolest things I've ever seen. The waves crashing against the rocks was incredible. I went on a rainy day and that didn't take away from how amazing it was. Since it was rainy it wasn't that crowded. I stayed longer than many people though. I just couldn't believe it. Stay longer if you want. Definitely try to see this in Jeju.

It costs a few thousand won to get into this attraction. BUT, I highly recommend that when you get to the area right before the ticket office, walk left instead of right. You'll be at a free beach with some very cool lava formations. My friend and I were able to climb the lava formations without a soul around. All of the tourists were at the paid location, so there was literally no one on the other beach (and it was a 1 minute walk from the main area. Why was noone there??)

The cliffs are a real sight to visit. You can see the nice natural rock formations, and the beautiful blue sea in the background. A really beautiful and peaceful place which we were told transform itself during the different seasons. There is a 'resident' painter who is there the whole year round and he captures the beauty of the place in all seasons and during different times of the day.
In case of typhoon, many tourism spot close in Jeju island, South Korea. In that case enjoy the beautiful scenery of waves and the 'breaks of water' See my picture too.

Here at the Jungmun-Daepo Coast, you see the very unique and naturally beautiful Jusangjeolli!These are basically volcanic rocks that have been naturally formed by winds and waves into what seem like artisan-sculpted pillars!It was astounding and amazing to see how nature can create something that you could only imagine a person could do!Usually, there are a lot of people so you can't really stay long and soak on the view and the soothing Jeju breeze!But hey, it's worth the stop!

When you visit Jungmun Resort, don't forget to visit Jungmun-Daepo Coast (Jusangjeolli Cliff). The location is near the ICC and the Seaes Hotel & Resort. For KRW 2000 entrance fee, you get great view and it is perfect location for taking photos! It is said that the best time to visit here is during sunset.
Those columnar joints are indeed very beautiful. Not to be missed. Entrance fee is 2,000 won per adult and large parking areas.

Whilst attending a conference at the ICC Jeju I took a walk to see this larva rock cliff. It's fabulous and well worth seeing if you are on Jeju. Must admit, the boat trip to see the cliffs up close looked really good.

There are a few coastal scenary within this area and it's all within 10 to 20 mins drive. Even though it's not extending for miles and miles along the coast, most of the major viewpoints were wonderful. It's a must see if you are visiting Jeju island.

we came here by taxi but i have to say that the public trasportation is not convenient here. luckily we found a taxi when we left. there are so many tourists and we can only see the scenery in a bit far distance.

These cliffs are very interesting and beautiful. There are a lot of great views. Unfortunately, loads of students in buses keep arriving and going. Therefore, you get a nice view for about 5 minutes and then thousands of students swarm the area for about 20 minutes and then leave again. It costs 2,000 won each to enter.

2000 won fee and well wooden path for tourist. Wind can be very strong since at the open sea and you can imagine the conditions in bad weather. If you like geography this is very interesting. Otherwise still a good place for some photo and walk in the south of the island.

We went here in a sunny morning and took a glance for the natural six-edges poles. We enjoy the mild sea breeze together with stunning scenery here.There was a giant seashell in the entrance and you may sat inside to take a funny photo. You could also enjoy a short walk for Olle route here if you wish.

It was pretty crowded when we got there at about 3pm on a weekday. From the parking area, It was a short walk down some stairs to the observation decks where you get good views of the unique (column) rock formations by the coast.However, we had difficulties getting photos of us with the rock formation because there were just too many people on the observation decks. As we exited the observation deck area, we saw a guy selling postcards of the photos he himself took of various scenic Jeju attractions and we bought some to support him.I am not sure what else there is to explore in that area because we were hurried off to the next destination on our guided tour.If you are into Geography, love cliffs by the sea and rock formations, I highly recommend this place! I loved it!

I went in the early sunday evening so maybe it's just not crowded at the time, but you still struggle to get a clear photo, but it was free admission for some reason. Contrary to what wiki travel says, the best views are from the observatory. What you should do, though, is go left from the ticket booth DOWN the pathway about 30 seconds. It's not signed and it looks like nothing, but you will get another view of the coast and you can actually climb on some of the rocks there. It is very safe and empty.

Our children really wanted to spend time on the ocean. This was a great introduction to the power of the sea. Big waves. Rocky coast. Perfect for sea shell collecting, sand castle building, and glimpses of aquatic life. We managed to watch the Haenyo divers bobbing their way across Jungmun Beach and later walked the length of the beach to see their catch.

Compared to seopjikoji, personally I felt that here is more worth the journey(no doubt the later also beautiful). This is solely a sigh seeing place. If you love nature, you gonna like it. The rocks are just unique, I only saw it in the movie! And it's kind of amazing that you see it in real! I visited here in end April with strong wind and warm sun. If you have time, you can even just stroll along the walkway or sit a bit to have a casual chat with your friends.  Please do expect a lot of tourist and students visits and long queue for toilet. But this is kind of normal for all the unique sight seeing point at Jeju Island. I would recommend this place if you happens to be in this area, and I will skip the waterfalls :)

The rocks here - Jusangjeolli Rocks - are just spectacular - well worth a visit. The formation of them is just amazing - great views and brilliant if the sea is a bit rough and the waves are hitting them hard!One of my favorite views while i was here

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.

Jungmun Daepo is the spot where the iconic columnar joint rock formations can be seen. There s not much to do here, except take a few pictures from a distance, but it s worth seeing if you re in the area anyway. I can t say much about it because there s not much to say. except that you should allot about 15 minutes in total (including the time to get in an out).Further down the coast is Jungmun beach. I went here in March, so there wasn t much to do when it s 10 degrees Celsius. I imagine on a hot day it would be fun to swim here. The beach is pretty   sand is slightly coarse but clean and lovely since it s golden in color. The slope from the parking area/restaurants to the beach is pretty steep. I don t know if it s safe for people with mobility issues.One downer: I didn t like the seafood restaurants playing loud, outdated music when we got there   I think it would be a pain to eat here if you have to listen to that. Someone has to tell the tourism board about this.Where: Seogwipo west coast

If you've been to Northern Ireland, I'm sure you've been to or at least heard of the Giant's Causeway. Jusangjeolli Cliffs are exactly the same. They're very nice to look at and easy to find. Of all the things we saw on Jeju, this was probably the best. That being said, they're just rocks and cliffs overlooking the ocean.
Definitely a must see. The rock formation is unique but its best to go during a high tide. For drivers, my adivce is to key in international convention center into your gps. It is located near it.
I think the tubes were eroding so the shape wasn't very distinct. Loads of people around the place so do try to plan ahead to avoid the peak visiting hours. The sea was very inviting!

I don't have words to describe my admiration for this place.For first few moments you think the rocks are cut in perfectly rectangular edges. But soon you learn its not the case. There's the whole explanation why they have so sharp edges.Its one of the most beautiful sites we've ever seen.
One of the must see attractions in Jeju Island. Lucky to visit during the non peak season. Nice views at the right time since we did not meet that many tourists.

it was interesting to see these column-shape geological formations. The sea was calm when I visited so i did not get to see the waves getting on them. Nonetheless, the formations made really good photos.The sheer number of visitors on the small and narrow viewing platform could spoil your trip!

One of the top places to see in Jeju.  Great view of some craggy coastline.  The other reviews are pretty good and we experienced about the same - great place, but really crowded even though it was raining!  Again...people come in waves, just wait it out.  The wind was high and seas rough so it made pretty spectacular wave crashes.  On one side there was a consistent high wind and mist/spray coming at you, so watch your cameras!  There is a 1,000 W Parking fee on top of the 2,000 entrance fee.
Do not miss this volcanic rock formation. It really is quite dramatic especially if the sea is a little rough.

It worth a look just to see the beautiful coastline of the Island.Most of the rocks come in various heights and sizes shaped like hexagons and if you look at certain angles, they can take on various animals etc.The black lava colour offsets against the outstanding sea and coastline.These cliffs are very similar to the Giants Causeway in Ireland with a pancake rock system but on a much smaller scale.It was crowded the day were there and we assume it is the same most days in the summer months. So a lot of people were snaking along this narrow path around the cliffs and we needed to wait our turn to see over the barriers.There are a few stallholders near the carpark (fee charged) selling fruit, souvenirs and the local home made confectionary similar to nougat.On the way out you can go to a park with some gardens and perhaps a museum type building.The hours vary seasonally however it is the standard KRW 2,000 entry fee for most monuments around the Island.Place it on your  must see  places to visit here just for the dramatic coastline and on a rough day you may get some blow hole situations with the force of the water.Enjoy your visit!

Also known as Jusangjeolli (Jisatgae Rocks). Be warned though, it can get very crowded with local tourists and foreign tour groups. When we were there, we found it hard to get a picture without someone else appearing in the background, despite the light drizzle.

This is known in Korean as Jusangjeolli (seaside cliff). The day we were there, there was a big sea so the waves were very big and it was exciting to watch. The volcanic rock formations are very nice too.

Even in peak season Sehwa Beach didn t have nearly as many visitors as some of the more popular northeast Jeju beaches mainly because most of it is covered in volcanic rocks.  We actually weren t even sure it was a beach at first.  We did see a handful of people in the water who had sidestepped all the volcanic rocks but most seemed happy taking photos standing on the rocks.  Cafes, restaurants, and convenience stores line the beach and all were good spots to admire the nice scenery of the beach.  For actually going in the water, the other popular beaches are more popular for that reason.
Amazingly clean and beautiful beach surrounded by cute cafes. Accessible by the bus and safe for swimming and snorkeling.

I was lucky to be here on a fairly sunny day, and saw the beach show its beautiful turquoise colour. Thanks to the shallow white sand bed which stretches very far out, under the sun, the water glistened and sparkled. The lava rock added the character of the whole scenery. It s very photogenic and well worth a visit. Do not mind the industrial surrounding, it won t interrupt your pictures.

Not a wordy person, but this truly is a must visit. A jeju local recommends it to me, totally fell in love with it. Not to swim but to explore, for kids to play with the fish and small animals on the rocks. Very safe.

Went there just because our driver recommended us to make a stop there (at first we only wanted to go to Hyeopjae Beach) but now we thought Sehwa Beach was a lot nicer and less crowded than the Hyeopjae Beach. The calm sea, the soft sands all to yourself! They also have one and two spot set up, specially to take picture, and it IS a very instagrammable spot indeed haha
The water was beautiful, so we stop by for a quick dip in the ocean. It was very shallow so we went out pretty far at one point. There were many schools of fish and clams in the ocean.

nice beach with many caf챕s and restaurants. The water is clean and i can only recommend going there. But there are quite a lot people, so if you look for a lonely beach this is not appropriate for you.
Turkoise waters and great views of the beaches from multiple restaurants and coffee places all along the shoreline.May be a bit difficult to find parking though.

The waters were gentle and one saw more people in water than out there, although a selfie moment happening is never far in South Korea. Also great for a walk( into the village area, but please don't take photos without asking, off the coast as they share the coast with visitors freely and it is respectful to enter their space on their terms)

One of the benefits of being an island is all the beaches. One of the drawbacks is that beaches usually draw tourists, and where there are tourists, the shallow villainy of tourist industries inevitably follows. Sehwa has not yet been targeted for development. As of this writing, the long, open expanse of Sehwa beach is still a beach in its rawest form. When the tide goes out, the volcanic rock formations nearer to the road are exposed, leaving tidal pools to explore, thriving with an over abundance of flora and fauna. The beach at low tide is enormous, and rarely crowded. There are no lifeguards. No music. No lights. Just a beautiful beach, minor waves, clean sand, and decent swimming. When the tide comes in, you can continue swimming, or you can visit some of the restaurants in the area that cater to the locals rather than skimp for the tourists. I had some shabu shabu (–₩대＿) very near Sehwa which was like a kick to the pleasure center of my brain.  Sometimes there's even a local crafts market right next to Sehwa beach, but you have to get lucky to catch it.   Basically, Sehwa is a beach that is still Jeju. It's part of a local community, part of a local ecosystem, as yet only mildly disturbed by ideas of profitability or development.

This beach is famous for its red and white horse shaped lighthouse. Great photo spot for photographers. Located close to downtown Jeju City. Camping is also allowed here so you can bring food and your own camping gears. Water leisure activities are offered here during summer.

I went to see lighthouse in shape of horse, one is in red and the other is in white. They are well made, attractive and iconic!I too a bus heading towards West, (bus#444, it has a stop at Jeju intercity bus terminal), you would need to walk to the lighthouses or you can get off at the stop of beach.The coast line is nice, airplanes are frequently flying over the sky as it s so close to the airport!
Interesting place,there are trailer houses and some sells food.  Walk all the way to take a picture with beautiful horse light house.

I came to jeju with my friends and the first place we visited is Iho tewoo beach! Ocean view is amazing and the tidal waves are amazing.We had really good moment as a group there despite the fact the weather was cold. Iho tewoo beach is a must go place if u're traveling alone or with your family.
Iho Tewoo Beach - A local beach with good waves and sand to relax yourself after a hectic week full of work.
Good to walk around and enjoy a nice meal or have a cup of coffee! Only 5min from the airport by car.

I visited Iho Tewoo Beach   several times. Here I found  cool sea, warm peope, meditation noons. I watched the sportsmen, spoke with tourists from  many countries, just enjoyed life. Next time will probably stay at one of the small  hotels near the bay.

We went to this beach during the day and kayaked and swam. It was a lot of fun! Then we went at night and it had a wonderful nightlife with restaurants and lights!  *I really recommend this beach!  It wasn't too crowded like the others, and there weren't too many black rocks, and no seaweed.  It was great to walk in the water at night too.  We're going back to this beach again this year!

Great photo spot, many people use this beach for camping. Hard to find eating place or restaurant. The public transport also quite hard here! We wait so long for bus and finally we use taxi for way back hotel
C1 ( 16.07.13 ) There was good beach with many cafe and restaurant. And the lighthouse of horse shape was located. There was one of good beach in Jeju island, I think.
A nice beach to pass time while enjoying the sunset. You can enjoy some snack by the beach. Nothing much spectacular.

Bring your own food or you can buy from the cafe nearby and sit by the stairs watching the locals fishing or enjoying the sea breeze. Beautiful red and white horse light-houses that stood out from far. We took a cab there and for return trip, just walked 5~10mins to grab a cab from the main road.

The Beach is in the middle of the city. I personally don't like this kind of crowded beaches and it seems a little bit dirty ( which is very common for city beaches). Wouldn't reccommend going there (for swimming).

Iho Taewoo Beach 댄명고대  is the closest beach to Jeju-si (city) and is closed to airport too, one can look down from the plane of the two very special red and white horse-shaped lighthouses when it almost reach Jeju Airport. Beach are sandy white and swallow water that are safe to swim. It is open for public and no admission charges except if is Jeju Iho Taewoo Festival.Visitors are welcomed to camp at the camping site. Facilities like charging room and shower room with locker are available too, is chargeable.There is two entrance to Iho Taewoo Beach, one is closer to the sandy beach and camping site located in the pine forest but less parking space. The other one is close to the horse-shaped lighthouses with huge free parking space and food trucks selling food and beverage. Here you can cycling and photographing. The two white and red horse-shaped lighthouse is famous for sunset photographing, it is best to be there around 5-6pm for the best sunset moment. Iho Taewoo Festival is around Jul-Aug every year. Local and tourist will be coming to witness the happening festival and event like boat ricing, fishing competition and many more fun activities. It will be a long day event.If you are driving, key in 728-3393.If you are taking public transport, take green bus 7,17 or 60 or blue bus 36

Geumneung Beach and Hyeopjae Beach are the two beaches of Hallim located about a kilometer apart from one another.  While swimming is not allowed for some stretches, both areas are absolutely stunning during sunset.  The stretches of the camping area looked like a great place to spend the daylight hours and at low tide, there was plenty of space for kids to run around and play.

This beach was a short stopover point for us. We were on the way to another place.It was mid afternoon & the sun was very very hot, probably that's why there were so few people then. My guess is that those who are here came for the same reasonThe roaring sounds of the waves & the deep blue sea always gives one a nice relaxed feeling. In countries like Korea, there are lots of similar beaches & seas. So although it is nice, there is no need to make a special trip unless you are on the way to another place & passes through here for a short stop. Or for toilet breaks.

We drove by after a visit to Hallim Park and couldn't resist this beautiful place.Totally unprepared for the beach, we went for a short walk around the area. The water was cool & clear. There were many tide pools for the kids to explore and catch crabs, little fishes & shrimp. The weather was perfect.The kids wished that they could stay there all day but we had to leave for another place.We would go back there again when we visit Jeju the next time.

We were heading to Halim Park and chance upon this on the way. Not many people as it was winter and really cold to be at the beach but the view is just so soothing. Blue greenish ocean waters, waves splashing against the rocks, white sandy beach, etc...just picture perfect.  The wind was blowing hard on our faces. There is a stine statue there at the parking lot.Definitely want to go back again.

It was a rainy day when we went to this beach after visiting the Hallim park, end of october. It was however a very nice experience, the sand is white and contrast nicely with the black rocks that you can see at low tide. The view on the island makes the picture even nicer.

Absolutely stunning beach with great views of Biyangdo Island. Avoid July and August, as it's crowded. Wait for low tide, when the water ebbs quite far and you even take selfie with Stone Man that usually is submerged in the sea. Also great to watch jeju kitesurfing scene i great activity to try out.
Quite windy, nearby Hallim Park and HyeopJae beach. Camping available. Showers with cold water for 2000 won. Foot washing station. Small convenience store.
Geumneung Eutteumwon Beach - it was a pleasant day when i visited the beach. The sun shone brightly we really enjoyed our day on this nice and clean beach.
We just passed by this beach as we felt it wasn't that nice. Although there were less tourists in this area but coming from a tropical country, this is just a basic beach.
The water is shallow and clear, full of sea shells, hermit crabs, and small fish. It is great place for little kids to swim safely.

Emerald color water with a beautiful long beach and white sand!!  a great place for families with children to play together and enjoy a quiet. It makes a beautiful scenery photo with Biyangdo Island is located directly in front of the beach.
Clean, plenty of foliage, great views, this is my fave photo spot and overall chill spot in Jeju. You'll find it less crowded than other beaches and a lot less polluted. Best during spring or fall.

This is unlike most Korean beaches because most Koreans go to the beach right up the road. Lots of space to play and relax in the sand and in the water. Beautiful sunset. Emerald water. And white sand. Shallow water is great for kids. No parasols (umbrellas), and no commercial building stores  - nice! Doesn't feel like a Korea beach at all. Tip: Park on the right near the camping area. That's where you will find a nice quiet sandy spot next to natural sand dunes. Wow!

Likes:Beautiful light blue waters, similar to HyeopjaeLess people during the July/August period.A few empty umbrella spaces for us to squeeze in (thanks to less people)Can rent floatablesDislikes:No wavesRecommend to others?Yes, if you want to go to a beach on the west coast of Jeju
Came by here because the cab driver said that its prettier that Hyeopjae Beach. It was pretty empty when I came maybe because it was in autumn and it might be cold.
This beach is so beautiful. The view is breathtaking. Clear waters, blue ocean, white sand, and can swim here too.

Near to Hyeopjae Beach with breathtaking views. It was very cold in the winter by beach so make sure get yourself wrapped up and enjoy the views here. The water was shallow and nice enough for us to walk around on the rocks and saw many green seaweeds here too.  A must visit if you are in Jeju Island.
I saw it in April when the medicinal value of the sands has not been overtaken by the summer trippers. So the colours and the sands were relaxing.

Beautiful white sandy beach framed with black lava rocks. Warm and calm sea. Even on a stormy afternoon is Spring it was still beautiful and a great place so sit and watch the world go by. Couple of cafes and shops are very close by. Tide comes in pretty fast and quite high.

Next door to the popular Hyeopjae Beach is the lesser known Geumneung Beach. Make sure you pack your snorkeling gear as it's teeming with all kinds of marine life. Like most of Jeju's North-side beaches, it's very shallow, which means you could easily walk for about a kilometre and the water hardly passes your middle as the tide's going out.

This one is located near  Hyeopjae  Beach,  so you can see the Biyangdo island as well. i liked it. Its pretty spacious and got necessary facilities like combini nearby, toilet and place with free water. it also got nice view and some of typical jeju sculptures of  female divers and spirits that protect the Island. Sand is white and feels nice.

We sought out Saryeoni Forest thinking it would be a great place to escape the July heat.  We visited the section with nicely laid out boardwalks which was great for taking our baby on a stroller.  The scenery was picturesque and even during peak season, it didn t feel crowded as the forest area is vast.  However, the humidity level was significantly higher as it felt like we were walking around wearing a plastic raincoat.

Most of famous travellers places are not free of charge but this place has no entrance fee :) I visited here in winter and fortunately there weren't many people so I was able to enjoy this forest path pretty much. Calm, beautiful and very peaceful place even thou trees were not that green. You don't need to wear athletic stuffs but sneakers are essential.One thing you need to be reminded is there aren't any trash boxes and they must be taken back with you.

Was with my photographer here for my prewedding photoshoot. The forest was amazing for a background photoshoot as the trees were tall and very densed. Lighting from the sunlight was just nice, and well covered by the tall trees. There were also a few spots that has wooden chairs built for resting. Recommended for prewed photoshoots!

There are a few trails here through the woods.  Nothing difficult.  I guess you might walk 10-15 Km here and there.  There are posted opening hours, but people seem to walk in after them since there isn't actually a gate (or staff).  It seems quiet even during the busy season.
Beautiful place to take a walk - 19km though !Paths designated well, lots of places photoworthy. With small crowd of hike crazy fans... and brides.

The guard told me I should've called to the office before heading for there. The snow made cars are stuck in the road. I could clearly see with my bare eyes. Even if today's weather was so perfect and wonderful, it is a forest under tremendously tall trees so lots of shadow made them ice. Maybe next week might be OK to visit inside but please call beforehand if it is allowed to get in. Even at the entrance, I could see beautiful scenery from a distance.
Really was a wonderful walk and experience. The path is well maintained and easy to find. We took the bus there and it is convenient and easy. Take a jacket as the forest can get a little cold
Like the title said. It s the same as every other underground mall I ve been too. Nothing special. This one had lots of clothes and beauty items.

Yet another underground mall. The usual clothing, fashion, cafes, etc, etc. They are all about the same.Perhaps the bright spot about these underground malls is that one can find some bargains especially clothings.

Was here during the winter, winter clothes sold at value. You can get a whole set here, from undies to mittens at a discount price.  Place is well maintained, underground so you're warm.  Not too many restaurants but the space is sprawling and windy, you can get lost. Thankfully there are maps, just remember your entry point to keep your bearings.  Toilets all around, with no bidet.  Things sold were all more or less the same as you spend a bit of time browsing.

The Jungang Undergroung Shopping Center was among the shopping stops that we had for our Jeju tour package. The area is sizeable. There are 12 gates conveniently marked I had to remember Gate 5 since this is where our tour bus was scheduled to pick us up.  There were beauty products, clothes, cosmetics, more clothes, more beauty products did I already mention clothes and cosmetics? The clothes and bags sold here are not your designer stuff but cheaper items. The cosmetics sold here are similar to what you have at every corner in Korea. If you are looking for really inexpensive items, it is better going to the Dongmun Market. If you want branded items, head to the Chilseongro Fashion Street. Both these locations are nearby, at Gates 2 and 3 respectively. The only redeeming factor that the Jungang Underground Shopping Center is that it is indoors and has climate control, which is useful for a cold winter day.

One just can not envision the size and number of stores in this underground mall.  Even if you don't buy anything, it's worth checking it out.  The clothing is very inexpensive.  Lots of cell phone stores but they only work in Korea so the employees won't even look at you if your not Korean.  But all the other shop are very friendly.
Worth the visit. Amazing. My kids enjoyed the place. Great time for exploration in the area.Visit the area.
They sale a lot of clothing with self brand, the price is more expensive that some known brand like uniqlo, h&m etc...

They mostly sell clothes and cosmetics here. This place is equivalent to those underground shopping centres in Seoul. It is a large space and you can try  bargaining too. Close proximity to Dongmun Market and a gem of a historical area called Gwandeokjeong.

Communication barrier is not a problem for us to shop here. Yes, they don't really speak English. But, we still had a good time to shop and bargain. If you want to shop korean fashion (but not the designer label or branded one), clothing, accessories, bags, cosmetic, skin care, this is the place. One place for everything so that you don't have to walk more. Innisfree, Nature Republic, The Saem, Skin Food, you name it. All are here.

We enjoy shopping underground. We were able walk from one end to another. Just remember where you enter. There is a number so you will not get lost.There were beauty products, children clothing, adult clothing, bags, shoes, restaurants, etc. They are not your designer stuff but cheap items. Since winter, they sell winter wear. We bought some face masks, cleanser for less than $10. We also bought bags for $15. The lady said made in korea so we think ok. The backpack is great cos very spacous. Good for traveling. Quality is just ok. Then at one exit near to the wet market, we found a shop called bang bang. It belongs to a friend of the korean actor who starred in the famous korean drama "my love from the star" we were able to buy simple T shirts, socks. They are less than $10. Socks about $3. We actually shop here 2 times when we were staying in ocean suites hotel. It was just 10 to 15 minutes walk to this underground shopping area.There are restaurants here too. We found a good korean restaurant here. It was good food and affordable.
Maybe coz it s winter, mainly promoting winter clothes. Not many knick knacks to see or buy. Haven t yet compared to shopping malls, but can t say it s very affordable either

Since my hotel is located at one end of this shopping centre, I visited this place every day during my stay in Jeju. Being underground, it was great to shield the winter cold especially in the evenings.The shops essentially sell similar products - clothings, cosmetics, shoes, accessories, bags, hats, etc. There are few eateries and fast food chains too. This shopping street tends to be crowded in the evenings. There are free toilet facilities at one end, i.e. exit 1.
good facility,many store and warm when winter season its the best place for shopping at Jeju.nearby to dongmun market and its easy to go by bus

It's probably the best place to shop for street wear in Jeju but it's nothing compared to Seoul. After visiting this place, one realised how expensive jeju is compared to the mainland Korea.Free samples are given out when purchasing cosmetic in Seoul. Nothing of that sort in Jeju. Fashion spotted in this mall is old and pathetic. Don't get your hopes high.Only saving grace is this mall protects you from the weather elements during shopping. But so is any mall in Seoul too.
Forget Lotte Duty Free, You can find almost every Korean Skin Care Brand here, TheFaceShop, Etude, Isoi, Banilla , Nature Republic, etc, all with cheap price and lots of bonus.

The entrance is an orange frame which juts our of the ground so it will be really hard to miss. But If you go for flashy shopping centre then this place is not for you. There s a lot on sale if you take the time to browse through. Unfortunately I am the type who goes for flashy shopping centre so we just came in and breeze through.
nothing much to see here, a typical underground shopping mall with the usual shops and F&B. good thing is that it wasnt that crowded.they do provide free wifi though.

When you vivit Jeju Island,  it is very easy for you to find cosmetic center in jugang underground shopping center. There are many kind of korean cosmetic product. Such as soothing gel, sheet mask, lipt tint, and facial wash. From airport you can go to jugang underground shopping center by bus or by taxi. You can ask tourist information in airport about bus number that can bring you there

My hotel was almost next to exit 1 of this mall so spent quite a bit of time here shopping for Korean cosmetics but otherwise it's just a regular shopping center, nothing special. Didn't try any of the restaurants down there, as I'd prefer to spend more time in the open air. But this mall serves as a great connection point to many other areas of interest within the city including the Mok provincial government historical site and Dongmun traditional market, with clearly marked signs at each exit.

You might go in the market which is partially underground and think you re in this. You re not. This is about 100 little shops with similar wares. About 3 places to eat including don burger. One neat thing about this is that they say it is the largest in the world. It s one block but in the middle flares out to several aisles. I don t know if anybody reads trip advisor unless you click HELPFUL. If you do this, it sends me an email and it makes me smile :-)

Came here after having our dinner nearby , stroll along this underground shopping which was not that long , bought some Korean brand cosmetic here that's all, not crowded , free filter water with paper cups for drinks , clean toilet to use , heated on a cold weather . If it's raining outside would be nice to spend some time here .
Underground shops over around 2 blocks. Nothing really interesting. You can skip it if you run out of time. Some clothing shops. Better save your money and time for Seoul.
Very near the Dongmun market, just like any ordinary underground shopping center. Nothing new, nothing different. Many entrances and exits too.
It's a good place to buy facial mask escorts from some famous Korean brand like innisfree or natural republic.
this ug shopping mall has a lot of entrance one of them was located near dongmun market.mostly sell clothes and food.

Its a short street UG mall sells things you will find in normal shops in Jeju.  The catch here is that this place is not just underground BUT its air conditioned.  Its maintained very well with clean toilets.  We spent about 40 mins leisurely but didn't buy anything in the end.  I won't say its a must-go place but if you happened to be at Dongmun market, its a short walk to this place.

This Underground Shopping Mall is again beside one of the walking street.  It also has many entrance/exit.  Basically, the shops are selling more for women and not for youngsters. It really make use of the space on the island, and place to hide during down pour.
A lot of selection, different price ranges for all the price brackets. Clothes, some gifts and food. Worth coming to see.

Can find almost everything here cosmetics (of course), vitamin, souvenir, fashion apparel, also few restaurants here. Almost can find everything here but not that fantastic. Some of the coat and sweater was expensive.This is good option to go for bad weather.

We were looking for a good place to shop and buy souvenirs and we found this place in Jungang area. Lot of cheap items from clothes, bags, shoes and beauty products.Tips:- GPS: 752-8776- There is a public parking in front of Jeju Bank along Ohyeon-gil. 3-4 hours cost us 3700Krw.- Jejumok Gwana is just on the West exit (exit 11). You might want to drop by if you got time.- There are Korean food in the middle section. Cheap but taste good.

Not being the world's greatest fan of shopping malls, underground or otherwise, I wasn't expecting very much. However, I have to admit that it was very nice and tidy, a long parade of shops stretching at least a quarter of a mile. Most of the outlets were selling clothes, shoes and that sort of thing. Be careful about payment since many do not accept MasterCard or Visa, let alone AMEX. Haggling over prices seems to be tolerated, but language might be an impediment.Happy Shopping !

Stumble upon it when wanting to cross the road. There's mainly women's stuff, plenty of cosmetics, very few man's stuffs and some restaurants. Looks like a typical China zhuhai gong pei type of underground mall, but smaller. The ships above ground sells higher quality stuffs.
It basically looks like a shopping mall in Shenzhen. There are a few cosmetic shops but most of the shops sell old-fashioned clothes. Not worth a visit at all.
Relatively clean and orderly but nothing special. Mostly clothing and cosmetics shops, surprised to find not even 1 souvenir stall that sells "Welcome to Jeju" t-shirts

Located in Jungangro of downtown Jeju this underground shopping mall was the perfect spot to take in some local shopping due to the rain on the day we visited.  Most of the 280 shop locations were open but quite a few locations were in the process of or still had yet to open.  Most shops here sold shoes, clothing, and cosmetics.  We found several shops for children apparel and a few shops of general items and a couple of places to eat (which we tried - very good).  Of the shops there we didn't really find anything to our liking but the shopping experience was pleasant.  The shops varied in what they accepted for payment.  Most accepted Wans and several Credit Cards.  If any, tenants spoke very little English.

This underground shopping street is kinda cool. It has clothes, beauty products, a large number of children's stall, and no doubt impresses the many thousands of tourists that come through Jeju City every day. However, if you have ever been to Singapore, and experienced the underground warren of the connected malls on Orchard road, this will not in any way tantalize you. At best it will make you smile at the 1970's feel of it all ;-)

At there if you looking for almost all kind of cloth and cosmetic there you will love it! Because some brand name is there and almost is a fashion cloths there! For cosmetic is so many brand there start from Korea product will go to almost every brand in the world  and the area is just next from dongmon market ...and don't forget you are shopping at underground shopping centre not in a big mall because I will experience some poor service...have a great shopping

Unfortunately we visited in the morning and a lot of the stalls were just opening up.  I was surprised as a lot of the markets in Asia open at the crack of dawn.  There are a large number of stalls selling a large variety of goods, some at fairly good prices.  It was a dull day so it was nice to be indoors.

It is just like the cheap Chinese market in my hometown, with small stalls, no room to try things on and dirty floor. We were quite surprised when we got there, as the reviews of this place are rather good. Did not buy anything there. If you want some normal shopping in Jeju, go to any Emarket instead.

Generally, a great place to shop for mask, body care, face care products with great prices. Do beware of some shops do actually give a kind of face/attitude if you touch or even asked for prices ( please note that, most shops dont include a price tag) after you  decided not to buy.
There are a lot of steps to negotiate - but on looking again a lift as found and used - very interesting mall - extremely clean as is the entire city

To be full of cosmetics and fashion items. If you're shopaholic you shouldn't miss an opportunity for shopping. Quite Cheap. If it's rainy days and can't go for climb mountains, you can go jungang instead.
Lots of shops, but I wouldn't go out of your way to see this.  I just happened to be in the area.  Wouldn't be very nice shopping if it was crowded either.

Lots of various beauty shops and shoppers crowded around those shops. You can buy some good Korean made health care products, and a lot of Chinese and various types of Asians. It claims to be a tax free zone, and the prices are more than reasonable. Also, the free wifi hotspots are good, as well as very clean bathrooms. Good place for shopping.

This market sells many products either fashionable clothes and branded cosmetics. There're many food shops available with reasonable place too. If you are seeking for sport shoes or toys.You can also find here. Some shops will give you the tax refund and some not.You need to check carefully. The famous cosmetic shops like ETUDE and skin food, some of famous items may not available. There're 11 gates which the even gate no. will locate on the right whereas the odd ones are on the left. It's not complicated and easy to walk. There's restroom available too.If you don't buy the well known brand, you will also find the local Korean cosmetic brand which is very cheap. I buy 12 hand creams with 10,000 won prize and can get the complimentary mask for 10 sheets. It's very good price. The souvenir shop also available here.I would also recommend to come as the choice of your shopping since it's not too crowded like duty free building and you don't need to buy a lot of same items in pack like duty free. As most of Korean cosmetics in duty free would be sold in pack of more than 2 pieces which sometimes you don't need that much.

This place is great for shopping with reasonable and cheaper prices compared to other places. Also, it is underground and covered, so u need not worry about the weather. U could take your meals at the big market on the  street level, get your fix of souvenirs such as jeju chocolates, crunch, tangerines and such, then head downstairs to shop. Most store ladies there could speak Mandarine and a little English so communication is not a big issue. Definitely a must come for shopping in Jeju!

Do not bother spending your time going here unless there is some specific item or shopping you need to do. Come on, you are on Jeju, a small slice of paradise on Earth, go see funny statues or climb a mountain.
Good for rainy day. Lots of little cosmetic shops to get last minute purchases, interesting clothing and shoe shops.
Many small shops mainly selling clothes.The best is if it's raining you can have a dry walk below the streets...
Came here with my husband and we had a great time negotiating and bargaining for prices. I will say it's a bit overwhelming and I didn't see much variety for food but overall we had a good time.

Nothing much to shop as underground complex is quite small. Had Doni burger which was not bad (near exit 5). Other than that it's not really worth a visit as there are better stuff to do at jeju. Spent 6d5n in jeju and didn't finish what we set out for.

As per title...not so friendly shop attendant. And the rude one are from mainland China if not mistaken. Such a disappointment. No intention of racist or whatsoever. Just personal experience at one of the shop.

This shopping centre is huge, full of goods like cosmetics, clothes, shoes, small electronics and mobile accessories. And people of course. Not different from underground shopping in Seoul or Incheon.

The cruise ship docked in Jeju South Koren for a few hours. We didn t plan anything, just walked around downtown.  We saw a flight of stairs, looks like it leads to some metro station, so we went down to take a look. It is a huge underground shopping center. They sell clothing, accessories, shoes and cosmetics. This is a shopper s haven. They also have free Wi-Fi that you can connect with family and friends. Although we don t know their language, but the people are very friendly and helpful. I don t mind to visit Jeju again.Happy Travelling!

This is an underground shopping center which is just around the corner of Orange Tree  Cafe & Hotel. This is just the normal shopping center which you would see in most of the subways thru out Seoul, however, the good thing about this underground shopping mall is that each of the exits leads to different streets which has more shops....eg. Uniqlo, ABC Mart, Daiso, and also various cafes.....and also to the Dongmun Market and also to the Black Pork Street.

Yeah, very nice for a waterfall that's in s decent-sized city. It's not Niagara by any means, but the walk through the gardens leading up to it are pleasant and it's very photogenic. Getting there early - pre 10am - is the best bet as the light is good for photos and the crowds are not as hectic.

Our family visited "Cheonjiyeon Falls" on June 8th, 2019. To get to the waterfall, you have to walk a lot. There were a lot of small markets that sold simple snacks, which was sweet, but the way to the waterfall was not worth it. Although the way to the waterfall was harsh, still the waterfall was beautiful. I recommend this waterfall to whom that likes walking. If your stamina is poor, you will be tired . I don't think the waterfall was worth walking a lot.
It's ok as a waterfall but nothing special. A pleasant and easy walk to it. You can also get a view of the falls from the park above.

We have been to many waterfalls & certainly this one is at the lower end of the range.Nothing spectacular, rather small & very normal. Skip this place if you have limited time - there are better places to go.

The park is built for the waterfall. Was there during dusk, though there are sufficient lighting around. The waterfall is a tad disappointing, especially when you came from Jeongbang Waterfall. However it is suitable for people of all ages, the walk to the waterfall is very easy.

This is my favorite as the waterfalls and the blue water coupled with mandarin ducks swimming and moving around, I really feel like I'm in a fantasy land or living in the fairy tales movie that we used to see.  Highly recommended for photography and relaxation!

After seeing Jeongbang waterfall, this Cheonjiyeon waterfall seemed average.  Admission was the same in both waterfalls, 2,000won for adults, and 1,000won for teenagers (up to 24). To see this waterfall, you had to go thru the park, which had other monuments, trees, and flowers to admire...worth checking even in winter.

Less than 15 min walking, the waterfall was beautiful, and there s food photo spot where everyone line up when u get to the waterfall. In my opinion, the admission fee was little too much for the quick walk and waterfall view. But good to visit once!
It was a nice place , i thought it will be a big place but it was not , you will spend 20 min in there .

I was expecting a rough n tough hike into the Falls but i was so wrong. Everything is nicely paved. Despite the fact that it is touristy it still does not take away the beauty of the place. The ducks and birds really add the beauty.

After paying for the tickets (2000 won per adult and 1000 won per child/youth), we walked about 5-10min to the waterfall. It was a therapeutic walk through the park to reach the waterfall. Recommend to stay about an hour here to take photos with the waterfall as the backdrop.

This is a nice place for sightseeing and exploring the Jeju waterfalls. There was a roughly 5-10 minutes walk before reaching the waterfall, which was fairly simple and pleasant too. The waterfall does not differ greatly from your other waterfalls, so if you re looking for a unique and different sightseeing experience, I suggest giving this a miss. However, it was still quite magnificient and beautiful if you enjoy sightseeing and waterfalls. Overall, do spend about an hour here to leisurely stroll and sightsee this Jeju wonder.

Good place for family. Easy to reach, no trailing or hiking and everything comfortable for elders and children :)On the other side - there is no any "wow"-effect. Just do a slow walk, relax and calm down.

We can't quite remember the order but my wife and I saw 3 waterfalls when we went looking for one. All the waterfalls were spell binding, gushing with water even in summer (April) However, 2 are fenced for safety reasons and the third one has a board warning you against swimming. You can, although, dip your feet in the cold water at the unfenced one. At the first one, you can make a wish and throw a coin into the shallow end of the fall. And if your schedule isn't packed, it's a great place to sit back and read a book.
Nothing compared to other famous waterfalls around the world. Nothing about heritage. So I am here only because I am on Jeju.After this, decided to skip other waterfalls. But good for some exercise.

The walk to Cheonjiyeon Falls is quite easy and beautiful. The waterfall is quire charming as well. However, compared to Cheonjeyeon Falls (which is a 3 tiered waterfall attraction in Jeju not mentioned in TripAdvisor), Cheonjiyeon is still second best.

According t the map the falls were 400m from my hotel - so tried to walk.  Reched the park above the falls easily but could not find a path down.  Turns out only way to access to to go 1km downstream and walk down to the car park and in the official entrance. From entrance it is a 500m walk back upstream to the falls. many people all queuing to take photos.On the way out saw a musical performance near the entrance.

We did this on a rainy day just before a typhoon hit. It was perfect conditions as it meant a lot less people were walking around. The falls are all beautiful, the bridge is picturesque and  made for great views. The walkways are very well signposted and there is a lot of information about. You are not allowed to swim there which is important to know when taking kids, it is a real shame as there were many potential swimming holes!

Cheonjiyeon Falls is a peaceful stop for those that want some refreshing time. Unofrtunatelly swimming is not allowed here. Good for a quick visit before visiting the Saeyeongyo Bridge. The nature also is astonishing, a glimpse of tropical nature in Jeju.
This place is very best and beautiful  ㅿ. This water flow  is nice and like look water poot from sky this In place..... This place stayed in South Korea..... Thank you andLike read...

This attraction is much smaller then the other similar sounding spot - Cheonjeyeon. There is just one waterfall here and its q quick short walk to the view point. Like all other spots, swimming is not allowed here as well. Good for a quick visit before visiting the Saeyeongyo Bridge.

Went here on a hot summer afternoon and could immediately feel the drop in temperature when entering the natural reserve. The water is clean, clear and very tempting. unfortunately swimming is not allowed. Need to walk and climb stairs to reach all the 3 waterfalls, but each one was worth it. stop by near the bridge to take photos

We went in summer, so the waterfall was less impressive (due to less rainfall in summer months) especially the 1st waterfall... the water was beautifully clear... be aware the the are plenty of steps up and down... my mum gave up after the first waterfall... the second waterfall is really pretty but there is no way to get access to the water below (unlike the 1st) as the observation platform was rise high from the river below... everyone including the fit and young gave up on the third fall due to the tough & long steps and punishing summer heat... its definitely worth going if you are in the area... fees for admission

The waterfall is beautiful, it gave me the urge to jump in it under the hot sun. There is a entrance charge for that. For those who are from places like Malaysia, Philippines where surrounded with beautiful waterfalls, you might don't feel like spending money just to see this waterfall.

I went Thursday morning with my girlfriend and it was quiet enough. Nice walk, but be prepared for stairs and bring water! The bridge you can cross is exquisite and crazily steep (so be careful in the winter). The views are outstanding on a clear day.I really enjoyed this site; the wooden walkways, the history behind the irrigation channels and of course the waterfalls really kept my interest.Would recommend!Shane & Jill

Fantastic nature preserve and historic monuments in Jungmun resort area of Jeju.  Very inexpensive to visit (about $2.5 for adults) and so many beautiful hiking paths and monuments. You can learn about Jeju island mythology as well as the US occupation of Jeju after WW II.  I wanted to come back another day but it rained. So gorgeous and great for a workout!

The Cheonjeyeon Falls was a memorable last stop of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour. The size of the entire park the falls are situated in is generally small, but it's loaded with so many sights to see. In the entrance, you're immediately greeted with a beautiful pagoda and lush well-kept gardens. There's also a wishing fountain called the Fountain of Five Blessings that's worthy of your participation as the coins tossed inside the fountain are donated to Korea's underprivileged. Entering the site, one has to cross an intricately beautiful bridge which is elegant and regal in its own right. After that, the trek to the falls; sites begins. The entire trek is paved with concrete steps which make it more convenient and safer for visitors, especially as the trek requires ascend and decline quite a lot. Although, be prepared for a light workout as the number of steps do add up if you complete the entire trek (there are quick detours to the exit for those who don't wish to complete the entire trek or those grappling with a fear of heights).Shoutout to our amazing tour guide from Yeha Bus Tour for going the extra mile in making our entire tour enjoyable!

Interesting waterfalls with a park. Lighted up at night. We came by at 8pm.  The clear and deep water of Cheonjiyeon Falls is designated as Natural Monument No. 27 and is renowned as a habitat for Mutae eels. Take a walk around the beautiful park. You can also take photos with the props such as 'Summer', hearts etc.

Pretty waterfall. It s easy to get to, a short walk brings you there. Unfortunately you aren t able to get into the water. This waterfall is more accessible as compared to Jeongbang waterfall. So for older folk and young children, this might be more suitable. I prefer Jeongbang just because I get to play in the water. Admission is 2000 won for an adult.

It was a relaxing short walk to the falls. We went during the evening and it was quite touristy. It's a great site to take pictures before the waterfall if there isn't too much people. The entry was only 2000 won and there are shops and restaurants near the entrance

No ! Not again another Fall ! But this one worth the peaceful walk in a nice park and by a small river. If you pass by, go there. You have to see the harbour with small fishing boats. I liked this even better.

Nice park surrounding this unique canyon.  3 sets of waterfalls.  An interesting bridge that goes over the canyon and a path that takes you through the woods.  Takes a bit of effort but it's worth doing if you're in the area.  The falls are not that impressive but the formations and the foliage is nice.

1st falls was kinda disappointing cos there was no water coming down. Perhaps dry season?
