On the + side, the still water surface made excellent photo opp. After more staircases, we had the option to descend a long staircase to 2nd falls. Which we skipped and proceeded on. We crossed the bridge of the 7 nymphs - indeed an odd architecture with such a curved surface to near centre of bridge. Easiest is to walk in reverse to give the hamstrings some relief. Later on, there was a lookout point for 2nd falls. Yay. All done, we rewarded ourselves with icecream :)

This is a place suitable for kids and senior citizen. It is just a short walk from the entrance to the waterfall via a flat road. We make this place the last place on our itinerary (late evening) as this place close later than any then attractions in Seogwipo. Quite a romantic walk and we even met some couples doing their wedding photoshoot here.

We stumbled upon this place whilst walking about but didn't regret it.I would be careful if you are accompanying very young children or old people as the stairs are made of rock and quite difficult to negotiate. Our 5 year old made it ok but required assistance.A nice place to visit but not much in the way of a waterfall when we were there. Perhaps they take the water in during the day? (that was a joke by the way!)

Nice walk down to the falls. Well organized. The waterfall is not spectacular, just a stream of water coming down the mountain. 20 years ago the made electricity here, but the whole installation is gone now.
Only the first without the water falling is best for picture. The other two you will be on a platform far from the water.  The bridge is very big and allow you a good view.
The Cheonjiyeon Falls is an amazing  spot in Jeju island. It is surrounded by  rare species of subtropical flora. The walk to the fall about a km is very pleasant  and scenic.
one of the smaller waterfalls of he two but very well kept. shades of water can be seen along with a wishing well and a few picture spots on the bridge and walk way
This one has 3 tiers of waterfalls as opposed to 1.  The pools are in blue and green colors.  It also has a beautiful bridge that is decorated with 7 nymphs.

Great Views, Must Go, Wear to walking shoes, Not Baby friendly for Strollers as you will have to climb a lots of stairs. If you have child s on stroller make sure you carry Baby Pouches/Bags for carrying the baby. Drink the Tap Water - Very Springy & Natural.
The walk towards and back from the fall is very well kept. Quite romantic with the trees around . The fall is not too big but there is a calm serene feeling looking at it .

It's an okay, nothing to be exaggerated. However, enjoying the walk towards the fall with serene and scenic view is very relaxing. During spring, strolling under the cherry blossoms trees and get to enjoy some local live band music show with people get to move their body to the grooves! Once you got out of the fall, several merchandise shops selling local snacks and merchandise. There are also arrays of local food store nearby serving varies pick of seafood. I went to the nearest restaurant near the merchandise store with red signboard. Food potion is huge and price is reasonable. It was really fresh and tasty! I stayed in the Choi Hostel around the area, so it's quite a walk and hike on the way back, what's with full bloated tummy. BTW, I only ate 2 dishes alone :P

When I went for the first time, my friend and I were late so we were rejected so please come earlier than 5.30 pm.We managed to find time to come again on another day and Cheonjeyeon Falls was a nice place to spend a couple hours here.Take note that there are stairs so it can be a little tiring to some. We had just came back from a day of Hallasan hiking so our legs were busted.
gorgeous - especially in the blooming spring.  cute bridge & stream. easy access from huge parking lot
Flat walk and just a slight gradient to actual falls. Cheap entry at 2000 won per person.  Scenic views and not very busy at approx. 11.30am.

This is my favourite one of the three waterfalls i visited in Jeju! (April 2018)This place consist of three level waterfalls. The first level you will only see the waterfall if it has rained enough and the waterlevel is high enough to create the waterfall. The second one is the biggest of the three levels. It can be seen from two places. First is by the staircase and upclose. The second one is going over the bridge and after that (stone) stairs up on your rightside after crossing over the bridge. You can get a great view for the 2nd waterfall!The third and last level is the furtherst and the smallest one of all. If you are not fit enough or you can't walk very well, I advise to skip this one as there are a lot of stairs to go down and up afterwards.The first 2 levels are good enough to get a great view out of the place.

You have to walk a little distance from the car/coach park, but the path is flat and well paved.  The falls themselves were, however, disappointing with little water flowing.  I m sure the falls would be more impressive after heavy rainfall.

Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls consists of 3 waterfalls. Such a nice turquoise water. There is an entrance fee to enter this place. Make sure you have some energy because you need to climb stairs to reach each point. There is a bridge called 'Seonimgyo Bridge', meaning 7 nymphs as there has an arch carved on the side. This place open from 8am to 6pm. We came here late in the evening in a rainy day but the admin staff were so nice to allowed us to enter but with time restrictions.
You need to pay 2000 Korean dollars to have a sight of this waterfalls. It's not a lot of money so it's good
I really enjoyed looking at the different waterfalls. It's a pity we're not allowed to swim as the warning sign said and I quote "You'll be died of heart attack".

It s a must visit place in Jeju. The time I went there was in Winter but surprisingly all trees along with the side walk bloomed so much. The walk in the forest and a big fall blew my stress away. Enjoy the view!
Not spectacular. Small waterfall. OK for first timer to look see. Flowers were beautiful, better than Camellia Hill. The bridge after the first two waterfall was pretty.

One of the 3 major waterfalls in Jeju, the water falls from a height of around 22 meters and thus named Cheonjiyeon   meaning Sky connected with Land. Though not as majestic as Cheonjeyeon , this water falls is as beautiful when it comes to its natural surroundings . A very well laid out path ensures one can enjoy the long walk from main entrance to the waterfalls. As there is not much climbing to do, tourists of all ages can visit this place.

This three tier waterfall is one of the three waterfalls in Jeju, the other two being Cheonjiveon and Jeongbang waterfalls. The forest surrounding the waterfall has been designated as a natural monument and as per Korean legend seven nymphs bath at the pond of this waterfall in the night.Located at a walkable distance from Seogwipo Harbour, the visit to this attraction calls for climbing of stairs. So avoid this place if you hate to climb steps. For others a good pair of shoes is a must.

Apart from the waterfall there are many beautiful shots you can take including the trees which have beautiful flowers, a bridge overlooking a stream, a river crossing with many  square steps  (don t know how to nest describe it), etc. Apparently this opens till night as well and I heard the night scenes are beautiful as well. Worth a stop.
This waterfall is easily accessible from Seogwipo city by taxi or bus. You can also take a walk in the Olle trail and park around the area
Another good place to visit in Jeju. Easy access from Seagwipo. Easy access from Seogwipo. Can go through the Olle trail and see this waterfall. No tickets required.
I prefer this waterfall for strolling about. It was a pleasant experience. Do expect a crowd as it was easily accessible and near to the city.

It is a nice place for locals and tourists to relax and chill out as you can really enjoy the beauty of mother nature. We just chill and take some pics while trying out their local snack there. It is walking distance to Saeyeongyo Bridge so just stroll slwoly while enjoying the view and breeze =)
You will have to walk a good while to get there. Worth the walk to see both falls. The bridge on our way was beautiful. Breathtaking view. We paid 2,500 won each. Which is under $5 for two people.
No climbing of stairs required at this location, which was great! The walk in was rather scenic and cooling.
Went there in the evening, nice place for sightseeing and taking of photos. Have a variety of food establishments there for tourists to catch quick bites before moving to the next destination.
Very close to the Ocean palace hotel. Easy walking trail. Worth a visit for people of all ages! Recommend to arrive early before the tour busses arrive.

Around 10-15 mins walk to view the waterfalls. Easy to walk if you have elderly or kids with you. Water is clear and kids love the ducks around. Very near to my hotel in Jeju (EINS Hotel) which is around 5 mins drive away. Good for a short stop.
Admission is 2500won per adult! Do expect lots of stairs and walking. Overall it was worth a visit and we love that rainbow we saw over the falls!

Located in Seogwipo area. Beautiful waterfall that easy to access as only reached 5-10 minutes walking their path. Mostly is stairs. Entrance Fee KRW2000. Have some small shops near the entrance selling local souvenir.
The walk from the harbour to the falls is pleasant and flat if a bit crowded on some days.  Well worth the entry fee though.

Cheonjiyeon, Cheonjeyeon and Jeongbang Falls are all located around Seogwipo, the southern city of Jeju. The first two has very similar names so don't be confused. This one is located nearer to city while CheonjEyeon is located nearer to the Ripley's and Alive Museum to the west. Cheonjiyeon is less majestic than CheonjEyeon. You can actually see 3 falls within Cheonjeyeon. Confused? In other words, visit Cheonjeyeon instead of Cheonjiyeon if you have limited time!

There lies 3 waterfall spots in Seogwipo, south of Jeju. I have went to all 3. But this Cheonjeyeon (not to be confused with Cheonjiyeon waterfall) itself has 3 waterfalls around the area. So in fact, there are 5 waterfalls in Seogwipo. The ticket is more expensive compared to the others but it is worth it as you can visit 3 falls and an arching bridge with nymphs (angels) carvings on the side. I prefer this place to Cheonjiyeon Falls.

While in Seogwipo, we don't need our car because most of the things are within short distance.First time we walked around the outside of the waterfall park along the traffic to find restaurants. The next day day we took a taxi uphill from our seaside hotel. We were quite bewildered why he dropped us just opposite the Twosome coffee complex, which wasn't the suggested stop by the hotel front desk. Nevertheless, we got off anyway because we saw the cashier booth.Taxi tips: later after the walk uphill, we realized we could have insisted the taxi to go a little further to the big parking area which was the main entrance. That way we would be walking downhill to see the waterfalls, and could exit at the mid hill exit near the temple, just opposite the Twosome Square. If desired, you can also continue downhill to the third waterfall.Photo tip: don't wear aqua or turquoise colors, or green or blue etc. as the the waterfall, although not big, is aqua and turquoise in colors in a sunny day. Is possible, should also go on a sunny day to see the colors, which I think are not so spectacular on a rainy or cloudy day.

We tried our best to reach the waterfall in seogwipoo , close to Lee Jung Seob musuem. The area is super green and you can pretty much see the sea and cliff, however, unfortunately today is rainy and they have shut the trails. Surely its totally different on a sunny day !

The water is amazing. There are 3 waterfall spots and a beautiful bridge to see at this attraction. Highly recommended although the walk can be a pain, especially the last waterfall.The bridge is also quite a sight to behold. This is probably the best waterfall in Jeju.

Not that spectacular. The walk to see the waterfall is about 10mins one walk. This is one of the star attraction in Jeju but I don't find it very interesting.At the entrance, there is a long queue for squid biscuit. It's worth a try.
We visited the falls as a group accompanying my parents-in-law s this was one of the places they visited on their honeymoon 50 years ago, yes!It was a privilege to visit and share with them.
Beautiful waterfall. The water has an intriguing blue color. Easy to get even for older people and children.

Good for laughs, because of the incorrect grammar of some of the warning signs it is nonetheless a very beautiful, breathtaking and (when not overrun with tourists) peaceful place. Have visited in 2014, 2015, and 2018.

This is the best waterfall I've seen among the famous ones in Jeju (Jeongbang, Cheonjiyeon, Cheonjeyeon). It also requires more physical effort since you have to climb and go down several stairs. There are also a number of viewing decks: for me, the one near the pavilion is the best (less people there too). Highly recommended unless you hate stairs. Best to bring shoes with good grip though since the stairs can be slippery when wet.

Just one waterfall, not much of a sight to behold. However, it's the only touristy waterfall that doesn't have stairs, so if you have knee problems, this is waterfall to see. On the plus side, the souvenir store near the entrance has good merchandise at good prices. They had nice hats on sale when I was there.
The park around the waterfall area was simple and not too long and tedious for a walk with your family. Waterfall was nice too for a photoshoot. Overall was great!
The water is very clean n clear.  Can see the fish clearly. Can drop by if have extra time. The entrance fee is 2000w for adult

The parking is free . Entrance fee was 2000W per Pax. You first descend about 5 minutes to a blue pond with the first waterfall . Beautiful and stunning . Then you proceed to the second waterfall about 10 walk . There was a third waterfall but it was about 40 minutes walk so we decided not to do that one . A five minute walk brought us to a bridge  which would bring you to another route . Overall expect to spend between 1-2 hours here .
I personally think this fall is over-rated - the view of all three falls is just average and they are alike each others. Just come here if you have spare time only, otherwise, try other places
Beautiful waterfall. I walked to the area as it was near my hotel (M stay hotel in seogwipo). It's a huge waterfall, and a tourist attraction. The water is very clean.

The area around the waterfall is big. There are three different waterfall in the same area. You will need to walk a bit to get to the second and third tier waterfall. You can also go to the seonimyo bridge in the same area.

We stopped at Jungmun tourist complex to visit teddy bear museum by taking bus no. 282 from Arang Joeul Street in Seogwipo.  It was 6 minutes walk to Cheonjeyeon waterfall. Do not confuse this waterfall with Cheonjiyeon waterfall. The admission fee was KRW2,000 per pax. You can kill two birds with one stone. You get to see two attractions the famous Seonimgyo bridge with seven nymphs carves (fairy bridge) and the three-tiered waterfall. We did not go for the third waterfall as the trail was quite steep. We only went to the pond of fairy and the second waterfall.
Very beautiful series of waterfall with each ranging 100 to 200 meters apart from other (3 stages waterfall). Recommended for nature lover and those who love to know the history.
My review was way too late.It was our first visit to seoul and went to jeju with our 1 year old daughter.Many people went here taking photos esp tourists.Nice scenery.

Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls are a must visit spot for Jeju visitors. These falls are surrounded by greenery and bewildering rock formations ideal for snapping photos. We took a nice stroll along the falls area and also on the scenic bridges for better views.

Located an easy walk from the Seogwipo Harbor, these waterfalls and surrounding area are quite pretty, and certainly worth the easy, pleasant walk to see them. It was only 2,000 won to enter the are, and about a 5 minute walk to the actural waterfall. As someone who loves swimming in natural water, I was a little disappointed, because you can't really swim here. It was quite crowded (when I went in early August), so all my photos are full of other people. It wasn't necessarily a beautiful nature experience, so in that way a bit underwhelming, but again, worth a look.

If you stay in Seogwipo, this is absolutely a nice walk and visit. We payed 4,000 won for two people for entrance, which is worth the small amount of money. The area is beautiful where you can see different trees, fishes and of course the waterfall. We were there around 12 in the daytime, and it was a little bit crowded by the waterfall (since everyone wanted to take a picture and the place is small), but there is a small place where you can sit and just watch the beautiful waterfall!
If you're in the Jungmun area, this is worth visiting.  The very large bridge leading to the waterfall is also impressive.

If you go in the summer, be sure to take some water with you.  It's a 10-15 minute walk to  the falls and there's not much shade on the return route or actually at the falls.  Everyone tries to get as close as they can, which is fine, but there are several places to take beautiful pictures up on the platform/courtyard in front of the falls.  There are also two smaller falls that you don't see much unless you cross the bridge about halfway between the falls and the parking lot.
The hike is not for everyone, but the -lace is defitely beautiful and deserves a visit. The waterfalls are gorgeous.

A short walk from the parking lot to the falls. Walk a little further onto the rocks to get even closer and feel the cool spray from the falls and nice breeze. Relax and watch the waves break on the rocks. Beautiful! Not to be missed!

We visited this area with kids ages 3-11. Easy paved walk through a beautiful scenic shaded walkway. The falls were breathtaking. We took our shoes off and soaked our feet at the end of stairs leading into the water. Ate an easy convenience store lunch when we returned to the parking lot before heading to our next destination of the day. 1,000won for kids, 2,000won for adults. Can t beat the price.
Breathtaking waterfalls, good walk with family and kids. Love the view, the air and walk. Kids enjoyed the walk too.
We were wondering near our hotel and found the falls it was a great way to spend afternoon.  Lots of stairs so wear good shoes...but every step is rewarded with a beautiful view ⋛

There are many waterfalls in Jeju, we decided to have a look at Cheonjiyeon. There is a large parking lot, eateries and a couple of souvenir shops, 7eleven etc when you arrive. To walk to the waterfall is about 10-15 min along a small tree lined river. Many tourists and tourists groups are visiting the waterfall so it will be quite crowded. The waterfall as such is nice, but not too tall or spectacular. everybody takes a few selfies and then heads back to the parking lot pretty much. If nearby it makes to stop by and visit but it is not worth a long journey just to see this waterfall.

Really enjoyed watching how the water flowed into the sea. Interesting. Pretty much that's all you can do with a Waterfall. Beware though, the steps to climb back up from the Waterfall are quite steep, so if you're traveling with elders and kids, be prepared to walk up.
The short walk to the falls is nice, and the falls are pretty.  They are good for a quick stop, but not a must see if you don't have time here.
One letter difference, but these are not the waterfalls you want to see. Better to go to the Cheonjiyeon falls which are 10 mins east. These ones are very average.
Another in the city waterfall which means that if you are staying in Seogwipo, you must go to see this fall. Entrance is 2000 won which is justified. Beautiful views.
I was expecting a bigger waterfall but was disappointed with what I've seen.However, it's still a good place to visit to see nature in its own wonder.
There are 3 waterfalls, but only the 2nd one is above average. However, the hiking between those waterfalls is very nice.

While we are attended an business meeting, after finishing all we went to visit some places. This place is very natural, but you need to walk a little bit to reach until the fountain.Keep some time for this place to explore and perhaps enjoy. Taking photos also can be very beautiful as it offers stunning views.

This place is beautiful but crowded. What I like about this place is the structure and handrails and stairs leading to the falls seem to be sturdy. There are lots of tourist here with a small platform. So you need to   take pictures fast.

I stumbled upon this area by coincidence, I had not made any plans yet that day so I decided to visit the waterfalls. My decision was a good one! The colours of the water, lake and waterfall are amazing. There were some people but it was not too crowdy, I could easily take pictures and just wonder around, which is what I did for a few hours.

The walk to the waterfall was nice although it is kind of man made. The natural sights at the side was beautiful nonetheless.However, the waterfall itself was just ok. It didn't seem like that's the focal point of this attraction but it was good enough for a trip there.

2000krw entry.    Just beyond the ticket booth are pictures and descriptions of some of the highlights of the area along with bathroom facilities.    Further on, are some small shops and food stalls.      It s a beautiful walk with lovely plants to get to the waterfall.   There are supposed to be 2 meter long, 20 kilo eels in the pool by the waterfall.   We couldn t see any.    Waterfall was nice but nothing particularly special.

positives: truly beautiful and amazing views of nature scenery and the waterfalls. also, one can take a leisurely stroll in the attached garden park. entry fee was only 2000 won.negatives: there was a bit of a crowd the day we visited, although it was still manageable. the entrance to the falls could be tricky to find if you planning to go there on foot from Seogipwo town. DO NOT follow google maps as it will only point you to the exact geographical location of the falls. You should walk down along taepyeong road until you see the bridge and the sea. cross the bridge and you will see a big carpark. the ticket office will be on the right side, near 7-11

We went down to the second pond in rain and the stairs is quite steep so u gotta be very careful with ur steps. Upon arrival there is a platform where u can take photo of the fall. For dipping experiences u can continue hiking to fall no 1. No 3 is the farthest. U can refer to the map.

We went on a very rainy day, so not many people.    Neither of us had any trouble with footing.   It was not slippery at all!     Huge level of water flow.    I can t believe they found it necessary to have a no swimming sign as if anyone would even attempt it.   Maybe when the water flow was greatly reduced.    We only went to the 1st and 2nd falls.     Enjoyed them.   Entire walk for the 2 doesn t take more than 30 minutes.   I imagine on a nice day there were be a large number of vendors at the end  but this day, there was no one out.

We didn't expect much for this attraction. But it turned out so amazing. We enjoyed the path leading to the main fall with pretty things from the trees to statues. It must be good to be here in early April as of many cherry blossom trees.

This is a beautiful spot to sit and enjoy nature at its best. We saw some amazing little birds and the waterfall is stunning. There was a lot of water going down the falls when we visited in April this year. This is a must do! Be ready to go up and down a lot of stairs. :)

There are 4 main attractions and you easily spend 1.5- 2 hours there, we only go to 2 waterfalls as we afraid there won t be enough time to go to other places.4 main attractions :Seoningmo bridgeCheonjiyeon Waterfall2nd Waterfall3rd WaterfallSome stairs here and there, don't miss it if you are in Jeju,

There are 3 tiers of the waterfall but we only opt to go for 2 of the tiers as the 3 tier is a long walk down the trail and path. And we know we will have a long walk up which we are not inclined to do. The 1st tier and 2nd tier is not far from each other and really have a lot of good photo taking points for memory keep sake. The path is well guided with sign board and easy to walk. The most well worth place is the bridge as the design and color is really unique.

The whole way from the car park to the falls itself was scenic. At the start was a pond with mandarin ducks and a bridge. There were various representative statues of Jeju. There were also souvenir shops if you want to buy some snacks or souvenirs. I liked the different types of trees grown, even though it is not autumn, the maple trees still looked very pretty. All along the way is a river, you go to the falls on one side and you can return on the other side of the river. There were plenty of explanation signs on the falls, the mottled eels and the rock face etc. The falls themselves don t look very impressive but I still like the whole place. On the way back there is a nice flower display and large sculpture as well a stone auditorium.
This attraction was challenging for people with mobility issues. It is however quite serene and beautiful.
This place show a 3 tier waterfall that you need to walk different place by follow the path. The 3rd tier a bit tough as very steep and staircases.

Compare to Jeongbang waterfall, this place is much more worth for a visit as it surrounded with cherry flowers. It will definitely a nice view when full blossom of cherry flowers. Be sure you go to the right place as the name just different with a alphabet. This is CheonjIyeon that near to Saeseom Island Saeyeongyo Bridge not CheonjEyeon (3 tier waterfall) that located in Jungmun.
Very beautiful waterfall. You have to go there The place is amazing. Not only the waterfall but also the nature, with the water and ducks and fish

The place is breathtaking, starting from the parking lot with all the old ladies selling the traditional stuff, the park is amazing with the clear water and swimming ducks & fish, the sakora tree is more than beautiful, then the waterfall i can t even describe its beauty....and the ticket cost only 2000 Korean won . Inside the park there is a clean toilet and services alsoIf you go to jeju you must visit it

In order to reach this beautiful waterfall one has to endure walking for few minutes. We went there on April, it was the start of the spring season, yet it was windy so it was cold. For me the fall is just average, may be because I have seen more beautiful falls from the other countries. However, this is worth the walk and time. We manage to have beautiful photos near the falls and in the park.

If you visit the waterfalls do not expect that the water is floating like crazy. They're  freeze!! We didn't like it at all. There was pretty much no water falling out of the water falls. You climb very steep stairs and get very tired. The bridge is good for a few nice clicks though.
Agree with many of reviewers is pathed very well with many stairs but was worth the visit. Close to the bus stop provided great access & has large car park.
This can be a quick afternoon activity for fit people. It was a lot of stairs but we got some great pictures, it was a beautiful little hidden treasure!

My 10 yo daughter and I have really enjoyed seeing the waterfall. It was a quick 20 minute walk up a scenic paved path with some other small falls. It was definitely worth a visit. Cost couple won to get in. There are several shops right outside and along the way to buy souvenirs and snacks.

You will have to purchase yr tickets first before venturing further as the next booth only inspects the ticket. you probably need about 10 to 15mins walk before you reached the waterfall.  Do take your time to admire the nature during yr walk.  You can take the other path when you leave the waterfall. I enjoyed that moment with my family.

Our guide dropped us at Seonimgyo Bridge at around 8am, and said he would pick us up around 11.30am.  3.5hrs for waterfalls?  I thought he must have made a mistake...Surprise surprise... We enjoyed the morning stroll across the park near Seonimgyo Bridge (with autumn leaves still visible in end Nov).  After a million selfies, we made our way to the 1st waterfall and was awestruck!  So beautiful!  Well strictly speaking, this is not a waterfall but a lake of some sort.  But who cares about the misnomer?To reach the 2nd falls, there is a well-marked trail.  A medium-distance walk with its fair share of up and down slopes.  Not arduous and I would definitely recommend it.  The waterfall is not Niagara, but I found it pretty in its subtlety.The 3rd falls has a warning - the trail may be difficult for children and elderly.  Since I am neither, I had assumed incorrectly that I would find it manageable.  Wrong!  It was a very very long way down (which was fine), and an equally long long way up (nearly killed me).  Was it worth it?  I am afraid not... for the 3rd falls. So my recommendation would be to visit the first 2 falls, but give the 3rd a miss (unless you want a workout).
A nice n serene place to stroll n relax. It took about 30minutes to walk around the reserve. Definitely worth the KRW2000 entry fee.

Our family visited the Cheonjiyeon Falls on the first day of our trip. We came out quite late, around 5 pm and we decided to come here as this was one of the attractions that were opened at that time. The admission fee was reasonably cheap. The area was not that big as I imagined, you walk from the entrance to the waterfall and then back. The waterfall is quite nice to look at and I'm pretty sure it might look more majestic if you come here at night. Even though I came on a cloudy and rainy day, it didn't ruin the mood much, it makes the waterfall more mysterious and I liked the atmosphere.

No point come to this fall, not even if you are nearby. Not worth your time. I walked all the way in just to find out that The waterfall is so small. I don t see how they made an attraction out of this.

Overall the park is very pretty with its vibrant colors of the trees and the famous bridge you can walk across.

Niagra falls these falls are not, but they are picturesque.  The are small, but the ticket price was also small.  It is a ten minute walk from the parking lot to see the falls, and it is a little tourist trap, but if you have the time to kill check them out, but there are probably better ways to spend your time on the Jeju.
This is a pretty fall wig a light walk.  The whole place is set up beautifully for a visit with a family. I thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

This is a three tiered waterfall. To see all three you must walk a lot of staircases. It is much smaller than what I thought but where it is quite beautiful. If in Jeju I recommend a visit(if you love the nature).
The falls can be viewed from various points. We went in October and it was perfect. Beautiful, well maintained.

The Halla Arboretum is a sort of giant tree garden/park spread out over a mountain with innumerable trails that span the mountain side, leading to the top.  Key trees are labeled in museum fashion though the information provided is minimal.  Think of the arboretum as a park on a hillside with paths leading to a summit with views of the peak and city.  It's quietly beautiful with the cool air gently perfumed by the trees and soil.  If you are traveling on Jeju and are looking for a place to spend d1-2 hours, the Halla Arboreteum is a good call.

On a hot day, between breaks in a storm, my girlfriend and I came here for a nice walk with a great view at the top, where we met a very friendly Korean chap who told us stories of his life. Would definitely recommend as a close place to get to from the city.

Welcome to the first Teddy Bear Museum in Korea. Here you will find everything you want to know about Teddy Bears. Teddy Bears have been loved and cherished since they were first introduced over 100 years ago. There are now millions of people who collect Teddy Bears. They seek out old, unique and valuable teddy bears for their personal collections. Our Teddy Bear Museum opened especially for the European collectors. The Teddy Bear Museum is more exciting than ever with "Teddy Bear" entertainment as never seen before. Jeju Teddy Bear Museum opened on April 24, 2001. It contains two galleries, a museum gift shop, and a museum cafe. Also, on site is a museum bar/restaurant, a wonderful place to meet friends, family, and lovers. From the outside garden, there is a view of Jung-Mun Beach.

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a  compulsory  destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a  grand  welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Since their official website is unclear about opening hours in June, I called the 1330 Korea Travel Hotline and was informed that the museum was indeed open late under summer hours. So after spending 45 minutes in and 30,000+ – on a taxi to visit the area with my girlfriend, who absolutely loves teddy bears, we arrived at 6:10pm. With doors still open and people still inside, we were told the museum closed at 6pm. After asking politely to let us enter the gallery and "No, no, no" being the only response, I asked the non-English speaking employee for management and soon they found someone who spoke English. I calmly explained the situation and again asked for an exception, that we were only here for a day, it would be doing us a great favor and that we would finish with the other guests and not prevent them from going home late. We were again met "No, no, no" To her credit, the English speaking manager(?) did include a "sorry" with her "no's" and did genuinely want to know how I received wrong information about their hours (and yes,if I can find a way to review the Korea Travel Hotline, they too will receive a poor rating). But ultimately, we were turned away. The only positive I could take from this experience is that, from what we could see from the lobby, the gallery looked small and over-rated. Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper "museum", I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The "attractions" are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess "who" they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and "E=mc2" to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no "history" of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any "exhibits", whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the "Elvis Stage Show". Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the "stage". On the quarter hour, the announcement is made - "The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!" The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and "Elvis has left the building" - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of "entertainment".

Cute, fun.. there is a place for you a teddy bear museum  Jeju, a nice setting museum and you can see many different teddy bear...

Nice place to stop by, especially if travelling with kids but an interesting attraction all the same for adults. Teddy bears in various displays from famous movie, artworks and different eras. Lots of photo opportunities!

If you like teddy bears and in the vicinity, take time to visit.Some rare teddy bears are on display and you can buy overpriced souvenir bears to enjoy.

If u like striking out poses with friends using the lifesize teddy bears in different costumes and characters, this is the place for u. Looks really good and I think it would be a nice feeling sitting around in the outdoor garden having ur lunch. That's provided it does rain. This is an in-door exhibits, with some out-door, but not during winter season. Probably 45-min visit will suffice.The in-doors exhibits were housed in glass, so not good for photo-takings, alot of reflections from the surrounding lightings. Some glass were dusty inside.

Main target is the teddy bear in Goong drama  but just one section there..a lot of cute, handsome, pretty teddy bears are gathered in this farm..you should spend hours here as the farm is huge! easy to park your car and enjoy your fairytales day there!!

It is an interesting museum with many Teddy Bear dolls in different suites. From Teddy bears in Berlin Wall destruction to Teddy bear in Kings suites as well as in Monalisa paintings! It is intresting for children.

Everything about our favourite bear and its history. The museum has 3 floors, where you can see many different displays of teddy bears and animatronics, in a different setting. The museum is located opposite of Jeju Korea Tourism Organisation and can be reached from Seogwipo or Airport on bus number 600. There is a cafe within the museum and a theater showing Elvis Presley lookalike teddy bear singing Elvis's songs. It is about a 15 minutes session.

Sounds odd that it is actually my favourite attraction.. I love teddy bears. You get to see Elvis teddy bear performing "live" with his friends too. First time seeing teddy bear moving, wow experience for me. The souvenir shop is expensive though... nonetheless do give it a visit if you are a teddy lover! There is a Steve Jobs teddy, Einstein Teddy, quite creative and a twist to the usual brooding teddy we see.
No doubt it is quite costly but there are a lot of teddy bear exhibits here which is quite worth the visit. Try it if you are nearby. Just pick one of the teddy bear museum in Korea would be enough.

I loved this place!!! Maybe because I love teddy bears and collect them. But objectively, I think they did a wonderful job to dress the bears up in adorable costumes and arrange them in all sorts of different themed settings. You start at the 3rd floor and walk down to the 1st. My favourite was the 2nd floor - even though the exhibits are encased in glass, I could put my own little bears (yes, I brought my own bears with me on this trip) on the glass and take pictures with them (no flash allowed). Some of the bears have even moving parts and some are life-sized. There is a scheduled musical and dance performance by Elvis bear and friends, which my parents enjoyed. At the outdoors area, you can take photos with life-sized bears in interesting poses and themed settings and there is even a clock that chimes hourly and is accompanied by bears dancing with the chimes. There is a cafe and a souvenir shop in the ground level and you can take pictures with panda bears (not real of course) and other cute bears, and buy a souvenir bear home (but price is quite ex).

Of all the indoor activities we did this was probably the most disappointing of them all. If you are into bears then you will enjoy the recreated scenes.lots of things to see and a good visit for young kids

Of course there is a gift shop where you can purchase teddy bears.  My wife and I enjoyed it and took lots of pictures.  I think you will enjoy this place, even if you don't have a thing for teddy bears. Bonus:  there is a really nice Starbucks right across the street.

Cuteness overload! They recreate the famous historical event, famous artpiece, famous public figure, which is starring the teddy bear itself! You can read about the teddy bear history, too. The museum is on the 1st & 2nd floor, while the ground floor is a merchandise store where you can buy some teddy bear dolls, etc.

This is a fun place to visit. I wouldnt get out of my way to see it, but if you are in Jungmun and have an hour, its a fun place to see. The place is small but there are a lot different section and concept bears in the museum from drama series to fashion...and my favorite Elvis Presley!! I wish they have more bears soon. Good place for adults and kids to visit!

A good place to go if you love Teddy Bear. For us, I had a good time having some history lessons with my 8 year old daughter. Located in the middle of Jungmun Resort right across from a Ripley's Believe it or Not museum, I would only recommend this kitsch and cheese-tastic museum to visitors on a bleak and rainy day. The idea is cute, at best - history and art through the ages represented by teddy bears (My Fair Lady, Princess Diana and Prince Charles get married, the falling of the Berlin War, the Beatles, Mona Lisa, the Creation of Adam, etc.), but I would expect a museum in an expensive resort complex to at least have descriptions in English and other tourist languages (Japanese, Mandarin, Cantonese). The entrance fee of 8000 won is a little steep for what you are able to see. Not surprisingly, there is an entire floor dedicated to a pricey gift shop. The most impressive parts of the museum are the architecture of the glass pyramidal shaped building and the views from the garden to the rear. Overall, it's an alright way to kill an hour or so, but definitely not a must-see for me.

My mother-in-law bought my husband and I entry to this "museum" and I went in expecting ultra-hokey and a waste of time. I was really pleasantly surprised!There are a few "galleries". The highlights for me were the Teddy Bear History gallery - where they use teddy bears to display historical dioramas including a Teddy Moon Landing, teddy bears knocking down the Berlin Wall, Teddy Disney World and more. These are pretty creative and well made. Some even include music.There's also an "art" gallery, with some famous paintings or sculptures reenacted with teddy bears. This gallery extends into more dioramas such as the "runway" and a Korean wedding scene. Not always logical in where they put things, but fun anyway. There are a few honestly significant teddies in the museum - a Louis Voittan teddy that cost millions at auction, and a small side gallery of Teddies combined with historical memorabilia from Teddy Roosevelt, with some brief English descriptions of where the teddy bear came from.It's not a top attraction if you're here for a short visit, but if you're around a while and want something cute and fun, it's worth an hour or two!
