This is a pretty informative museum where it shows how teddy bears in the past till where it is presently.However, adults wont probably enjoy it as much. The place is small and this attractive can be finished easily within 40 mins. Go only if you have time or when it rains
Some of the bears on display are quite old and dusty. Generally, give it a try if you have not been to other teddy bear museum.

The museum is full of teddies of all sizes created from all the Korean dramas begining with the classic "Winter Sonata" till the American President Obama. On the rooftop, you can view the whole valley of Jejudo as well as the scenic Hallasan. There are some cookies for sampling and plenty of teddies for sale in the shop at the end of the tour^^~
museum, full of teddy bears, so nice. we seem so much of different types of teddy bears with different way of presenting, cute way, rock way, lovely way and so and soooo...

Unless you really really love Teddy Bears, this place is rather overpriced. At 8,000KRW per person, it gets expensive if you're in a group. And, they won't let you enter the gift shop without paying for a ticket. In the end, we found their gift shop not terribly different from the Safari Teseum (7,000KRW per person, but you can go directly to the gift shop). The Safari Teseum gift shop actually had more options (aka other animals for those who don't like stuffed bears).Still, if you really love Teddy Bears, you can make a day of it between the two places.

I have always wanting to visit Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju because of the K-Drama - Goong.But I felt is abit over-rated as I myself is not a soft toy person.If you love soft toys or teddy bear, is a must go, otherwise, you can drop by and have a quick look.

If you are going with little kids, definitely go. But otherwise it's just OK though I would say worth a visit if you are bored. Pretty much all the information is in Korean, but then again doesn't take much to identify the teddy bear version of Steve Jobs or Albert Einstein ;) The place has two floors of teddy bears, and I must say after about 25 teddies they all start looking the same. This was close to our hotel and it was raining so we paid a visit. I would advise the museum to put more info in English as Jeju is becoming more internationlised in terms of tourists.

I had to go there because of my girlfriend who was really excited to visit! It was nice, very well organised and unlimited versions of cool bears, if you're in that kind of things, you definitely need to give it a try!

It is one of many museums in Jeju, and it's dedicated to Teddy bears. It is full of its history with all the teddy bears from all over the world. All of the ancient teddy bears is well preserved but with relatively minimal background story. Some of the information are written only in Korean, so there isn't many interactive attraction here. There is also an open garden with a few sculptures on it, a Lotteria restaurant and of course the store. The merchandise there is quite expensive and we didn't buy anything. The entrance fee when we came there is 8000 won, a little bit expensive, but quite worth it.
I wish i can bring home all the teddy bear back home but unfortunately i cant... so sad... Keep up the good job as this is the 2nd time i came here

Went in Feb 14. Admission fee: 9000 won eachIt is located near to Alive Museum and Believe it or Not Musuem. The Seogwipo tourist center is also nearby.The whole touring of the museum took us about 1hr. It was quite small but filled with loads and loads of teddy!Worth a visit if you love teddy bears, else you can forget about going there since the admission fee is not that cheap.

The teddy bear museum is exactly what it's title states.  It's teddy bears in every shape and size.  The first area has historical teddy bears, dating back as far as the turn of the century (1900's).  The second section is works of art redone with teddy bears and finally, there is an outdoor exhibit including a 9 meter tall teddy bear that makes a showing every hour on the hour.  Young kids that like teddy bears and such will have a great time visiting here.  My daughter adored everything.  It is a little pricey, but if you rent a car to get around they often give you a book with coupons for the various attractions on the island or you can book in advance online at a discount price.
strictly for teddy bear lovernothing much to see hereyeah..maybe a couple of rare teddy bearmight be good for families with children

My friends and I visited this museum in Jeju as our ode to one of our fave korean dram Goong. So we looked for the bears used in the drama like Alfred and the rest of the bears featured in the drama and we were quite excited seeing them in the flesh although a bit disappointed as it was not for sale.The museum features also life sized bears, bears resembling famous celebrities like michael jordan, elvis presley, the beatles,superman or bear?,old bears like old winnie the pooh, bears in hanboks, drewsed like emperors in  joseon dynasty,astronauts,a vampirebear, a Ronin bear, a Leonardo da  Vinci bear,A bear in LV get up,paddington bear,care bears,polar bears,there were bears in the outside depicting picnic, inside a telephone booth,fishing and even a bear taking a leak....one will enjoy if you are a bear lover. they also have a souvenir shop to buy of course different kinds of bears

The title summed it all up. I love stuffed toys, but even I found the place overpriced and boring. The ones that held my interest were those actual historical bears. But that's the end it. The elvis show was terrible too. We left the place within the hour.  Take your money and time else where. Jeju has more to offer than this!

The museum is quite small and expensive....there are 2 floors with old teddy bears and teddy bear versions of famous painting and famous people. If you are nearby you can go but I would not specifically go there. My 3 years old son was little scared by the giant bears in display! Koreans seem to like it more
It would worth your time to visit if you have kids along or yourself personally fancy about all these bears. The collection of bear is alright though. But they are really cute

This is a very expensive museum that is not worth visiting.  Although they have a lot of antique teddy bear and nice gallery but most of the explaination are in korea that make us difficult to understand their history.  The staff are not good in speaking English or Chinese.  The only good things is their surrounding scenery are nice for photographer to take photo.

You can find all kinds of teddy bears in the museum and the "cosplay"is simply amazing. I was impressed by how creative they are. There is a garden behind the museum for which you can have a short walk with a couple of photos.

This place is a must-see if you're a fan of teddy bears, but it's not just for the rabid fans.  I don't count myself as a particular fan one way or another, but I don't dislike them.  The bears here are displayed as various characters and in a variety of situations.  They're cute and can be interesting, but if you're not really into this kind of thing then you'd be bored.  I'm sure children would enjoy it.  For myself, I enjoyed it but I've seen it once and wouldn't go back.

I am not a teddy bear lover, but I found the collection very interesting. First of all, these were the collection of a Ms. Joanne Oh, a teddy bear artist. The bears date up to generations of collectibles. The design varies with time. The size of the bear are from tiny to bigger than man size. There were several hall showing different themes. Of course it will end with a souvenir shop showing many bear designs. In the international bear, there was even one of President Obama, with a letter of President Obama to Joanne Oh. The museum also has an advocacy of bear conservation. All in all, it was interesting with plenty of Photo opportunity for my wife who loved it so much. By the way, the materials used in Ms. Oh's bear were all made of ecological-friendly materials, another advocacy of this fantastic bear artist.

The collection of teddy bears is good and very nicely organized according to themes. I especially loved the collections of very old teddy bears and the stories behind them and their owners that really touched a soft spot in my heart. There were also very vintage Winnie the Pooh bears that were really an eye-opener, as well as bears wearing traditional korean costumes depicting scenes of ancient korean life that I liked. The outdoors section of the exhibits were however not very impressive and when my friend and I visited the museum in June, the museum was very warm indoors. We were sweating profusely as we looked at the exhibits and in fact found it a joy to go outdoors into the sun, which turned out to be cooler. This prevented me from giving the attraction a four star rating. However, the collection is really a must-see for teddy bear lovers and it will undoubtedly be a more enjoyable place to visit in other months of the year.

Not to miss, though you are not a fan, you will be bought after going their collection of bears and display theme. Explore your soft side. Admission fee is reasonable, you will definitely not feel any weight lifted off your wallet.

Let's first get this out of the way: If you're not a teddy bear fan, if you're an over-serious person, or basically, if you had a fun-less childhood, don't bother visiting this place. Because then it would be pretty much a tourist ripoff kind of place, with nothing really worth seeing.But, if you do like bears, and regardless of how cheesy or a ripoff this place can be, you just want to have some fun, then by all means, check it out!Admittedly, I quite like teddy bears myself, and right from the moment I stepped in, I was constantly tickled by all the teddy bears modeled in the form of famous people, famous artworks, and even historical events. It can be sometimes strange to see the head of a bear in the place of what should've been a human one, but toss the strangeness aside and you'll realize there is so much to see and chuckle over. Having teddy bears in place of humans in the exhibits add a touch of innocent cuteness to everything.Do note that there's both an indoor and outdoor exhibit, so if you're on a schedule yet really want to see everything, make sure you plan your time well!

We would have never imagined that you can make so much out of a teddy bear. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience and I would suggest it for any bear lover but especially for families with young kids. As for the Alive Museum, I would strongly advice to go there either in the morning or early in the afternoon. We visited it in the morning and it was a bliss, but my guts' feeling tells me the crowds in the afternoon must be a little bit more stressful to deal with.PS: Don't forget the Elvis Presley Show. Yes, it is kind of tacky but really cute anyway!

The entrance fee was quite high, but it was a very fun family outing.  Our son loves teddy bears so this was great.  There were a lot of displays of bears in various famous places and dressed as famous people in history - cool.
We enjoyed this museum thoroughly.  Thousands of teddy bears with a multitude of poses, extremely creative. Very good history of teddy bears.
Much bigger than I thought. it is a nice visit and they have many different type of bear. Amazing! because they still can keep them in very good condition.

Appreciate the effort put in to do up the various exhibits. The fact that they were in closed exhibits surely help the maintenance of the whole place coz comparatively, the Teddy Bear Teseum/Safari was more run down.

My wife and I enjoyed taking in the detailed research and work that were put into this teddy bear exhibition. They have records and teddy bears from the 1900s alongside an outdoor teddy bear garden to soak in the teddy atmosphere.

As a bear lover, I enjoy this museum & appreciate all the hard work put into each & individual presentation & its theme. Be warn that its really for the young & young at heart. My only regret is that I missed the outdoor cafe. Didnt realised after I exited & look down thru the windows. Must have missed the signages? Overall , a good way to spend 1-2 hours
romantic feeling but at the same time feeling creepy. So many cute bears inside please be prepared the cuteness of the bear..:)

We didn't think our 11 year old and 7 year old boys would be interested in this museum at ll. Much to our surprise our oldest request to go. It was actually a lot of fun. It was a challenge for the boys to identify all the various moments in history that were depicted.

The Teddy Bear Museum is a pleasant surprise. The museum is very close to The Lotte Hotel and just across the street from Ripley s Believe it or Not in Jungmun.  The exterior is nice. I wonder if the Louvre Museum was an inspiration for the conical architectural design of the museum.  The exhibitions consisted of many famous pictures and major events in human history. The difference is that in this museum, the teddy bears have taken over. So you will see Teddy Bear versions of Neil Armstrong on the moon, Michael Jordan dunking a basket ball, Elvis Presley rocking a guitar, Psy showing us Gangnam Style, and Marilyn Monroe, etc.  It is interesting, cute and amusing.  I am really glad I visited this museum and you should visit it too even if it is just for the laughs. It is adorable.

This museum shows the history of teddy bears and put them in different scenes depicting their eras.There is also an Elvis Presley show at the level 2 theatre at every 15 mins. Do catch the show!This place would be fantastic for teddy bear lovers and the children.
Love teddies and this museum is better than the one in Seoul.  Just loved all the different stories and also examples of the different teddies during the ages.  So worth a visit for young and old!!

I don't have a big thing about Teddy Bear but was curious enough to see what a museum full of teddies would be like.  There are quite a number of interesting teddy bears along the exhibits and my favourite ones were probably the Elvis bear, the MJ bear and the Terracotta army bears.

I have 2 little boys. One thing for sure, this not a place for them. Probably the girls might like it. I don't recommend this place to those who do not fancy Teddy Bears. But if you wish to buy teddy bear souvenirs this might be the right place. In fact we bought several souvenirs for the little girls back home. My advise is SKIP this place if you're not Teddy Bear lovers.

This was pretty entertaining. I had no idea what would be in a Teddy Bear museum... PLEASE go though. There are tons of bears from every period imaginable, wearing period and geographical clothing to match. Everyone is represented and it was actually a lot better than I thought when I hear "we are going to the Teddy Bear Museum".... don't let that fool you! There is also an outside where you can walk around and see life-sized teddy bears. The gift shop is at the very end, and you WILL want something from it. Class Act, and a welcomed surprise!

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).
Description of the various teddy bears on display are in korean. You can only take photos and look at it without understanding about it

believe there is another teddy bear museum in the area which offers a slightly different experience, the teddy bears are special along with the LV bear which is termed the most expensive bear in the world. tried looking for the world's oldest teddy but cant seem to find it as appeared in the TV show. the organisation/directory can be better~!

Expected the place to be bigger. Only reason we went here was to kill some time before heading to the airport. Could have gone to the Ripley's museum instead which was just across the road. As expected, lots of teddy bears in the museum. Only interesting part was the history section. They had teddy bears from as old as 1905 on display. The bears were still kept in good condition.

Having just visited the newly opened Teddy Bear Museum in Chengdu, Sichuan Province, China (by the same group), this original museum in Jeju was a little underwhelming, even for a solid teddy bear fan like me. Unlike those in Chengdu, I didn't appreciate the fact that all teddies in Jeju were enclosed in glass cases. Impossible to take a decent pic with them!There was a good collection of antique bears. Great for a collector like myself. Also there was the supposedly most expensive teddy bears in the world. The LV bear and the diamond bear.For sale of their Elvis bears I believe, there was a small theater on the second floor showing 4 mins Elvis teddy concert every quarter of the hour. Perhaps I went at a later hour (5pm), I was the only one in the theater. Appreciate that the museum is opened till 8pm in the evening, so it's great as a quick destination pre or post dinner, if you are staying or hanging around the Jungmum Resort Area. The museum was located right next to Lotte Hotel. There was a Lotteria on the ground floor but it was closed during my visit. An attractive and well stocked teddy store on the ground floor too, unlike its sad and sparse Chengdu cousin. Happy that there were some collector grade Korean handmade teddies for sale. Their house brand "so-called" limited edition replica made-in-China white Alfred bear (real limited edition would come with serial numbers) came in a nice copycat Steiff look alike gift box and a photo with a Korean prince. At only USD 35, it's great as a souvenir/gift!I like the outdoor park area. Great for kids to run around. Overall not a very big place. Whole place would take about an hour.

The Teddy Bear museum is near other attractions in Seogwipo.  Opposite is the Believe it or Not Museum.  If you have watched the korean drama Goong (The Palace or Princess Hours) , this place place is probably something you would like to visit.  I like teddy bears and it's fun to look into all those dressed up teddy bears.

is kind of pricey. there are only 2 levels of bears being exhibits and it is all behind the glass. The bears are just being display in different themes and costumes. we were impressed at the beginning but started to get bored a moment later. Overall, it is still worth a visit.

basically its a museum filled with teddy bears arranged to replicate some famous events and daily lives. The worst part is, there is only 2 exhibition halls for you to look at. If they were to do it like "Its a small world" theme, i think that would be more entertaining. Not really worth going, sadly.

We went in, looked around the first 5 minutes and then left. I like teddy bears, I'm actually a bit of a big kid, but this was all a bit boring. Lots and lots of bears dressed in little outfits. Maybe good if it's raining but if the sun is shining outside I'd advise you to try other things. It was crowded too, so you couldn't easily see the displays anyway.

Enjoyed this attraction a lot. There are bears everywhere and everywhere is a shooting spot. Most of the teddy bears are quite big in size thus everyone will have different pose to take pictures with them. They are all so adorable and even the smaller size teddy bears are very cute. Liked the giant teddy bear where have to climb up to sit on its back, I tried for at least 10 times and finally I am able to climb up, it was real fun. Also like to sit on the giant sofa in the teddy house surrounded by so many giant teddy bears. There are bears that feature Korean movie and pop stars but yet to see a Psy teddy bear

This is definitely a place for kids & ladies. Sorry guys. It is bear, bear, bear & more bear wherever you turn your head. Thank goodness photography is allowed in here. Most of the bears are small, about the height of your palm. I guess that makes them all the cuter. There is a giantic bear in front of the souvenir shop. Do take a few shots with it. Considering the number of bears on display, the number of teddy bear related memorabilia is quite limited,. I wonder why.

Worth paying for. There are so many teddies in various costumes and postures. There are elvis, the paddington bear, bear at the markets. For those who loves teddy bears, you can also see the evolution of teddy bears . My personal favourite is the teddy bears as featured in Princess Hours and also few diorama of korean culture; the women's diver, korean traditional wedding. Dont forget to take the picture at the park too! My take on the souveniers, as expected is a bit pricey, but if you want to have a momento, maybe you should buy the postcards.

Historic timeline of bears from all over the world. Endless phototaking of them in the exhibition. Feeling closer to bears after teh bear musuem ... :) Must go for bear loversHowever, if there were more life-size bears for photo taking will be fantastic. The bears were all inside the glass panels except for those on sale. The bears on sale were not very cheap.
The teddies in the museum are all so adorable!!! My family and I enjoyed every minute in the museum, taking photos with the teddies indoors and outdoors! Must-visit!!!

The teddy bears in many styles, very funny and complete! We can also do the interactive pose in the stage and take some picture there, ex: go hunting with teddy, being proposed by teddy (!), sing along with teddies band, etc.
This is quite an interesting place, even I'm not really a teddy bear fans, I quite enjoyed the visit because there are many different "styles" of teddy bear!

There are 2 teddy bear museums in Jeju. I don't have the address of the one that I went to, but it's not the one in Jungmun, which is the older one and where you'll only see teddy bears in glass cases. The newer teddy bear museum has teddy bears that are displayed according to themes, where you can pose together  with the teddy bears, and even touch and hug them. This is definitely more interactive than the ones in glass cases.

This teddy bear museum is one of a few around the world.  Located in Jungmun tourist complex in Jeju, Korea, is this tiny museum for teddy bear fans alike.  For 8000 KRW you have unlimited day access to 3 floors of teddy bear exhibits and the outside grounds.  This museum carries interesting themed bears like the Mona Lisa bear, the Leonardo Da Vinci bear, a Marilyn Monroe bear, and so many others.  Currently they are displaying the Elvis bear.  On the ground floor there is even a really nice restaurant if you get hungry.  Not much choice in  terms of breakfast, they do offer mostly burgers and different types of coffees.  Also there is a gift shop if you are interested in taking home one of the really cute teddy bear souvenirs.Well worth the visit and few hours for both teddy bear fans and those with just a passing interest.  Remember to use the lockers next to the admission counter.  We didn't and carried all our jackets and bags for the entire exhibit,  It will make the visit a whole lot lighter and more fun.  Enjoy!
Visited the place for the first time and really love their bears! Check out the Mona Lisa bear. Took a lot of photos.
Our 4 yr old son was bored after 1 min. Can see the whole place in less than 10 mins. We paid w22 k for 2 adults and one child. Go only if you are a teddy bear fanatic.

Teddy bears comically arranged to recreate different points in history. I must give credit for the details of the handiwork, including teeny-weeny plates and swords. A must-see for teddy bear afficionados... if you happen to stumble into it, you may be like WTF.

Without considering visitors could visit and shop at this museum, they charged the highest entrance fee among all other natural sites we visited in Jeju. If it were not for the kids, it was certainly not worthwhile to pay 4 times the entrance fees to other UNESCO sites.
This place was pretty kool, and it's great to take the kids there. I wouldn't say it would be a lost if you didn't have time to go here. Unless you really want to see teddy bears...

Interesting number of teddy bear! A bear for a lot of historical event and people... From superman to world war 2! But the LV bear was not around though, which a bit disappointing !But generally quite nice to see their creativity in the design of the bears

My frd and i been looking forward to visit the teddy bear museum cos we heard tat it hv a outdoor areas displaying e bears but reslise it is jus a small area which u can finish within 15mins.The 2 storey museum seem smaller than e 1 at seoul tower.Overall,is still worth to visit if u hv e extra time cos u will find e bears cute and hv a interesting background for each display.

Unless you are under 12 years old or have a stuffed toy fetish, this is a very overpriced place. Nothing really much to see. Save your money for the caves and falls of jeju instead....real natural wonders.

Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju opened in 2001 and boasts for owning the largest collection of teddy bears.  What differentiates this museum from the rest is that Korea's history was told using the bears.  It was cute and a not so serious approach that would cater to the children.The museum consists of 2 Exhibition halls namely the hall of history and the hall of art.  This museum serves as the home for as many as 1,500 bears that includes the luxurious Louis Vuitton bear.
A very very cute and creative ... we really enjoyed to see all the classic teddy bears... and especially the LV and Swarosky studded one! My son really enjoyed it...

you can view the teddy bears from different countries,enjoy yourself at the museum shop, caf챕, restaurant or the outdoor park where you can view the spectacular Jungmun Sea. At the museum garden, you can meet the teddy bear sculptures and models. The garden decorated with various themes such as the Korean Black bear family and the magical pond. Children under are free. Lots of free parking.

Thought it was gonna be some just rows and rows of teddy bear displays but was pleasantly surprised by the presentation and the whole set-up...the curators really have got a sense of humour!  :)was more like entering an art museum...

The history of teddy bears is interesting and there are some examples of early teddy bears.  There are also teddy bears dressed up in various outfits, including as astronauts landing on the moon and a fashion show.  Don't miss the Elvis Teddy bears, including the singing Elvis.
I have never seen so many Teddy Bears in one place. Many bears were produced about 100 years ago. It is interesting place for children as well as for adult visitors.

Kids were enjoying this, but for an adult, it's a waste of time. I was in and out in less than an hour, including the "Elvis show." It is a bunch of teddy bears dressed up in famous scenes. There are some antique teddy bears on display, but everything is only in Korean. The Elvis show was a mechanical teddy bear in a jumpsuit that played Elvis music. It said things like, "Mahalo, I just love being here in Hawaii," but no one else seemed to notice. Total. Tourist. Trap.

This museum, like most of Jeju's other similar attractions, is but an excuse to get you to the gift shop. You can finish it in one hour, because they want to get you there fast! As opposed to most other museums in this resort island, this one is cute and amusing. It consists mostly of tableaus or displays with teddy bears re-enacting some important historical or popular culture event. Some may frown at the "Gandhi" teddy bear as perhaps not quite tasteful, but must surely enjoy the "Beatles" teddy bears, the "Chinatown" teddy bears, etc. You get the picture. Oh, yes the gift shop! It works; I bought a little cute bear as most everybody else seems to have done. Not that expensive and well-made. In other words, if you are going to see at least one of these museums that dot the south of the island, you may want to give this one a try. It's enjoyable.

smaller than what i thought. But a lot of bear with different characters inside. For a hurry visitor, you would just need no longer than 1 hour to finish all part of the museum. The elvis bear show was nice but quite short and not really worth to see, thats why it is free.

If you like bears, it would be fun because there are many types of bears and collections of bears from around the world and there is a outdoor park where you can take picture with human size fake bears. But it was not as big as expected and it can be finished within 2 hours.

I spent few hours at the museum, I had jet lag  because of 6 hours difference in my biological hour, & it is near Hana Hotel where I stayed. It is a nice walk to the museum. I thought it is a happy place, because most of the visitors were happy especially those with children. I took my time looking at the museum & the shop. I enjoyed my time. The museum have stairs & elevator. I took lunch at the resturant , it is fast food, with reasonable price.Bathrooms at each level & they are clean. The view from outside the resturant is nice & relaxing, & the outside garden is beautiful.I watched the Elvis show,it is nice & professional work. I think to enjoy & appreciate the museum you have to spend few hours, not a quick visit.I thought it is a delightful happy place.

The indoor section of the teddies was not big and could be completed within an hour. There are teddy bears of different celebrities and famous events. There are also exhibits that shows the evolution of teddy bears over the century. There is also the world's most expensive teddy bear not to be missed.There is a short mechanical Elvis presley teddy bear show every quarter of an hour. I did not visit the outdoor section of the museum.

There is actually nothing much in this museum. Only Teddy Bears depicting some celebrities and events. I had expected more exhibition so I was disappointed with what I saw. I read that there is an outdoor museum but I didnt manage to find it. Recommended for kids only.

lots of different types of bears to satisfy the history buffs and also people who just want to see cute bears.  Souvenir shop was great.  The best part was the teddy bear garden in the back..spent close to an hour there just strolling and taking pictures through the well manicured grounds..

We had an afternoon to kill and it was too hot for any outdoor activity so we decided to visit the museum. It had a fairly interesting display of teddy bears - displayed by era and themes. Highlight was the most expensive teddy bear in the world - the Louis Vutton teddy bear. If you had limited time on Jeju, this is not a must-see, but I'd like us you had an extra day, then, this is worth going on a hot or rainy day.

I collect Teddy bears and it was only fitting that I should bring home with me the symbol of JeJu - Haenyeo woman (Mother of the Sea - diving since 200 BC and tradition is still alive.  These women are what made JeJu what it is today.  They were responsible for agriculture, diving for abalone, sea cucumber, squid etc and it was these women who stood up against the Japanese invasion during WWII.

We found this museum in our travel guide and it sounded fun to visit. However, it was quite disappointing starting with the price which was much more expensive than all other museums. It only had a few rooms with teddy bear representations that got repetitive and monotonous after the first. On the other hand there was a nice outdoor park with fun sculptures to take pictures next to. Overall might be good for children but not so worth it for adults.
We spent only about 30 minutes in here, there was nothing much to see.  Full of bears in different settings, like The Beatles, or during the war, or circus.
Very entertaining and cute. Nothing much to see other than bears, but all were made perfectly for each scene represented.
A definite fun experience. You wouldn't spend too long here but you would definitely enjoy Teddytanic :)

Dived back to those nostalgic childhood moments when teddy bears once played as friends in your life. This Teddy Bear Museum has a wide array of collection of teddy bears, dressed beautifully in different costumes. The most popular bear will probably be the one dressed in Louis Vuitton clothes.What particularly caught my attention was the exhibition which actually used famous paintings such as the Mona Lisa, and the Teddy Bear was dressed to depict her. A creative way to carry out this exhibition. However, those expect to see a wide range of "depiction".Overall, I felt that this was only an average stop-over, but will be good for families traveling with their young children. There's a souvenir shop on site too, where I'll be expecting young children to be bugging their parents to get them a teddy bear each!

There's two Teddy Bear Museum in Jeju Island. One is Safari Theme that has an entrance fee of KRW 8,500 (Php 369) for adults. This has a safari theme great for pictures but on the second floor, there are more which has a variety of themes. Every stop you were  required to queue to abroad. This bus went to most attractions including black sand & Udo lighthouse. The bus route was also the route for E-scooters /car. We went there yesterday and this my second time here! It s so beautiful and amazing it s so nice to relax and have fun in the same day you have to go here if you are in jeju you will have the best time , you can go for a day or you can stay overnight it s very safe !

We visited Udo Island in October 2016 and took the hop on hop off bus and got off at the first stop to climb up to the peak where the lighthouse was.  The climb took about an hour and though there were steps and a well travelled path, it still required some physical effort. There were hardly any trees and you would be well advised to wear a hat and sun block. Wear comfortable walking/hiking shoes and bring plenty of drinking water.  We climbed to the peak on a hot sunny day and had to stop a few times before we reached the lighthouse. The view was worth our effort.  Then we climbed down to the surrounding park, which was basically grassland with minimal trees and hardly any shelter. There were lots of other tourists.  We saw some horses grazing here and could see across to the mainland and sunrise peak as well as parts of Udo below.  This is the most enjoyable part of UDO for us and highly recommended.

Jeju Island in Korea is a exceedingly wonderful place to have vacation for family and also a  place to have honey moon for lovers. After doing some traveling plans, I went to Korea with friends in April this year. The walking trail at Yongmeori Coast is just a few hundred meters (~700 m) long, but the layered sedimentary structures made from rocks and volcanic ashes, and dramatic shapes created by erosion from hard ocean-waves and wind make it breathtaking art of nature and truly resembles Geopark. It is known that the site is indeed designated as one of the nine Jeju sites certified by the Global Geopark Network in 2010. Personally, this is one of my best scenic places in Jeju in the view of both geology and photography lover.The part of these cliffs appeared stretched out from nearby Sanbangsan Mountain. The meaning of Yongmeori in Korean is Dragon Head. Interestingly, the rough surface of rocks and dramatic shapes formed by rocks due to erosions make it look like a dragon's head going underwater.This part of Jeju is also famous for women sea-drivers. During our visit, we have got an opportunity to try out a few fresh kinds of seafood sold by Korean grandmothers along the coastline. Another attraction near this cliff is the huge shipwreck which is actually a reproduction built as the Hamel Castaway Memorial to commemorate a Dutch sailor (Hendrick Hamel). It is said that he was drifted to the shore of Jeju by a typhoon in 1653. He then wrote a book providing the West some insights into Joseon Korea for the first time. All together this place is very impressive and must not be missed.

My family and I drove to this awesome natural attraction and walked along the layered rocks and cliffs produced as a result of a volcanic eruption on a beautiful non-windy and sunny morning. Safety concerns: Yeongmeori (Dragon's Head) Coast is opened from 8 am to 6:30 pm from May to September. It will be closed when the weather changes in a way that impacts people s safety (e.g. high tidal waves, strong winds), so it is better to call to check before going. Also a rainy day means that the rocks and coast will become slippery and you may have problems taking photographs. in any case, you definitely need a good pair of walking shoes.2 walking trails: You have to take note that there are 2 trails and entrances to Yeongmeori Coast. Both trails meet each other but are not connected due to safety issue, which means you have to pay separate entrance fees. However, I saw a white bridge is presently being constructed that links the 2 trails, but it remains unclear as to when it will be opened. Between the 2 trails   Trail 1 and Trail 2 (described below)   I found Trail 2 to be  safer for walking and has more spectacular sandstone rock formations and cliffs, and because of that my family and I spent about 3 hours admiring the attraction and taking photographs.  Trail 1: This trail is where the tourists go, and starts after the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the Hamel vessel. You park your car (along with the tour coaches) at a car park that s next to a mini theme park (with the Viking amongst others). You then walk along the seaside promenade next to sandstone layered rocks along the sea, which takes about 1.5 to 3 hours return after the ticket booth (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children). Since certain stretches of the promenade are narrow, you have to walk carefully so as not to fall into the sea and onto the rocks.Trail 2:  This is a shorter trail that in theory should only take about 30-60 minutes return after the ticket booth. You park your car just beneath the temple. Parking is free. Cross the road and look for 3 bronze circular structures with inscriptions of  Jeju Island Geopark ,  Global Geopark Networks  and  New 7 Wonders of Nature  and a green signage  Yongmeori Coast Entrance -> 300m  From there, you just walk down the steps and follow the path which will take you past several shops. After about 10 minutes  walk, you will reach a ticket booth. After buying the tickets (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children), turn left and you would come to the top of a narrow and steep passageway to the coast. Take your time to carefully choose the big rocks as your steps for your descent (and then I realised what the term  stepping stone  means). There are no handrails. Once you reached the bottom after about 6 minutes (longer when there are many people), turn around and look up at the challenging and difficult passageway and appreciate your achievement! Looking across the sea, we saw Mount Hallasan. Instead of going left, I recommend you go to the right and once through a archway or hole in a rock wall, and you will soon encounter the spectacular irregular layered and wavy sandstone cliffs that often contain  pot-holes . The rock formation at certain places was carved out by  a blade that cut itself into the layered rocks, creating v-shaped clefts. And when the waves crashed into the rocks, it sounds like roaring thunder   awesome!  There s a short cement bridge where standing on it allows you to take a superb photograph of the rock formation and the narrow stretch of turquoise-coloured sea. It is also around this same spot that you can take another superb photograph of the cliffs with Mount Sanbangsan in the background. There were 2 ladies (I didn t think they were the famed  Haenyeo  sea-divers) at the shoreline with 3 basins of sea animals - sea snail (sora), sea squirt (myeonggye) and sea cucumber (haesam)   who would be happy to enable you  to experience Korean culture of eating raw seafood by the shoreline. I didn t like to eat raw seafood so I didn t try.Overall, my family and I think that Yeongmeori Coast is one attraction in Jeju that ranks it as among the top 3 attractions in Jeju. Don t miss it! It will blow your mind away!

This is one of the most remarkable scenic attractions of Jeju. Our Korean driver brought us here. We told him we are not interested in arts museums or teddy bear or maze park. We only wanted to see the natural sites and wonders in Jeju and he brought us here and we thanked him for that. There was a Buddha Park directly at the car park where we alighted. I could see the golden face of the Buddha from the highland opposite the park. From the car park,  the panoramic view of the beach was amazing; the lush green vegetation studded with autumn foliage with long stretch of gorgeous coastline and natural cliff view and the azure sea horizon. It was nature's master-piece presented in so marvelous and harmonious form that I could not find better words to describe this stunning, breathtaking and jaw dropping scenery. For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. From the coast, I could see the majestic Mt Sanbangsan loomed at the site of the Buddha Park and I could vividly see some of my group members were resting and relaxing at a pavilion below the car park enjoying the gentle sea breeze.You must pardon me for my excitement and exhilaration as I came from a city with urbanized concrete jungle with little natural scenery. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.

Absolutely beautiful place - a must-see-experience if you go to Jeju. Amazing what nature can create and then its just next to a mountain and a small temple with a giant gold-Buddha. Go see this asap! :)

My friends and I traveled to this scenic coast in year 2011. It was not part of my itinerary but it was introduced by our driver. I really impressed by the nature of this tourist spot. It is located along the Coast of South Western of Jeju Island. I can say it is the most Scenic spot of Jeju's Coastline. Yongmeori Coast looks as if a dragon s head is going underwater. This area is made of Sa-am stacks, built up over millions of years.It is the place where the mountain dips into the sea at the Yongmeori Beach. Formed out of the natural piling of stacks of  Sa-am  that have been occurring for millions of years, the locals equate the formation of the Yongmeori Cliffs in Jeju with the image of a dragon s head going into the ocean for a dip.You may find more information through the website. In year 2011, there were less tourist as it was not as famous as other hot tourist spot like Seopjikoji that time. I cannot remember whether is there any entrance fee needed. However, please wear sport shoes as there are some climbing the rocks to tour this place. After the long entrance, our driver guided us and we walked in the circle of the shape of dragon's head rock. Our driver was a very good photographer who shown us to climb near the cliff just for the nice photograph position. Recall back, my legs were shaking and didn't dare to make a move for posting all those difficult photography position! I think I will never this again!      Along the road down to the coastline, there is the Hamel Castaway Memorial, in remembrance of Hamel who drifted to this place in 1653 where Korea in the history did not open their door to the World yet.

Along the walk, there are women selling raw seafood meals for 10,000 a pop. It's a very simple set-up: plastic stools and chairs, some garlic, gochujang, and soju if you wish.

they charge admission now to see this seashore.  as if that's not bad enough, it was closed by the time we arrived at 5pm.  but what wasn't closed were the numerous vendor stands that seemingly sprung up to cash in on the tourists here.  the most interesting thing we noticed were various coconuts with small holes drilled in them with a straw sticking out.  this is supposed to be 'fresh' coconut water.  protip: there are no coconuts in korea.  superprotip: they re-use these containers without rinsing them out, over days/months/years, you get the idea.if you don't mind paying to see this 'natural wonder,' at least avoid the vendor stands like the plague, cause that's what you'll likely catch there.

This coast is easily the most impressive of Jeju's natural sites. It has a small entrance fee and may close due to high tide, but it is a must-see on Jeju if the tides are good. The water pools on the cliffs are really blue and many women divers sell their catch along the coast. I'm not into seafood so I didn't have the nerve to try it though. The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone "stairway". To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

I highly recommend a visit here! My friends who came to visit said it was their favorite experience on Jeju.The sandstone cliffs have been intricately carved by wind and water over the years. They are stunning up close, and most days you can see crustaceans, interesting bugs, and other life in the tide pools. Check out the gorgeous bright-blue water. And possibly see some women collecting shellfish and sea urchins to eat and sell!Be sure you walk all the way around the point. It's easy to think you can't, but the narrow path hugs the rocks to make a loop. Beautiful and totally worth it!

I came here expecting mundane rock formations. Ohh how wrong I was. This is one of the most beautiful places in Jeju. The rock formations are gigantic and so artfully formed. Be careful when walking as you're walking beside the water and it can get slippery. We even sampled some fresh raw seafood like sea squirt, sea cucumber, sea snails and octopus with rocks as table and small children chair as our seat! No soju for us as we're driving!You park at the base of Sanbangsan and walk across the road to reach Yongmeori Beach. Entrance fee varies depending which location you want to visit.

One of the best stops we made in Jeju. This rock formation is pretty cool and the stop is more worth it since it's a good hour's worth of walking and snapping photos (as opposed to a number of the really touristy places where it's just one kodak moment).Check the tides. The rock formation that people walk on are really close to the water, so if the tides are high, it gets slippery. Actually, some parts are slippery as it is.You have two options: going counter-clockwise, which ends up being an upward movement OR going clockwise, a downward movement.  The views are nice-ish both ways (personally the counter-clockwise views were nicer). More than that though, going counter-clockwise is a lot easier as the steps are easier to deal with moving up. Many of the people coming down were cursing the steep rocks and were tired even before it began for them. Might not recommend this if walking is difficult for you as climbing and hoping around is a must. Little children were around and they seemed to be enjoying themselves, but none of them were younger than 3 years of age.No bathrooms once you enter the formations, but ladies will sell you food and drink (mostly alcohol) if you're interested in a seaside meal.

As our tour guide said nest stop is the beach... i was wondering how can any beach rival Philippine beaches? The best view suddenly came out. no amount of words can describe the rock formations we saw. we felt small beside it. They dive without oxygen tanks. After the walk we were all tongue tied at the beauty of the past 30 minutes. Yongmeori means dragon head coast. and it really took a dragon size breath away from me. Entrance only 6000won (6us$)

Yongmeori is a rough and dramatic coastline shaped from lava eruptions. Walking along the spectacular rock formations is an experience that only Jeju-do can offer. Firstly, some of the water pockets with bright turquoise water are striking in their uniqueness. Secondly, the sometimes bizarre rock formation are nothing if not eye-catching. Lastly, the strange (slightly grotesque) insects that scurry along some of the rocks are strangely interesting. They never touch or climb on you, every footfall makes them scurry in all direction. Yongmeori is a bit off the "classic" tourist itinerary. Most visitors enjoy a beach or two, maybe a hike at Hallasan or the Seongsan Ilchulbong, and perhaps they fit in a waterfall and museum. Jeju has so much to offer that is often overlooked. Yongmerori Coast is one of these places.
