Definitely a MUST for those who love KPop. Even if you aren't that crazy over Kpop, go and experience korean technology. Quite an experience :)

Being a fan of kpop I thought this was awesome. The whole experience was great and good fun while waiting for the rain to finish. The 3D concert is amazing I never seen anything like it before. It was like Bigbang was in the stage ! Worth a visit !!

My Korean friend brought me to this place when I visited Jeju. It was a hidden jem. I spent a couple of hours to take holographic pictures and watched the Kpop videos at the 3D theater. It was close to many tourist spots in Seogwipo city (Teddy bear museum, lotte hotel, and etc.). If you are a kpop lover, you will have unforgettable memories. It was so much fun!!!

It was sooo much fun to visit this place. When I visited Jeju, my Korean friend brought me to Playkpop museum. I had so much fun to watch kpop stars' videos at the 3-D theater. I spent most time to take holographic pictures. It was a hidden jem in Jeju. If you love kpop music, you will love this place!!! I definitely wanna visit again, if I go to Jeju.

This is a great find for me. The museum is full of interesting things. Live hologram concert, G-Dragon, is super-duper:) The staff is awesome! very nice and friendly.I would highly recommend. Playkpop is not comparable with other Museum!!!

This is one of my favorite beaches on Jeju.  As someone who lives here, this is mainly because the beach is big enough to hold the droves of tourists who come here every summer.  During off season it is even more spectacular.  Wide stretches of sand with very few people filling it.Around the beach areas there are enough cafes, restaurants, shops to keep a person full and happy throughout the day.  ProTip: Midway down the beach (there is another set of bathrooms up the stairs.  Save yourself the trip of trying to make it to the main ones!
I really loved my day out to Gwakji Gwamul Beach with friends. There were a lot of families here too.

Can be extremely busy during summer but the beach is beautiful.  Can rent umbrellas to lie under or just bake in the sun.  Some rocky areas in the water but you can navigate around them to enjoy the blue sea.

The main attraction of the beach is the inclusion of a somewhat historic public bath.  As it was November and no one was using the public baths, I was able to get into the public baths for a look.  Don't worry, you're not missing out on much as the public baths were not very impressive in size or scope.  I can imagine these public baths would be very busy in the summer when the weather is more appropriate.The beach itself is good - there is plenty of sand so I could imagine people swimming in the sea near the beach in the summer.  However, there are some rocks there as well for people to walk around.All in all, it's a typical beach - nothing to write home about.

The beach itself could do with some TLC from the council.   There is a lot of debris which washes up daily onto the beach and along the coastal walk. Most of it travels in from China and for the most part seems to be from fishing boats.  The coastal walk is good, good paths and I have seen everything from flying fish, the women Abalone divers, wild cats, cute puppies to feed and dogs kept on short leads and some I'd say rarely fed (I feed them too). The selfie people are many along this walk it's quite comical to watch them all.
when we arrived it s almost 6 pm and their it s closing time, still have some food to eat. People are nice over there and never rush us.

It is a big market selling vegetables and local products. However plenty of plastic tent restaurants at the end of the market and prices are much lower than in town. You can get all the cooked korean food here and delicious too.Also a place to buy all the korean street food and snacks.No problem with taxis as there is a proper taxi stand. Market is clean and well arranged.
Is a nice market, a lot of things there. If so happen you can meet the day, then must go and see. clothes, vege, bird, fish, food, groceries bla bla bla.....

We were caught in a traffic jam and arrived at about 7pm which we were we told an hour too late. So whatever you do, if you want to be here, do it in the late afternoon say 4pm at the latest. And of course, be aware that the market only opens on 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd and 27th of each month.

The market is full of local appeal with fresh fruits, vegetables, and local snacks to seafood and various sundries. A great way to spend a few hours walking around, doing some souvenir shopping, and eating local treats. The market is full of warm and friendly people who are interested and appreciative of the tourist that venture to visit the attraction. I would recommend to any one who appreciates the local things about traveling.

The Jeju City 5-day traditional market is a place to visit if you happened to be in Jeju on the 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd and 27th of the month. It is the biggest and oldest among the other 5-day markets. The place is big and the locals sell wares ranging from fishes, livestocks, clothings, hats, crockery, flowers, agricultural produce, local food stuffs, etc. The place is noisy and colorful, crowded and they add excitement to your visit. It is " When in Jeju, do as the local folks do".

quite big & locally, i reached here at 8am, just open 1 hour but seem that over 90% stalls already open & operating. same as the wooden brand said that was grandma's market so that many elder near around. they were selling & buying everything. many diff stuffs inside the market. maybe time was early, i don't see any tourist inside the market but local people to buy much stuffs. that also has movable breakfast service that was same as what i saw in most of market of southeast country. some selling by movable truck some just deliver by tray. busy job. besides, seafood stall also interesting as i saw a seller cut open the Devilfish, first time to see it as seem he was struggle with the fish skin. ha. impressiveanyway, good for visit here if you got time at day of 2,7,12,17,22&27.
Be prepared to walk a lot. Stores selling similar items tend to cluster together. Traffic and parking can be a harrowing experience. From what we observed at the taxi queue, it can be a long wait.

This is an authentic market which embodies local life on the island. It has so much to offer... There is an entire section devoted to the economy of the elderly, selling their goods and calling sweet encouragements to passerbys. There are regional fruits and veggies, artisan crafters, cloth and clothing sellers, seafood and fresh meats, animals, and a multitude of food trucks/stalls.This is the ideal market for immersing yourself in Jeju and Korean culture. It's open every day ending in 2 or 7: 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27thPictured: a pressure cooker used for puffing rice and corn, cooking beans, etc...
This is a real locals' market and has the full range of foodstuffs one would expect. Lovely wickerwork and some kitchenware as well as some fairly meh clothes.
Place to buy famous jeju orange and the stuffs related.. Fresh seafood and vegetables are all around. A must visit place when one spend the time in Jeju

Lots of variety here from plants, pulses, clothing, fruit and veges and fish and local street food.  The prices aren't cheap as you would expect in a market but that's the same all over Korea.  A good variety is why you would go there.

The 5 day market is named because it opens every 5 days only. There are other 5 day markets in Jeju but this market is said to be the largest in Jeju with 1,000 over stalls. This market opens on the 17th and plus / minus 5 days before and after.Fret not if you missed the opening of this market. Because apparently the other 5 day markets are operate by the same stall owners. They rotate among the different markets and hence will be back to the same market after every 5 days.We went there on a morning and expected to spend the whole day there. But we were out in 2 hours.There are indeed many stalls in the market but many of them are carrying the same stuff. Clothings, household products, fruits and vegetables, kimchi, cooked food and of course Jeju mandarin oranges which are famous. Interestingly, pet dogs are sold alongside with fresh chickens. And ironically, there are stalls selling dog meat at the other end of the market.Same animal but different fate.We bought the famous mandarin oranges here although these are available at other places in Jeju as well. There are many similar-priced stalls selling this famous product in this market. We chose one of the varieties on display after sampling. It has a sweet aftertaste after the first tinge of sourness. The one we purchased is the 2nd most expensive type at $25,000 Won per 5 kg. There are other varieties at $30,000 Won per 5 kg and $15,000 Won per 10 kg etc.It s a nice experience after all and I would say it s worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

If you've never been to a traditional Korean market, the Jeju Five Day Market is a wonderful introduction, and if you are an old hand at these sort of things, then you will enjoy Jeju's style. Pros: Roughly the size of a football field, there's a little of everything at this market. And every market is a little different too, so it stays interesting even over multiple visits (seasonal goods are fantastic here). Fruits, vegetables, herbs, roots, jams, honey, traditional medicines, gardening supplies (including seedlings); clothing, shoes, traditional crafts, a sprinkling of electronics now and then, kitchenware, furniture, rugs, and a whole host of things you won't recognize. It's truly a bizarre bazaar, and I am hopelessly in love with the sights, sounds, and smells of this style of capitalism that hearkens back to a time of more hooves and mouths than credit cards and smartphones. Go! Try everything! Buy everything! You'll love it!Cons: Sensory overload. Severe introverts should farm their energy for at least a day prior to going to this market. Expect to be shoved, bumped into, pushed, and in every other possible way have your personal space invaded. The shouting can be persistent, and the din is incredible. Trying to park your car can induce migraine headaches, and the traffic jams that lead up to the parking can be even worse. People here are generally honest, but I urge you to be extra vigilant when you buy perishables. More than once I've gone home with a great deal, only to have it go bad the same night. Also, check around for prices. Often you will buy something and then find a better version at a lower cost just a meter away. And finally, don't hesitate to haggle: the "foreigner price" rule is definitely in effect at this market.
I really and strongly recommend you to visit this market. Lots of food and other hand made goods are there. You will enjoy about 3 hours af hanging and buying things there

This market is a great embodiment of a traditional market. There are vegetables, fruits, fish, clothes, shoes, Korean food joints..etc. I recommend visiting it in the morning as it become more crowded after that time. Food smell might be disturbing but you may be able to overcome it. If you are a fan of traditional markets then visiting this market is considered a MUST.

We were very excited that our trip coincided with the market. The market was packed with people and it seemed like all the locals were there and had been looking forward to it all week.We bought fruits and snacks there. Prices are definitely cheaper than at the marts. Although the aunts and uncles manning the stalls didn't speak much English, they were all very helpful and we communicated mainly with gestures and our limited vocabulary. Do try all the snacks and eat at the food stalls there!

When my group and I first went to this market I assumed it would be small like a on the side of the road market where they sell fruits, veggies, and jams. This market was that times ten and the market even had the kitchen sink. When we first walked through they had fresh picked flowers, potted plants, fresh spices, 15 different types of kimchi. As we walked around it wasnt just food and plants they had housewares to clothes even puppies, rabbits and chickens. then we realized that they even had a fish market. This market of cousre smelled of fish we consumers selling squid, shrimp, and tilapia. This market is such a good way to imerse oneself into a the korean culture on the island. This was one of the places on my wish list to see while my group and I were in Korea and it was much more than I expected and I am so glad I went.

Our stay in Jeju coincide with the operational day of one of the biggest and oldest traditional market in Jeju - Grandma Market which runs on days that end with 7th of the calendar month. There are lots of other smaller scale traditional markets which are opened on different days (e.g days ending on 5th, 2nd, etc...) thru out the island but we were told that this is the biggest.There is also an area which are designated for elderly ladies aged 65 and above whereby they are not charged any fees for selling there, hence, the name of Grandma Market.Lots of things can be found in the market, from plants, to snacks to clothings to housewares. We bought some fresh ginseng, chilly flakes and also fresh gingko from the market (after tasting some that were steamed and sold as snacks), The gingko there is different from those that we get in MY (most imported from China). Their is more creamy in texture and rounded as compared to ours.Overall, quite an interesting walk for an hour or two if you're looking to buy some of foodstuff.

Bangju Church is a picturesque little church that s unmissable on the way to Bonte Museum.  It s the unique ark-shaped exterior along with the surrounding water that makes it photogenic and there isn t much inside (which is off limits most of the time anyway).  Despite being a short stop, there were always a half dozen cars in the parking lot with people busy taking photos around the church.

It was a bit difficult to find but totally worth the drive. It is so peaceful and pretty that its hard to believe it is a fully functioning church. There is also a cafe across the church building that has good coffee and good views.
To do after Hallasan hiking. Very good place to feel relax and quiet for one hour! In case you feel hungry, go to the hotel next to it they have a grocery!

A stunning architecture, indeed a church. Public access available except for church service hours. beaturiful view of the island from the location too.  There is a coffee house by the parking lot with pretty good coffee too.

It was a rainy and foggy day when I visited. It was very hard to drive, but went there anyway. As it is very famous place, not an attraction, for its artistic figure, it was a Must-See place.It is an actual church, so we had to respect the environment and the rules of the church.Do not wear sleeveless top, flip flops, mini shorts if you want to go in and pray or have a service.They seemed very conservative. :)

It offers one of the best view in Jeju. It is free to go, no need to book, super easy to walk. I was lucky with weather this time and was able to see hallasan from here! I cannot describe how amazing it was.  It is breathtaking and good to visit anytime of days. Many people came for sunset and sunrise. It is definitely one of my favorite places in Jeju. Be prepare for strong wind and amazing view. Recommend going during fall
It was a fantastic day out to Yongnuni Oreum Volcanic Cone. Really loved the adventurous hike with friends.

Teddy Bear Safari is the world s first exhibition theme park with various real life-sized wildlife and marine stuffed animals and teddy bears. Moreover, you will also meet our teddy bears dressed in traditional clothes of countries around the world and as gods from Greek mythology. Lastly, some of our teddy bears will be dressed up as Korean celebrities whom you may be well aware of.

In 2018, I went there with my friends. I don't plan on coming here at first. I'm so angry because of the hot weather. So we decided to enter a very nice building. And this was the building. Contrary to the expectation that teddy bears couldn't be so cute, teddy bears were so cute!! The teddy bear museum reminds me of the past when I really liked teddy bears when I was very young. It was good to take pictures because it was full of cute teddy bears. After returning home, the picture in the Teddy Bear Museum was the best among the other pictures.
Great place for kids, also for adults. There are alot of teddy bears, in second floor. This is standard place for tour. We enjoy this place.

My husband and I visited this one May day. This teddy bear museum had some decent variety for photo opportunities. Unlike some other reviews, I wouldn't say it was small. There was a safari section, an underwater section, and a royalty section. We were there about 30-60 minutes. It was pretty packed too.
It s a rather small place but filled with lots of cuteness. Safari themed, royal themed... etc. different from teddy bear museum but worth a visit at least once if you love teddy bears.

For a teddy lover like me, this place is heaven I ve been collecting different teddies and seeing all sorts of teddies here, big and small is like a dream come true. Kids and kids-at-heart will truly enjoy and treasure time spent here.

It is an interesting showcase of lifesize and all sizes of teddy bears being used to personify famous art pieces, fables, fairy tales and etc.  There are many interesting photo opportunities.  The Koreans are very creative in coming up with such a museum dedicated to teddy bear lovers, but I would not return a second time.

This is a cute collection of teddybears and other stuffed animals in a variety of settings (a castle, a safari, etc.), but it's not what I was expecting with the name "Teseum" (teddy+museum).  There's a very small display of older teddybears (mostly photographs), but the main attraction is the displays you can see in the pictures.  There must be thousands here, ranging in size from one inch or shorter to probably eight feet tall. I imagine kids would be in hog heaven, but some of the older people in our tour group said it was a waste of time.  My favorites were the safari and the teddybear versions of old paintings.
Museums of pushies, teddy bears, etc... Diff kinds of pushies, made into a safari, underwater, kingdoms, Olympic and more
Kids would love it....lots of dolls from very small to gigantic size wearing varieties of cloths. You can take a photo with the dolls as well. Other than teddy bears, nothing much to see.

If you're a fan of teddy bears, then you should visit this place. You can probably complete this in 1 - 2 hours time. There's a outdoor park with more pictures to capture. Didn't really change much as compared to the first visit few years ago.. You have to pay an admission fee to enter, which i can't really remember but it's not expensive.
Came here with tour, cool installations to take a lot of photo. Will probably take about 1.5hours to slowly see all the teddy bears across 2 levels. Cool to see.
There are so many celebrity or art related bears arranged in a very spacious and comfortable place.  Really out of my expectation and would recommend to go.  You will feel happy when you are there!

I personally don't like teddy bears so didn't expect much for the visit. However this museum did show something beyond expectation. The teddy bears are used to demonstrate memorable moments in history, scenes from classic movies, etc! Among the many so called museums around the area, this is the one I do recommend.

The place was rather quiet when we visited (it was on a Sunday morning) despite the heavy traffic from Seoul the day before. We were given pamphlets in English, while most of the displays were in Korean language. There are many teddy bears in display and most have been displayed/posed in accordance with certain themes (like Hollywood, Snow White, landing on the moon etc). It was interesting.There was an Elvis show, with teddy bears swaying their hips to Elvis's concert in Hawaii (if I'm correct) and that was entertaining for the kids.Outdoors is a small park with human size teddy figures, great for picture taking. Remember to take pictures with large teddy outside.There is also a cafe but we did not stop by since we had breakfast earlier. In the pamphlet, we saw a train ride but we couldn't locate it anywhere. May have missed it.There was one floor for shopping and there is a large selection of teddy bears to bring home. Maybe pricey but the quality is quite good.The place is convenient for families with small children (the kids were not terrified) and stroller friendly as there is an elevator available. There is also free parking outside.As usual, for Korean tourist attractions, there are discount vouchers available. Just have to know where to get it :)

There are 3 terry bear museums in Jeju. The one which we visited is Terry bear and safari. The lower floor is the safari and upper floor is the bear. Think this also to attract the kids to visit the place thus the safari.Take your time to see and enjoy the many characters of the terry bear. One corner of displays is a very expensive due to diamond crown.

I literally went gaga after stepping into the museum. You can play with the stuffed animals ergo, take pictures. There are lots of exhibits from safaris to castles. It's very interesting. All the toys are very clean and well-maintained. Kids would definitely enjoy this place.

If you love teddy bears and stuffed animals then this is the place to visit. There are thousands of teddy bears and many photo opportunities. There is also a GS25 near there to buy snacks and ice cream.

This museum is a lot bigger than expected, and housed so many different teddy bears in fun settings that it made even adults excited. Would highly recommend if you have little kids, as they would love being able to touch the bears and taking photos with them.

There are many many many uncountable (which may count but hei! not necessary man~) teddy bears inside and a lots of other animals dolls like brown bears, sheeps, monkeys, elephants, snakes, lions, tigers, etc. Me and my siblings are having a great photo time inside there. I feel lovely and joyful for all interior design which teddy bear had placed. Love this place much! Worth to visit once in lifetime.

A quaint but charming little place with lots of teddy bears! Highlight was the Greek Gods teddy bears and the teddy bear art gallery. Fun photo opportunities and a teddy bear safari to boot. It is an imitation attraction but not a bad place to spend an hour.

C1 ( 2016.07.15 ) I visited there on my way to Psyche World, because there was located beside this one. But Psyche World was close and out of business. So I visited this Teseum Safari. But there was under my expectation for price, and many tourist was crowded by bus. If visited Teddy's museum in Jungmun, no need to visit there, I think.
Quite fun to see all diorama with Teddy Bear as different celebrities. They're beatles, michael jordan, etc.

As the name says it all, it's a teddy bear safari. So what you see inside is tons of teddy bear!I think all the bears are hand sewn. Its nothing special on the teddy bear design since it's just a teddy bear but the quality of the material is thereThat's a reason why it's quite expensive for a bear merchandise there
More like a showroom for a Teddy bear manufacturer. Girls and little kids might like it. I headed for the exit and kept warm with a coffee. Maybe should have tried some Sochu beforehand......
There were so many characters of teddy bear, very cute and lovely. Heaven for teddy bear lovers. Girls and kids will love it.
All things teddy bears. Cute and creative. Loads of photo opportunities. Good for kids, girls and families.
Well basically all you do here is just take pictures but I'm a fan of teddy bears so I looooooved this place!
This is another product of Korean creativity. This is just a place where a Teddy Bear collections located and opened for public. The shape of the dolls were not so perfect and some were ugly.
Absolutely love it. If you have kids, this is a must go. It's fun to be around lots of teddies. The huge teddy bears are great to take pics with and are hug-able..
Cute bears everywhere, for bear lovers to take photo. Visit can be done less than an hour. For people who do not like soft toys, you can skip this.

Compare the teddy safari museum at seogwipo, Teseum is much more better and fun. Teseum you can hug touch and take pictures with the bears as close as you wish. Teddy safari it's all protected and u can't touch it.

Visit if you are a fan of teddy bears. Not much to do besides taking pictures and you might have to queue to take pictures. There is a souvenir shop at the entrance/exit.There is also a small stall selling snacks to the left of the entrance and down some step of stairs.

The teddy bear musuem is filled with a vast variety of teddy bears in different sections. These teddy bears were build to replicate a safari zoo, an aquarium, a palace, an art gallery and many more. There is side information of history of teddy bear and a gallery with ancient greek gods. Try to spot the most expensive teddy bear in the world! Apart from that, its located beside an expressway. Travelling to there might need a bus or taxi ride. Its worth a visit, but not interesting enough for me to come back again. There is too some eateries around there to settle your hunger needs. The musuem requires some entrance fee.

Basically it is a place where you can hug, touch and take photos with the giant teddy bears around. The teddy bear there are based on novel idea, which they showcase teddy bear of all sorts, sizes and costume. They are very charming and creative but the place itself is not too big, it only take about 45 mins to 1 hour for the leisure walk. One thing is, if you go on peak season, Teseum will be very pack and hardly to take some nice photos, or maybe you have to wait for the photo session.
A novel idea to showcase teddy bear of all sorts, sizes and costume. Very camera-friendly but it's not a big place. We had a leisure walk in here and comb the area in about an hour.
This is the place you can hug, kiss and take photos with teddy bear. Jeju Teseum is Korea's first and largest teddy bear museum. If you likes Teddy bear this is the place must visit in Jeju Island.
Teseum is very charming and creative. I like very much the teddy bears couples donning national dress of different countries of the world.

Well, if you like teddy bears, drop by this place to see their collection.  Honestly, I get more excited browsing teddy bears at a departmental store.  This place is probably losing its charm as it is mainly visited by tourists sent here by tour buses and very little koreans or free-n-easy tourists.
My 2nd time to this place and it's never disappoint us. My daughter really enjoy this museum so much. Will be going there again next year.
For those who love teddy bears, here's the place for you. A 2 storey building filled with all sorts of teddy bears of different sizes and characters.

It's so fancy. We can take pictures while hugging,touching,kissing the bears. If you go by tour and they just give you an hour,don't take too much time on jungle area, because there are many areas in there. I think my fav area is the castle area.
A museum with full of teddy bears, not to my liking, just take a stroll, take pictures then buy some teddies if you like, thats all

This was suppose to be one of the 1st museum in the world to exhibit all sorts of teddy bears. Not a very big place but pack with tourists. For the really young at heart or the really young kids this may be a novelty.

You can discover your favourite teddy or safari animal here. With 3 floors of huggable and adorable animals there is much posing, hugging and choosing. You can even get a teddy to propose marriage to you.Teseum should not be confused with Teddy Bear Museum located in Seogwipo (near Alive Museum), a more 'serious' museum.
We will meet, hug, touch, take picture or even kiss the teddy bears. Cute background for taking picture.

This is a straight-up collection of really adorable teddies all in different themes and characters!Some are the classic teddy bears that we grew up lovingSome are teddies dressed up as music icons, roman gods/goddesses, characters from movies, etcIf you need your fill of cute things, this place is loaded with itIt's nice if you ask meAnd it doesn't hurt that we even got free teddies after the visit! yay!

It's a nice place to take some nice photos with the teddies.  Lots of them there huge ones as well.  The most I've seen in one single location. Good effort. You can touch them,  hug them,  even climb over them.  Our children had a fun time.

So, perhaps this comparison is unfair, but if you have to choose between the two: the Teddy Bear Museum and this Teseum, I would personally choose this Teseum because the Teseum is slightly cheaper, closer to Jeju City, and way less pretentious (that may sound weird, but that's more or less what the difference was). Teseum was laid back, a bit more interactive, and generally understanding of that a visit to see Teddy bears would mean visiting the childish side on all of us. The Teddy Bear museum was more like an anthropological study of teddy bears or something, aka, less fun, a bit more uptight.For those in the group who were not as interested in the actual display, they could opt out and still purchase teddy bears. The gift shop was conveniently open to everyone visiting and there were a few convenience stores and such around.

Our visit to Teseum was part of a tour package, and we had a lot of fun.  Photo opportunities were plentiful, even if there were a lot of other visitors.  We enjoyed posing with the huge bears, with different theme displays.  As well, the section on classical art was quite remarkable.
Good fun to visit this museum of teddy bears. Seems that this museum contrary to the other Teddy Bear museum allows you to take pictures with the bears.
i liked it because my kids love it. you can hug, touch, take photo etc but the service is not quite good. they seems don't like to smile too often.... I'm sorry

There are 3 teddy bear museums in Jeju Island, but this is the only one you could touch and hug, that s why it s called safari, while the teddy bears in the other two are kept in the glass box. Although I am not a big fans of soft toys, it s still cute to see them.

Nice to go with kids..there are two similar museum in Jeju,initially I planned to go Teddy bear museum,but my tour guide,Mr Gang recommended me to go Teseum,because it is bigger and you can hug the teddy bears for photo,while the teddy bear museum is just for the display.We had fun here.Worth for a visit!Entrance fee is 8000 Won for adult and 5000 Won for children.

There are 2 major teddy bear themed attractions in Jeju, One is the Teddy Bear Museum and the other is Jeju Teseum. The Teddy Bear Museum is for mohair connoisseurs, but the bears there are all boxed up in glass exhibits. That is why given the limited amount of time we had in Jeju, we chose to visit Teseum. There are a lot of photo opportunities where we and especially our kids can pose with the many cuddly large-sized teddys at Teseum. The keyword here is interaction.

Air con wasn't cooling in the sweltering summer heat and the crowd of tourists in the place. Basically a photo taking kind of place but seeing how worn and musky the stuffed animals were, I shudder. The concept is cute but guess I should have come maybe n years earlier when things were still new. They need to spend some money to maintain the animals.

All sorts of soft toy replicas of animals made according to their actual sizes. Lots of fun for the kids. You can pose for photos with the many displays, sit on some of the displays.  There are also displays of teddy bear replicas of famous artwork by the masters. There is a display of all the bears dressed in the national costumes of different parts of the world.

It's a Safari Theme Teddy Bear Museum. There are all kinds of bears, including giraffe, zebras, sheeps, monkeys, pandas, etc. On the second level, there is even Egyptian theme bears decorated with crystals. Don't miss that. There are also international bears on displayed on level 2. Enjoy your visit. Don't miss out on purchasing the bears at the gift shop for souvenirs, you will be spoilt for choices. All the bears are made in Korea and worth buying for keepsake.

Before starting the Hallasan hike I checked out the Gwaneumsa Temple near the entrance to the trails.  It s in a secluded area and visited by mostly locals and not really a tourist spot.  The big Buddha statues along with a few rows of small Buddhas are quite impressive although the main halls are not.
It is very near city center although it is difficult to go there if you take public transportation. If you use your own vehicle, you can easily access it. As it is a calm place, you can get healing.

Walk thru a corridor of two rows of Buddha leading you all the way to tis great big golden gwaneusmsa Buddha. This golden Buddha backdrop contains many small Lohan buddhas in rows....there is also a small temple for you to pray

We were the only tourists there. It seems this temple is visited more by the locals, and not a typical overseas tourist spot.It was a nice place and we got ourselves plenty of photos. Worth the drive to see this temple.
It's 35km drive from Seogwipo district. I don't think it is easily accessible by public transport. I would strongly recommend to explore Jeju with a rental car!
Gwaneumsa Temple - Gets busy on the festival days otherwise it is a relatively solaceful place to visit.
A close temple that near to Jeju-Si.Nice decoration with free parking. No actual operation timing but suggest to visit before 6pm.
This is a big temple with lots to see.  There are a couple of large budda statues and many small ones.  It also has a nice gift shop.It is far from downtown and a bit hard to get without a car.

Lovely peaceful spot , nice statue at the start then all the buddas on the walk up to the temple offset by the lanterns. The temple is nice take a good look at the food and painting but the golden Buddha at the side is worth a look. Nice cafe and shop on site well priced.

Gwaneumsa Temple is close to Jeju National University and about 1 KM from the Gwaneumsa trail head to go to the top of Halla-san (the tallest mountain in South Korea).  I've been to the temple many times and always found it peaceful and beautiful.  Usually there were not many people here either so you can enjoy some quiet time.
Sure not the most beautiful Temple (of jeju) but if you are near the place, go and take a look. I can say that the Temple near the Sangbangsan Mountain is much more beautifull.
We went with friends who had kids and everyone enjoyed walking around the buildings, statues and garden.
This is a beautiful and large temple. I love it the moment i step out of the car. Must visit place at Jeju.
This temple is the most beautiful temple I have ever seen which allows tourist to take some pictures. The Buddha inside is outstanding. The landscape around is breathtaking.

Came to this temple as we only wanted a view of Mt Hallasan. But we kinda ended up with a pleasant surprise. Temple grounds are huge and it's peaceful to be away from the hustle and bustle of the city for a while.

It was so quiet.  No one was there which made us think that we werent suppose to be there.  The monks were setting up for Buddha's birthday.  We didnt bother going into the buildings and i am sure we didnt see everything.  Overall it was a nice peaceful little stop away from some of the more crowded places in jeju
The place is beautiful, scenic and great for photos. The Buddha sculptures are grand. A definite place to go in Jeju. In winter time, expect snow here and it can be few inches thick.
I really liked this Temple in that quiet area! I rent a car to go there and I really enjoyed visiting the temple together with driving in that area.

Of all the places we visited in Jeju via our taxi tour, this is what I would rank as #1 (see  http://www.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/SI/SI_EN_3_1_1_1.jsp?cid=1121529), with Sunrise Peak as #2.  This is a Buddhist temple set in a vast very pretty land.  Interesting Buddha statues   very exotic particularly for those who have never been to a Buddhist temple.  Our taxi guide politely asked, I believe a caretaker, to see if we can actually go inside the temple.  We were allowed.  I m not sure if it was early or this is not a traditional tourist place, since we only saw very few people (as compared to the other temple in Busan packed with too many people.)  Felt a little bit odd being a tourist spectator in a house of worship, but glad we did.  The landscaping and statutes in the area were very interesting.  So there's more to see other than the temple itself. I would recommend this place for sure.  Would go back again if have the chance.  Hopefully with less rain this time.  Free to visit.

There was so much to see and do, and the actual burning of the hill is spectacular. I spent half a day there and hadn t seen everything. The thing to be aware of is the time it can take to get out of the car park afterwards, but totally worth it !

This is one of the biggest festival celebrated in Jeju island. Free shuttle buses were provided in various pick up point within Jeju City such as Top Dong station, Jeju City Hall station and Jeju University station and more.People of Jeju and tourists like me would gather around the oreum (hill) for the stage performances, fireworks and eventually the field burning event. It is definitely worth visit if you are in Jeju.

Jeju is know for horses and mandarins. I'd say, this is a must see for those who visit Jeju for the first time.Tickets can be bought online in Trazy.com. You should receive your e-tickets within 24hrs. Then exchange this at The Ma park's ticket booth. To get there, we took a taxi from Hyeojae Beach (costs KRW9,000). It's a must that you buy ticket in advance due to limited seats. A lot of private tour bus go here. Public transportation is very seldom in this area. If you can arrange a round trip transpo, please do so. As for us, we walked 2 KM to the main road. But again, the 1Hr show is worth seeing. =)

This was not part of our main itinerary but we visited it as it was raining in other parts of Jeju.We saw the acrobatic performance, it was rather entertaining and sometimes hilarious though some parts were boring for us. The kids enjoyed it though. There was some reenactment of a story but it was all in Korean so we only got the gist of it.
Do catch the performance at the Ma Park on Jeju Island! From horse riding to acrobatics and showmanship, the show is a great family experience for young and old.

Friendly staff: worked hard to communicate with me in English as best they could.  We took the B course for horse riding.  The leader allowed me to guide my own horse as I am an experienced rider, which I appreciated.  The leader guided my daughter's horse.  Horses were well trained with kind temperaments.  The horse show was well rehearsed and the riders and horses were skilled.  My daughter is 8, and she loved the show.  After the show, we fed carrots to the horses for 1000KWN a piece.  I would recommend buying a horse riding ticket as soon as you arrive because there was a 95 minute wait for use to ride.

Think: Cirque du Soleil on horse back combined with the Akira Kurosawa film "Ran." Uniquely trained riders from Mongolia in colorful costumes perform precision riding and acrobatics as their horses gallop and trot through the stadium field with dramatic music in the background.  Meant to tell a story, the riders and horses go through act after act with costume changes.  There is drama, feats of precision and humor.  Included is archery from a trotting horse, which is pretty amazing, IMHO.  The 50 minutes passed quickly.

Bought the tickets online to enjoy a discount. We arrived early to be amongst the first cars within the car park. Thus, we had a fuss free horse riding experience for the kids. The 50mins performance was also enjoyed by the kids. Unfortunately, the go karting wasn t available due to rain a few hours before.

Before traveling to Jeju I was unaware that there was a horse show.  Our guide asked us if we wanted to see a horse show and we said  sure .  We had no idea what to expect.  It appears that this show caters towards Korean tourists and the show is only in Korean.  However, there was a pamphlet available in English.  I didn t see any other foreigners in the audience.  The show takes place in a large arena and lasted about an hour.  The seats are covered in case of rain.  The show is supposed to take place during the Mongol invasions of Korea during the 1200s.  They had mock battles, displayed archery skills, performed equestrian vaulting, and a variety of other skills.  I thought that the show was entertaining, well performed, and the Mongolian riders were very talented.  My 3 year old, was a bit scared by the battles.  The horses appeared to be well cared for and healthy.  At the beginning and end of the show you can purchase a carrot to feed to the horses.  I believe that the cost of the show was 18,000 won, but our guide was able to get us a discount.  Overall, I thought that it was fun and would go back.

I am 6 years old and I love horses. I like the horse show and now I really want to go to horse school. I liked to feed the horses carrots. I really liked riding horse and I can't wait to do it again. I especially liked the little ponies. They were funny. I was in Korea for a long time and this is the bestest thing we did. If you have children you should come here so they will love you more. Goodbye
The narration is not in English, but the story line is easy to follow. The performance is engaging and polished and well worth going to.

A wonderful hour of Korean/Mongolian drama with beautiful horses and very talented Mongolian riders.Had a chance to pet and feed the horses before the show.Great acrobatics.Would be good for all ages.

Visited Ma Park and we were pretty excited because we could feed the ponies! Then, we realised that there was a show and got ourselves a pair of tickets. Amazing stuffs! Stunts with horses and there was also a short drama. The only downside was my partner and I were just assuming of what they were talking about because there weren't any translations! We played the Gokart after that. The karts weren't really fast but that was alright. Had a few rounds and they took nice photos of you! Once is enough for this place!

The Ma Park was one of the best theme parks I've ever been to.  We started off with horse riding, which was led by a friendly staff along a route for about 15 minutes.  I was surprised that he spoke English quite well!  We then headed for the go karts.  The venue was very spacious and the karts were very easy to handle.  I had a lot of fun.  After that, we watched the spectacular show which was performed by around 50 elite Mongolian riders.  Before the show started, we were able to feed the horses with carrots, sold at 1000 korean won each.  I had a blast at the Ma Park and I strongly recommend families to visit.

Very skilled young Mongolian horseriders, who perform a small Korean/Mongolian (horse)drama in an hour. Be aware of the showtimes, because I think they only have 4 shows a day. We were too late for the first show and while waiting for the next show we requested the taxidriver to bring and wait for us at Hallim park, which is only 10 minutes away. We also combined this with a short beach vsiit and local brunch at the beautifull Jeju-beach.

Entertaining Mongolian horse show. We caught a taxi here as it's not easy to get to by other public transport. Impressive expert performance by the young horse riders who did some amazing acrobatics on horses. The Park's website is in Korean and the show was all in Korean but we managed to follow what was going on!  The horse show is on 3 times a day. After the show, kids can have fun riding a horse or driving a swing car (7 minute ride) or go kart (not sure of the minimum age for that).  Need to pay additional fees for each activity.  Worth spending a couple of hours or half a day here.

All guys performing in this show are all Mongolians. From 1270-1340 year Mongolian empire was held in Jeju island. So horse riding culture is came from Mongolia. Very skillfull and somehow funny show.

It s my 3rd time to visit there. When I was there in the last time with kids, we just spent time with feeding carrots to horse.And my son had experienced horseback riding. Whenever, I visited there the time of performance didn t allow me to enjoy it.This time I see the performance firstly. At first, I didn t have any expectations. But all audiences were driven by their enthusiasm when the actors started to the taster performances. They were danced horse-dance with PSY s gangnam style.Main theme is the origin of Ju-mong and his foundation of a country.Even I didn t understand the story well, the equestrian(riding skill) was really amazing and wonderful. I really enjoy it with kids(9, 5yrs).The cost is a little bit expensive but really money worth performance. One thing you should mind, there are not supplying English translation.  And the actors are Mongolians then they don t speak Korean and Englsih.

The horse performance was quite good, except they don't have english translation.. so just enjoy the act..we tried the horse riding, but only less than 10mins circling around the front gate with the guide holding on the rope.. Super Expensive for horse Riding, so Not Recommended.

Rather interesting show about the life of Genghis Khan. But a lot of dialogs on Korean, so it is better to speak Korean or know history a bit. Anyway, there was beautiful and spectacular stunts on horseback. We were glad we visited this show.

This is a great show reenacting the life of Genghis Khan. The horsemanship and acrobatics are amazing and the riders, I believe, are all horsemen/women from Mongolia. There is also horse riding, but the guide maintains control of the reins.  The show is narrated in Korean and some Mandarin, but the action speaks for itself. It is a little out of the way, but if you rent a car or have some form of transportation I highly recommend it!

I came with two friends to visit the LAVA TUBE SYSTEM and they did not let us get in because there were other internationals in the queue and they said that we were all together when we did not even know each other, which i consider is pretty racist.I would never recommend to visit a place where internationals are not welcomed and discriminated by their appearance.

The oreum was not that difficult to hike, and the guide provided quite a nice explanation. Geologically and Botanically meaningful place to visit. But reservation is mandatory, and every Tuesday is off.

UNESCO World Natural Heritage. Geomun Oreum represents more than 300 oreums in Jeju Island. By experiencing the primitive form and history of oreum, u can learn the awe of nature. Anyone who wants to know the essence of Jeju Island must challenge. Even if u do not understand Korean, u will be impressed by what you see. Reservation required.

If u do not object natural scenicThis place is the most value for money u must visit. Entrance fee is only 2000w for adults . easy walking path for child.the only deficit is the tour guide can only speak in korean. The most amazing wonder is the entrance fee includes a 25 minutes well filemed 4D movie

We drove ourselves and although a little hard to find, it was worth the effort. The area was quite well set out with information and small local restaurant and gift shop area. Entry is free to Jeju workers but about 5,000 won - the steps down are step but well made. We walked about 2 kms to the end of the tunnel - it was damp, cold and generally well lit. Wear sturdy shoes and a warm coat, take a water bottle.  Worth a look.

It was unfortunate that the immersion tour group was delayed in setting out on a one hour journey to this natural heritage centre that we were not allowed to visit the 5 lava tubes. However the 4D film of a little boy 's adventure on this island more than made up for the disappointment of not visiting the lava tubes. It would have been a great trekking experience to the lava tubes from the museum exhibits & brochures ... perhaps it warrants another visit to this island?

I went with three friends to Geomunoreum on a Sunday in February 2016. The first thing I'd recommend is ensuring that your taxi driver takes you to the right place as ours dropped us off an hour's walk away from where we were supposed to be at an abandoned building.When we finally got to the Oreum we got in for free as Jeju English teachers. I think the prices were around 5KWon per person without Jeju residency.We had to join a tour group (obviously Korean-speaking guide) for the whole walk. The stops were far too regular and spoke for too long. This is why the route options are 1 hour/2.5hours/3.5hours (I think), because the guiding makes them so long! I guess it was our fault for not being able to understand, but it did mean the walk was interrupted and the experience ruined a little by travelling in a pack. We tried to pace ourselves between groups but kept getting trapped in them. I don't think you can do this walk without a guide.That said, the views were beautiful.

We went with high expectation, thinking that we could go into the larva tube. To our utmost disappointment, besides a 4-D movie, It was just a museum with some picture exhibits, and glassed up exhibits of a very small part of the larva tube. Admission was W3,000. It took us a long time to get there, as the bus was a 50 minute wait and it was extremely cold that day.

This is not a common attraction but it's a place where we can follow the path and walk around the crater. Though pitifully there is no more water in the crater, it's still an interesting place to visit. The walk just take around 30 minutes. Apart from the crater, it's also a good place to overlook the plains and farmlands.The only offset of this site is its accessibility and limited car park. There is no public transport to go to this place. We drove by ourselves. After we drove off the main road, we entered a small road to the peak. The path is so narrow that only one car can go through, but it is for two-way traffic.

Please visit this place only if you really love and in great passion to help preserve the nature. This attraction requires reservation as it only allow 400 hikers daily. There are 10 sessions and 3 different trails, a one-hr one, a 2.5-hr and a 3.5-hr one. All hikers will be lead by a center guide. Though the guide speaks only Korean and knows only limited English, there are signage and descriptions on each special location.We joined the first session and started at 9. We were required to arrive at least 10 minutes before 9, then bought the ticket (2000 won each) and showed the tickets to the Information Desk. Then we were given a badge which we needed to put on all the time and returned to the Desk after the hike. No food, including candies and gums, are allowed. Only water, without colours or tastes, is allowed to bring into the site. There is a water machine inside the Information Desk.The "Gotjawal" forests, grow in the center of the Geomunoreum crater, are very dense and luxuriant. While you can only look from the outlook points at Sangumburi 掠긷訝 and Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone 掠길ε뷴낡, this activity is an authentic encounter inside the crater, with the geological formation, vegetation and traits of lava activities

Nexon Computer Museum was surprisingly a fun visit.  Having grown up during the 1.44 MB floppy disk era, it was cool to see the now ancient artifacts from that era like the first Apple computers and the 8-bit graphic video game consoles (and of course the floppy disks themselves). The interactive zone with some of the classic video games like Galaga arranged in chronological order were a lot of fun.

I came here after visiting the nearby Jeju Loveland. This museum has 4 floors. First floor is the Welcome Stage, which traces the history of computers and hardwares. Second floor is Open Stage, which depicts the history and development of computer games. Third floor is Hidden Stage, which showcases how computers changed and expanded our everyday life. The Basement 1 is Special Stage, which is used for special exhibitions.Second and third floors allow visitors to play old computer and arcade games such as Space Invaders, Galaxy etc. Playing these games bring back fond memories of my younger days. Before leaving, I headed to the cafe at B1 and ordered the keyboard waffle for its novelty, not cheap at 12,000 won.Admission fees 8,000 won. Note it is closed on Monday. Worth a visit if you have half a day to spare. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Jeju Loveland.
Nexon Computer Museum - I went there with my buddy and we were so excited to see all those old computers on display... lol!

I loved how not only did they have a lot of things on display but also that you could actually use and play with the majority of things they had on display. Time flied and staff was very helpful every time I needed any help. Would go again.

This museum boasts its huge variety of old computer related exhibitions to a new one. You may enjoy the old memories of punch card, MS-DOS, APPLE I~II, to VR, motion recognition, etc. The only point you should consider is entrance fee. I was ok because I can get Jeju resident discount. But most of visitors from outside of Jeju island should try to discount chances such as Naver booking, etc.

I think it was more academic then entertaining. Despite cutting edge technology based attraction, this place has enough mixture of both interesting facts and entertainment. Restaurant was lots of fun as well. And I think it means a lot to see the corporate name. People all know "Nintendo" but not many knows a top Korean game corporate. I think it is nice.
4 Floors of a journey in time from the 70s to the very much today technology.Experience interactive games and tasks, good for age 9+

This has to be the best museum on Jeju. I have lived here for over 5 years and I have been there at least 3 or 4 times. The exhibits are interesting and there is even a couple of places where you can play old video games for free. If you enjoy computers or video games at all this the place for you.

Good day out with children and their Grandparents as we could all enjoy something in the museum.  Lots of interactive displays and activities.  Amazing to see how much computers and technology have changed!

What a great place to visit especially on a rainy dayIt traces the history of computing from the 50s to the present day in a very informative wayHowever of somewhat more interest to particularly children is the very interactive history of computer gaming. This includes the ability to play the old games like tv tennis and space invaders to more modern gamesA great way to spend a couple of hours , it certainly kept me and the grandchildren entertained

The museum was ok, computers and computer games are not my kind of thing but it was interactive so really kept me engaged.The keyboard-shaped waffles in the cafe with four side sauces/cream/ice-cream in the cafe in the basement are awesome. Go for them!Walkable from Nohyung Lotte Mart.

A great museum in Jeju with all its collection of computers and video games. Pay around 8 USD and we can enjoy this museum along with playable exhibitions.Not only we can go back in time with old videogames and computers, we can even try to play the latest videogames (Xbox, Playstation etc) and just forget the time while you are inside!Basement is worth to visit if you really want to spend your day playing games.. quite a varsity of collection.Don't forget to try ordering the keyboard waffle... ^^
A pretty rock to look at and the surrounding area is also very pleasant to walk around. It's best to get there early to avoid the crowds and heat in summer, but definitely worth a visit.
The highlight of this place is the lone rock, where there is a lookout near the car park. Go past the lookout to see a different aspect of the rock. We were glad we did that.

Easy boardwalk to see the attraction.  If you follow right, you will see the Oedolgae rock.  We happened to be there at sunset, and the view was magnificent & romantic!  You can also follow the boardwalk to the left for more view points.
The cliff is good and legends about it - too :)But couldn't recommend it as "must see" (sorry, Oedolgae!)

I must confess this was not on our radar to visit. But due to the unforeseen weather conditions we were unable to visit Mount Hallasan and  so we decided to visit Oedolgae. This place was stunning and I am so glad we actually decided to visit. The guide books I think play this place down but it should be a small highlight of Jeju Island.

We went for Oedalgae and ended up taking an unplanned walk along Olle trail #7.It was drizzling when we arrived, we took some photos of the rock and explored the area. Further into the park, we followed the trail which hugged the coastline. Beautiful views all the way... We went past a cafe at some point, it would be a nice place to relax but we were short of time. We ended our hike near Storyville as the pathway was blocked by fallen trees/branches due to the recent typhoon.
Visited Oldolgae on a stormy day.  Spectacular with waves crashing on the cliffs and strong wind blowing. Very close to Seogwipo town (5 minutes drive). Nice cliff top walk.

It is stunning.  You can wear walking shoes or sandals to trek along the coastline. Most of the trail is paved with wooden boards.  This place offers many scenic sites for photos. The photos don't give this place its justice.  Have to see it in person to take it in.   There are small cafes along the trail offering refreshments and a place to sit.
This place is very best and beautiful like a very big mountain in the Sea . This place name is Oedolgae.
This is a great place to go snorkeling and has some great views. There were a lot of people, but if you get there early you should be able to beat the crowds.
We were even so lucky to find some  diving women  (All 60+) - catching abalone and octopus. Dont photograph them or try to take selphies with them. They are as fierce as they look.

Very impressive cliffs.  The blue ocean and crashing waves into soaring cliffs 20 meters high.  Great area to stroll around take some pix.  There's options to go down to the shore with a bit of a hike. Really unique land formations.

It is located near seogwipo (southern region in jeju island). I stayed in value hotel seogwipo hence decided to pay a visit in the morning before my afternoon flight back. Just 10mins away from the hotel. No parking or entrance fee needed. U just need to trek 250m to come to the best photo spot. Overall worth paying a visit if you staying in seogwipo area.
This place is worth a visit as the rock and the surrounding area is lovely. The foot path was well-designed, making the walk enjoyable.
This was kinda close to our place. This area is beautiful. The rock formations  & the ocean  are stunning. We stayed there to chill , took some pictures and walked to the next scenic area.
Family fun...there were views in every direction & everyone was friendly...a family allowed our daughter to walk their dog. The beautiful yellow flowers were everywhere. It was a nice little hike.

The trails to the sight were well marked and easy to walk. There is no entrance fee and the view at the end is spectacular. It s totally worthwhile. Be wary of the elderly gentlemen at the car park collecting a parking fee of 2000Won, it s not legit because the sign at the carpark says it s free parking. I wonder why the local authorities have not acted on this.
We visited Oedolgae as part of our Yeha Bus tour - South Course and it is just another perfect spot to stop and see Jeju's beauty.
Another must see place in Jeju . Easy access from Seogwipo city. Olle trail around this avea is good to explore. This can be the most scenic place for sunset.
The views are magnificent as most of the places in this beautiful island. The place has been the scenario for some films such as Jewel in the Palace. Must go place
It s view is spectacular and stunning. It gets famous due to one of the korean drama. it s breathtaking scenery and you should not miss it when you are in Jeju.
Walk down the trails to be able to view the cliff and rock at different angle. We visited there around 9am, very good weather for morning walk along the trail.

Interesting rock formation open for imagination. Otherwise the area has not much other sights. There is no ticket required, so you can see the popularity is not great. Anyway, nice forested area is good for a quiet walk.
It was probably way less crowded than normal because of the rain. But the rain and gloominess of the sky, contrasted with the pounding of the sea, emphasized the loneliness of the rock.

You can start the trail downhill from Story Ville villas and end at Oedolgae. On that Ole trail there is a museum and a coffee shop on the way. If you drive there, there is plenty of parking and small restaurants, etc. people come here to watch the sunset.
The real beauty of Oedolgae is walking along Olleh Trail 7. You can start from the observatory for Oedolgae rock and walk along the coast to enjoy the scenery. It's also free of charge.

Its an interesting rock formation. I think it's not as impressive as the Jusangjeolli Cliffs. It was one of those take a few photos and go type of attraction  to me. There were quite a few people wearing their swim wear and snorkels. We were prepared for that. So, we just went for a glass of iced drink at the caf챕 by the parking lot. Our server was very helpful and fun.

My number one favourite place in Jeju. The views are amazing and it's free! As you walk along the trail, you can get different views and there is a pool right down there where one can go for a dip or a swim. Although I didn't go for a swim there, just watching others dive and swim there is already a joy

Good scenery location for photo taking & trail walk. Area are clean and windy. They are free parking area that i just realized after finished my activity here and my rent car parked in the paying area! Paid 2000 won to old man already waiting next to my car as i went to toilet.

Information given in English about the legend of the rock.    You really have to use your imagination to see the woman.    While I didn t think much of Oedolgae, there s a lovely hike right along the coast, with pretty views.
The sunset at Oedolgae was beautiful. It was free parking and free entrance to go in. You can go down to the sea level but we chose to be seated at the top where we can see the skyline.

We visited Oedolgae with Jejueco Suite s package tour.  Victor, our guide, told us an interesting story of a lady praying for her husband who is lost at sea.  As it was then near sunset (about 1 hour prior), the rocks were backlit and we could not take a photo of the  praying lady and her fallen husband . Victor told us to continue along the Jeju Olle Trail (marked by ribbons) for a seaside hike, and he will wait for us at the next carpark.  I forgot to ask him how long the walk is expected to be, so when I can t see any carpark after 10-15min, I kept wondering if I had somehow taken a wrong path.  So for the benefit of Victor s future guests, these are the approximate GPS coordinates:Oedolgae: 33.2390574,126.5446144Carpark: 33.2397470,126.5318070(You will pass by a cafe called 60 Beans)Along the path, there are other viewing platforms of Oedolgae Rock where it was not backlit by the sun.  However the angle was wrong, and from these other platforms, you can t see the shape of the  praying lady and her fallen husband .

This rock has the legend of a beautiful wife praying for a loving husband who has gone missing when fishing. When you look you may find the shape of a lady praying with a man on the bottom with a big tummy. Even more impressive is the walk around the coastal nature. It is considered to be number one walking trail in Jeju, Ollegil no. 7.
A short walk from the parking lot to see Oedolgae rock. Keep walking along the trail to get more views of the rock from different angles.

We came here but it was very hot and the sun intensity was very high. Its a long walk from the parking lot but worth it when you reach.We didn't go in the water because it was quite crowded when we went. It can be a bit tricky to climb and walk on the rocks so be careful.
It is a naturally formed pool with sea water, good to go with swimming gear.  The view is good too.  Good for the teens and young people.

I enjoyed this place even more than Jusangeolli, maybe because there were less people, or maybe because the view was just so serene.  It was a nice walk through some trees before getting to the viewing spot.  We went in the afternoon so the sun was just perfectly positioned.  I got some nice photos of this place, especially including the trees on top of the cliff to the right of the rock.  You can't miss seeing this place, even for just a few minutes.

Aside of the rock on the photos, if you follow the way out sign, there's also a place for you to swim in the sea. Unfortunately, I don't have much time to swim there. But I saw lots of people are having fun there.

On my 2nd day stay in Jeju Island,  I visit Oedolgae and the Olle Trail:) There are many tourists at that time but it didn't spoil my day in taking landscape shot. There are few stalls where you can buy drinks or grab some chips and buy simple souvenirs such as keychain and a lot more.  This place where the famous Jewel in the Palace used as backdrop. Amazing view and breathtaking how nature formed this pictureque scenery.Try to visit early morning where few people are roaming around. Noontime onwards, tourists are increasing in numbers.By the way,  the weather forecast that day, it will rain. Luckily, the rain pours in the evening on my way back home to Gongcheonpo Olle guesthouse

We made a quick little stop here on our way back to the airport. We came in the morning and it was fairly easy to get parking and not too busy for taking pictures. It's a nice spot if it's on your way somewhere, but it's not a super must-see attraction.
Worth a brief stopover on the way to other attractions on the south coast of Jeju but if you've seen stacks before, this is just another one. Accessibility is excellent though.

As we stayed in Seogwipo, we followed part of Jeju Olle Route 6 and  7  from Chilshimni Poetry Park to Oedolgae. We started our personal trail from Saeyeongyo Bridge and went up to Chilshimni Poetry Park through a wooden stairway. The wooden stairway was located along the road where a lot of tourist buses parked (towards the end where there was a brown building beside) away from Saeyeongyo Bridge. My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli    Jeongbang Falls   Oedolgae   Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary.  Oedolgae  means  Lonely Rock . Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying  250m . It s then an easy walk of steps and path that s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama  Dae Jang Geum  (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

We engaged a Jeju Korean driver at 180,000 won per day for 2 full days to bring the 9 of us around for sightseeing in Jeju. On the first day, the guide headed to the attractions in the north and east of Jeju and on the second day, he covered attractions in the south and west of the island. Oedolgae was located at the southern part of Jeju at Seougwipo city. We came to view Oedolgae on the second day afternoon. It was free entrance. From the car park where we alighted from our van, there was a signboard that indicated Oedolgae was 250 m away from the car park. As we strolled our way to the cliff area, I noticed that this attraction was crowded with many tourists and everyone was trying to take good photos by standing at the barricaded area overlooking the azure seawater with the 20 m tall Oedolgae rock as the background. The scenery was amazing. Our guide spoke good Mandarin and he told us of the mystical tragic sorrowful legend of a saddened wife who feared the death of her beloved husband jumped into her death on seeing the body of her husband flushed to the coast. The Oedolgae rock was the embodiment of the wife who had committed suicide and the base of the rock represented the body of her husband. The sad story dampened my spirit momentarily but the awesome view of the stunning rock blended seamlessly with the azure sea and the clear blue sky. The fresh cooling sea breeze that caressed my face lifted my spirits and the next moment I found myself squeezing among the crowd to take good pictures with my group members against the picturesque backdrop. As we strolled along the weaving coastline, we viewed the Oedolgae from different perspective and each angle projected a captivating scenery. At one point was a big board depicting the picture of popular Korean drama show Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace) and of the famous Korean actress Lee Young-ae who acted as the great Palace female physician during the Joseon Dynasty. This place was the filming location of this popular traditional korean drama.  I really like this place. It is so picturesque and I was totally immersed in the magnificent scenery appreciating that rhythmic splashing of the seawater against the high cliff. That short juncture, the clock stood still and I just could not believe my eyes that I was standing and facing such a fairy like breathtaking natural attraction.

Walking along the path (towards the Oedolgae Rock) was one of the highlights (since this was the final stop) of our Jejueco Tour. Being almost right next to the sea and surrounded by nature, it was a good place to take photos with its awesome coastal views, clear sea blue waters and ocean breeze in the background. There is no admission charge to see the Oedolgae Rock, which is located on the Seogwipo side of the island. However, I think if you purposely made an effort just to visit the Oedolgae Rock, you might be a little underwhelmed, because it is after all just a lone rock that stands at 20m high and surrounded by sea. What made the difference was the mystical legend that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock as well as the scenery that greets you when you walk along the path that weaves its way along the coast, allowing you to view the Oedolgae Rock, which is also known as the Lonely Rock, from different angles. Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol ("sam" means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a "must-see" in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective "stone grandfathers") remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

According to legend, Samseung Hyeol is where three demigods emerged from the ground to become the founding fathers of Tamna. This is the basis of the legend, and it is well-known to most Jeju residents. The Tamna kingdom ended in 1404 when it was absorbed by the newly founded Joseon Dynasty. While this rather small shrine is undobutably not THAT ancient, it is a unique site. There is a small museum which shows a video that tells the full legend of Tamna's founding.One plus of this site is the original Dol hareubangs (Grandfather statues) located at the entrance. These statues are unique to Jeju island, with a similar variation in Korea's southern coast. There are only 48 remaining Dol hareubangs left on Jeju-do. These "grandfather" statues were made between 1763-65.
